The middle cave (cave II) was quite breathtaking and again once the masses passed the beauty can be appreciated.  I would recommend going as early as possible to beat the crowds and the heat.

The climb was well worth the visit. I have not seen anything like the Golden Temple in India. The vast caves and huge statues of Budhha takes the breath away. This first century well preserved temple is simply magnificent. Thankfully, the day was cloudy and reasonably cool.

This is truly a beautiful temple and every cave is worth visiting. Come early in the morning if you can before it gets too hot as the daytime sun plus the throng of tour groups almost guarantees that you will be sweating profusely, especially after climbing up the steps to get to the entrance. If you don’t have a driver and are not coming with a tour group, be warned that the official ticket counter is not at the top of the stairs, and is kind of hidden away in a separate lower area. Read the other reviews first to get directions. Similar to Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic in Kandy, I’m surprised no one has mentioned this in past reviews but bring an extra pair of socks to change into as you'll need to take off your shoes. You can keep your socks on, and they will get pretty filthy. We were glad to change into new socks before putting our shoes back on.

Is a must visit if you are in the Dambulla Area. it's glory is recognized and that is why it holds the title of a world heritage site, Dambulla Cave Temple lies in the central part of the country and is also known as the Golden Temple. People from faraway places come to see the cultural beauty with their own eyes. Inside the caves around the golden temple there are paintings and statues strewn all over, all related to the life of Gautama Buddha, his life and the events that took place in it. Vishnu, Ganesha and Demon—Mara are historic gods and goddesses that also have some paintings and structures sculpted for them, situated in the caves. It's predicted that the site has 2700 human skeletons buried underneath it. Be careful to carry food in your Hands as monkey's come and try to steal your food or Harass you.
Worth climbing many steps to see these well preserved caves with fantastic paintings and Buddhas.
Visited in this full moon poya day, many tourists and local people who are close to Sigiriya City is visiting the Golden Temple. Long walk but good for your health.
Simply a must see.  Amazingly  ingenious!  Take a scarf to cover bare arms and legs or wear culturally responsive clothing although they do provide.
An exceptional experience. Our driver got us to arrive early and was an excellent guide. That said, I wish I had done some pre-visit reading about Buddhism as the visit would have been even better.

The caves which are one of the worlds oldest cave temples dating back to the 1st century BC, are reached via a long 350ft climb up steep steps. The caves contain a number of Buddha statues and ancient paintings, it is helpful to have an appreciation of the history of this place to get the most out of your visit. Shoes will need to be removed and respectful dress is required ie no knees or shoulders on show.
Probably this is one of the best temple I visited during my Srilanka trip! Truly exceptional as they have 2 different sides of entrance.

Not often that our expectations are exceeded, but Dambulla caves is definitely an exception. It was quite busy with tourists but we started at the last cave and worked back towards the entrance which worked well with avoiding the worst of the crowds. Quite a few steps (about 365) to climb to get there but there is also an inclined walkway. Best to walk up from the ticket office rather than the Golden Temple.

We were on a cruise ship from Trincomolee. It took over 2 hours of hair raising driving to get there. Our driver dropped us off on the main street in front of the giant statue of Buddha. As it turns out, that is not where you get the tickets. You have to climb up a long set of stairs and then down a hill and up another hill to get the tickets. Then the long climb to the top begins. The temple was interesting and unique but not worth 5 hours of driving and climbing hundreds of steps to see it for 2 hours.
We went here before visiting the five caves, it's a pretty impressive site, the  Buddha is huge.  Just to stand before the golden statue is awe inspiring.

This is one of the oldest cave temples in Sri Lanka and a must for Buddhist ‘s. We love the five different caves with all different Budha’s and wall:ceiling paintings. The walk to get the tickets and then visit the temple is not for the faint hearted. Remember to wear trousers or long skirts or sarongs.
The climb up to this site is worth it. The 5 caves contain a large collection of statues that are well maintained.

I visited the 5 cave temples with my wife (both 27) last week. They are absolutely fantastic and very much worth the visit. The Tuk Tuk from Dambulla to the bottom of the steps was 300 rupees and was very quick. The 5 caves contain countless Buddha statues, some of which are really elaborate and most of them in fantastic condition. It is on top of a hill but there is plenty of shade and good quality steps to the top. As it is a Buddhist site shoulders and legs should be covered. Great place, would recommend to everyone.
After about 300 steps or may be more you reach to the Cave Temple. Populated by the tourists and locals, it may be crowded too. Nice and interesting enough to visit.

Very nice place. These caves offer Marvellous and interesting Buddha in various position, standing or sitting next to small Stupa making the place unforgetable. Alto the wall painting very very interesting.

We stopped by on the way from Sigiryia to Kandy. It was very interesting and the art work inside cave temples was very interesting. Highly recommend to take your time and walk through the different parts.
Great view climbing up and well worth it when you arrive and enter each of these temples.  It was useful to have a guide who charged little and approached us at the entrance.
A very unique temple and well with a visit if you happen to be in the area. A bit of a climb to reach the cave. Stunning views once you reach the top

Place : Dambulla Royal Cave Temple , Dambulla, Srilanka It is also known to be UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITE. Must to see place. Has entry tickets & dress codes. When we hear about the name about Dambulla royal cave temple we think of Golden Temple of Dambulla. Let us be clear both are different, even though it's on the same route. BOTH ARE DIFFERENT. ( Images attached with is post is taken directly from the Dambulla Cave Temple via smartphone and belongs to The Wanderer- RR page) Dambulla cave temple's the most largest conservated cave temple which was built by King Wattagamini Abhaya (As per W.A.M.R.R. Dharmasena of Walagamba Pirivena). Before this period also many monks were living in these caves for meditation, these things were proved by inscriptions. Total of 75 caves were found from westside. * Five caves were built as a shrine rooms. a. Dewraja Viharaya - Cave 1 b. Maharaja Vihraya - Cave 2 c. Mahaaluth Viharaya - Cave 3 d. Pashchima Viharaya - Cave 4 e. Dewana aluth Viharaya - Cave 5 * 22000 Square feet were used for Canopy painting in the walls of shrine. Some indicates historical events, & some indicates Buddha & Bodhisathwa characters. * There are 151 Buddha statues with many positions & symbols (Mudras). * There are 2 statues of Gods, 2 images of bodhisathwa, & 3 images of Kings. * These caves were used as dwelling by monks. * 35 inscriptions have found from the Cave temple & hope to get more details.
This is a lovely place to visit, but not for the elderly. The steps are too high. Ensure you’re not in shorts or sleeve less clothes. On the way down, visit the golden Buddha temple.

This was a fascinating series of cave temples packed full of Buddha statues in different poses. The hike from the backside is not that difficult, in fact it was far easier the similar caves we have been to in Laos. It is maybe a 15 minute climb to the top. I recommend bringing a plastic bag to put your shoes into since you must remove them to enter the temple area. This saves you the nominal fee to store them and ensures they will still be there when you leave. Going down you encounter the giant sitting Buddha and museum. We skipped the museum but took a few pics. Note: Do not try to ascend from the Buddha statue to the caves. You can ONLY buy tickets on the other side. Hopefully this saves you from making multiple climbs.

Depending on your fitness level it’s a nice hike to the top. The caves are not large but quite interesting to look at. It is a prime tourist destination so be aware you will be sharing the small spaces with ALOT of people. If you are not responsible enough to cover your shoulders and knees before you arrive you will need to pay a fee for the scarves you borrow. The temple also temporarily closes for prayer time so you might be waiting around if you get there at the wrong times.

We recently visited the cave Temples at Dambulla. It is an amazing place, and well worth a visit. The workmanship involved is fantastic. It’s a bit of a climb up to the temple with monkeys for company!

This was a huge disappointment. It is supposed to be a sacred place, and as respectfull people we took off our shoes and covered shoulders and knees with a scarve that was provided by a man at the entrance. You are not allowed to carry your shoes inside, you have to pay to have them stored. When we came out of the temple after 10 minutes, since temple is not that spectacular (quite small, no information provided), we went to return the scarve and it turned out we had to pay for this also. This information was not provided upfront. All these costs were quite minimal, but it still made us feel like they were taking advantage of us being respectfull. Besides this, the view on the top is nice, but when you look closer you notice that there is garbage everywhere. It was disgusting and ruined the already bad experience.
Five cabes from 1st century b.c. Very fascinating and well maintained. Some of the cave have been carved out of the stone

The caves at the top of a very steep climb , were well worth the visit, the Buddhas and paintings on the caves were lovely and you felt the holiness. Didn't feel it at the golden Buddha at the bottom though, but too glitzy

The cave-temples are really nice and gives you bonus for the hard and steep walk up the many srairs. Start with the cave in the far end, as the caves become larger and larger. A great experience that makes you wonder

Up the side of a hill at the edge of Dambulla is the Cave Temple.  There's a series of caves with Buddha's in various poses.  Ceilings are painted with traditional designs.  It's an easy hike up to the caves.  10 minutes at the most.

Although the Golden Temple near the road has a Las Vegas vibe, the cave/rock temple at the top of the hill is serene and reverent. It was too hot for my girlfriend to ascend all the steps, but I'm glad I went. Even though there was a bit of drama getting in - you have to pay to store your shoes with the designated vendor and their are people selling stuff - once you get inside the gate, people are quiet and there are intimate spaces where all the buddhas rest. To look at the walls covered with paintings of buddha gives one pause.I found the far reclining buddha particularly affecting.
Calm and beautiful temple. Defintely worth to climb the rock. There were only a few visitors in the afternoon when we visited the place which was very peaceful at that time.

Visited here on Jan 19th,2019. Bit of a scenic climb to reach these temples. You have 2 options - either the slope walk or the step walk. Monkeys can be found on both. The cave temples have Buddha statues in different poses - the meditation pose, the sleeping pose (at death apparently) etc. Ancient wall and roof paintings (frescoes) can also be found here.
there are 5 caves, all with many different aspects. Most of the caves are very large so you can take your time to walk around inside and look at all the amazing artifcats
After having seen temples and stupas for 9 days this cave temple was still a wauw. So many buddah statues and frescos. Certainly worth the effort and entry fee of 1.500 rupies.

Our driver dropped us off on the main road in front of the large stupa and Golden Temple.  We could not locate the ticket booth in that lower area and then later found a sign directing us to walk uphill on the path to the left of the Buddha.  Once we passed several fruit vendors, you hit a intersection/fork in the road - the left path indicates "Purchase Entrance Tickets to Cave Temple".  Tuk tuk drivers were offering rides to the ticket purchase area which was several minutes away. Another major problem we were unaware of was that there are two paths up to the Cave Temple.  The path behind the ticket booth is narrow, uneven steep in some sections, has no shade and hugs the side of the mountain.  When we spoke to another visitor while we were removing our shoes at the top of the mountain, we learned that some people took a tuk tuk to purchase their tickets, then tuk tuk back to the intersection/fork in the road to take the larger, wider, path up to the Cave Temple. Once we finally made it to the Cave Temple, we were very pleased even though we had to pay a nominal amount to store our footwear.  The different buddha statues inside the painted caves were a marvel.  It can be warm inside some of the smaller caves if there are too many people.  Just step outside and wait for the crowds to clear out. After exploring all the caves, we took the main path back down to the Golden Buddha.  Definitely recommend the main path as it was so much wider, had shady spots and even seemed shorter. The restrooms at the base of the Golden Buddha next to the stadium were filthy and smelly.  One would expect a reasonable amount of cleanliness if we had to pay 100 rupees.  Perhaps there was an event the night before and the maintenance crew did not arrive that day.  The restrooms consisted of long rows of stalls with doors - one side for women, other side for men.  No western style toilets, all squat style.  We had to fold up our pant legs because the ground was wet.   Using the restrooms was a necessity because there were no restrooms at the top of the mountain and our next stop was 2-3 hours away.

We visited the cave temples at around 4.30pm. It was slightly cooler and so the climb wasn't too tiring. It is very dark and difficult to see all the different colours so a little bit of flash photography will bring the place to life. I thought it was definitely worth the climb and entrance fee.

Maybe I would have found this much better value for money if I had a guide, but without it was an interesting sight, but not enough to keep my interest for any more than an hour and for this length of time the entrance fee is too steep. As other reviewers state the climb can be a little tiring if you are not of average fitness. Great views at the top and lots of monkeys around

Again, relativyly high entrance fee for "foreigners" but still cheap for westerners. A fairly straightforward climb to the caves. Pay for shoe storage and to cover your knees, shoulders etc should you be wearing something unsuitable but not expensive. Guide books also available and not included with the admission. People prepared to guide you round - for a fee, should you need it. Just use Google, phones are fine to use ! Lots of Buddha's in various sizes, hands in different configurations etc as with all Buddhist temples. If it's your thing, great, if not, slightly underwhelming! Stroll down the steps the other to the museum and golden Buddha. We didn't bother to go in either but the toilets were the best 100LKR I spent that day! Beware, make sure you enter via the cave temple side if you want to see them And get your tickets you cannot get tickets from the golden Buddha side.

The caves open at certain times following the religious ceremonies. The climb up the steps is a bit tough and you have to leave your shoes outside (paying if you want them to be safe) The first cave is small with a reclining Budda. The second is much larger with lots of Budda statues. The painted ceilings are great and it really is a work of art getting all these up the side of a mountain and built into the caves. There is another large cave too.

Entrance fee 1500 rupees per person (only foreigners). Plus they charge you extra for place where to leave your shoes (25 rupees) and 100 rupees for blanket to cover your shoulder. I don’t think that for entrance sacred place you have to pay. It’s business for them. Toilet was 100 rupees (for foreigners), there is no toilet bowl - only hole in the ground.
Interesting but one can get get slightly over stretched if you are not into Budha

Despite having to pay for your shoes to be put aside and pay an entrance fee ( In Thailand the Buddhist temple are all free to enter, just donations are appreciated) , this temple was well worth the climb. The statues were amazing in in the rock face and to think that the work was done centuries ago.

Our destiny was Sigiriya from Negombo, and in our way, we stopped in Dambulla Temple. This place is amazing, no crowded and go will love this place. the painting are originals and you have only to enjoy. At the beginning, there's a little climbing in stairs but nothing crazy, and you can rest if you need to
I just love the culture and feel knowing that was a special place. A must visit. Put on your walking shoes!

We went to the cave because it is the main thing to do in Dambulla. The ticket to ey inside is 1500 rupees, which is quite expensive for Sri Lanka. We expected to see something different or amazing but it wasn’t like that. There are MANY temples which are much better than this one. In addition, if you don’t wear something to cover your legs, you have to pay 100 extra and 25 extra for the shoes.

We visited this Temple with friends..there is no entrance fee but if you go up for cave temple you have to buy tickets..but Tickets available on other side so recommend after visit Golden Temple take your vehicle and go other side entrance of Cave temple and buy tickets and than go..

Dambulla is a very beautiful Buddhist temple and the main temple and stunning Buddha's statues are on the top of a small mountain.The cave complex is also full of  colourful cave paintings. It is a small climb but the surrounding area is breathtaking. Greeny environment everywhere and lots of monkeys.

Quick stop off at the Golden Temple of Dambulla and wow!!! It is huge and so decorative! Beautiful colours and statues. It is just down from the temple in the caves so easy to get to both. Great stop off!

The Golden Temple is a Disney-esque and rather tacky building at the base of the mountain in the centre of Dambulla. It should not be confused with the Cave Temple which is much higher up the hill -and, whilst it can be accessed by climbing up the hill from the Golden Temple, should not be done so unless you are prepared to walk down the other side and get your ticket before climbing back up! To get entrance to Cave Temple, go to the base of the hill away from the town - buy a ticket then climb up.
Nice to see on top of a hill (be prepared for some steps!). Amazing sculptures under the rock. And remember as always: no shoes and hats allowed, knees covered!
In Dambulla town , people can offer prayers and move around the temple , very peaceful and well maintained

I never thought I'd say it, but the big gold Buddha on top of this temple seems a bit tacky. There is a series of monk statues on one side of the temple, it looks as if they are lined up to give offerings.

A standard tourist site. It may at one time had significant religious significance but this has given way to being more a tourist site. Access to tickets is past the tacky big golden Buddha site. You can walk up from the Golden Temple site but you will find yourselves being sent back to the ticket booth at the bottom of a different entrance .It is not too long a walk up the many steep steps until you'll join a queue of predominantly Western tourists waiting to enter the caves. They are interesting with the many Buddha statues and frescoes on the walls but unfortunately in my view a slightly overrated site.

Dambulla cave temple is one of the ancient temples in the country with very beautiful and ancient arts. The temple is one of the national heritages in the country and have a very huge Buddha Statue. You have plenty of hotels around the temple for accomodation.
When in dambulla, you have to go and visit. Well spend time. Dont forget to follow the temple rules, and enjoy also the Open view.

Dambulla seems to be a popular stop-off point on the Sri Lanka tourist trail, more than likely because of it's proximity to Sigiriya.  But this cave temple complex just south of the town is also worth a visit.  Walking there is not ideal as you have to head to the back of the complex to buy tickets and to head up the stairs to the top, but once you're there it's all pretty easy to follow!  The stairs up are fine (even for someone a couple of days out of Adam's Peak!) and if you take your time you'll see a few monkeys.  The entrance is 1500LKR, which seems to be standard for most of these things in Sri Lanka.  The caves are smaller than expected, but impressively decorated and maintained.  It was pretty busy when I visited, but not enough to cause problems.  You can hire a guide if needed, but I'm not sure I could see the point personally.  Head back down via the golden buddha at the front to complete your visit.  Worth a couple of hours of anyone's time if you're in Dambulla.
Some negative reviews exist - don't listen to them. This is worth a visit. Both my husband and I felt very priveledged to visit. Great views and meditative walk up. Go early.
Serene with hundreds of ancient wall and ceiling paintings on the granite cave walls.

The history and the beautiful Buddha statues are out of this world. Not forgetting the view from the top. Make sure you convey your legs and arms. I think the climb was much easier than Sigirya. A must see old temple. There’s is modem temple on the top of the road don’t get confused. That’s just not the original temple.

This is one of must visit places if you are in Dambulla. You need to climb a good number of stairs but definitely its worth. The paintings and sculptures in the caves/temple are fascinating. Make sure to sip Thembili (King Coconut) once you are back from the visit...it will definitely keep you refreshed. There are ample parking spaces from where you start climbing the stairs.

The museum at the Golden Temple was worth a visit as it provided a great overview of historic celebration.  We wish there was more information in English, but we used google to fill in the blanks.  The hike up to the cave temples was easy and we really enjoyed artifacts stored in the caves.

If you are like me and the sound of visiting yet another temple has you silently screaming "noooooo" first give it a chance. The walk up was not easy (especially since we had just climbed Sigiriya). Once at the top you must take your shoes off, pay the little man 25rs to mind them.  Maybe take socks as the concrete is hot in bare feet. Make sure shoulders and knees are covered,  both female and male. The caves themselves are interesting,  lots of Buddha statues.  The art works on the roof is worth going for. I didn't see anywhere to buy drinks,  so make sure you bring some with you.

There is a steep climb up to the temple, but it was worth it. Great views from the top. There are many beautiful statues and the cave paintings are extensive, varied and colourful.  Best to go early in the morning as it gets very busy.
Wonderful Buddha statues over 150 including in five  caves. frescoes are significant, raveling Buddhas life and the ceiling as well

There are 5 caves that can be visited. It is a must see. In the first cave there is a big buddha statue, impressive. the other caves have many buddha statues. Most of the caves have been painted. Beautiful. A nice view over the mountains from the terrace.
Wonderful carved mainly Buddhist statues and also great views from the top of the rocks . Worth the climb. Go early.

this main review os for the Dambulla Rock Temple or Cave Temples which are a climb up from the bottom Temple.  We were on a three week intinerary of Sri Lanka, and gave ourselves one week to explore the Cultural Triangle.... Anuradhapura.. Poolanarama.. Sigiriya.. and Dambulla.  We were absolutely blown away by Dambulla Cave Temple, or Dambula Rock Temple.  We paid our entry fee and entered and climbed may steps and reached the terraced area where there is a white temple complex with 4 to 5 different rock-cut caves. Inside each cave are massive, adorned, reclining Buddhas and dozens of other Buddhas, other statues, mounts/vehicles and more. The ceilings we our favorite part... filled w vibrant paintings, mandalas, images of Buddha attaining Enlightenment.  After visiting the caves, we descended down to see and exit out past the Dambulla Golden Temple... This is a modern golden statue and Stupa, Not as culturally interesting as the Cave Temple.  There are pay toilets on the lower level.
There are 700 steps to and from the temple but the effort is well worth it.  The temple is spectacular and the views from the rock are fantastic!

An attractive must visit site. You need to climb fairly steep steps of uneven height. But its doable & can be done at own pace. The return journey from other side of the hill is comparatively easy. The cave temples are worth a treasure & surely one would be enchanted by them. Not suitable to do with babies in arm or in a stroller.

TripAdvisor has put everything under the heading of the Golden Temple, but there are actually 2 sites here. The Golden Temple is a gaudy building with a Golden stupa outside. But the main attraction is the Rock Temple at the top of a steep climb. These caves are pretty, particularly cave 2, but beware they are extremely stuffy and hot. You will certainly sweat your way around these caves on a warm day (and probably any time!) Also beware that you can’t show your shoulders or knees at these temples - something that the guide books and ticket office don’t tell you. The guards at the entrance are far from helpful and will just send you away, but you can rent sarongs at a little cubbyhole next to the entrance (at the top of the steps) for Rs100.

I was blown away by this Buddhist temple complex. From the fish cave paintings dating back to 3BC in the second cave to the serenity and beauty of the reclining Buddha in the first cave. There is a so much history in these caves from pre Buddhist to the present day. It is well worth doing you research or using a guide as there are no info points as this is still a 'working' temple. Be respectful of the temple and its traditions, no bare knees  so men are required to wear long shorts or trousers and no hats. It is a brisk 15 - 20 min walk up steep steps to the temple so take water. You are required to remove your shoes and deposit them with the shoe keeper so take small domination notes 100RS to pay him.

UNESCO world Heritage site, One of the best places to visit in Sri Lanka. The Cave temple dates back to 1st and 2nd BC. Do not miss the drip lines carved in the rock to keep the interiors dry! Calm and spiritual atmosphere, crowded on Poya days. Dress unrevealing clothes and mind not to disrespect the Buddha statues. Friendly locals,  five star hotels and cheaper hotels nearby. Walking distance to economy centre where you can experience many vegetables and fruits grown by locals. Largest vege and fruit collection market in Sri Lanka. Most local taxis have metering and is cheap.

As per my experience the best time to visit there is morning around 7 am. Because you can see the view ow sunrising clearly if the weather is ok, at the top of  temple premises. This is a must visit place if you go to Sigiriya, Anuradhapura area.

We spent only 30 minutes here. It was beautiful, but I definitely expected something more! I would recommend the site to others, as it’s a very important site in Sri Lanka. It cost 1,500 rupees to enter, and be prepared for a lot of steps up!!

Located about 350 feet above the plain, the Dambulla Cave Temple is yet another architectural masterpiece that boasts some significant value to the Cultural Triangle of the island. There are five caves here with arc full of statues of Buddha and various personages of the Buddhist Order and History. There are 150 Buddha images in these caves representing various epochs of Sinhalese sculpture and painting. The early paintings of Dambulla are believed to be belonging to the 8th century A. C.

Firstly it wasn’t clear where to get the tickets. If you approach from near the Buddhist museum you have to climb a lot of steps (lots of fruit sellers, opportunist monkeys and lots of litter!!!) to reach a point where the path splits and you then have to walk down (500m or more) to a ticket office. Then you have a choice - take the new steps from the ticket office which are very steep or retrace your steps to where the path split and take the slightly older steps, which are fine. You only have to take your shoes off when you get to the top and the entrance to the caves, although some locals do the whole thing barefoot. There’s a place to leave your shoes for 25 rupees per pair. Then you get to the caves. We did them in reverse order as the guidebooks suggest (I.e. walk all the way along the corrridor). Not sure if it was the noisy crowds but I found the whole experience underwhelming. Yes, they are interesting but not mind blowing and it certainly was not a very spiritual place.

We visited this place on a Sunday morning before 8:30 am. It was the perfect time for us to start climbing  as later it got hotter. There are different caves and all of them have Buddha statues. There are plenty of monkeys around. Easy climb.

The cave temples was a real high light of Sri Lanka for me. I am so happy I changed my travel plans to visit here. It is a must see,  and the walk up is great exercise as well I hope the temple will be there for another 2100 years. For all too enjoy.

Here you can see the golden colored giant size sitting statue of God Buddha at a height. The temple is excellent looking and idle place for sitting in peace for sometime. No entry fee is there. Well stairs are there on both sides of this statue and very nice attraction of Dambulla.

It’s quite a hike up to the cave temples, but it’s worth it : the view from up there is gorgeous! The cave temples are nice, but I believe that it’s way too expensive for what it is ; in 20 minutes you have seen it all. If you have seen any cave temples before, like the ones in Aurangabad, India, it’s really nothing special, but if you’ve never seen cave temples, it’s quite nice. Do not bring food up there, there are lots of monkeys who will steal everything.
We visited many temples on this trip and to be honest they start to blur, but each and every one of them was unique and interesting. The depth of history is amazing ... well worth visting.

I visited Dambulla caves as part of the Buddhist temples circuit in Sri Lanka. I had hiked to Sigiriya in the early morning and visited the caves in the afternoon. It's a short hike up the mountain and the views are mind-blowing to say the least. The environment is so clean and pristine; the hills as you walk up as well as the caves complex. You may need to carry a sarong or skirt if you are wearing shorts since you need to cover your legs in the caves-temple complex. The paintings in the caves are simply mind-blowing and it is worth every hassle to view them. If you know the history of the place, then you appreciate the cave paintings better. I saw a few guides accompanying German and Chinese tourists. It takes a couple of hours but you can enjoy them at a leisurely pace if you come early in the morning. After that, you can enjoy the scenery around since you are at the top of the hill.

If you thought the climb up Sigiriya was bad, then don't attempt (as I did) the climb up to the Dambulla caves the very next day. Result - severely cramped and aching leg and calf muscles!!!...  There are in fact two ways up  - the old route,  which is quite steep in parts, with broken stone -cut steps and uneven surfaces; and the new route, which ascends from the car-park of the Golden Temple museum. Most people use this latter route to descend, but I would advise you use it to both ascend and descend if you can, as it is very level,  with evenly-spaced steps and platforms.  Why a cable -car has not been installed here as at other relatively inaccessible sites (eg at Masada) heaven  knows - it would certainly help. The climb up to the caves using either route in high heat and high humidity is quite draining and exhausting.But once at the top, you are amply rewarded.  Each of the 5 caves have wonderful painted ceilings and carvings of the Buddha in various poses - sitting, meditating, standing or lying down - and the site rightly deserves its UNESCO listing.   Best to view them in reverse order (i.e. start at cave 5 first).
Amazing. Very interesting how they turned the cave into a sacred place. Just like the pictures in the magazines. Long walk up especially if you climbed Lion Rock the same morning.
Superb  wall paintings and Buddha statues, a pilgrims destination. A steep climbso not for the faint hearted, mornings are easier begore the heat builds.

Recommended way to do this site.  We started at the front of the Golden Buddha which is very impressive and then walked up many steps to the cave temple. It would be preferable to go to the road behind the Buddha to the ticket office and then either walk up steps from there or travel further up the road and come in beside a large gate. From there the preference is a “road” with no steps (or a stairway of about 200 steps). We chose the road which although steep in places is easier than steps for some. The cave temples are incredible. From the caves it is down steps to the Buddha. This would be my preferred way to do this trip rather than a steep climb all the way. Certainly worth the effort.

The Golden Temple of Dambulla constitute a Large Statue of Golden Buddha at the road level and group of caves located behind the statue on the hill top. The caves can be accessed from two sides and there is a steep ascent of few hundred steps to reach the top. There is also a Buddhist Museum near the Golden statue. The entrance to the enclosure of the caves is charges, there is also a fee to enter the museum. At the entrance of the enclosure to the caves, there is a Hindu Temple. The caves are fantastic and primarily display Buddhism related artifacts. The colourful murals are everywhere on wall and ceilings. There are also statues of Buddha in various poses, in the caves. Photography is allowed inside the caves. There are lots of Monkeys and dogs around the caves, especially along the stairs leading to the hill top.

Visiting the Golden Temple of Dambulla is one of the main reasons we came to Sri Lanka. The temple complex dates back to the 1st century BC and its five major caves contain a treasure trove of amazing, polychrome, murals on the walls and ceilings, mostly on Buddhist but also Hindu motifs, as well as Buddha statues. The colors and the details are amazing and so is the state of their preservation. It is a unique and amazing site, not to be missed...

- This is one of a ancient place in Sri Lanka which is near to Sigiriya, Pidurangala located in Dambulla. - You should control your behavior/word once you entered to this place. - There can be various type of animals/birds in this place and don't go to disturb them and be-careful. - You have to climb this mountain for enter to old temple and first of all you will met new temple once you entered to this place. Keep in your mind to visit to old temple as well since you can see many old statures and very beautiful scenes. - There are lots of people who are selling valorous things and be careful from those guys. - Once you entered to old temple please don't touch any thing inside the cave.
Dambulla Cave Temple dates back to First Century BC A Short climb through the Staircase Route. Good Views from the top. There are 5 Caves to be seen
The climb to these cave Temples going back many centuries was worth the time and effort to see this ancient culture

Nicely done temple in Dambulla and probably a must see for every buddhistic human. For me as a Cristian it was impressive to see this temple. There are two entrances to enter to the temple. As a foreigner you are used to take the entrance on the back of the temple. It is impressive to see this historical building and don't miss the view from the entrance of the citizens to take a photo.

We only stopped here as our driver to Sigiriya basically added it you our itinerary and I’m so pleased he did. It was hot and the climb all the way up was hard work but once inside the caves, they were very impressive. Really worth seeing as it’s so different to anything else and unique.
Nice cave temple. Lots of Buddhist statues inside and amazing inside decorations. Lots of steps to climb. Must see in Sri lanka

We stopped here on our way to Sigiriya - and would highly recommend it in that capacity for a couple of hours' stop. The temples are built 'into' the rock, creating very impressive and atmospheric temple-caves/caverns. Great views from the top (including of Sigiriya) and we walked past the Golden Temple & Buddha on our way down.

Stunning temple with 5 caves of a incredible Buddhist artwork. Make sure to arrive early to miss the crowds of largely disrespectful, noisy bus tours that ruin the atmosphere and any chance of soaking up the peace and quiet of a Buddhist site
Our guide took us up here, which was very useful for our understanding. The history is fascinating. Worth spending an hour/hour and a half here.

As many others have said, this is a bit of a climb, but certainly nothing too strenuous. The temple itself is gorgeous with great views of the surrounding areas and the caves are extremely serene. Women must have shoulders covered and both must cover knees, but sarongs and wraps can be hired for a small fee. The only thing that stops me giving it 5 stars is that there's quite a lot of rubbish I the way back down (to the golden Buddha statue). Given the entrance fee is 1500 LKR each person and it's busy all the time, please employ someone to keep it clean (plus tourists, stop throwing your empty water bottles away)

We came back to Sri Lanka so that we could come here and other places. This temple is amazing, I seem to be at piece with myself just from being here. I also found That some people had no respect of where they were, chatting all the time, which kind of pissed me off.
Bit of a climb but worth it, with 5 temple caves to explore and fantastic wall/ceiling paintings. Views amazing.

The golden temple (large golden Budda) and the Temple caves are slightly apart. Pop to the large golden Budda for a quick view and photo opportunity and then get a lift around to the temple caves, tickets are 1500 rupees and its a short walk up the stairs (15 mins) to get to the temple entrance. If it's a hot and sunny day take some water and maybe socks for you feet to protect against the hot stones. Cave temples have great painted ceilings and remember to look at the back of the doors. Dress appropriately, cover shoulders and knees and remove hats/caps when entering. You can take pictures of the statues but not with people in the photos next to them.

The golden temple of Dambulla was a great experience! We walked up and got to see an good view over the city and all the statues. It was so cool to see the temple. It is a lot of monkeys on the way up and on the way down- which is a cool experience itself. They're actually all over the place! A must see when in Sri Lanka
This  rock Buddhist temple is beautiful. The view from the top also beautiful.  The Time  you need here  depending  on your ability to climb.
Make sure to include this Buddhist cave temple in your trip, an unforgettable experience. Make sure you take your time to look at all the beautiful statues.

Take your time climbing the 1000+ steps, The effort is worth the great views when at the top, and don't forget to climb the last two steps that are on their own. Go in the morning when it's less hot and fewer crowds

Definitely worth a visit - lots of steps and monkeys up to the cave temple section. But like many of these sites, feels a lot like religion for sale and being used to exploit foreigners. You can just leave your footwear outside without paying the 25 LKR fee if you want, but have heard they may go missing. Guides available for a fee - can bargain.  1500LKR for foreigners.

This is a UNESCO site, and you can see why. The climb up to see the temples was strenuous, particularly in the hot humid weather, but there was some shade along the way. It was a special Buddhist holy day when we were there so there were lots of people visiting, however the temples are incredible! The statues and the murals are very different to anything else we've seen, and the temples had a wonderful sense of serenity despite the crowds. Worth the effort to climb if you can.

This temple was magnificent.  Steep climb (especially after just climbing Lion Rock) but worth it.  So many beautiful Buddha’s etc to view.  Make sure you wear longer shorts as I had the same shorts that come to below my knees that I worn in all the other temples and was knocked back and had to hire a sarong from a very unusual man.  I thought they would be acceptable as they had been everywhere else.  Didn’t take a sarong as had not needed one anywhere else.

climbing up the hill may be tough for seniors but one could appreciate the view along the way. The cave and the architecture is nice. The temple house many buddha statute but the most impressive is the drawing that fills up the caves. No shoes in the area.

Visited with family. It was interesting to see the statues and worth a trip if you’re prepared for the potential airlessness inside the caves. We visited during drizzly weather so it wasn’t even that hot. There is a 20-min walk up by steps from the ticket office to the temple. You can get a guide around the place - we decided not to as the children were already complaining of the humidity when we arrived.
Lovely site to visit whilst in Sri Lanka. Lots of steps leading to the site so probably not great for those who aren’t in the best physical shape. Lots of cheeky monkey en route!

It is a fantastic place with a huge Buddha statue welcoming you. Under the statue, they have a nice museum. The entrance onwards, the cave temple offers an out of the world experience. The numerous statues of Buddha along the way adds value. A must see in Sri Lanka

What a fantastic place , after climbing the steps it feels like your on top of the world , great views And then there is this fantastic very old cave temples ! We were shown around who was funny and informative! This was one of the best places we visited on the beautiful island

Without a great history there is no great future... When you start your journey to climb up you want get a much calm or peaceful mind but in your end of it you will so dont worry but climb up. And you will experience a small part of our great history and even that bit will make you satisfied....

A steep climb but worth it in the end. We did Sigariya on the same day and that was a little too much so you may want to spread those trips out. Beautiful sculptures and don't forget to look at the paintings on the roof of the caves.
Very beautiful temple and really worth going to. I loved all the details inside and highly recommended to go to

We went en route from Sigiriya to Kandy.  The guide dropped us off, and it's a steep five minute walk up from the car park to the temple entrance.  The views from the top across to the south are fantasic. The temples themselves are fascinating: very well preserved, incredibly elaborate.  However, you either need a very good/detailed guide book or, preferably, a human guide to the get the most out of them.  The available info in terms of signs or leaflets provided is minimal.  My knowledge of Buddhism was equally lacking, so I was very grateful to have a guide to hand who could explain things to us.

This is a must see if you are in the area for other attractions. The climb up to the top is a bit steep and can be quite tough on a hot day. You must leave your footwear to be minded for Rs 25 and I would recommend socks as the stone walkways are very hot and not much shade is available. You will be required to cover your knees and shoulders. The caves are magnificent and beautiful. Our guidebook has some description of each cave, so we opted against a guide (they were a bit put out). If you want a really detailed explanation there are more than a few guides available. The Buddha statues are amazing and really worth seeing firsthand.

Really enjoyed our visit but it would be so much better if there was some information to explain each cave. We weren't offered a guide so came away somewhat disappointed. I have no issue with the £7 entrance fee but hope they will use some of the money to make it more informative to visitors. Area around the temple was amazing, lots of monkeys and incredible views. Pleasant walk back down through the gardens.

Impressive painting and sculptures in 5 different caves, however probably not appreciated to it's potential by my partner and I. Can understand why Buddhists and historians/religious followers flock there though as is very impressive. However, we were more interested in the monkeys on the walk up.
A very good place to check the Budha, and great view for pictures over Dambulla. Also you can check the monkey all over the climbing.
Tough climb to the top of the hill takes you to the golden temple with its cave complex. Take time to explore the caves where ancient temple complex was established.

The caves are over 2400 years and in pristine condition. It is important to cover your arms and knees. They sell scarves but it is a waste of money. You can take the car up to the second level and it is About 300 m beyond that. I would strongly recommend given beautiful statues of Buddha, kings, Lord Vishnu. The view on top is spectacular and makes the steps worth it. Beautiful lotus palms adorn the courtyard.

The cave temples of Dambulla are well worth a visit. Entry is reasonable at 1500Rs per person. Its a short steep uphill walk to the top, be prepared to pay to have your shoes minded 25Rs a pair as you cant take them into the cave complex (even in your backpack). The buddha statues and paintings in the caves are beautiful, the colours really vivid.

Golden Temple of Dambulla is a Buddhist temple is built within a cave complex, and has a beautiful view of the Dambulla town. The temples are beautiful and has a lot of Buddhist statues of various type. Definitely visit if on the way from Kandy to Sigiriya. The temples should take 1-2 hours.

Having seen many temples over the last 8 months travelling this one was up there with the most disappointing, £7 GBP to go to the top up some stairs for 5 dark rooms.The big buddhas inside were quite impressive but still for the entrance fee it isnt worth it.
Impressive historical temple carved right into the caves, great view over looking Dambulla. There is also a massive Buddha statue that is rather unique.

Impressive buddhist temple with perfect view from the top over the countryside. Its incredible how they build this place within the pure rock. The wall paintings are also mindblowing. We enjoyed very much to see this place!!
After climbing many stairs, we arrived the temples . The view from above was really nice, the temples in the caves are really nice and interesting. It is a beautiful place , worth visiting.
Really worth visiting... amazing bouddha statues in the cave of this huge rock, see the details on the ceilings... going up to it will also offer you a lovely view on the region... enjoyed it.
This is a very spectacular sight, wonderful pieces to look at.  You do need to be covered up to enter here and it is a rather steep climb up but worth it.

The five temples carved into the rock are just amazing. It is a long climb to get there and take a backpack to put your shoes in otherwise you have to pay for someone to look after them!! Once inside (after paying your entrance fee) moving from temple to temple is an experience. The paintings in some of the temples only come to life once you use a light or flash from your camera and wow the colours are so vibrant. Don't miss this.

The Golden Temple is definitely not to be missed. After we ascended the path we were faced with a relatively unimpressive looking temple complex. However, once inside the caves within the rock face we were faced with a very large and impressive collection of statues. A relaxing place to visit and definitely very highly recommended!
Beautiful temple amazing to imagine how it came to be. Recommend going as early as possible in the day to avoid the heat. Remember to wear long sleeves and pants.

Was blown away by these temples, went with a tour group, the temples are built into a huge rock on the side of a Mountain & they are amazing to see & to think how old they are 😱the art work is also amazing, there is a huge Bodhi Tree growing outside, it is quite an easy walk up approx 160m & the view from the top is good, on the way down we saw plenty of monkeys & a snake charmer & for a small fee he will let you take his photo with the snakes, don’t miss this if visiting Sri Lanka, oh & cover your shoulders & legs & if you do forget to there are Sarongs to borrow just before you enter.

The cave temples of Dambulla are pretty incredible. Not expensive to get in and five large rock cave temples to see. There are other free cave temples dotted around the cultural triangle but these were the most impressive we saw. The artwork that is still intact is remarkable and to think about when these temples were constructed. If you can I would advise to get a guide to gain a deeper insight into the history behind them as the details really make it. Guides are available at the temples for 1000rs, worth the money.
Very nice cave temple consisting of impressive carvings of Buddha. Well worth the visit but make sure to cover your knees and shoulders!

Arrived on a bus (22 guests) to the main car park  before a walk up the hill/stairs to the  temple on the top of the hill. Quite a lot of people around and it was a 'quite' day so I assume on a busy day it would be pretty chaotic. After entering the complex, you proceed through various temple rooms (some are very small with only a single doorway for both entry & exit. Rooms have various Buddhas on display with clear warnings regarding appropriate photographs. The art work and statues are very old and genuinely in good condition. This is a sacred & highly valuable location and should be treated with respect. The trip down the hill is a realtively simple walk, being accompanied by various sellers of souvenirs, food and drink  and of course the local monkeys (we saw a new born). At the bottom was another large golden buddha to admire - much newer & glossy without quite the same reverence as those inside the temple but much more easily accessed & free.

This was our first temple and what a wonderful place it was. The caves housing the Buddha we so intricate with the roof paintings.  Can highly recommend but be prepared to climb to to see this wonder.

We visited the cave temples on 14th of September. We arrived by bus from Sigiriya to main bus station Dambulla. From there we took tuktuk. You have to say to the driver to take you to TICKET OFFICE, not to the "big gold Buddha". Ticket office is on the other side of the hill. At ticket office you can leave the backpacks. Tickets are 1500 rupees per person. Then you climb the steps but it is not difficult. On the top you have to leave the shoes in the shoe storage (if I recal correctly it was 25 rupees per person). There was a sign that prohibited storage of the shoes in your own bag! Do not forget to wear socks (the floor is hot). The staff also controlled if you were properly dressed. You could rent sarong. Temples are nice, quiet. It takes 30 min. After you recollect your shoes head straight forward and down the other side of the hill to the golden Buddha temple. There is also a bus stop. We waved to the conductor for the bus to Kandy and there were only 2 seats left for the 2 hour journey. For bigger choice of free bus seats go back to Dambulla main bus station.

Cost us 1500 Rupees each.  It's a hot walk up the hill.  There's someone at the top who watches your shoes for 25 Rupees a pair.  It's a lot cooler inside the caves.  Only took us about 20 minutes to see everything up there and then we headed back down.

This temple complex is a fairly quick climb with easy accessibility. Once on the top, we did have to avoid the tourist chasing touts, trying to sell us touristy items. The cave temples itself were interesting in how the walls and ceilings are painted. We didn’t hire a guide, so didnt quite understand the significance of the myriad of Buddha’s in each cave. Personally I found that a bit repetitive. Lots of signs to say not to take selfies but tourists were doing that anyway .. very disappointing behaviour. On the whole interesting visit for the rock paintings 🙏
Still wonder how the history was beyond modern technology... When you visit the Cave Temple, you will amassed...
The largest cave temple complex in Sri Lanka... 5 major caves with Buddha Statues & Paintings... Surrounding area full of monkey families... Very nice place... Calm & Quiet...!

After a five hour drive from Colombo, we arrived at Dambulla not knowing what to expect. We were initially greeted by 400-450 stairs to climb, (which was greeted with much joy), but on arrival at the top of the climb we discovered the climb was worth it. You're free to roam around up here in the temple which houses around 5-6 underground chambers. Each one was unique, and worth the climb and visit. Some of the chambers you'll see need some work, but one feels the Sri Lankan people know what they have here, so a lot of restoration is happening. It's best to climb in the morning when it's cool, not only for your internal temperature but also to avoid the crowds and buses that visit here. Also be aware the girls must have there shoulders covered and it's a sign of respect to cover your knees as well. You'll enjoy this tour of a Sri Lankan landmark, even if your knees and legs might be a tad sore from the experience.
this is amazing and a jewel to visit especially with a guide or someone with knowledge of the site. do not miss this

It costs 1500 rupees to enter and then 25 rupees to store your shoes and if you don't have your knees or shoulders covered it costs 100 rupees to borrow a sarong. Then once inside the staff will try to take you on a guide which will cost you. Other than that, this is one of the most beautiful temples I visited in Sri Lanka, so peaceful (if you beat the crowds) and beautiful views from the top. You can also walk down to the golden Buddha statue.

I visited Dambulla Temple Complex in the morning hours on 11th August 2018.  “Dambulla Cave Temple” and the “Golden Temple” are one temple complex designated a UNESCO world heritage site and situated along Dambulla – Kandy main road.  The Golden Temple is at the bottom of the rock.  This newly built portion of the temple with the large striking golden Buddha statue and the long line of statues of monks is open to the public throughout day and night.  Devotees throng here to venerate the sacred bo tree, the stupa and the Buddha statue throughout day and night.  There are two car parks, one for buses and the other for light vehicles. The Cave Complex situated 160 metres further up is however open only from 7.00 am to 7.00 pm and requires an entry ticket costing Rs 1500.00.  Entrance is free to Sri Lankans to visit this most revered location in Dambulla.  The entry tickets need to be purchased from the office of the trustee at the lower temple complex.  If you get to the top with no ticket you will have to come right down to get an entry ticket.  Notices to this effect are posted in a number of locations on the way up. It is little known that you can reach halfway up to the cave complex by driving along a road branching off towards the southern end of the temple wall.  Parking is limited at the small gate that allows you to join the main stream of climbers.  I parked my car a little distance away along the side of the road.  Do not forget to purchase your tickets before embarking on this option. During both ascent and descent are monkeys on either side along the embankment and trees.  Some of these had been fed by devotees and have learnt that there is food carried in the parcels and bags.  At the top there are shoe-keepers who charge Rs 20 to take care of your shoes.  As is the custom, you have to be respectfully dressed. The Cave temple had been built in the first century BC and had been a sacred pilgrimage site for Buddhists for 22 centuries.  The vast cave complex consists of five main caves under a massive overhanging rock chiselled with drip line to permit water to fall without wetting the interior.  There are hundreds of Buddha statues as well as others within the cave complex together with murals painted on the walls and ceilings depicting the events that took place during the life of Gautama Buddha.  These are still well preserved.  You are permitted to take photographs within but with no flash.  I carried my tripod that allowed me to capture reasonably sharp photos with the little artificial lighting available within the caves. Archaeologists believe that this cave complex was the dwelling of prehistoric peoples as burial sites dating back to 2700 years had been found at nearby Ibbankatuwa village – another site that I later visited. Walking through the well-preserved cave complex amongst the carved images, statues and murals was an extraordinarily memorable and an unforgettable experience.
Didn't go inside. Only took photos of outside garden area which were very nice. I had heard others say the museum inside was not so interesting so we skipped

Yes... it is a steep climb but well worth all those steps. This place is amazing with caves built into the rock face and filled with the most amazing Buddhas... and so many of them. It was quite spectacular wandering in and around these caves. This place is an absolute must visit in this area. Entry fee was fair but remember to cover shoulders and knees before heading there or you'll be up for fee at the entrance to the caves to hire scarves to cover these areas, and then there is the fee to store your shoes as well. I tried putting them away in my little backpack but was told that was not allowed??? Do not miss visiting these Cave Temples.
If you want to see a golden Buddha that is exactly what you will get but take the time to climb up to the caves... a much better experience

The start to the caves are right by the car park, entrance fee is not too bad then it’s a steep climb up some stone steps to the entrance proper. You will have to enter bare footed so there is a small makeshift shoe locker manned for 25 rupees per pair, be warned the stone walkway is extremely hot in the mid day sun so bring socks or plenty of water. If your in shorts or short sleeved tops both men and women will have to hire saris to cover up, there is another manned room where you can hire them, prices for these are somewhat unpredictable, you put them on then pay on return, we where quoted one price on way in and different on way out. You enter a courtyard and a white pillared balcony with entrances to the different caves, head right for the furthest cave as they ascend from here in stature so the farthest is small then as you enter in turn they become more grandeur. The caves are really impressive especially the latter ones, with huge carvings of deities out of the stone. Apparently these used to be one big cave that dates back 100BC, then where partitioned off into the caves that now exist and adorned as time went by over and over again.

These unique caves were by far the most interesting of the Buddhist temples we saw in Lanka. You have to walk up either 300+ steps or a long meandering rocky road so go early in the day when it’s not so hot. Beautiful views, cave paintings and statues.
We arrive on September and you need to take off your shoes to get inside the caves, I highly recommend good socks to avoid the heat from the ground. The caves are amazing and not overcrowded!

We visited Dambulla temple and the caves during our last holiday to Sri Lanka. If you are into the history and stuff Golden temple at Dambulla is a must visit. And of course one of the World Heritage Sites in Sri Lanka. There is a climb up for about 300 metres on the stony stairs. On a hot day it would be hard as the stones are too hot to walk on bare foot. But then we got to know that you can wear shoes till to the entrance of the caves. The paintings of the walls and ceiling are simply stunning and are spread over five caves. You can observe a lot of statues of Lord Buddha. There is a museum at the entrance to the temple before the stairs to the cave.  It only got the Buddha statutes received from different countries. nothing special there. But caves are must see! Beware from monkeys! Stole our fruit bags :) but it was all fun!
It's a nice place to visit Tickets cost 1500 LKR n is a climb of 20 minutes People with walking issues, heart issues do not climb Rest is fine and a nice view of Dambulla from above
When you are in town this is a must see. It a temple built into the rock with lots of chambers that have wall paintings and  buddha statues. Go and see for yourself.

My wife, little son and I visited the Dambulla Caves in September. The hike to the cave is rather easy. After reaching the top, the view across Dambulla and the surrounding area (e.g. the Golden Temple) is brilliant and it's not too crowded so that you can definitely enjoy the atmosphere. However one point is deducted as the entrance fee is comparatively expensive. Nevertheless we enjoyed visiting the Dambulla Caves and from our perspective it is definitely worth a visit when you are in Dambulla.

Beware that there are a number of steps up to the cave temple, however, most people will manage this. There are a series of caves built into the rock with Buddha statues inside each. It is a peaceful temple and well worth the visit. There are nice views from the top.

Just a 20 min climb to the entrance gate. But don’t get rude and upset if you arrive at the gate without a ticket like I witnessed a fellow Australian do. I apologised to the gate attendant for his rudeness and advised that most Australians are not blind nor rude, and we can read the big sign at the bottom warning foreigners to buy a ticket at the office before we proceed up all those steps. Once in the entry, you will be treated to an excellent exhibit of ancient Buddha history buried inside a variety of caves. As with all religious sites of this nature it is a must to remove your shoes and cover up. Worth the 1500lkr entry fee. Proceed past the big golden Buddha on the left to get up the hill. Probably give the museum a miss where the golden Buddha is. If you want a cheep local eat before or after your visit, with fresh juice for 50lkrs, go to Hela Bojun which is just past the Sri Lankan radio tv building on the right of the Buddha. It is Government run and ladies do a great job.

5 caverns filled with images some of which are very beautiful, cavern number 2 is probably the most impressive. Check out the art work on the ceilings too. There's not much lighting inside but if you don't use the flash on your camera you can get some good, somewhat eerie photos. Nice walk upto the top too. Well worth a visit.
Very atmospheric and interesting caves and the Budhas are all different and awesome. The surrounding grounds are full of stalls though and this a bit tacky.

Definately the thing to do in Dambulla. Great display of Buddha Effigies from the past. Well kept and restoration in progress this is definately worth the visit. Just make sure your driver drops you at the bottom at the ticket office. Buy your ticket walk up thr steps, see the caves - you must take off your shoes - u can pay to leave them outside or hide them in your backpack for free! A good tip - you can wear socks and the ground is hot so take an old pair with you. And watch out for the naughty monkeys - they can be agressive - wave a selfie stick at them and they leave you aline. Tuk tuk from dambulla should only be about 300lkr.
Ancient temple carved into the rock. Climb up to the top of the rock is easier than the climb down. Take plenty of water with you .
It's a truly amazing experience for those who love art and culture. Unbelievable representation of the Buddhist art.

A temple up on a hill with a lot of colorful wall paintings and statues in several caves. Very cool! There are some stairs to get up to the temple but you can stay on the way up to rest while admiring the view. As this is a temple, visitors need to take of their shoes, and ware cloths that cover shoulders and knees. As you are up on a mountain, you will walk on stone so wear socks if it is a hot day, otherwise it might get hot under your feet. Entrence fee to get in to the temple and you pay down on the ground before you start climbing the stairs.

The problem with all the temples in Sri Lanka is that you start comparing them to each other and this one was not as impressive as I thought it would be. There are a lot of steps to go up, so not one to do on the same day as Lion Rock. As it is a temple you will need to dress conservatively and remove your shoes. There are 5 caves in total but after you have seen one cave the others tend to be a repeat only on a bigger or smaller scale. Each cave contains multiple statues of Buddha in various poses. We were glad I visited but was not blown away.

Seeing a multitude ancient Buddha statues (each unique) carved out of the cave stone and wood were both beautiful and peaceful to behold. Walking on top of the hill top, surrounded by nature and taking in the view was breathtaking. It’s definitely on our list of “must-sees” for the region.

Going to Sri Lanka means seeing a lot of temples and this is one of the better ones. You must wear clothing that covers you legs and arms.  You can't wear shoes.  My advice is to either carry a sarong with you or wear trousers with zip off legs so you have shorts that turn into trousers when needed.  Take a pair of old socks as the ground is too hot to have bear feet and socks give s a bit of protection from the rough and hot ground.

The back story to these caves is another story of a Sri Lankan king needing to go into hiding and using these caves for a while, they started the process by carving out one of the Buddha from the stone and starting the cave paintings. Since then, many Sri Lankan kings have added to the Buddha statues and as a result the whole complex is now regarded as extremely sacred. Dress code the usual, knees and arms/shoulders covered, Head ware off and shoes off. The drawings, for me, where the most interesting part, as if you are not Buddhist, the statues came be a bit repetitive. Some of the designs, especially geometrical, are amazing considering how old they are. I understand the a I tings have been regularly touched up, so the colours are still quite strong and it is incredible that they have remained part of the Sri Lankan religious life for such a long time. The walk is steep but shortish, very hot to do this in the middle of the day, so aim for early morning or late afternoon. The views are superb and there is plenty of car parking.

Impressive 2nd century and 18th century temples. Amazing cave art and giant Buddha’s calved from the granite. Hard not to be impressed. Remember long pants for men and below knee for ladies. A ten minute climb up about 400(?) steps to consider, but well worth it, not to mention the beautiful views.
Worth a quick view - this modern temple is an impressive prelude before you see the historic cave temples.

At 1500LKR I’d say it’s worth the money due to its uniqueness. And it’s certainly less touristy, more relaxed and you get to see more for your money than the tooth relic, Kandy. Tip: the ticket office is to the rear of the temple - not on the main road where you see the huge golden Buddha. Take a tuk tuk or a long walk around the back of the hill. You will then face a climb of many many steps so bear this in mind. Also you will need to cover up knees and shoulders. And there’s a place outside the temple where you’ll be directed to leave your shoes whilst inside - You could just hide them in your bag but it’s only 25rupees so don’t be tight. Enjoy!

Yes it's kinda interesting for a short period of time, but the kids scooted in, saw and left fairly shortly afterwards.  The adults pretend to be to more interested but it was hard because once you've looked, how long do you keep staring before accepting, yes I've now seen some stone buddhas carved in a rock?

My family of 6 with 3 kids under 8, one under 3 all hiked up to see this temple. The kids were amazed at all the Buddha statues and enjoyed going in and out of the caves. It’s a simple hike even in the heat. The monkeys at the top provided amusement for the kids too. Total round trip took about 90mins morning which was about right before the kids got bored. The temple is maintained to a high standard and very easily accessible. A must do if you are in the area.

The series of 5 caves housing many statues of Buddha and the elaborate ceiling paintings was very impressive given the age of them! The walk up many steps to see the caves would be a challenge on a hot day and the fact that you have to take your shoes off prior to entering the caves is unusual in our culture, but acceptable knowing that this is a sacred place in Sri Lanka.  The statues become a little repetitive but all in all its a great place to visit to see something as unique as these cave temples. Recommend visiting this site!

At the entrance there’s a huge Buddha statue. There’s a stairs to reach caves but no one mentioned entrance fee, past mid point we were told there’s a ticket counter down so had to go back and get overly priced ticket. It’s very beautiful cave with huge sleeping Buddha statue, nice to explore.
It is a good climb to the top of the hill where the caves housed many statues of Buddha and Buddhist teachings...
Very expensive compared to the life cost of an average Sri Lankan. The temple does not worth the price. We were quite disappointed.

Absolutely loved the place. There is a great historical story about this cave temple and it has a beautiful hand painted ceiling. You're not allowed to wear sleeveless tops or shorts inside the temple. Take one route to go to the top and another route to get down so that you could see the beauty of Lanka.
The view from the top is really astonishing and beautiful. The caves have many beautiful Buddha sculptures but at some point they become a bit repetitive.
My favourite bit of "culture" in Sri Lanka.  Stunning Buddhas in cave complex.  Must see. The only let down would be the area below the caves with all the vendors and mess.
There are several cave temples holding many buddha statues in different postures. Look out for monkeys fooling around on the way up to the temple - they can really make a show ;-)

We had heard great things about the caves, which had many impressive statues and paintings of Buddha inside. The walk up is uphill via steps, but was quite short and had lots of monkeys and good views. The caves are beautiful and don’t take long to see; a worthwhile experience but they seemed less impressive after Sigiriya, so perhaps visit Dambulla first?
It's amazing made of human. Unbelievable arts and crafts. Please note have cloth which cover your shoulder and knees.

Amazing experience, especially the 2nd and 3rd cave when starting from the bottom. Do not be afraid of the climb, which is not that bad (we did it with 2 young children of 5 and 3 who climb all the way up - taking some time of course)

This page is a little misleading. There is essentially two parts to this area: 1. The Dambulla Cave Temples Which are the five caves in which many amazing Buddha statues can be found. 2. The golden temple Which is the temple at the foot of the hill where a huge golden Buddha statue is located. The caves themselves are a sight to be seen. Yes the walk up is fairly tough if your not used to climbing many steps, but once your up it's quite amazing to think that that long ago these very large statues were placed into these cave structures. The entrance fee only applies to tourists (which I always find a little unfair as tourists are often squeezed for their money, but then again this at least allows local worshipers to visit without crazy costs). Prices are 1500 rupees currently and a 25 rupee charge to hold your shoes outside the cave area. Not too bad considering what it is but be cautious of people trying to sell you flowers and jewellery as some people may want to give items but it's not compulsory. The entrance to the cave temple is on the opposite side to the Golden Temple, but this allows you to walk up and see the cave temple, and then walk down the other side and visit the Golden Temple on the way down. The golden Buddha is also quite a sight, but please be respectful to the rules and customs (for example not taking pictures with your back to Buddha and not sitting on the bench things in the caves as signs clearly flag). Otherwise have fun, enjoy it and be amazed by the incredible caves of Dambulla!!
Good insight but there was not enough explanation for each of the cave. Also the storage of shoes could be better organised. The walk up to the cave is a bit steep for older folks.

From the outside this doesn’t look much more than some steep steps to get to a view lookout. However on entering the caves of which there are a few you are met with these true historic treasures. Absolutely beautiful and truly impressive, you should do it!

Most tuktuk drivers will drop you in front of the golden temple (you will see a huge gold Buddha), but that is not the entrance!!! That is the exit! So unless you want to walk and climb a lot of stairs for nothing, tell them to drop you at the ticket office! That is further away and you start climbing the steps there. The tickets are 1500 rupees per person. The climb itself is tidious, but not long. A lot of kids there. The caves itself are nicely painted with a lot of statues. I enjoyed the walk on the top watching the view and relaxing. There is a place where you can leave your shoes, or you can put them inside your backpack if you do not want to pay. Keep in mind there is no third option (you cannot keep your shoes anywhere visible in the temple) so I suggest you bring a backpack. Bring water with you, and I advise you to go early, around 8a.m. You must cover your shoulders, and wear long pants to all of their holy places. If your feet cannot stand the heat, bring socks with you, because you will be barefoot. The stairs down are nice with cool views, and they lead you straight to the golden Buddha.

We made use of LocoMole, a newly launched experiential app by the Ministry Tourism to explore this place by ourselves. The app provides a list of must-see sites and uses a combination of Storytelling, Suggested To-Dos and Gamification with content that are pushed by GPS and AR tech to make exploration of this amazing UNESCO sites both enriching and rewarding.

We used LocoMole, a newly launched experiential app by the Ministry of Tourism to explore the key points of interests in Dambulla by ourselves using our own mobile devices. The app uses a combination of Storytelling, Suggested To-Dos and Gamification with rich content that are pushed by GPS and AR technology to make exploration this amazing UNESCO World Heritage site both fun and engaging.
We really weren't expecting much when we climbed up to the caves, but found them interesting and glad we made the climb.  Good views from the top too!
If you ever go near sigiriya this is a must visit place. Little step climb on the rock to get to this special sacred place.

We walked around the premises, without really stepping inside the temple. We did not see the point, as it semt very similar to the cave temple that we just had visited. The premises and the structures are beautiful and you will be greeted by monkeys, which is always nice.
We spent around an hour at this attraction, and it was a well spent hour. The writings and drawings on the wall, as well as the statues are interesting. I am glad we took the trip.

Don't forget to have something to cover your shoulders and knees when you come here. I borrowed my drivers "skirt". Really incredible cave temples. A must see when traveling around Sri Lanka. An easy stop heading north or in your way south towards kandy.

The ticket cost itself was Rs 1500, and no sooner we started our tour, we were told that the temple doors will be closed for the next couple of hours for worship. I would have expected either the money to be returned or even better, this could be told at the entrance as we bought the tickets that the doors will be closed for an hour or two.  Also, it is expected that footwares to be removed and there are men at the entrance advising visitors to leave footware at designated sites, my advised is that visitors should carry a backpack, where footwares could be stored and carried in person.  This will cut unwanted cost.  There are many trying to make some easy money and tourist and foreigners should be aware of it.
Make it a point to reach there by 7.30 else it gets crowded. Know the dress code there which full pants & full sleeves.
Scared place, incredible history, Suggest to go early in the day to beat the locals and other tourist.  The cavings and painted ceilings outstanding.
Great sight but there's only so many temples one can see as a non-Buddhist tourist. The roof area is good, where rhe monkeys hang out and the restaurant is FANTASTIC AND CHEAP

I know Im a plebeian but we'd already seen a lot of Buddhas in caves so this was a bit samey. The construction under the rock lip was good and the views were fine. Good exercise walking up but lots of steps

We traveled to the temples early in the morning and were able to have some time in each cave all to ourselves - an incredible experience.  It was far more impressive than the pictures suggest - the ceilings were beautiful and the statues themselves remarkable.  It's also a nice hike up the stairs and beautiful views of the area.

We really enjoyed visiting the dambulla cave temple. It is a really sacred place up on a mountain and was a very beautiful place to visit. We went at around 4:30pm and it wasn't too busy. You have to take your shoes off and it is best to wear clothing that covers your knees and shoulders, although you can hire a silk wrap to cover your legs.

Good views from the top of this rock, and need moderate fitness to climb the 700 steps.
