be ready to climb up around 400 steps before u reach to thys temple in the cave. its worth a visit if u like to know the historical stories on buddha and r inclined for the same. we hired the guide too to get the maximum information. the main temple inside closes at 10 30 am so be ready to start early and visit that first and then cover the rest later( its just a llittle tip). there are small jewellery vendor, if u puck stuff dont forget to negotiate until 75 percent! very important info, u hv to be covered from ur legs and shoulders( means no sleeveless or shorts). so either wear full pants or cover ur legs vth sarong etc... kids are ok vth anything.

Although I have been so long in Sri Lanka I had never been inside the Cave Temple in Dambulla and I must say it was a stunning experience. There are five caves that are decorated with in total 153 statues in different postures, most of them Buddha statues. The most impressive and largest cave is definitely Cave 2. with a big amount of beautifully arranged statues, all nicely illuminated. In the middle is a small dagoba, surrounded with a series of buddha's. All caves are decorated with murals in different designs. The oldest ones are the most beautiful ones. The best skilled artists were those up till the end of the Pollonaruwa Kingdom in the 12th Century. Later paintings were done under the influence of the South Indian Deccan School of Art; however not matching the skillful qualities of the old masters. The Cave temple is very old and dates back to the 1st Century BC..King Valagamba took refuge with the monks in this cave for some time when he had to flee for the South Indian conquerors of his Anuradhapura Kingdom. After he recaptured his kingdom he decorated the caves with Buddha statues and murals as a gratitude. It is the largest collection of statues together in a temple in Sri Lanka and absolutely worthwhile visiting. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage site. Entrance fee for foreigners Rps. 1,500 p.p;. for locals it's free. .

After buying a ticket and trekking up the steps, past all the monkeys, the views we were greeted with were worth the cost alone. The caves themselves are impressive and worth a visit but can be strolled around in about 20 minutes so maybe the ticket price is a little steep. Nevertheless I would recommend it as the overall experience is great.

After climbing up about 350 steep, uneven, inconsistent stone steps you’ll be rewarded with the marvellous cave temples. Definitely worth the effort to see all the sculptured & painted Buddha’s inside five cave temples. Bring socks to wear & a backpack to carry your shoes in whilst checking out the temples. Good value for only 1,500 LKR per person.

I loved this place, the painted ceilings in particular were fantastic.  My only issue was that there was no apparent place to buy a ticket for it at the bottom.  There's a gaudy Buddha museum and a sign for museum tickets and that is actually where you need to buy the ticket for the cave temple as well.  I didn't know that and climbed 3/4 of the way up and there was a sign for tickets off to the left.  Well I wound up walking downhill about 1/2 mile to buy the ticket and then hiking back up again.  There are lots of monkeys so watch your belongings very carefully, they're very skilled at stealing things out of people's hands.  All that said, I loved my time at the cave temples, they're very unique and I highly recommend a visit.

A bit of a trek and steep climb. In all take about twenty minutes to reach the summit but ones you are up there the views are mesmerizing. This ancient temple on top of the rock is actually built into a cave. This is a must visit for all tourists and locals alike. The wonders of our ancestors ability to have done all this.

This is a fascinating Buddhist temple of extraordinary history.  Words don't do it justice, see the pictures and go see it yourself!  Tip: get your driver to drop you off at the "back " entrance and take the quitter walk up to the top, then down towards the main road and golden Buddha.
Enjoyed the trail to the dambulla cave temple. Have to climb around 150 steps amidst greenery to get there

After clicking Lion rock in Sigiriya this one felt like an easy climb. But it doesn't mean it's an effortless climb, there are close to 250 steps I think here. Elderly people should rethink as I saw some older folks struggling really hard on the way up.1500 LKR per person(for foreigners) was charged as an entry fee and upon reaching at the top you again need to shell out 50 LKR for keeping the footwear out. From there you must walk bare footed and it's quite rocky so it's advisable to put on the socks. Once you enter the cave, you will be amazed at the magnificence of the Buddha statues and murals. There are 5 caves all abundant with beautiful statues and paintings of Buddha and other Gods. It's a world heritage site for obvious reasons. Most of the paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses. The latter include Vishnu and the Ganesha. It's advisable to get a certified guide as there are a lot of interesting stories behind all those murals and structures.

It's definitely a beautiful place, including the sight from above. Like all heritage sites in Sri-Lanka, it's quite expensive for tourists; at the end of the day you realize you left 50 to 60 Euro per person behind. It's a good investment, if you consider the care sri-lankans are applying to their heritage, but it's quite controversial thinking that 90% of the monuments in Italy are free of charge...

To see the cave temples you'll need to climb some stairs. There are not a huge number of temples but each one is very ornate and have lots of Buddha statues. Shoes off and a short walk across hot stones if you go in the afternoon. Worth a look, (if you're not suffering from temple overload?)

You will have to wear appropriate clothing to this attraction, but it is worth the visit. The statues are amazing and very well looked after . There is a climb to get there, but it is not too difficult and the views of the area are lovely.

The artwork and statues are very beautiful. There is a climb to get to the rock temples but you will not be dissapointed. You will have to remove your foot ware and cover your shoulders and knees, so be prepared for this. The temples are very beautiful with many different statues and paintings throughout. The crowds were not to bad either.

The Dambulla Cave Temple is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The main cave complex is composed of five caves of varying size situated around 100m from the ground level. This is a World Heritage Site. Various statues of Load Buddha, kings of Sri Lanka, gods and wall paintings can be seen inside the cave complex. A must visit attraction if you are visiting this area, the best time to visit is early morning around 7-9am or in the evening around 4-6pm when the sun rays are not strong. Be prepared to climb up the rock (steps/walk way) and bring a camera (no flashing)

Worth seeing heritage temple of Lord Buddha, I wish basic amenities like railing on the side of steps, benches to sit, drinking water and washroom facility should be added to make it more convenient to climb, especially for children and senior citizens.

The steps may feel tiring but it is worth the climb. The caves are stunning. The amazing statues of Budha, the wall paintings, the sheer beauty of patterns and colours of the wall and ceiling paintings is to be seen. A must visit.
It's all about Lord Buddha and a must see in Sri Lanka. IRemember to bring a pair of socks if you are likely to have the same problem and enjoy this marvelous place in comfort !

Steep stairs, cheeky monkeys, beautiful view and amazing cave temples. In the end I was sorry we didn’t take a guide because if you don’t know much about the place or buddhism and hinduism, you just wander aimlessly through the five small caves looking at statues and frescoes but the few sentences I overheard from other people’s guides sounded very interesting. As always in the temples, make sure your clothes cover your knees and shoulders.

- It’s an expensive Climb as tickets are expensive. - close to 250 steps one way - beware of monkey - you can’t attempt with kids you want to carry them - half pants (naked legs) not allowed though they won’t stop you before climb or while selling you tickets. They are interested in selling tickets and then you gets stuck once you are there - inside is beautiful. It’s almost 2000 years pic statues inside and you live different world inside

Truly impressive. The caves have admirable statues and  paintings. Place of worship for many devotees, requires description from the tourists. Probably the most remarkable visit of our stay in Sri Lanka

Whoever complains about the price - This as an art gallery, national treasure or point of interest would not disappoint. Of course you are well aware that this is a lot of money in local currency (which is why they pay less), but keeping this for future generations is essential, and, frankly I've left bigger tips in the UK than the price of admission. I suppose it's all in context. This place is sacred, spiritual a wonder and a place that I could not have imagined in the UK. In my (humble) opinion - well worth a visit

Historic place to visit !  climbing  the rock is bit hard. But worth to climb. Dambulla Cave  Temple complex    is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. There are 5 caves  with historic paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues.

We bought flowers for offering at the top and at the last climb one came and made direct eye contact. I questioned whether it had the balls to do anything, meanwhile it was sussing out my reflexes and ability to do anything about the future destruction and stealing of flowers. The parking lot is just outside Dambulla. There’s a large (20 metres) golden budha statues on the hillside on top of a temple. Quite a few monkeys roam the area. I am so happy I visited Golden Cave Temple, and even more happy that I invested in a tour guide so that I could fully appreciate everything. The space is a wonderful glimpse back into history.

When my husband and I visited The Golden Temple, I am so happy we invested in a tour guide. The site is simply amazing. There is a bit of climb on the approach, which is good to know ahead of time in case you have any limitation. Once there, you can immerse yourself in beautiful history.
Highly recommended to visit the Golden Temple and the cave Tempels in Dambulla. I love this place. You have also a nice view  on the top.

First things first, don't get too excited to climb right away to the top where the cave temple is at. You must buy entrance ticket first (worth 1500 rupees for foreigners) which is located on a very isolated area. You have to walk 200 meters or more from where you can see the sign that says, this way to ticket booth. Don't ignore the sign, otherwise you have to go back all the way down just to buy a ticket then climb up again. Unless your fitness is at par, then there would be no problem going up and down twice. Secondly, the temple is worth your time and sweat. The view from the top was magnificent. Lastly, the cave temple was one of the most impressive temples I've been to. The paintings on the ceiling, the Buddha statues, and the sculptures inside these caves was beyond beautiful. Dambulla Cave Temples " This temple is renowned for its mural paintings and numerous buddha statues in several caves .
I really looked forward to visiting here and wasn't disappointed. The caves and statues are incredible. Worth the travelling

It's a stunning and beautiful place to visit. So much history to take in and experience. I went for a day trip there and learnt so much about early life in Sri Lanka as well as the islands culture, people, religion and life. Some amazing views of the land too. get your camera ready!

After a long steep climb up winding steps you reach the main temple and caves. The climb is worth the effort, the temple is situated at the top of a rock overlooking the surrounding plains, the view on a clear day is awesome. The main 5 caves contain statues and paintings.
Pros: - Stunning architecture - Unique atmosphere - Fairly priced at 1500SLR - Tons of monkeys - Great views over Dambulla and beyond Cons: - None

We travelled to the cave temple in August and reached there around noon. It was very hot and there were quite a few people there with us. The buddhas are reasonably well-maintained and worth visiting once. There are murals as well which are quite beautiful. The tickets for the entry are located only at one of the gates. So, be sure to get your tuk-tuk driver to drop you there and not the other gate.
Def worth a trip. After a lot of steps - get to 5 caves hidden in the rocks. All filled with a lot of statues and some large reclining buddhas. Very impressive

I didn't go inside but the whole complex is quite big. The golden statue of Buddha is awesome and the building below it made me giggle. Not sure if it wanted to eat everyone or burst out into song lol. Slightly Disney feel to it 😊 Worth a look and as you have to pass it on your back down the hill, why not.
It's very impressive and worth the effort to visit. Go early before the crowds arrive by the bus load 😁 Don't wear shorts but you can hire a sarong outside by the shoe place.

There are five caves under a huge overhanging rock. The Buddha statues are well preserved and so are part of the wall paintings. Access is through a climb of over 300 steps. with nice views to the surroundings. Don't confuse it with the another Golden Temple which is a modern temple with a huge golden Buddha statue you will see after visiting the Golden Cave Temple. It is recommended to arrive early to avoid queues. The place is worth a visit as it is quite unique. And don't forget to bring cover for your knees and shoulders. Alternatively there is one stall on the way up where you can buy sarongs,  trousers etc.
Worth a look not too sure why the dress code is enforced for some and not for others. Worth seeing the caves though.
when visit dambulla must go there.  Beauty of the buddisum and art of the tradition. Mind and soul going to be relax.
Its located on top of Mountain You will need to climb on mountain to visit this temple it's really Awesome Temple I will call it one of wonder of Sri Lanka

Do yourself a favour and just go there. But DO NOT MISS the ticket counter halfway the steps. Been there, done that, got the blisters. Oh, and Don't take the Same way down as you came up. To go down, take the stairs in front of the temple's exit/entrance.

It’s an amazing and very beautiful cave temple to be visited in Sri Lanka. Don't plan to go there in the daytime cause it is really hot and going up all the steps in a hot weather won't be nice. Early morning is the best time for the temple and make sure you dress properly for the temple. If you are a photographer, you must bring your tripod there, the caves are dark. If you use tripod and get the long exposure shots, the pics will be amazing…

I visited here during a 19 day tour with srilankannishatours@gmail.com and found it to be much calmer and quieter than some of the other tourist attractions in the cultural triangle.  Really beautiful place with a calming feel to it, definitely worth a visit if your in the area.
My entire family and I enjoyed the visit to this historical place. This experience will be a memorable one.

Set into the overhang of what can only be described as a ridiculously large boulder, the Dambulla Golden Cave Temples are accessed up a steep set of stairs - elderly and unfit beware. The temple comprises of 4 individual temples created at different times. Inside are ornate paintings on the cave ceilings as well as a large variety of state representations of Buddha in various poses including sleeping and deceased. The guides are knowledgeable help you get through quickly and then allow you to return to each cave temple to get the photos. Be warned though flash photography is not permitted.
Visited on Buddha day so the place was quite busy. But the experience was very nice and spiritual.  Be careful of the monkeys!

It‘s a little bit exhausting to reach the temple but the effort is worth it. In the front one has to get out of the shoes and hand them to a caretaker for 50 Rupies each pair. Of course there are guys trying to sell you cheap souvenirs of poor quality. The entrance fee for tourists is 25US$/person. Once inside the temple there are beautiful cavepaintings and lots of statues in the five different caves. Unfortunately some of the paintings are destroyed or bleached out during the several centuries. Be aware that the caves are closed during praying time and opened afterwards, so depending on the time you arrive it could take longer as expected. The view is breath taking over the island, there when you leave the temple. Attention there are lots of monkeys so keep an eye on your valuables like smartphone, backpack and else you carry around. In case of insecurity ask before you take photos, e.g. it is prohibited to take a photo of a statue when someone turns the back on it.

An important spiritual centre for Buddhists in Sri Lanka. It dates back 2200 years. A cave temple with five ares , with beautiful paintings on cave walls ans exquistely carved statues of Buddha in different postures.One must take a torch to see inside the caves clearly. The grand Buddha statue at the entrance os about 100' in Dhama Chakka position. The smiling Buddha is enchanting. The way to the caves is by a flight os stairs of about 300 steps. A bit difficult for the aged. But worth the trouble. The well maintained UNESCO temple is a must see in Srilankan tour. There vast space for parking and a good restaurant in the huge complex. The rest rooms are also available. The entrance fee for the temple to be paid in LKR is a bit high for foreign tourists. It is the same story everywhere in Srilanka.

THIS IS THE MUST SEE ROCK TEMPLE IN DAMBULLA...! Unfortunately many people confuse this authentic heritage site with the modern golden temple with a large golden statue of the Buddha in their posts/pictures on TripAdvisor. The Dambulla Rock Temple is simply awesome. It is one of the 8 Unesco Heritage sites in Sri Lanka and has been in existence for many centuries. If you are short of time, then Dambulla Rock Temple and Sigiriya Rock are the top two sites in Sri Lanka. Maintaining/restoring the site is problematic so your entry fee is important..! The ticket office is near the bottom of the climb to the rock. Do dress modestly as shoulders and knees need to be covered in a temple. Garments are available for rent at Rs 100 each where they check your tickets just before you enter the temple itself so do not buy clothes from the touts along the way. There is a little booth at the top which will hold your shoes for a modest fee. A tour guide is not required for this site.

PLEASE NOTE THIS IS NOT THE FABULOUS ROCK TEMPLE WHICH IS ONE OF UNESCO'S  8 HERITAGE SITES IN SRI LANKA. Many people are mistaking this temple for the famous rock temple both in their comments and pictures on TripAdvisor which is a huge pity. This is one to take in while driving past rather than actually visiting as there are better modern temples elsewhere.

This is a vast isolated rock mass where King Valagambhahu took refuge in the 1st century BC.  He later turned these caves into a Rock Temple. It consists of a series of five caves containing many statues and paintings, including a 47 ft long statue of Buddha. One has to climb steep steps for about half an hour to reach this spot, but it is worth the efforts.

Dambula is a must visit on Sri Lankan tour. Enjoy intricate cave paintings and Buddha statues that tell stories of Buddhist life, allegory and happenings. Accessible by car and tuk-tuk, mainly, the place is connected by a route of rocky steps from the Golden Temple as well. In fact, we walk down to the Golden Temple from here. Note for SAARC visitors: There is no discounted SAARC ticket here. We were asked to pay the full or 'non-SAARC foreigner fee'. Unless there's something fishy going on, blogs and guide books are outdated in saying SAARC fee is available. The cave temple is situated 300 or so steps above ground level. Before you enter: Leave your footwear to the right of the gate with a designated care taker. Cover your shoulders and legs, as applicable. Cloth for both purposes is available for a fee. What to do here: There are three main things to look out for (a) Buddhist cave paintings (b) the Buddha and Bodhisattva statues, most prominently, in my opinion, the sleeping Buddhas (c) the Hindu deities. There are five caves to see all, set into the megalith to the right of the entrance. As soon as you enter the main arch, you will see the the Hindu temple with statues of deities Lakshmi and Ganesha. The next one is the first and foremost sleeping Buddha. The temple is active in that you can make a traditional Buddhist offering of lotus or other flowers. This is a narrow cave and patience pays in the mini tour of the cramped space. There are several faded cave paintings here. The other caves are bigger and deeper. These provide elaborate painted depiction of Buddha's life, the sermons and as said Buddhist allegory. Statues of Buddha in various meditating states are common. Easily more than a hundred statues can be seen. Others are statues of Bodhisattva and early Lanka kings. In the courtyard, there are a couple of little pools of water with lotuses in them. They are worth a picture too. Beware of monkeys. They are a rowdy bunch. Forget food items, I saw many offering flowers beings snatched away. The monkeys like the fruit at the heart of the flowers. Note for Lanka Tourism: Flash photography must be discouraged in a world heritage place like this. I saw dozens of people shooting away without knowledge or care with their camera flash and mobile flash on. The bright light does irreparable damage to the sensitive cave paintings. What next: Walk down to the Golden Temple from here, unless you went there first.
Hiking hiking to the top until you visit the epic place. The statues were 1000+ years old and still preserved well.

Beautiful statues but also drawings on every inch of the ceiling of these caves! Mind you not all are spacious and as this place is very holy to the locals it gets particularly busy. Well worth the visit though!

Well, we were suitably impressed with the caves and their stunning frescoes - mesmerising! A number of reviews refer to a significant climb, however from memory we walked uphill for circa 10 minutes. Our 9 year old was particularly keen to avoid exerting too much effort after the previous day and even he (barely) complained. He was possibly distracted by the monkeys however! Dambulla cave temple is on of the most attraction and anciant place where you can see very old paintings which it is still remaining.

Employ a guide to take you around this wonderful tourist attraction. A fascinating insight into Buddhism and the history behind the caves. You must remove your shoes so take some socks as the stone floors outside the caves become very hot, you also need to cover shoulders and knees. So happy that they still haven't made up their mind whether to close for renovation, and we could visit this beautiful place! Lots of monkeys there but they must have been tired after a long day as they did not bother us at all (but we took plenty of pictures!)! ok for an hour. make sure you get dropped off at ticket office to save walk. 1500 rupees

The Dambulla Cave Temple is magnificent! The detail of the statues and cave paintings are spectacular and learning the ancient history of the temple dating back to first century BC! Most of them more then thousands years old (the local guide claimed). The caves are on the top hill and there is quite a climbing. As everywhere in Sri Lanka temples your body should be covered and shoes off. But you may wear socks. The entrance fee is 1500 SriLankan rupees. Pay attention that immediately after you enter the temples space a local guide will come and present themselves as guide of the temple, but this is not included in the price. And after the short walk (the guide narrative is about enumerating the statues and frescos, nothing more) they claim 10 USD, which is quite a lot. We gave 1000 rupees, which is still a lot for this but we couldn't avoid it. But is a really fascinating place and a must to visit.

The Rangiri Dambiou Temple or more known as the Golden temple is a beauplace to visit. It has a climb of about 25 minutes but real worth seeing. Frescos, the water collection and the statues are amazing creations. This is a.must go place for every foreigner who.comes to sri Lanka. Dambilla could also be a cheaper accommodation option than Seegiriya. It is only about 30 minutes away from the Seegiriya lions rock by tuk tuk.

We visited in the afternoon after already climbing Sigiriya rock earlier. Both were possible to do in the day and real highlights of our holiday. The caves are incredible. It is amazing to see how they decorated the five. Huge reclining statues of Buddha lie amongst colourful and interesting decorations. The climb up is pretty simple. The monkeys are plentiful so watch out! Dress code is strict so cover up. We took a tuk-tuk from Dambulla bus station to the entrance of the caves, and could then walk to the main road rather than do a loop.

The temple is within the caves on a hilltop. Its quite a climb up the hill to reach the temple and has an entrance fee o 1500 Srilankan rupees for all foreigners. There are five caves with Buddha statues in it.

The temple is on a hill top and had an entrance fee of around 1500 Srilankan Rupees for all foreigners. There are almost 5 caves which are open to public amng which the irst cave is the biggest and having the most statues in it.

The stairs up to the caves are not for those with knee problems or weak hearts and it can be very hot if you don't get there early. The cells themselves and the fabulous frescoes make this place a real delight. Look up and see the special drip edges that were made and the carved writings under the drip line. The frescoes are magical. We loved the caves. We didn't love the awful huge Buddha and supermarket style Buddhist centre over the hill.

It is very impressive. There are 5 caves to see with beautifull statues. It is very old and in good shape. It was overwelming. It is a touristic highlight but most of the visitors came from sri lanka. This is something you must see.
Very beautiful and well maintained cave temples of Buddhist era. You need to have your knees covered while entering though officials can be biased based on your skin color.
Very calm and well maintained piece of history and must visit for all visitors to Dambula. Walking distance from city center.

Vast granite Buddhas carved from the walls within the hilltop caves. These amazing temple spaces were carved, frescoed and painted around 200 BC. Still an active place of prayer, people have sought blessings, peace and wellbeing here in the stone cave temples for more than 2,000 years. This is a place of quiet contemplation, immersing oneself in this ancient human destination. The frescoes are complex and symbolic. The carved Buddhas are majestic. Sacred place, so white sarong and sleeved shirt for men. Bare feet .
A hidden gem in the stony mountain. The Buddhist monastery with beautiful lord Buddha idols on top of the mountains beautiful with long history and great views . Worth a visit
Temple in a cave that is 2100 years old. 5 caves with different carvings. It's a 300 step climb but not too difficult. Defo worth going. Remember it's a temple so hats and shoes must come off.
I saw this temple with my friend after sigiriya so we were quite exhausted. But it's well worth the climb up the stairs. 1500 entrance is abit better then some other places that charge way more.

A world heritage site, dating back to 1 century BCE. 5 caves with beautiful age old paintings. Generally peaceful, avoid holidays (Too crowded). Should follow traditional attire to enter the caves. Make sure you hire a guide to explain the caves, painting and history of the location. If you are not in the traditional attire (Covered under the knees) you can hire a lungi at the entrance for 150 Sri Lankan rupees. Need to climb quite a height, so pack up some water

A world heritage site, dating back to 1 century BCE. 5 caves with beautiful age old paintings. Generally peaceful, avoid holidays (Too crowded). Should follow traditional attire to enter the caves. Make sure you hire a guide to explain the caves, painting and history of the location. If you are not in the traditional attire (Covered under the knees) you can hire a lungi at the entrance for 150 Sri Lankan rupees. Need to climb quite a height, so pack up some water.

Well worth the couple hundred steps to visit all 5 of the cave temples.  There are two ways to the top: drive to the upper car park and climb the steps, or visit the lower temple first and use the path from there. The amount of work and dedication from the builders goes beyond description.  The views are incredible too!

We visited the temple later in the day around 5pm. I would say it's a perfect time to go as there weren't so many people. Keep in mind ticket counter closed at 6pm, temple closes at 7pm. There are 5 caves with 153 Buddhist statues inside so it was really interesting to see them all, however there is absolutely no literature about the individual caves so you have no idea what you're looking at or the significance. I suggest reading up about it all online before going so you know! Also you can buy flowers on your way up the stairs for 100LKR as offerings to the buddhas... TIPS remember to break the stems off before you offer! Make sure you take a small bottle of water with you and watch out for the sneaky monkeys!!! Worth the trip 😊

The Cave temple is situated on top of a small hill and you have to climb a few stairs to get there. Its not a difficult climb and will take just a few minutes. Once on top you have to leave your shoes - they provide a counter for this which charges around LKR25 per pair of shoes. As is the case with most temples in Sri Lanka - you need to be dresses aproriately. This means that ladies cannot wear sleeveless tops etc. Carrying a couple of long scarves with you is probably a good idea. There are many vendors in this area and will try to persuade you to purchase some items. One ineteresting item you will find here and in other parts of Sigiria is a 'magic book'. The vendor will approach you with a wodden book and ask you to try and open it. If you do try you may not suceed as it cleverly designed - he will then open it and show you the secret compartments inside. It is a pretty cool creation - but they price it very high. If you do wish to buy it - you should have good bargaining skils. My wife liked it and we bought one of these things at the elephant rock in Sigiria - We paid LKR2000 and the initial price quoted was LKR6000. The cave temple itself is beautiful. There are many caves and each one has many  statues and paintings related to the life of the Budha. The paintings and statues are well preserved. One issue is that there are no information boards in this temple - so one does not really get good information about the history of the place. There were a few local visitors in the temple when we had visited and we struck up a cpnversation with them to learn about the history of the caves. Their stories were quite interesting, but language can be a bit of a problem as they were not very fluent in english.

My family and I stopped just after here after climbing Lions Rock - although it has a climb to reach the golden temple it is well worth it - such beauty is behold in the temple an amazing feat - people are extremely helpful and kind and keen to talk and tell you anything you want to know - a definite must when visiting Sri Lanka 🇱🇰 from top to bottom we spent about 2 hrs here
every place in srilanka is hugely ticketed this place is one of the free monuments. worth a visit. dress modestly. cover your legs and shoulders

A few hundred steps to climb, lovely views from the top. leave your shoes (give a tip), take socks, be mindful of the Buddhist monks & enjoy. the history of the place, carvings, paintings & ambiance of the place is stunning. Be careful, as sometime they close the Temple to pray. Men, long trousers & T-shirt. Women, skirt/ dress & shoulders covered. No hats or shoes.

It was great to see such well-preserved statues and paintings, in a serene cave setting. The trek up to the temple was quite steep (a few hundred steps) but the walk was peppered with monkeys which served as a welcome distraction! TIP: take some small notes (50-100 rupees) for having your shoes looked after at the entrance.

The Golden Temple is part of the Dambulla Cave Complex. There's a lot of stairs to climb to reach it but it's well worth the effort. The statutes are beautiful but I really would appreciate some information, there's none, on what i was looking at so I could appreciate it fully. I would happily buy an audio guide, or such like, if there is one but instead you need to hire a guide to get the most from your visit. As I said before, the need for a guide keeps some of the local people in employment so that's possibly the reason behind the lack of information.

As with all good things, you are made to work for it and the Dambulla Cave Complex is no exception. There's a lot of stairs, some of which are very uneven towards the top, but it's worth the visit. Tickets are bought at the bottom before you start climbing and, as with all Buddhist sites, shoulders and knees covered with shoes off mandatory before you enter the cave complex. The caves and Buddhist statues are amazing but there's no information about what they are, when they were created or the significance which is a shame/missed opportunity so you need a guide. I had one with me but as always there were local people hanging about outside offering tours but a polite "no thank you" with a smile sufficed to stop them asking. I suppose no information means local people can be employed so it's a difficult one but it is frustrating that you can't walk round and explore the caves fully without a guide.

what i enjoyed most were the little monkeys playing around the area and the view. before reaching the cave u have to climp up. sometimes stairs were steep and there were no handrails. on the top u have to remove ur shoes and pay 25rupees for the shoe attendant. u also have to wear covered clothes (legs) as they dont allow shorts or short dress inside the temple. however there were locals selling sarong pants in the place.

I visited this on a relatively quiet day, which made it rather special. It felt quite impressive, with many Buddha sculptures of various sizes. Thinking about the age and it is even more impressive. I throughly enjoyed it. The kids were not bothered though.

Its a small but interesting trek to the top. Once at the top, there are five main caves which we can visit. These cave temples are built under a huge rock. The buddha statues and the wall frescoes are amazing and well worth a visit.

We had a private driver. We stopped off and bought entrance tickets, not really knowing what to expect. Bit of a climb as well, but the these chambers in the wall of the top of the hill at impressive. Not seen anything like it. One of the highlights of Sri Lanka. Definitely worth spending a couple of hours.
Stunning place, a hardy walk to get there. Amazing sculptures and very serene. Make sure you watch out for the monkeys, they will steal anything.

1500 rupees PP to enter (£7.50/$9.75). Truly lovely, peaceful temple carved out of the rocks. It has four chambers, each from a different period. But the carvings and the paintings are truly brilliant. This is a MUST if you are in the area. We were taken though a slightly easier route up and not through the main entrance, still a little bit of a trek.
It's a relatively easy climb up to the Dambulla Cave Temple.  There's a series of caves carved into the rock which display many statues of Buddha and the Gods of Buddhism.

This was an incredible temple that I almost missed! I had climbed Sigiryia rock earlier that day, and when I saw the hike required to get to the top I thought very seriously about not progressing, but I am so glad I committed to the walk up to the top burning thighs and all. Its a completely incredible experience and temple, and really, for me outdid all of the other temples I had checked out whilst in this part of Sri Lanka. The carvings that are essentially in the side of a rock cave are truly incredible, and the talent and dedication it would have taken to build the temple is inspiring. Like all temples, you need to have your shoulders and knees covered so make sure you wear the right clothing and comfortable shoes for the walk up.

It might sound obvious but there is no obvious indication of where the ticket office is and only tells you to buy the ticket on a sign at the top. you have to go through a hole in the fence and walk down  to the bottom to buy the ticket and then go back up. I worked up an appetite.
Very peaceful place (apart from tourists and monkeys that will steal your lotus flowers), excellent scenery and above all amazing, richly decorated cave temples

Really special place to visit when in Dambulla. Make sure to get your ticket before commencing the climb up, otherwise you can redo the whole climb. Prices are low compared to other sites in the area.
Amazing place must see!!!! It's quite high up so wear good shoes but the caves are amazing The statutes and paintings inside are beautiful.

Although I heard it was approx 700 stairs up to the caves, it wasn't so bad and for most of the way you can use a footpath instead of climbing the stairs. It is well worth the effort to see the incredible statues and cave art. What a cultural heritage!
Very peaceful place .A place of great historical & religious significance.The view of the surrounding from the top is also beautiful.

It is really a long climb up there with monkeys on the way that may steal your food. So be careful not to hold anything in your hands. You need to take off your shoes up there. There is a man that can store them for you for a small fee.

This was my first historical/cultural site on my Sri Lankan trip.  The stairs at first appear steep and yes they were however as I later discovered after visiting other sites and treks, the stairs weren't too bad!  Just a few pesky monkies along the way! Unfortunately I fell victim to a "guide" wanting to show me the way and then rip me off for money however I eventually got rid of him.  Regardless of where you leave your shoes as you enter, they'll be taken to a shoe collection area and you'll have to pay to get them back.  By memory it wasn't much, maybe AUD$0.50-$1.00 The caves were just amazing, you'll be awe inspired the whole time.  Make an effort and do some reading or research on the various caves so you can truly appreciate what you're looking at.

We did the climb in the late afternoon, sun heat is less and the place gets something different at the time not cheap but worth Different caves with plenty of boeddhas dating different centuries. pity for the fence who is limiting the view over the area. some monkeys on the outside.

After a climb of several hunderd steps, you will arrive at the entrance. In the different caves you will find different boeddha statues of different ages as well as the paintings on the ceiling. No cheap to visit, but worth th trip, nice views on the surroundings. So monkeys at the outside. Pity for the fence around the temple

This is a truly beautiful temple, we saw it last of the temples in the Golden Triangle, and I loved it best of all. But some lotus flowers to take up but beware the man keys don't chase you for them! It's a steady climb past the golden Buddha but the reward at the top is spectacularly preserved cave temples with rich red, ochre and gold  painting and hundreds of Bhuddas throughout the many caves. If this is your first temple you should remember to take small change to give the person who looks after your shoes. Take some old socks as the steps are boiling hot to walk on. Also some water for the journey. Truly awesome.

The Golden Cave temple is an UNESCO site that provided a surprising and enjoyable afternoon.   After hiking up a staircase (easy for those active, fit), you get a great view of the mountains and valleys, as well as wildlife, like wild monkeys! Once inside the caves, you wonder at the paintings, some of which go back to the First Century. Definitely worth a trip if you find yourself in this part of the Sri Lanka or are visiting Sigiriya nearby.

If you are in Sri Lanka right now, you should definitely go and visit because this site (unesco) might be closing in the coming months since they are not able to renove the paintings anymore! Entrance fees quite expensive as the rest of the other in Sri Lanka - no surprise here!
Good for travellers who want to explore more about sri lankan culture and Buddhist religion. Parking needs more improvement.

it was a steep climb to the caves so  it would not be good if you had  difficulties walking.The caves are really beautiful and although  they all have a selection of Budas in them  they are all different
Nice cave. Crowded and does not really offer any peace and quiet like a Buddhist complex should be.

Worth the climb but steep steps in places and a lot of steps. Fascinating to see stone carving / paintings from BC period though and how these have lasted for well over 2000 years. Careful on descent - uneven
Nice buddha temple and lot of buddha statue with paintings nice to see the paintings on the rock over the ceilings.

This is around 200 to 300 steps climbing the hill, worth climbing and you can see lot of buddha statue and with paintings, we can take pictures of the statue but not showing our back and selfies are not allowed. wear proper attire

From the entrance it's a short walk to purchase tickets. The steps to the 5 temples. They are all very beautiful. Some paintings have graffiti on them and I think the caves would benefit from security to ensure no future graffiti occurs. Flash photography is allowed but I'd like to see this banned the flash is damaging to the art work.  After the caves walk down the path past the shoes rack and bear left to to the road where you cannot miss the Golden Temple. Don't do the walk the other way round as you'd have to climb down past the caves to purchase tickets to come on back up.

Just off the road you can't miss this beautiful golden Buddha. We didn't visit this museum as we spent a lot of time in one in Kandy. It's best to visit the Cave Temples first then walk to the Golden Temple and not the other way round.

You have to walk many steps to get up here, also the ticket sale was in a weird place (we took a tuk-tuk there). You also have to take off your shoes and cover your knees and shoulders. There were a lot of statues, also very big ones. A recommended place to visit!

It's like climbing a hill with one temple on the top but in a cave, where you see lovely statues and can hear about buddhism and Buddha, and while descending the hill on the other side, you see a big golden Buddha and visit the Golden temple which is also a Buddhist museum. It's the most important thing to visit in Dambulla. Just don't forget it's a temple so you need appropriate clothes and walk barefoot when inside.

These cave temples are interesting if you haven't seen a lot of Buddhas and temples elsewhere. There are much more impressive examples in Burma or Thailand. However, for Sri Lanka this is a good site to visit. As a bonus you get very nice views over the surrounding landscape and you can take good pictures of macaque monkeys along the steps leading to the temples.
Very good place to visit old cave temple and top of the rock is windy and nice view. we climbed from the rock can see lot of monkies

After having read a little about this place I must confess that I was not expecting much from it. However to my surprise, found it  quite impressive. The drawings and paintings on the walls and the ceilings of the caves (there are 5 in all) are a little "raw" when you make comparisons to other places of worship  but be reminded that the history of this venue is supposedly much more older. Do take your time when you go through this place  to appreciate it better. Failing this; the impression you might conclude with is, "all the caves are the same "
You can see Tempura Painting in Dripledgered Cave. It has more than 2000 years history. This is also a world Heritage site approved by UNESCO.

This is an awe-inspiring collection of Buddha statues, collected and donated from all over the world. The views from the top are also gorgeous and it's a great place to explore and wander through each of the caves seeing the incredible array of statues.

Steep climb up to the top but you can stop regularly at view points. Caves are dimly lit and all of them are pretty much the same. I thought I was looking at really old ancient history but it was a bit spoilt for me when I was told some of it is only 75 years old.  If you are a religious person it may mean something to you but as my title says, I wouldn't make the effort to go again; I have seen more skill and craftsmanship elsewhere and better preserved by stewards who care more for their treasures rather than making money from them.
The temple is a bit different than what you can see in Sri Lanka. The cave like temple is really great and has a special atmosphere. Many monks were visiting the site when we were there
I saw a lot of Buddha's in my life, in Thailand for example and it all looks the same! But it is special that it was in cave!
Very beautiful and full of history. Learn the difference of the paranirvana and sleeping Buddha - feet position

Climbing up worth the effort. The view from to is stunning. Moreover, the temple it self impressive. You need a ticket to go in. Beware of monkey en route. Show storage is 25 rupee. There are also guides if you wish. Ask your driver to take you half way. This is also where you buy a ticket. On the way down go to golden temple.

We came down from rock cave. Buddha and building are nice.  Got for photo op, not more. Parking cost money, monkeys everywhere. Building and surroundings worth seeing. There is also a Buddha museum, we didn't go in.

We visited during the afternoon after doing Lions Rock in Sigirya in the morning. We arrived around 4.45pm and there were no crowds. We went on foot through the frontage with the golden Buddha which was huge. There is hardly any signage and we didnt know there was a dirt road along the back which would avoid the steep steps and ascent but was nice to see the Buddha coming in from the front. The Ticket office is half way up the second lot of steps and is 1500 SLR. You will need to cover your knees and shoulders and leave your shoes for 25 SLR. There are some stunning views on the climb up and the Buddha statues are very intricate. Took around 45 mins to have a good look in each of the 5 or so caves. Would be nice to have some better signage on the way up but just follow everyone else as there is nothing else around that anyone else would head to.

There are a series of five impressive caves to be found just outside Dambulla. Not all are as impressive as one another, but the beautiful statues, and stunning paintings on the ceilings of the caves speak of a very long history. The monkeys are also very entertaining, but do be aware of the number of sellers: although they will try and sting you to look after your shoes whilst you visit, but you could easily pop them in your bag in order to miss the excess fee. We visited outside of peak season, but do be aware that the ticket office is up the right-hand staircase, rather than the left. We found this out the hard way, and needed to make the relatively steep descent before ascending to the temples again.

The hike up to the temple provides beautiful views of the surrounding landscape.  The temple itself is Amazing...the detail within the ceiling artwork is amazing and the calming energy within the Temple is beautiful.

This is not a temple but a cave in which you can see lots of buddah statues; there are 5 caves but not all the caves are well preserved. Bear in mind that you have to climb couple of stairs to enter the caves.
Great place to visit and learn all about history of the place. I was definitely blown away. Give yourself a couple of hours to see everything and also see the rock temple if you have the time

It was really nice to see all the statutes and murals in the Buddhist  caves. There really where a lot of statutes!!! It was very pretty and well worth the visit. It is also cool to see the golden buddha down below. Don't forget, as with a lot of sacred sites, to cover your shoulders and knees. It is also chill to wear socks for when the sand is hot and you have to leave your shoes or slippers behind.

My fourth visit here and for reasons unknown they have changed the flow of people so you now have to find the ticket office which is hidden away below and to the left of the steps going up to the temple. A great pity because the previous ascent through the Golden Temple was a much more enjoyable and dramatic approach. If you have a driver they may well take you around the back in the car but if in doubt just keep asking as all the locals seem to have become accustomed to seeing tourists who can't find the place and they will happily point you in the right direction. Once you reach it through the hoards of very entertaining monkeys you will find glorious views of the surrounding countryside and a lovely temple. The temple has five caves each of which contains multiple Buddha images in various poses. The origins date back many centuries but the painted ceilings are much more recent (19th century I believe). Definitely a place to visit as part of a tour of the ancient cities and DO NOT FORGET there is something similar but with a difference not far away at Aluvihara.

This temple is situated just south of Dambulla town close to the Dambulla rock temple so you might as well have a look whilst you visit that. This used to be the way in to the rock temple but to confuse matters they now have a ticket office for the rock temple round the back. It's not easy to find as there is a real paucity of helpful signage. Anyway as to the Golden Temple it's basically a large seated golden Buddha figure that was donated by Japan a few years back so it's not an ancient relic but nevertheless is impressive. You can climb stairs to get to the base and there is also a small Buddhism museum there. Great views from the top and I would go here first and ask for guidance on how to find the ticket office for the rock temple

I think the story behind Dambulla is about a king hiding out from his enemies and then sponsoring all the paintings and carvings in gratitude to the monks who sheltered him. There are endless carved and painted Buddhas in the caves.  Reclining Buddhas, seated Buddhas, Buddha sheltered from the rain by cobras. I find Buddhist sites as inspiring as anything in the West.  All the UNESCO sites of Sri Lanka I saw - Dambulla, Kandy and Sigiriya were unforgettable.
But 'The Rock' is still by far the best place around Kandalama Only a quarter of the climb up that 'The Rock' was though

Bit of a climb going up to the cave temples, wouldn't suit the elderly or very young. Good climb to work off the Hotel restaurant food haha. Once you reach the top you have to leave your shoes with an attendant. We where taking around with our driver and tour guide so he shared the history of the cave temples but otherwise I would recommend buying a Sri Lanka travel guide book because the history and significance off the temples are really rather interesting. The Buddha's and wall paintings hae been kept in great condition considering their age. Lots of cheeky monkeys and stray dogs :( and an amazing view from the top.

We were taken by a tuktuk to the backside where the ticket office is located. We first walked to the front side just to hear the tickets are sold somewhere else. We wish there would be some better information about this! The climb isn't bad at all after having climbed Adam's Peak or Sigiriya. We spent in total maybe 1,5 hours walking up and watching the caves and walking down. The air up is quite cold but inside the caves it's quite hot. Come here prepared as there is no information given anywhere.

There are nice views of the surrounding area after climbing the top to reach the caves. There are 5 caves in total. We enjoyed the visit and it was interesting, though as others have said there was no information to hand unless you paid a guide. I have enjoyed other aspects of Sri Lankan culture more during this trip. Worth a look if you're in the area.

Our first stop was a visit to Dambulla Cave temple. Picking our tickets we made the steep climb through a side way to the caves. Plenty of Buddha statues in different poses placed in 5 caves depicting the strong Buddhist culture. Lots of monkeys moving around staring at human creatures. Then you begin the descent down the steps towards the main temple with the giant Buddha Statue which is a masterpiece in itself. Views are amazing. Entrance - LKR 1000 per person Notes - 1). Ask your driver to go further than the main entrance which leads on a gravel road right below the ticket counter. Steps from there lead you directly to the caves and then you can descend to the main temple. If u do the other way round u will have to go down to take tickets and climb again to visit caves which is not recommended at all. 2). We carried a bag huge enough to hold our footwear else you need to store them for LKR 25 a pair. 3). we dint take a guide, depends on individual preference.

My second visit to the cave temples, the first in 1999 and was not disappointed seeing them again. Make sure you have clothing covering your knees and shoulders to enter the site. You are greeted by a long set of stairs to make your way up to the caves, but it is worth the climb. The views are stunning and the 150 statues of Buddha, paintings and artefacts are fascinating. We did this after we had climbed Lion Rock, Sigiriya and found both sites in one day very manageable for our family with two teenagers.
This is the place where the rebellion against English colonists started in 1848! There are four caves filled with statues and pictures.

We reached Dumbulla after a couple of hours drive from Colombo, stopping at a ticket counter atop a small hill. We continued to climb the rocky steps till we reached the temple. It is a group of 5 caves each located after the other in one straight line. Every cave houses statues of Buddha from different periods and in different styles representing the period in which they were made. The view from the top is great. Worth a visit only if you happen to be in the area.

We had a great day trip to the cave temples from our Hotel in Sigiriya. We spent around two hours exploring the caves and the Golden Temple, after a hot and sweaty climb to the top! We found the caves really fascinating and peaceful.

The history and culture experienced is worth the climb to the top ( maybe five minutes at most so not long) though I maybe wouldn't advise with very small children as there are monkeys about and it can be steep. I do recommend taking up some small change at the top so you can leave your shoes with someone as it is a temple and you should respect the no shoes.

We visited this tempe with friends soon after the Sigiriya Rock and this was yet another set of steps! About 300 we were told.  Our driver dropped us at the bottom and met us at the top.  We took our time to walk up to the caves.  There are five each with their own unique 5th century carved Buddhas and 18th century frescoes. The only one problem with the site were the rough stones that were present when walking with bare feet. Ouch! Some of the stones were also hot from the afternoon sun which also didn't help. We eventually reclaimed our shoes and stood to wait for the sunset over the mountains which was very moody.

Quite a taxing climb to the top if you are not fit. Once there we were shown around by our guide and he explained the paints on the walls and the statues. As they are billed as caves I was expecting to go further into the landscape. Instead the caves are more akin to rock overhangs. Although interesting, it was not a highlight of our Sri Lankan trip. I am glad we went to see it however.

This place is having multiple caves and inside all caves the stupas are almost similar. The art work inside the caves are interesting.You can visit the place but its not kind of much attrative. One the way from Sigiriya you can visit this place.
A pretty temple and interesting art...we were there on the full moon holiday so had lots of people there to meditate.

It's a big climb but amazing!! Our driver recommend and we Went to the caves first rather than coming up through the golden Buddha. This avoided a further climb. Kids are 3.5 and 7 and they were shattered by the end of it, but well worth it as its pretty special
Definitely a must see when in Dambulla. The temples are in good condition and are well looked after. The views are spectacular, Sigiriya is visible in the distance.

We arrived at what seems to be the main entrance and went up the stairway. Midway the stairs splits - one leading up to the temple one down with a sign about ticket office. We followed the sign for the ticket office and ended at a closed gate. Then we went up again and paid for leaving our shoes outside the temple only to be told to return down and buy tickets. We never found the place to do this but probably behind the closed gates?

This site was not cited in our pre-organized tour, but our guide agreed to pass by this temple. You have to climb the hill along with some monkeys around. In the top of the hill, the caves are filled with statues of Buddhas and other "Gods".

This was one of the most centred I have felt in my life. A sense of calmness engulfed me as i walked into the caves. I just felt happy, at one, and this was definitely a highlight. I will forever remember this day. As you walk down, there are also amazing ice-creams (to cool off from the heat)
Place to catch a glimpse of SriLankan Buddhist culture, A samll musem is an added attraction, Nothing much special about the place

Well preserved buddhist cave temples. Walls of cave have have frescos similar to ajanta cave paintings but are not well preserved. Interest to Indians will be Lord vishnu temple co-existing with buddha statues, A shared heritage. Surroundings are spotless and clean. However the climb up the hilly terrain is taxing for elderly and those with joint problem. Must see on tourist  list
This majestic temple is a gem hidden inside this cave. We took some of our friends from the US who was in SL on vacation. They were amazed by the architecture and the paintings on the rock.
The cave has separate chambers housing statues of Buddha.  The paintings on the walls and ceilings of the cave is amazing.
This temple is very eye catching.. truly a must visit place in dambulla 🙏🏻 Clean place not much crowded .
Not for the faint hearted! Steep climb up soooo many steps! I felt my heart was going to jump out of my throat! Once your there it's just fabulous! Carry water.. very imp.

Very well preserved cave complex, amazing paintings and statues. Really awe inspiring. Our driver guide really brought the trip to life too, his knowledge was invaluable. Need around 2 hours here if you're with a guide but less if you just wander around on your own. £15 each to enter, so one of the cheaper tourist attractions.
There's nothing intrinsically nice or old about the temple, unless you are religious and wish to offer supplications and offerings.

The Dambulla Caves Temple is a steep but short climb up a small hill. The cave complex consists of 5 "rooms", each with its own set of Buddha carvings. If you've seen one, you've seen them all. Only the first room has a deceased Buddha (you can tell by the way the reclining Buddha has his right toe planted forward from his left, not aligned). The others are sleeping Buddhas. Oddly, there is a Hindu shrine to Vishnu in the middle of the complex. The dress code (long trousers, no hats, no shoes, modest tops) is strictly adhered to so please come appropriately attired. You need go deposit your shoes at the entrance and a man will watch over them for 25 rupees a pair. I would still wear shoes because it's a short but steep climb up.

My favorite temple in Sri Lanka so far. Really interesting and well preserved carvings on the cave "roof", really beautiful view from up there, baby monkeys playing around, good scenario for photos and really good atmosphere. You have to pay 25rp to leave your shoes out the temple with a couple guys that look after it. Really recommended and also one of the few things that you can actually do in Dambulla.
Our introduction  to bhudism  very atmospheric but read about it first so you  know what you are looking at. Get there early to really  feel the atmosphere of this very holy place.
Great experience to walk up to these 5 cave temples having large statues, mostly of the Buddha, from different periods.

Up 394 steps is one of the must see sights in Sri Lanka dating back to around 100 BC.The individual caves are man made created by building petition walls into the space created by a giant rock overhang. Most of what you see now dates from the 1600-1800 period. At the time of writing it is 25 rupees to leave shoes at the entrance. For maximum impact I suggest starting with the cave farthest from the entrance and working back towards the entrance. You will see 5 magical dimly lit grottoes full of statues and murals of Sinhalese art increasing in size and magnificence. They may be closed for 10 minutes or so for prayers at certain times. This gives a perfect opportunity to admire the view or have a sit down, but not on the walls adjoining the temples. Photography is permitted everywhere so you can bring home your personal record of a superb UNESCO site. If you are visiting the Cultural Triangle this should be on your list. If you are on an organised tour it will undoubtedly be included.
Must see heritage site in Sri Lanka. The talent of the ancient artists are beyond imagination. The paintings and buddha statues are deteriorating and should need attention fast.
I have seen many Buddha places in the world but this one is real unique! Nice place to go! Don't forget to buy the ticket first before you go up!

We went on a trip to see the golden temple with a group of other tourists at our hotel and I can easily say it is one of the best tourist attractions I've ever been to! We had an amazing tour guide who showed us the best views to take photos and we thoroughly enjoyed the views from inside and learning the history of it! Would definitely recommend!

One of the great places to look Sri Lankan Artist Arts inerrant, This is at Dambulla town and in mountain hill. When you will be Sri Lanka you must visit here. Dambulla is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka.Dambulla cave temple also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla
The caves are amazing but time it right to get the sunset across the plains. It isn't as steep to get to the top as Sigiriya

The ticket system is very bad if you come from the Golden Temple, Then you have to walk up and Then down again to buy a ticket and Then up again, but its Worth! So beautiful and the view is beautiful too!

We stayed in dambulla (and visited sigiriya, golden temple and polonowaru from here) and visited the golden temple but were a little underwhelmed. It is worth seeing if you are in the area but we agreed we wouldn't go out our way to see it. The ticket office is a bit confusing-you follow the signs and continue down a road after turning right, for about 5mins (be warned of the tuk tuk drivers!! They try and sell you a ride to it as they say it is very far but it is not too bad). You then carry on up the stairs from the ticket office. We went at about 3pm, when it was about 35C and would recommend doing it earlier/on a cooler day as it was so hot and tiring! You have to cover knees and shoulders to get in (men and women). There are people trying to sell you trousers on the way up but if you wait until you're right at the caves-where you leave your shoes for 25rps, you can rent a sarong for 100rps.

Apart from the Sigiriya Rock, this is another World Heritage Site took visit.  Our guide drove us half way up the hill , saving us time and effort to climb up the hill.  We walked another 15 minutes up a mostly gentle slope to get to the caves. Upon reaching the entrance, we have to deposit our shoes at a counter. Kept our socks on as the ground was hot from the afternoon sun. Inside a number of caves were Buddha statues, most of which are centuries old.  Took us an hour and a half to complete the visit.

The ticket is pricey compared to how it is maintained its better you see Tooth temple as alternate instead of spending 1500LKR ticket. You have to climb & trek a bit to reach to the caves. You will see same Budha Statues in all the caves almost & its not maintained properly. Its not the worth of that ticket. This place is much hyped

Honestly Sri Lanka, charging $15 per person to see modest temples is starting to rub me the wrong way. Plus tips for taking your shoes off, more money if you want to read an explanation of what you've paid to see, a sarong if your shorts are deemed not far enough below the knees, and then donations. It becomes tiresome. This place is cool in theory but it's pretty small and takes about ten minutes to wander through. You can easily give it a miss especially if you have seen similar elsewhere. The most annoying part is despite paying there is zero signage in English etc that let's you discern what is old, new, meanings etc. Thats fine in the ruins of Bagan or middle of nowhere sites but not where you've just paid and had your ticket stamped and been abruptly dealt with by staff. Value: 500 out of 1500 rupees Interest: 6/10 Ease of access: 7/10 Memorable: 5/10 Time taken: 25 minutes including walk uphill

I visited this place in February this year on my way back from Sigriya. Beautiful cave temples with lots of Buddhas and it is worth that steep climb. On the way beware of Monkeys and do not eat anything as they attack you to grab the food. I would advise you take thick soles socks if you are travelling in the afternoon. You are required to remove your shoes before entering the temple and the ground is extremely hot to burn your feet. I had to literally jump and run to get inside the temple. It is one of the “must-do” while visiting Sri Lanka!
This is a must see place, although hard work climbing there but well worth it. Watch out for monkeys, they will grab anything! Fantastic history, really is worth a visit.
Easy to reach- very nice small model of Perahera and hall of Buddhas of various styles donated from several countries
With the aide of a Tour Guilde found this very cultural. There is so much to know about the history of Sri Lanka.
With the aide of a Tour Guilde found this very cultural.  There is so much to know about the history of Sri Lanka.

Pretty spectacular sites to see inside the Dambulla cave temples.  There are over 100 buddhist statues inside the temples and literally every inch of the ceilings of the cave are painted and/or have some sort of art decoration on them.  It is pretty incredible to think how long it would have taken someone to do all of those paintings. A little bit of a climb up some steps in order to see the cave temple, but is definitely extremely worth it in my opinion.  A must visit if you are traveling to or from Kandy from the Sigiriya world heritage site.
Worth the steep climb. The Buddhist statues at every cave were breathtaking and the landscape was beautiful especially on a windy day . The caves are well well preserved

One has to climb 200 odd steps to see the 5 caves. If anyone has seen the ajanta-Ellora caves of Aurangabad, India it's similar. Five caves with statues of Buddha in the sleeping pose and meditating. Nice place. Worth a visit

We visited Dambulla cave temples on a day trip from Kandy. A tuk-tuk driver offered a good price to take us to both Dambulla and Sigiriya so we were able to see both in one day, and didn't have to choose between them. I recommend doing this if you can, because both sites are well worth the visit. When you arrive to the cave temple, be prepared to walk up a lot of stairs. It can be pretty hot, and having a water bottle and comfortable shoes is helpful. There are vendors selling trinkets and fruit all along the way, There are also lots of monkeys! On the way up you are also treated to great views of the surrounding mountains. They caves themselves are truly impressive and filled with paintings and Buddha statues.

This temple has a series of caves cut into the rock face with a huge number of Buddhas inside.  It is really spectacular and I don't think there is anything else worldwide like this.  The climb is quite a way to the top, where you can leave your shoes outside for a fee.  There are several caves, so visit them all!  Side note: don't take photos with your back facing Buddhas - that's considered disrespectful.  Overall, highly recommneded!
Make sure you have a knowledgable guide as the history is worth hearing. The setting is beautiful and you can just imagine it has not changed in 100's of years.

Never seen such beautifully heritage. Well kept. The stairs are worth to climb. Shoes have to be removed at entrance and are guarded for 25lkr. Ticket office was not indicated from the golden Buddha but everyone can show you the way towards it.
Built right in to a cave, approximately 1000 years old, 4 separate cave tombs, very cool carvings and paintings, and a wonderful history. Stairs to climb to get up there, but not too difficult.
Marvellous architecture..not a long climb easy to climb the mountain steps. Good place to understand Buddhist architecture and religion.
Statues and paintings inside the caves, that are over 2000 years old. A windy place where one can relax and connect to the nature. It's definitely worth the climb.
This needs climbing up nearly 100 steps but it is worth reaching the top to view the city.  The architecture is incredible.  A temple worth a visit.
I like this temple and art work. though the light is not good and the place was smelly. they can maintain it much better. If you go to Sigriya rock then u can skip this. the entry fee is too much

we visited here as part of a tour and spent approximately 2 hours looking around.  it was very hot and very humid and the steps are steep and there are many so not for the less mobile and even testing for us , struggled a bit and out of breath but able to stop for a rest and once at the top its worth it . the temple is very well maintained , beautiful and peaceful .  so much to see , you could spend a long time if you studied everything . the views from the top are superb and the walk down doesnt feel too bad !!  Definately worth visiting

We went without any background information  and the so called guide only showed the way up.But our thrill started with the sight of the impressive golden Budhdha statue at the entrance. The entrance to the beautiful museum nearby ,offered excellent photo op. We did'nt go into the museum as the entrance fee for foreigners ,we felt, was quite high. We climbed our way up to the caves. Steep climb, but manageable by anyone with normal health.At the final stage of climbing, there are two pathways, one goes by the left and another on the right. there are also steps to climb up straight. No sign boards to say clearly, by which way to go. All foreigners should go by the left side , and obtain the tickets from the counter located  midway to the top. We chose the right , as guided by some people sitting there. That was a big mistake, as we found after reaching the caves , when the guards asked for tickets. We had climb all the way down to the counter and climb up again, cursing the authorities for not keeping a board. The ticket counter should either be at the top or at the bottom of the hill. Or there should have been clear direction boards on the way. Hope the authorioties take care of this. The ticket prices are the same for all foreigners (1500 SLR per person). On entry you will find an array of caves. In each cave rows of Budha statues and beautiful ancient paintings on the wall can be seen. Very impressive,considering their age. No detailed description or information about these is available inside. So, either on has to take a guide or go prepared well in advanced through net. Pay and use toilets available at the ground level, by the side of the museum. Reasonably clean. A small cafeteria is also located  near the entrance.
Dambulla Cave Temples :2100 years ago Temples. 1st century built. Hand carving inside the cave. 370 steps up to reach to it. Beautiful

This is remarkable.  It is both beautiful and awesome.  I have never seen anything like it.  There are five chambers containing over 100 buddhas all carved out out the rock.  The ceilings have been smoothed and elaborately painted.  Impossible to describe and do it justice.  You need to see it.
Several temples in cave cavities. There are plenty of budha´s statues. And also walking up and down to temple is great walk and view.
if you are going to sigiriya, you have to pass the golden temple in Dabulla. This is a place you mus visit. The painting are old and beautiful
if you are going to sigiriya, you have to pass the golden temple in Dabulla. This is a place you mus visit
Besides the dificulty to buy the tickets, the temple it's very impressive. It's incredible what the men did 2000 years ago. It's a long steps way, but not difficult to climb.
Besides the dificulty to buy the tickets, the temple it's very impressive. It's incredible what the men did 2000 years ago. It's a long steps way, but not difficult to climb.
You need to climb up around a hundred steps but after reaching the top the view of the city is breathtaking. There are temples built by different kings at the top with some really amazing sculptures.

The Cave Temple is vastly over-priced for foreigners, and though it is nice to look at, I dont believe it is quite worth what you pay ( if you're travelling on a currency weaker than USD, as I was) Foreigners need to walk around to another entrance.  You walk past the golden buddha and up a bunch of stairs and then off to the left where there is a shut gate.  There  you will be offered a tuktuk for 100rupees, for a 450m journey.  If you dont take the tuktuk, walk down the boring dirt road and then pay at a ticket booth there. For foreigners it is 1,500 rupees <10USD> (free or nominal charge for Sri Lankans.  This, you will see is quite common in SL, foreigners alays pay more.  Due to economic inequality, I dont mind this, hoever at times the price difference is a bit too extreme and the price that foreigners pay does not really represent the value you get.  Sigiriya Rock Formation is a prime examplee of this.. After you ascend the stairs to the temple area you must remove your shoes and pay 25 rupees to have them looked after. There are several little entrances you can visit, but its quite repetitive after the first two.  On the outside of the cave a typical temple like structure is built that you enter through. There are laying buddha statues in each cave, and an assortment of other buddha statues, with painted rock throughout the cave. It is nice to see but if your budget is running low I dont think you ill miss too much if you skip it.
The place is packed with Buddha statues and paintings on the cave walls. I would definetly recommend taking the stairs up, and seeing this for your self!

such a beautiful temple well preserved. the statutes are gorgeous. it is on a top of a hill so great views you will enjoy the monkey experience on your way up it was my first time in Sri Lanka and in a country where people warship Buddah, so i was infatuated by the rich culture and the beautiful statues highly recommended

amazing sight , the view from up the mountain is beautiful , the interior of the caves are fabulous , the colored status are remained intact with beautiful designs and various shapes . It's a very impressive sight , taking you into a special world through the caves .

Forget about the Taj Mahal this is Indias best attraction. The whole area surrounding the golden temple is very grand and really well kept. Entry to the temple as well as the shoe storage is free. You need to cover your head to gain entry but everyone is most welcoming. All I can say about this place is wow. Hundreds of volunteers keep this place in pristine condition and also feed you if required. I'm not really into religious sites but went here twice. You can bathe in the holy lake surrounding the temple and the only restriction is no photos inside the temple itself
Visited as part of a Mercury Holidays Tour and did not disappoint.... Highly recommended.  Was left breathless at the beauty of the site.. Enjoy your visit, a must see and do when here.

The cave temples are quite stunning but compared to most other temples we visited in the Cultural Triangle, Dambulla is overrun with tourists. The street vendors line up all the way from the bottom to the top of the rock persistently trying to sell you their crap and the staff controlling the admission is absolutely rude.

Again, this was a trip well worth taking, we arrived on a sacred day, so all the locals were walking up the mountain to offer flowers to Lord Buddha. The monkeys were entertaining, but not to be messed with. The views from the Golden Cave Temple were amazing, I would recommend going just for the views! The skill that went into creating these historical and sacred pieces is incredible, to think that they were all carved out of the rock. Our tour guide was able to give us a detailed explanation of they making, meaning and history. There is a dress code when attending, you cannot wear shoes around the Cave Temple, however there is somewhere to leave them, however you will need to pay a tip. Long sleeves and trousers are advised.
It is amazing to think that there were all carved out of the rock, the paint and detail was amazing, our tour guide was very knowledgable about their history.
We really enjoy this temple, very unique. However the ticket corner to buy tickets is not well indicated and far from the temple itself so we had to walk a lot before getting in.
Must visit cave temple and Golden Buddha. Nice view. Lion Rock view much better but no need pay expensive, they charge much for tourist

Not like anything I have seen before, the cave painting is really well done and preserved and almost makes you feel like the ceiling is covered in material. There are around 5 caves, each with Buddha statues and ornate painting. It was all a little more gaudy than I expected and the giant golden buddha at the foot of the hill is an awful site.
