However, the caves themselves are quite a wonder and nice to be able to visit a temple without burning your feet.

There is a bit of a climb to get up to the caves but nowhere near as bad as climbing Sigiriya. There are 5 caves which are quite stuffy but worth visiting to see the amazing number of Buddhas there and the painted ceilings. You need to remove your shoes and pay for them to be kept for you before going into the temple complex. Take socks with you in case you find the ground too hot for bare feet.

There are about 400 steps to this amazing site. Once we near the temple there are breath taking views from above.This temple complex has five caves under a vast overhanging rock with beautiful  Buddha's statues. The ambience in each of the temples is very peaceful and serene. For travellers, please ensure you have upper arms and legs covered while entering any Buddha temple. There are many monkeys in the complex so do keep an eye on children for safety and avoid carrying any eatables, lotus flowers in hand- keep it a bag. We entered from one side and descended from the Golden temple side and thus enjoyed both aspect and descent with different views.
I had been to Buddha Caves before but these 5 caves carved into the rock are amazing and very beautiful. A good tip I was given is to work backwards from Cave 5 to Cave 1.
Don't think it's just one more buddisth templo.  I've seem many of them,  in India, Nepal,  Myanmar, Laos....but this one has something that reveals the refine Lanka painting.

Dambulla is driving distance from Colombo, about 4-5 hours. It was our first destination in our Sri-Lanka Visit. From Dambula you can visit several places the Golden temple and caves is a "MUST". You can see breathtaking cave wall paintings and statues. Climb is easy, just few stairs, and there is not much walking. Take socks you can use when you take off shoes, stones could be hot. Female guest please remember to take a shawl to cover exposed shoulders or legs in all Buddhist temple sites in Sri-Lanka

This place is beautiful.  It's about 300-something steps to get to the top (be careful of the monkeys!).  There are 4 main rooms across the temple, each with its own flair based on the ruler of the time.  A can't miss.

Wonderful cave temple well worth the visit. if you walk up from the golden temple think its is about a thousands steps, but our tour driver took us nearer in the car so we only had about 300+ steps to climb, beautiful views, you have to leave your shoes outside the temple, it is a good idea to take a pair of socks as the ground can be very very hot to walk on, ladies need to have there arms covered and men no legs showing above the knees. in most temples it is forbidden to take photos with your back to Buddha.
Several caves full of statues of Budha sitting, standing and lying down repeated ad infinitum. Not for me, but I'm sure some people will appreciate it.

We got their at 9am in the low season but it was packed with Chinese and french tourists. We managed to climb the stairs to the cave temple and explored around. In the first cave men will approach you to offer free tours which are definitely not free at the end.. we politely declined.
We can see the Golden statue of Lord Buddha from the main road itself. Its huge and attractive. The temple is spic and span as everywhere in Sri Lanka.. Worth seeing
This is just adjacent to the Buddha Golden temple and also there is a seperate approach road to the caves . Its a nice cave temple and worth the walk
400 steps in stifling heat but worth the effort! the caves are remarkably well preserved and you can get a local guide at the entrance for rp1000
It's quite a hike, especially that I went with a baby. But the fresco is beautiful and the temple sits on a breathtaking view.

The caves were pretty interesting, but most of the significance was lost on me, mostly out of my own ignorance.  My only real beef with this place is the POORLY marked ticket office.  We, like many tourists we met, climbed all the way to the top of the mountain only to discover that the ticket booth was at the bottom, around the back, far from the main entrance.  It's not marked... at all.  :(  If you travel without a guide, you won't likely find it.

The caves are surely one of the most impressive places to visit in Sri Lanka!! The Golden Temple is strange, but if you like buddhist temples, it's ok.When you arrive at the Golden Temple and ask for the ticket office to the caves, people tell you to go up to the caves and it's wrong!! Pay attention: the ticket office is NOT in the "Golden Temple", but in a road at the other side of the rocky mountain. There's no information about that in the Golden Temple, so when you go up, after many steps, you'll see many people selling things and other people saying that you have to pay for a tuk tuk to go down the hill (500m) to buy the ticket and to come back (the tuk tuk guys want to charge 500 Rs, it's too much). Don't take the tuk tuk, it is not necessary. Go down the hill and the ticket office will be at your right. From the ticket office, it's easier to go up to the caves. If you are coming by bike, take the road straight to the other side of the mountain directly to the ticket office!!

It's surely one of the most impressive places to visit in Sri Lanka!! But... When you arrive at the Golden Temple and ask for the ticket office, people tell you to go up to the caves and it's wrong!! Pay attention: the ticket office is NOT in the "Golden Temple", but in a road at the other side of the rocky mountain. There's no information about that in the Golden Temple, so when you go up, after many steps, you'll see many people selling things and other people saying that you have to pay for a tuk tuk to go down the hill (500m) to buy the ticket and to come back (the tuk tuk guys want to charge 500 Rs, it's too much). Don't take the tuk tuk, it is not necessary. Go down the hill and the ticket office will be at your right. From the ticket office, it's easier to go up to the caves. If you are coming by bike, take the road straight to the other side of the mountain directly to the ticket office!!

I don't want to be rude, but from my point of view, those caves are just too similar to each other. The price is quite high – 1500Rp – and you have to climb the stairs twice to get the ticket since they're not available to buy at the entrance but on the other side of the hill. Caves are nice, the paintings are impressive but I feel like it is overpriced.
It's an interesting experience, and the climb all the way to the top is nice, but there are more interesting sites to visit
Interesting site and very beautiful carvings on the wall - not a definitive MUST because it's just like any other Buddhist temple

Located on top of a hill, we have to climb over 400 uneven steps, which can be quite a challenge. There are about 5 caves housing numerous statues of Buddha and well-preserved paintings on the ceiling & walls. Be mindful & respectful when entering into these sacred caves. Do not take photos with your back towards any of the statues.

A must see if you are in the area. The caves are a short walk up several steps. You must remove your shoes to enter and ensure your shoulders and knees are covered for both men and women. This is still a practising temple so occasionally a cave may close for 15 mins for a ceremony. The statues are very interesting and well worth the climb.
Called the Golden Buddha Temple,  it is claimed to be the Largest Buddha Temple in the world at 100 feet. The Buddha is in the Dharamchakra Posture

Its Situated on hill-top so u hav to climb so many stairs which was really difficult for us as we hav to carry our kid .  view from top is  mesmerising. Their is a small pond in temple with water lillies :) Note- Our guide informed us that they wont allow too short -shorts inside temple . And there is Entrance fee for temple.

A beautiful temple with with 5 caves and more than 150 Buddha statues and beautiful paintings on the roof. You can reach the top of the hill either through steps or through the stone path. It's located in Dambulla and must visit in that area

Make sure you purchase your tickets before reaching the cave.  We took a hike up to the temple; we had to hike back down to purchase tickets THEN HIKE BACK UP AGAIN!! .You also needs to take off your shoes before entering the cave. Need to pay a small about to keep your shoes. There are monkeys so be aware as of your belongings .there is two ways to go up by stairs or the king’s path. Attire neither sleeveless dresses nor shorts. Once you reach the cave temples, there are no shops selling sarongs or scarves, so one must remember to carry those.  I couldn't see any toilet facilities. Also bring plenty of water because there's none sold at the top Lot to see here in plenty of history. Probably a good idea to check out in the internet.

Make sure you have your tickets and be prepared to take off your shoes. Also bring plenty of water because there's none sold at the top as far as I know. However there are plenty of folks selling stuff like cut mangoes and trinkets. There's a lot to see here in plenty of history. Probably a good idea to check out the Wikipedia page or something so you know what you're looking at.

It's a long hard climb up to the golden cave temples but well worth the effort. We used a local guide and I would recommend them as he certainly added to our understanding and appreciation of the five caves and numerous statues and artefacts.
incredible temple, the Budha in gold is very big and so peacefull atmosphere. view amazing. easy access

Dambulla cave temple was one of our favorite places in Sri Lanka.  It is fascinating. I am in my  mid 60s and found the climb quite steep.....but it was well worth the effort. You have to remove your shoes when you reach the top, and although there were carpets paths in some places, being unused to bare feet I was hobbling in some places because of the tiny stones.. So ! Remember to bring a pair of socks if you are likely to have the same problem and enjoy this marvelous place in comfort !

Right up in the hill, these 800 years old caves are carved into beautiful place. It's all about Lord Buddha and Moksha. A must see in Sri Lanka. Overview of Dambulla city and surroundings is just awesome. Carry water while scaling this place. Happy travelling!!

A climb to the top but well worth it. Warning: buy your tickets at the Southern entrance (not the Golden Bhudda end) or you will have to go up, then down for the tickets,and then back up again for the caves. Our driver knew the ropes and saved us unnecessary exertions in the heat. There are several caves and the price gives you entry to all of them. You can take photos here which is a refreshing change as many places don't allow pics (even if non flash).

We visited these caves because we were in the area and thought we 'might as well' and my goodness am I pleased we did! This should be an absolute must visit place for all Sri Lanka holidays. You drive up a very unappealing dirt road and pull into a dirt car park. Pay the lady in the white wooden hut on the left 1,500 Rps each. Climb the steep steps (there are a lot of steps!) and deposit your shoes (take socks to walk around in if you go past 10 in the morning as the floor gets hot) with the men at the top on the right hand side. Proceed through the archway and you'll see the 5 caves along the wall on the right. The second cave is the most amazing. Statue upon gorgeous statue. Please note - Do not turn your back and take selfies!! It's considered rude! It will only take about an hour and a half to see all five caves and you will be so glad you did. This place is serene and beautiful.

Found out the hard way you need your tickets at the top as you will not get in, and in the heat double the effort,but worth the climb.we went down the kings way steps on return and a French man had some fruit and mobile phone in a bag,which the monkeys stole,so be aware as you will not catch them,
This place has a got a lot of history and its a great feeling that one cannot describe. Its a must visit if your in srilanka.
This is the most secret place in Dambulla Town. There are beautiful wall paintings done during Kings period.
Ancient cave temple - Make sure you see the real ancient cave temple behind the golden Buddha statue
I really loved this temple. It had a very spiritual feel to it, and the amount of detail is breathtaking. Don't forget to look at the ceiling!

We visited here today on our tour, it was a cost of 1500rps per person, the climb was steep however there were little areas where you could stop along the way to catch your breath and have a drink. It only took us about 15 minutes to get to the top, and was definitely worth it, the view was fantastic and there were plenty of opportunities to take some pictures and get right up on the edge of the mountain. After we got to the temple we gave our shoes to the shoe minders, they charged 25rps per pair and proceeded into the temple, there were two entrances, one specifically for tourists. A gentleman approached us in the entrance and asked us where we are from, we replied "England" and he then told us to follow him and he showed us around. Being the second day into the tour now, we are not stupid and know this comes at a price and he would be expecting a tip at the end of it. The gentleman showed us around quite quickly and shared information along the way, although it wasn't an awful amount, it was information we wouldn't have known without him. After he had shown us around he ask us for money. I gave him 500rps which I feel was more than enough for a good tip and it is roughly the amount I have been tipping everywhere else. The gentleman took the money and then said his service charge was 1500rps.... this was quite frustrating. We asked the man if he was sure that's how much a 10 minute tour cost, he insisted we should pay him that money, even though it was the same amount as the entry. When we refused he lowered his charge to 1000rps, we again refused to pay and said the only money we were offering was the money he had in his hand. He took the money thanked us and then we left. Overall we had a good time however I feel this slightly ruined it for us. We have found that on every occasion we have gone to a place, whenever a member of staff has spotted us and heard us speaking English (as we have noticed people speaking other languages are left alone) they insist they show us around without the option for us to say no and at the end expect money. Sometimes we have been happy to tip and the help has been nice and insightful however many other times we would like to be left alone. The temple itself wasn't great, it was quite small and it was pretty much all the same stuff on every room, for us we much preferred the walk up to the temple and the views along the way. We would probably wouldn't revisit if we had the opportunity but we don't regret going the first time.

So amazing, everywhere you looked, including the roof of the cave, just covered in the most amazing artwork.  Absolutely loved this place.  If you go nowhere else in Sri Lanka, you must visit the caves at Dambulla.  Five caves, from small to large - statues, paintings.  We went by car but it is accessible by bus if you are brave enough - I preferred air conditioning and the security of a seat belt.  A bit of a walk to get there but quite easy and good views.  A must - don't miss it.

NOTE!! DO NOT MISS THE SIGN!! The sign for purchasing your tickets at the ticketing counter. We didn't see the sign (and actually many other foreigners missed it as well). When we took a hike up to the temple, we had to hike back down to purchase tickets THEN HIKE BACK UP AGAIN!! Really pretty cave temples, you may choose to buy flowers before entering temples. They had some english speaking guides but we chose to explore the area ourselves. Worth it!

For 1500 rupees, it may be considered a bit steep for visiting 5 small caves but they were filled with Buddha statues. I took some amazing photos of the Buddha statues and marvelled at the details and intricacy of the statues. The entrance is to the left of the golden temple so we got dropped off there. We had to climb a few steps (7 min uphill walk) and then take our shoes off. Make sure to cover your knees (bring a sarong) and cover your shoulders and bring socks so that you don't burn your feet on the ground when it's hot. Instead of paying to leave my shoes, I just put them in my bag. I feel like it was worth the visit. We spend 45 minutes there in total.

A bit of a trek up the hill but once you have climbed Sigiriya Rock this is easy LOL. It's amazing to see how they carved the images out of the rock and the paintings on the ceiling are beautiful. A wonderful peaceful feeling as you walk round. Beautiful vista at the top too.

The Golden Cave Temple and caves are well worth a visit.   Very impressive and accessible on public transport.   Only downside was we arrived off the bus from Kandy with rucksacks on the main road outside what we thought was the main entrance, as there is a large gold buddha so looks like and entrance.  Unfortunately then discovered we had to walk quite a long way on a hot day to the ticket office on the opposite side where there was a bus car park..  (Could have got a tuk tuk) but wasn't exactly sure how far away it was.   Could have had ticket office on both sides I would have thought.

I'm very glad I put in the effort and made it up the uneven, hop-scotch stairs to get to see this incredible Temple. Cost was 1500rup, or $14AUD, and it took me around 10-15mins to get to the top.  That included a few stops to admire the view/catch my breath and take a few snaps of monkeys. At the top, you remove your shoes (take note where they end up - I found out the hard way, they were taken by a "Shoe Carer" and cost me 25Rup to get them back) and wander through the caves. There are 5 caves in total, whilst someone who is particular claustrophobic may disagree however you aren't having to crawl or bend - they're huge.  The innate work and detail across the statues was incredible across a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses.  The murals were amazing. Watch out for the "guides" who will start walking with you, talking and next you know you're on a paid tour only you never agreed to that!  I saw them following a few people who didn't speak English trying to say no. The walk back down was a little quicker however the uneven steps made it an almost equally challenging trip down. There's a stall at the bottom to purchase cool water, and toilets available (however you'll need your sanitiser after them). Definitely worth a visit, thoroughly enjoyed it and would recommend to anyone with a history or cultural interest.

We visited the Dambulla cave temples directly from the airport. It takes about 3 hours to reach. En route there are not too many breakfast options. We ate a simple breakfast at Garden Cafe. At the cave temples, the ticket prices are not listed at the entrance. The tickets are 1500 LKR for adults and free for kids upto 11. No discount for SAARC members. The steps are a steep climb, but the views from the top are worth the effort. Also the caves are at the top. One has to remove ones shoes though socks are permitted. During the day time it gets quite hot, so remember to carry socks, water. Caps are not allowed inside, neither sleeveless dresses or shorts. Once you reach the cave temples, there are no shops selling sarongs or scarves, so one must remember to carry those. Overall well maintained, though I couldn't see any toilet facilities.
Really loved these caves! You can feel the spirituality of this place. So much attention to detail. The statues, the ceilings, and the caves themselves. - must for visiting Dambulla

It was our first trip to Sri Lanka and we booked a 10-day trip with Golden Isle Travels. The experience was amazing. We had a tailor-made itinerary according to our wishes and the whole team had been extremely kind and helpful. Our driver Hanry, welcoming us at the airport and escorting us during our entire stay, was super: very nice, always smiling, ready to assist and to give advice! The country is awesome: wonderful places (as unmissable Dambulla) with cultural and naturalistic sites, lush vegetation and beautiful beaches. Golden Isle Travels organised for us a very rich and varied programme and booked lovely hotels. We are planning to go back to Sri Lanka very soon and we will definitely book our second tour with Golden Isle Travels . Thank you to Paddy and her team for the great organisation and assistance!
Great place - worth a visit if your in the area. In expensive entry fee and good views from the top.

A beautiful and serene place to visit, but some things I'd wish I knew before I went: -You HAVE to wear respectful clothing (below the knee, cover the shoulders) -There is a decent (15-20min) hike up (steep stairs) -There are monkeys, they will be close to you -The ticket office is half way up (there is not ticket office at the top) -You cannot wear shoes, there is a man who runs a locker room for 25 rupees each -Bring socks (ground is too hot for barefoot) -Get a guide, as always there are no signs or audiotours.

Another climb, but well worth it. (If you have a car, your driver can take you half-way up!). The temples in themselves are very impressive. What I also liked was the fact that there were no restrictions on taking photographs.

I'm a Buddhist and have studied medieval Sinhalese Art. One of my favorite places. The temple is situated on top of a rocky mountain. There are two routes for the temple. -We took a taxi[A tuk Tuk,A local taxy from the bottom of the rock costs less than 200 LKR] from the hotel and reached a mid way point[~0.5km from the new Temple at the bottom]. Then it was a matter of climbing stairs. -Or else you can take a direct path[Stairs and rocky floor] from the Rangiri Dambulu temple[New]. We recommend this route when you are climbing down. -If you are a Buddhist you can buy flowers at the bottom of the mountain and there are also places along the way when you start climbing. -Be sure to take a camera since you will need to take pictures of the amazing view from up there.

Read up in advance.  There is no guide book available and it's not clear what the caves refer to without some sort of explanation.  Allow around fifteen minutes for the climb up.  Watch out for the monkeys as they are a bit mean looking.  Make sure you don't take any food in with you or they will smell it and try and take your bag.  Take twenty five rupees per person for the man who minds your shoes.  You may wish to wear socks as the ground is so hot.  Be sure to cover your shoulders and knees here and do not wear a hat or head covering when you enter the sacred area.

The various temples are built into cave in the rock.  Statues inside each are plentiful.  Meaningful.  And high quality.   Strangely the ticket office is not close to front gate.  You can walk from the office but it is needlessly hard from there.  So buy your ticket.  Then get dropped off at front gate for an easier experience.
A very scenic hill top Buddha cave temple. centuries old temple having hundreds of Buddha statue in excellent condition.
A must see place in Dambulla. Hundreds of Buddha statues are carved and painted inside of a one single rock.

We visited these caves on the way from Sigirya to Kandy, and it was a favorite for the entire family (myself, my husband and two teenage sons).  A short but steep walk up stone stairs takes you to the vista and main entrance.  Note that this is a holy site and proper dress is required (knees and shoulders covered for both men and women).  The statues and paintings on the walls and ceiling are gorgeous and very interesting, including "Holy water" which flows uphill along the cave ceiling and falls into a pot for collection.  Small enough that it is easy to see (we were there about an hour), and cool inside the cave.  Beautiful views of the surrounding hills.  A very memorable stop! PS: remember that this is a holy site and do not touch the statues.  One was damaged by a tourist who thought is would be funny to take a selfie on one of the ancient Buddha's lap.

Astonishing cave circuit with more than 150 Buda statues! We got a little burn in our feet beacuse the floor is rock and during the summer if yiu go barefoot you suffer, you have to leave your shoes at the entrance, just prior to enter the actual caves, but that little bit can be a pain in the foot ;-) So keep your socks! We didnt and was a big mistake. If you climb down the stairs to the other side of the complex you'll find a big golden Buda and a museum (which we didn't visit). Lots of monkeys, beware with your food or beverages!

Ticket was USD 10 each for the Rock cave where you can be amazed at the construction feat and see enormous lying stone Buddhas. The Golden temple on the way down was free but uninteresting. The mango snack sold by ladies on the steps down were good though.

Words cannot describe how overwhelming this CaveTemple is. This is a must see site and cannot be missed. It is hard to imagine a time when these amazing statues of Buddha were created. What a wonder. In addition to over 50 statues carved from the rock and painted by the monks there is a drip of water that drips from the ceiling of one of the 5 caves and is considered sacred. The water has never stopped dripping from this one spot and is collected in an urn and considered holy water. Wow that is amazing.
It is very magical place with beautiful view of landscape. Inside the temple are very beautiful wall paintings and old statues.

A World Herritage Site and one of the must see attractions in this central part of Sri Lanka. There are five caves in total and you only have to pay a small fee to visit. It's a good climb up a staircase to the caves, so make sure you're wearing trainers of walking shoes of some description.

I would definitely recommend you to visit this place for sunset . When you climb up to the caves , just before you enter the caves to your left . There's a spot to sit down and watch the beautiful sunset !!
I was 3 times and I will come back all the times I travel to this area. The history and place is amazing. Now, the entrance is free and I recommend, of course!

Dambulla's Cave temples are worth a visit.There were 5 cave temples and the paintings are really good. There are few ways to walk to the temple and only to find ticket is not sold on top at the entrance. This made us (infact my husband ) to climb all the down in another direction. Fetch the ticket and climb again. They should mark the ticket booth properly.
Golden temple on the way to Cave Temples, so its better to include Golden temple along with cave temple visit.
This is one of the most famous place in Dambulla . its situated on a rock and we can experience a lovely view around and this temple got lovely paintings in the caves as well
5 Caves filled with amazing sculptures, paintings, alters and tourists! Not a place to meditate, but an awesome living museum. Photos attached

Caves filled with Fresco Paintings and sculptures and alters created 2000 years ago. Unfortunately no place to sit and meditate. Also the ticket office is hidden on the backside. Be sure to find it before you climb to the top and are turned away!!!

Outstanding place... You need to listen all guide speech to understand what is this place and its meaning for Budhist. View from Summit is very nice. Watch out the monkeys as they are waiting for food although local people offered food out of temple. You need to remove your shoes to go inside temple. There is a Museum on lower area close to main road about Budhist Culture.

We stopped at this temple after climbing the Sigiriya Rock. This temple has a giant golden Buddha at the entrance and then you start to climb the steps. As you start climbing, you will see lots of monkeys but be careful with your food and even flowers.  The veiw from the top is also amazing.

One has to toil quite hard to reach the Dambulla cave temple. The combination of a gravel path and steep stairs in the afternoon heat is energy sapping, and the rocks and paved areas can make your feet fried! But once at the top, the coolness inside the caves is a big respite. Carry water on the way as the throats will definitely get parched. The cave temple complex has 5 caves built over a span of 22 centuries. The first cave is small with a large sleeping Buddha. The old paintings on the ceiling and walls had largely darkened due to lamp soot and have been repainted around 18th C. The second cave is certainly the most interesting with a stupa surrounded by 11 seated Buddha statues. The paintings on the walls and ceiling are beautiful with impressive designs and colours. Another fascinating feature is the dripping water droplet collecting bowl in the cave. It is said that the water source has not ever dried up. The third cave is interesting as well but is much recent…18th C. A 30 feet reclining Buddha statue is carved out from the same rock. The mural paintings on the wall are in wonderful Kandyan style artwork. The other two caves are less interesting but worth a quick visit. Two things to take care: The ticket counter is right below before you start to climb. Secondly carry water to compensate for the sweating you will do climbing 300+ steps

Great views from the top! The hike is not so hard, but be aware that you are not allowed to wear shoes when entering the Cave Temple and the rock gets pretty hot in the afternoon which makes it hard to walk on it. But the Temple itself is definitely worth visiting. I suggest to klimb there later in the afternoon when the sun is not so harsh and stay there for the sunset.
The cave is very good. It gives a very good feel of the ancient history and architecture. Was lucky enough to have a guide and listen some of the pieces.

It wasn't the steepest climb of our visit to Sri Lanka but the combination of the climb and the heat was taxing. Wear socks for when you take your shoes of as the paved areas were hot enough to fry eggs on! The cave decorations are stunning and so steeped in history with the most amazing aura - it makes you feel particularly humble and small. Some hawkers/pedlars but not intrusive.
I went up their to see the sunset , it was amazing experience, the most beautiful view from the top of the caves , Just before you enter the caves , you can sit and watch the sunset !

Costs 1500 rupees. Was really interesting but would probably recommend getting a guide or reading up on each of the caves beforehand. Really cool to see but wouldn't say it is a must. Remember to cover knees and shoulders.
gorgeous views and peaceful temple. The paintings on the walls and ceilings are absolutely beautiful. The museum and Stupa at the bottom are also worth visiting

Be prepared to climb 800 steps to get up there. (takes about 10 - 15 minutes). There is another route through a forest over a hill if you want to avoid the steps. This route takes about 40 minutes and is better if you are looking for a trekking experience. The caves temples are beautiful and peaceful with amazing paintings on the ceiling and walls. I've never seen so many Buddha statues in one place in all shapes and sizes. The little lotus filled ponds outside look very beautiful too.. Definitely worth going up the stairs to check out the 5 cave temples and the views. If not, there is a beautiful museum at the bottom with a massive golden Buddha on top along with a Stupa that is also worth visiting. Does not require a ticket to visit any of the above as mentioned in some other reviews here.

You can visit the main temple for free. Really big and impressive golden Buddha at the front. But really complicated to get to the rock temple, tickets are almost impossible to buy due to the office location!

What a fabulous row of caves with meters and meters of painted ceiling  and walls and carved Buddhas in all shapes and sizes. The climb up there requires a little effort but it was totally worth it once u get to the top. Unbelievably beautiful sculptures dating from the 1st Century. Totally worth a visit to the caves.

The caves are pretty special with the incredible drawings on the walls and ceilings. If you are into Buddhas of all shapes, sizes and differing positions then this is the place to be. Two words of warning: 1. Try and get there early or late when going with young kids as the trek up to caves carrying a 19 month old is a sweaty and exhausting experience 2. Also make sure you do not go up to the caves without a ticket. If you can not find a ticket counter when you are at the complex then you have come to the exit and not the entrance. We got to the top via what we learnt was the exit route and when we got to the entrance of the caves, and we were told we had to go all the way down to the ticket office at the entrance on the other side of the hill. This experience was painful in the heat of the day Well worth a visit!
Walk up wide fairly steep pathway to access the complex. There is a series of caves each containing numerous/varied  statues of Buddha
Very atmospheric. We visited as offerings were made - lots of ceremony/ drumming etc. Beautiful paintings around a hall telling story of the tooth.

The temple resides at the top of a rock mountain, overlooking its surrounding area. To get there you need to climb many steps but the view and the temple itself are worth the effort. Don't let the humble exterior full you. The temple itself is located in five caves and they are all covered in beautiful murals (walls and ceilings) and house many statues from the Middle Ages. Definitely do not miss when in Sri Lanka. Tip: As you'll need to remove you shoes before entering, come with flip flops. Also, don't forget to wear something that's covering your shoulders and knees.

Must see temples, but if you're going without a tour or guide get your tickets at the bottom beforehand as you may end up climbing the steps to have to backtrack a little to get tickets. The walk up has some lovely views and you can see Sigiriya rock in the distance from there too. The caves themselves are so impressive, one has a number of Buddha's carved from the rock and decorated. All the ceilings are painted with Buddha's too. Careful if your belongings the monkeys will jump into you and take things from you and your bags.

The caves are incredible and visiting them is just a fascinating trip as to how these were created so long ago. The caves themselves are intricate and full of wonders to view. The views from the top of the hills are spectacular. Make sure you take water with you as it is really hot up there and is a fairly steep walk up the hills.

We were taken here by our guide, we reached this space by walking up lots of steps, was so worth while. Absolutely in Awe of this space, we went to all five Cave Temples and the original art work is just breathtaking. I just had to stand still & quiet to take in the atmosphere, very spiritual.

We climbed the many steps up to the caves and although we had a driver/guide for the holiday, he advised us to get one of the local guides.  Unfortunately we could barely understand what the man was saying so whilst I'm sure there's a great story here, we didn't really get to discover it other than 3 caves are very old and 2 aren't.  Take care with the monkeys as they can be quite spiteful.  Great views from the top though and you see Sigiriya Rock fortress in the distance on a clear day.

This amazing temple is at the foot of the hill that contains the Dambulla Cave Temple complex. The size of the gold Buddha is remarkable, as is the rest of the building. Time did not allow us to go inside, however, visiting this site just to see the Buddha is very worthwhile.

We visited this truly amazing caved monastery during our recent 3 week holiday to Sri Lanka. The uphill walk to this World Heritage Site complex is quite strenuous, particularly in the heat, but you are rewarded hugely when you get there. Being a practising monastery, shoes must be removed at the entrance to the complex. (Don't forget to tip the shoe keepers on the way out). All the buddhas and ceiling paintings are truly remarkable, considering that they were all carved out of the rock in situ in the first century! We found our visit to this temple complex to be one of the highlights of our holiday in Sri Lanka and would recommend anyone visiting this country to go there.

we climbed the 300 steps up to the temple and each of the caves were beautiful with wonderful decoration. A very peaceful place to visit and experience our first Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. Then we experienced our first thunder storm so had to walk back down the 300 steps in the storm. So if a storm threatens remember to take waterproofs or an umbrella!!

Fantastic temple, situated at the top of a fair number of steps! (We went up the "new way" on a constant climb up steps, and down the "old way" on a mixture of steps, and slopes to the Big Gold Buddah). We hired a temple guide at the entrance to the caves, who proved to be a mine of information, and took us in turn through all of the caves, explaining the history of each. The colours are fantastic, and you only realise the intensity of the colours when you review your photographs.

Had heard better things about other sites in the area so went without great expectations, but was pleasantly surprised. Arrived pretty early before the Chinese crowds and got to experience the tranquility of the cave temples largely to ourselves. Some are outstandingly well preserved, and the restoration where it has been done over the centuries has been very sympathetic. It's a short, steep climb but well worth it to experience the harmony of the natural caves and the stunning carving and painting.
We visited a great number of temples but this one, with the Temple of the tooth relic in Kandy was one of the best.
It's nice.. for a people thats not in a good shape it could be quite hard..:) be aware that you get the ticket before you climb all those stairs;)
Vivid colors are very impressive  to add to the size and shapes of the caves and Buddahs. It's worth all the effort to go up the hill.

The Cave Temple is at the top of a lot of steps but is well worth the climb up and down. You will need to leave your shoes outside before you enter and the ground can get quite hot. we spent a couple of hours wandering through the various caves.

There seems to be a lot of confusion about the entrance fee and how to reach the caves.  They have recently added a new ticket office located in a different place than the normal starting point of the long climb (our driver was unaware of this, but I had read about it here and showed him the information).  This is down a very narrow road, and after buying tickets, it is only about a 10-15 minute climb to the top, very easy.  We thought the caves were worth seeing, we went in the afternoon and they were not crowded.  We had a driver/guide and he helped explain some of what we were seeing.  There is no posted information.  We were not aware of a museum; it is located in a different area. We were there in the afternoon and it was not crowded at all.

One of the best places I've been to in india very clean ,quiet ,relaxing place People there are friendly I slept in the golden temple its a spiritual place i just loved everything about it People offer u food deserts over there They have lockers but the man tells u to keep valuable stuff with u In day and night the view is outstanding Don't miss
It's a bit of a climb but well worth it when you get to the caves and Buddhas at the top. I'm glad we did it at 8.30 in the morning before the heat of the day hit.

Nice place to visit if you are around. But nit necessary to visit Dambula just because of this. If you came from side of Golden temple you need to go down to other side to buy a tickets. Which is annoying a tired in this weather.

The place, view and history of this place is so amazing. everything was well preserved. Recently, they have implemented the collection of entrance fee, but be aware that you need to take the ticket in another place and you may need someone to buy it for you because its  offsite. From the entrance, someone from there will guide and tell the history of the place/statues. Sri Lanka in general is a nice and beautiful place and its a great place to visit, what ruins it is the attitude of the locals that expect tip on every little thing they do. Just like the guide on this place, we already paid fee to enter the place and its not cheap and after the tour the guide will directly ask you for money. It ruins the whole experience for you expect you already paid a fee to enter and once your there these guys will even force you to give more money saying it not enough.
Buddhist cave temples set in the hills. Well worth the walk up (nowhere near as strenuous as Sigiriya!).

Golden Temple is well known temple of Lord Buddha in Sri Lanka. Olden Statue of Lord Buddha. I could not access whether it was made of Gold or Golden Colour because Statue covered by golden colour in Sri Lanka is common. What I nice statue to watch. There is a museum of Lord Buddha. There are some statue of Buddha and some pictures also. They charge a nominal fees as entry. From here you can start climbing for Dambulla Cave Temple. Must see place of Dambulla.

Climbing the stairs in the heat straight after doing the Sigiriya lion rock was not my favourite choice but it is not too far up to the temple and well worth it. The caves took my breath away and were really really impressive. You have to make sure shoulders are covered and shoes come off but it's worth it to explore the rand buddhas and artwork. Don't miss this!

The new entrance requires you to climb 300 steps. Doable for physically challenged people. However, well worth the climb, the maze of rooms in this temple offer exquisite buddha statues and intricate paintings on the walls.

Maybe the Buddhist's have the right idea if the whole world lived by their philosophy it would be a far better place for everyone. Certainly no wars and no cruelty to mankind or indeed animal kind. Certainly merits investigation when we get home

Great place to visit after the walk up the hill and avoiding the monkeys. 5 caves with statues of Buddha and a number of Hindu shrines as well, do not miss the inclining statue with massive feet nor the beautiful psi tings on the ceilings.

This is such a cool experience. A nice walk uphill with the monkeys and then the extraordinary buddha statues and frescoes in the cave temple. Reduced one star as the day we got there they decided to go from free entry to about $20.00! Our guide was a little embarrased.

The five caves are filled with marvellous statues of the Buddha and wonderful decorative art. Unfortunately, the authorities do not seem to have realised the deleterious effects body heat can have on these ancient artworks. I did not see any dehumidifiers installed to lessen the effects of the humidity. There also probably needs to be a limit on the number of people admitted into the caves. With this said, the artwork is amazing.

The Dambulla Caves are quite impressive and worth a visit, despite the 1,500 rupees entrance fee.  Many others have complained about the confusion of the ticketing, but we didn't find it all that unusual. The caves are accessed off the main road and up a steep side road. After buying a ticket, the caves are accessed by climbing a couple of hundred steps.  The climb is really a "piece of cake" however, relative to Sigariya and others.  There are five "rooms" of the cave temple and it is indeed a good approach to start with the one far in the back and work toward the front, where the most impressive images are found. Each chamber includes a number of Buddha images, with the last including a large reclining Buddha.  Visitors must remove their shoes; you may wish to carry them in your backpack to avoid the minor charge for the minder to keep an eye on them.  Alternative is to pay 25 rupees to the keeper of the stand.
Amazing cave carvings and paintings. Lovely. Bring bananas to feed the monkeys. Go early in the morning as it gets very hot.

There is a climb up to the temple, lots of stairs. Views from up top are pretty. The cave itself is nice to look at but during the middle of the day it is extremely hot inside and on the floor since you need to take shoes off to walk around. Maybe take a pair of socks just for this tour. Walking back down you will encounter monkeys, they are not dangerous but if you have food with you they may come up to you for some.
This is a very beautiful temple. We can see lot of Buddha statues & can see one of the big statue in Sri Lanka. Its really a golden temple.

Its another area where you need to climb a lot of steps abt 300 steps to reach the golden temple..but heres a tip for those with knee problem or who have difficulty climbing stairs..get ur guide / transport to alight you at the half-way point..from there take the paved ascent at the side instead of the steps..not many guides know this short cut..the ascent will be worth it..the statues of buddha and the frescoes are marvellous!!

It's the largest and best preserved cave temple in Sri Lanka. On top of the rock, which is over 160 m the surrounding plains, are located 5 caves containing paintings and statues of Buddha and his life. This is a mystic place to visit.
Enjoyed visiting this temple, it was peaceful and the craftsmanship was extraordinary.  If you are in Dambulla it is very much worth a look
Enjoyed visiting this temple, it was peaceful and the craftsmanship was extraordinary.  If you are in Dambulla it is worth a look

Hey One big point in the beginning, we searched for the tickets in the entry area and we didn't found them. On the top, after store my shoes, I have to go down to the other side to get the tickets, like many other tourists. The spot was cool, we saw a lot of funny monkeys and the temple was charming. Enjoy the view there!

Dambulla caves are a great place to visit. The cost is 1500 rupees and one needs to climb up to reach the caves. Shoes will have to be removed-you can put them in your backpack rather than pay for storage. Have socks ready as the stones get hot to walk on. The caves are spectacular with lots of wall paintings. Groups usually arrive at midday so go early. It's possible to reach Dambulla by local buses.

This temple is well worth a stop. We are not great temple fanatics but this one is quite special, given its cave location. Here are a few practical pieces of advice for visiting the temple: - it is a fairly steep climb of about fifteen minutes up stone steps, easily manageable for anyone of average fitness- something to consider if you have any health issues though - the ticket office is at the bottom of the steps and the collection booth at the top, before you go into the caves - do not go up without your ticket or you will have to redo the climb - do not take any food with you - there are lots of monkeys at the top and they are quite aggressive about looking for handouts - flash photography is surprisingly allowed in the caves in spite of their elaborate fresco decorations - start with cave five first and work your way backwards - the best caves are the early ones so it is a bit disappointing if you do them in the numbered order - as in all Buddhist temples, shoes must be removed so make sure you wear socks, preferably of a dark colour - the stones can get very hot and your feet quite dirty - knees and shoulders must be covered

This place is kind of understated in its way. You wander in, you look and see, you imagine what it is all about and wonder and then you leave. Unless you go out of your way to research the place, have a guide (as we had with our tour driver who told us not too little and not too much), pay someone to show and tell you on your way around (there is no need) there is a risk that you don’t get the full effect of the history and culture of this place. All the same we found this place to be very interesting and in its way quite beautiful and well worth the hour or so we spent there. It is a bit of a climb to get there and the steps and roadway is not the best but a reasonably mobile person can easily manage. There is an entry fee which is inexpensive. I would not put much store into a tiny Hindu temple stuck in the middle of this attraction. This was the only bit that felt as if it is meant to fleece the tourist and in my humble opinion far removed from what I would consider a “proper” temple. I am glad it was on out tour map.
Unless you go with a tour group that has arranged tickets for you, save yourself the trouble. You'll end up climbing uphill and not being able to go in like we did. Disappointing and rude staff.

although most of the temples are quite the same but this temple is worth visiting as well as the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, the stairs are a bit high up and a lot of monkeys on ur way up, we didnt hire a guide so not sure we got to know too much about the historical facts i wud suggest to hire a guide if ur interested in the history, its a fascinating place overall.

Visited here as part of a tour. Quite a few steps up to the temple which is a little taxing if it's as hot as it was when we did it! However you can take as long as you like and stop on the way. It's worth the effort. Beautiful ancient Buddhas (huge - over 30 feet long) carved out of the rock in the natural caves. Also has many other Buddhas added later on. The cave walls (there are a number of caves) are decorated with ancient paintings too. You have to remove your shoes before entering and the ground can be hot, however you can wear socks which may help. Overall a lovely and thought provoking experience which is recommended

nothing to do in Dambulla besides these caves. And it is very poorly organized. It used to be free but now it is 1500 LKR per person. You will have to buy the tickets in a very small office, and take off your shoes, you can't carry them you have to give them to a guy that will charge you 25Lkr for it. You can't put them in your bag either! It is not much money but it is still exagerated to treat tourists like cash cow. No explanation at all in the caves. 3 lying buddhas that look exactly the same. No regret if you don't put it in your itinerary!

You'll need to climb about 400 steps to get up to the caves/murals, but unless its raining (when the steps get slippery), it is well worth the climb. There are three caves open to the public (but the complex has many more caves yet to be renovated), and each is magnificent. The Buddhas are as in many other places - resting (or our guide claimed dead), standing and sitting, over a hundred in the three caves. But the most amazing sight is the murals (frescoes) on all the walls and ceilings. Truly magnificent.

By the the time we got to the Golden Temple we had been in Sri Lanka for nearly 3 weeks and seem many temples. This is an easy climb up lots of steps and well woth a visit. There are a lot of Buddah's here and you should remember to be respectful and dress appropriately. Dont be conned into a guide (anywhere) you really can read everything you need online. It is worth carrying a Sri Lanka guide book if you can.
A lovely historical and religious sight to visit. Climbing up the 300 or so steps in the hot sun was difficult but worth every bit of it. All five caves exude peace.
Some climbing and huffing and puffing.. but you reach a set of caves with rich paintings, Buddha statues and a serene atmosphere. We enjoyed our visit.

Climb up the hill was especially tough, as we had just made it up sigiriya rock fortress earlier in the day. Entry into the cave temple costs 1500 Rs per person. Did not get a guide though may be recommended to have one, otherwise not sure what you are looking at as there is no info provided at all. Nice, peaceful setting with interesting paintings and statues. But for the price, you would think they could include some signage giving more info on the history of the place.

Seemingly like most tourist-aimed things in Sri Lanka, this place is overpriced, lazily-operated and badly organised. It is however a fantastic experience to see such rich history in 5 caves. The Buddha statues and wall paintings are amazing, and really interesting to experience. The walk up to the caves isn't too bad, although try and get there early or late to avoid the heat! Don't be put off by the garish Golden Temple at the bottom, this Vegas theme park-style spectacle is far tackier than what you find in the caves! I came here from Kandy on a local bus and was finished and on the bus back within 2 hours, so I wouldn't say staying in Dambulla is necessary. I do balk at the thought of paying 1500 LKR for entry when locals pay around 200 LKR, but it's worth it. One thing that is absurd however is the ticket situation - to get a ticket you have to climb a third of the way up the hill from the front entrance to the complex, then climb down again at the back and walk for 5/10 minutes to a tiny hut, to then walk back up several steps. The entry at the main complex is more of an exit point to the caves, but nowhere is that made clear. They may also be a bit precious at the ticket office if you're not covering your lower legs, although I saw plenty of tourists and locals wearing shorts... A great experience all in all, if a little exasperating....

There are five caves in this cave temple.  Two caves are pretty big, and comfortable to walk about in these two caves, while the other three are very small, with limited room to move. The statues and wall paintings are elegant to a certain extent, but they are not as fine or complicated as those you find in China, such as Dunhuang or LongMen. The temple is full of tourists, so it is not a place where you can have some quiet moments to ponder the important things in life.

All cave temples in Sri Lanka are relatively alike but this one is really worth the visit. There are 2 large and 1 smaller cave and a nice view to the surrounding area. Please note: the entrance has changed and is not any more close to the golden temple but on the other side which requires some walk from the main street. Admission was rs1500 and there is a little hike to the top.
It is religious place. Unbelievable when you consider the time this was made. Ideal if you visit in the evening because of hot weather during this time of the year.

Indeed a wonderful place & worth climbing upto the cave to witness the rich culture & art of srilanka.. The frescoes are amazing and prove the richness of the ancient srilanka. Tips - *Pls be mindful to wear a modest ( decent ) clothes as a respect to this Buddhist temple ( preferably arms & legs covered) *If day time,you will for sure need a bottle of water,hat or an umbrella,& socks not to get burnt by heated rock surface *Cave temple is opened until 1800hrs & better avoid mid day climbing as it could be super hot. (choose morning or after sunset) No too much restrictions even if you might have found here reading..It is worth going..& Do not forget your best camera!

I am sick of seeing temples but I really wanted to see this one. From the front it looks like a gimmick (Chinese style) but inside it is supposed to be very nice. It was very hot but had to quickly change into my jeans as you have to cover your knees. What looks to be the entrance, isn't. You have to go around the houses to get to the ticket office but it's not sign posted and it looks highly suspicious and unsafe. Prior to that we walked up a twisty hill to try and find the entrance! It would be common fence to put up a couple of signs or have the ticket office in the other side as well. So stupid. Am a bit miffed with our driver, he should have also been more clearer. It was after all the hottest part of the day. We were dripping wet so we decided to go back to the car. I should have read trip advisor so that we would be prepared. I'm sure we missed a gem but saved approx 15 euro each!

This place is a must place to visit. So many Buddha's to see, especially the sleeping Buddha. Also it is in a very picturesque setting where there are lots of monkeys roaming about. Be warned! Take some socks to wear for walking on the extremely hot stone floors in the grounds. Shoes and sandals must be left at the Entrance!

It was fantastic to see the progression of cave temples that had been built hundreds of years ago. Well worth a visit, but make sure you understand the ticketing system we saw quite a few people who got to the entrance only to be told to go back down the hill!

The cave temple at Dambulla is a wonderfully preserved site with 5 relatively small caves all dating back at various stages over the past 2000 years. They are all painted with various versions of Buddha and each cave has many statutes. It's well worth having a guide when you get up there otherwise you could easily loose its history as one cave will look like another unless it's explained properly. Only downside is the steep climb up the steps.

The cave temple is awesome in its own right, keeping in mind the 5 different caves that hold over 100 statues of Buddha. Keeping in mind that the bulk of what you are seeing is over 2000 years old, this is a place to visit.
The temple structure is just one part of the experience, with the options of the museum, library, heritage centre and others available, allowing you to deeply delve into the Buddhist culture.
Very interesting spot - great views....a lot of culture in a small area. Quite a long walk up a lot of steps bit well worth the effort. Make sure you get a ticket at the bottom.

After climbing Sigiriya rock the day before, a further steep climb was somewhat off putting, but it was well worth it. These rock temples are carved out of the rock face, and in some of the temples, the images inside are also carved out of the rock. Suggest you start at the far end, as that way they get more impressive - and impressive they are.

Be careful if you're arriving there by the main road entrance and alone (I mean without local guide), you may have difficulty to find where to buy the tickets (1500 Rps). I climbed the rock and once on the top, they told me I had to go back down to buy an entrance ticket. So I went back down but didn't find the tickets... Then some local people helped me. Actually, you have to climb about half the rock, then you will see some souvenir and fruits sellers, at this point you have to go down behind the rock by another path and you will finally find the tickets selling place after about 15 minutes of walk. I was so tired... but happy I could see the caves. They're worth it!

We were lucky enough to have this place to ourselves, go at 7am if you want the same experience, and the calm and quiet exuding from these magnificent constructions (for want of a better word) in devotion to Buddhism is incredible. The caves have been maintained extremely well and the frescos and statues are in magnificent condition for some that date up to 2000years old. A must for a trip to Dambulla

We weren't sure what to expect here and we thought we'd seen enough Buddha statues already. However, the age and detail of both the statues and the wall painting was amazing considering some are 2,000 years old and carved out of the rock. There is little restriction on photographs so snap away at your leisure even with the flash. I would recommend a guide as ours knew the history of the caves and which statues were the oldest and what they symbolised. The downsides is the that I wouldn't recommend it for physically restricted people as there are a lot of steps leading to it and no ramp access anywhere. Also due to the change in which monastery is running the site, the ticket office is somewhat displaced from the entrance.
We didn't even gamble on entering this place. The vegas style entry and design is enough to throw anyone off.

I expected many and big caves filled with big Buddha statues. Instead this was a small cave with many small statues. Also this was claimed to be free entrance but then at the top it was informed that starting today we charge entrance fee, and tickets can only be bought at the bottom of the cliff, 500 meters below. Do not engage guides at entrance, they only want money (1000 Rs) and give little additional information. Shortly put; a rip off, not worth visiting.

After Polonnoruwa we decided to take a detour to Dambullah and do the temples there. On arrival, you can see the massive golden statue of the Buddha which is quite breathtaking. You then walk up the steps, go to the ticket office, pay 1500 rupees, walk up some very steep steps for 8-10 mins and then you can see the caves up there. Note; you must wear trousers and cover shoulders and knees. Or long shorts would be fine. The caves themselves are great. Lots of statues and drawings/carvings of buddha's etc. Also great views over Dambullah. You also have to pay 25 rupee for someone to look after your shoes! Recommended.
Visited when in Dumballa. I like this because it is a temple in a cave as opposed to the usual constructions in other sites around Sri Lanka. Beautiful decorations all around and nice views.

Loved this site. Unusual temples in caves on top of a hill / mountain. Prepare for a small climb and bring water. When there, you will be rewarded by beautiful views and a site different from others in Sri Lanka. The caves are beautifully decorated and popular with locals as well as tourists.
After climbing the steep hill you get to the temple hiden in the rock. I discovered comlete new world ther . All around budas and statues.0

Both the temples are located side by side with some difference in altitude, it is a big attraction for tourists. As we read reviews earlier, we prepared everything to visit this temple and we really astonished to see the level of architecture and art involved in building this temple. Excellent one.
Main attraction of Dambulla and worth visiting this place. Ancient temple, very well maintained and reflecting culture of srilanka and Buddha. Very easy to access
We visited this temple as part of our trip to Sri Lanka and found the history of this place extremely interesting. Well worth a visit.

This temple really takes you back in time and after an enjoyable but slightly challenging climb, you can explore the caves and see the ancient paintings and statues at your leisure. You must leave your shoes outside so if it is a really sunny day, then you will find the exposed concrete very hot to walk on!! There are also some lovely views on your way down and photo opportunities aplenty!

An easy walk to this place. The caves complex is interesting (we had a guide to explain everything and guide us with tickets, direction to go,etc.). Beware the Macaque monkeys. They lie in wait to ambush you and grab your camera, phone, food- whatever they can get.

Loved the history at this place, and some of the paintings are marvellous, but wish it had a little more of the self explanatory boards instead of hiring a guide. The approach to this temple really lets one appreciate the scenic views this region has to offer, and the views from the top are fantastic. The climb to the top is not that high, nor is it difficult. The place closes at 6 but make sure you're there by 3 or maximum 4 so that you can descend the hill by sunset. Also make sure to buy the ticket from the ticket office at the base of the hill before beginning the climb, because there isn't one on top. Ran into many fellow tourists who forgot to, and they'd already climbed all the way up!

You can easily walk there by foot from Dambulla. It was rather hot when we made our way up to the temple. Unfortunately if your coming from Dambulla by foot you aren't passing the ticket counter (afterwards it looked like there is a street which you can follow to get to the ticket counter directly, but it is not really clear where to go) and you have to get down again from the temple entrance to the ticket counter (10min down and up again). The tickets were (if I remember it correctly) 1500 LKR per person. Definitely a nice temple to visit!

Easily my favourite sight! Ok, not so much for the access bit - it wasn't easy finding the ticket office and entry point but after some asking around, my driver managed to find the right way.  As far as I can recall, it's away from the museum/Big Buddha. Be forewarned that there are flights of stairs before reaching the caves.  It wasn't too crowded when I visited in late afternoon.  There are 2 big caves and 3 smaller ones.  Cave 2 is the biggest and most impressive!  For photo-bugs like me, bring your tripod. My only regret was not having time to visit the museum.

There are 3 rooms/caves where you can see statues of Buddha. the ceiling is full of buddha paintings. I think that one cave is like the other so not really worth the entrance fee. WATCH OUT where to buy tickets. There are 2 places from which you can approach the cave which is on top of a mountain. They do NOT sell the tickets at the entrance where the dambulla museum with the golden statue of buddha is, but on the other side of the hill. So once you go up the hill from the side of the golden buddha, you will have to go down to buy tickets and then back again.

The temple is impressive to me. It is not that I haven't seen Buddhist temples but those are really special with all the drawings inside the cave walls. On the way climbing to the temples we saw a lot of monkeys who were really funny and attactive. As a lot of other people, we were told that the temples are for free but this is totally wrong! With no ticket point on the way, you understand at the entrance that there is somewhere down the road that you have to pay the tax (you cannot pay at the entrance) of 1500 rup/person... It is not a problem for me that we had to pay but the way they collect the money (they say it is something like charity) is not appropriate... Nevertheless I enjoyed the temples and I'm glad they didn't deny me from going with their attitude.

Firstly, after reading reviews on TA, I assumed this was going to be one of the few things we could do for free in Sri Lanka. Not true. There is an admission ticket but very reasonably priced. Secondly, there are two parking lots, one in front and one behind. The ticketing office is behind the big golden statue of Buddha. Our driver parked in the front parking lot, told us to take pictures of the big statue and then drove us to the one behind. We bought tickets here and then climbed up to reach the main temple with the 5 caves. Beautiful temple with different forms of Buddha. We hired an English speaking guide for 1000 LKR and he gave us a brief tour/description of each cave. Then we took our time looking at each one in more detail. There are no signs explaining anything, so you need a guide or a guide book to know what you are looking at. The ascent and descent was not too hard, even my 7yr old did it quite easily. Saw quite a few monkeys along the way. You need to remove your footwear outside so wearing socks might help on really hot days.

I've decided to write a review for this object to inform potential visitors that one has to buy a ticket to visit this place. But the tickets office is located not in front of the entrance, but somewhere else and not near by. We have climbed a long way up and very very disappointed as we havent bought tickets beforehand. And actually we were looking for the tickets office downstairs, but couldn't find it. So be prepared before visiting and make sure you have a ticket.

It's worth the stairs and the hike! If you are in Dambulla then you should take the time out to go and see this cultural sight. It won't break the bank, it's a good walk and it doest take more than an hour and a half. Just watch out. Talk to a Tuk Tuk driver before you enter the site. The tickets to the temple are out the back of the site not near the entry to the temple. If you get to the top and you haven't got a ticket you will have to redo the stairs all over again. It is best to purchase a ticket from the ticket office before you take a single step. Tuk Tuk driver know where to go to get the tickets so discuss with them. But don't expect the ticket counter to be an easy find.

If you're in the area, you should visit it. It's on the way from Sigiriya to Kandy. It takes about 1h to visit. 15 minutes walk up the hill (nice views). It was not too crowed and the different caves were impressive.

Having climbed up the Lion Rock - Sigiriya - the previous day we were a little daunted to be confronted by more steps. Fortunately there were considerably fewer than at that location but once again the climb was worth it. The five caves show amazing statues and frescoes whilst the views are stunning. A camera is a must as are sensible walking trainers.
This temple is one of the things you have to see in Sri Lanka! There is to many people but you have to see it. Very big statue of Buddha, paint on the rock, an amazing site to visit!

Very interesting 18 th century cave complex with temples. Great views from the top but a good 50 m climb to get in. ( vertically) and steep approx 200 metre drop on exit where you will find grossly overpriced poor toilet facilities.

This place is facsimile naming, make no mistake. Here are 5 caves of varying sizes with multiple frescoes dating back several hundred years as well as Buddhas in varying sizes and positions. Apparently those lying down represent the ageing Buddha in retirement. This is an important site with justification. Sadly access issues are a problem. New traffic systems are being introduced and unsurprisingly the result is chaos. One goes I. A road along the side but this remains two way though this is too narrow. A motorbike or a Tuc Tuc is one thing but another 50+ seater coach? Yup you guessed. This brings you out half way up to the cave and there is a choice of a pathway or stairs. Relatively short albeit steep climb which the overwhelming majority should handle happily. The coming down is another matter. Those who struggle ( knees arthritis for my wife and vertigo for me) are relatively OK going up - down us the problem and 6 of our 30 struggled with the descent not least in that the coaches are then moved to another car park right at the bottom of the hill and the 2nd part is longer and steeper than the first. Not good. A big bugbear at the bottom. Ticketed Toilet visit LKR 100 each (55p EUR 0.65 US$ 0.70) , the steepest I found in Sri Lanka. Yet toilet facilities were amongst the worst we encountered- holes in the floor only and substandard hand washing facilities- toilet paper BYO. One of my major dislikes is being charged first world prices for a third world offering. I accept standards will not be at UK levels but also expect prices to be compatible with the local economy -LKR 20 seems to be the norm. Grading based on fascinating caves- deduction for access and toilet issues not made here but others may feel I am being generous.

A climb of around 10 mins to the cave. The ancient paintings and statues have a story to tell. Having a guide is good to know the stories behind. Beware of monkeys, and have Rs 25 with you to keep your shoes before entering the temple. Be properly dressed like in all other Buddhist sacred places.

Make sure you buy a ticket before you reach the top. We went up by the steep stairs and down by the longer but more gentle sloping walkway. Some people came up that way but missed the ticket office and had to tip sonone to go and buy them a ticket. 1000 years of Buddhist cave art and more images of Buddha than you can shake a stick at, whether meditating, standing or reclining. Worth the climb. Go early in the day to avoid the crowds. Take socks to wear as you have to remove your shoes and the ground is hot and rough in places.

Of all the Temples and Heritage sites I visited in Sri Lanka , I would rate this the best. There are 5 caves carved out of a huge rock . The temple at the entrance has a large Golden Budha Temple which can be seen from far off. The caves themselves have statues of Lord Budha both in sitting and lying positions. Also there are lots of well preserved paintings which are so lovely. Unlike some of the heritage sites I had visited which were mainly ruins, the statues and paintings are well preserved and a marvel to look at. To get to the caves you need to climb up about 150 steps but they are not that difficult.

Great day our guide took us we parked at bottom of Hill we got a tuk tuk halfway up the hill very steep hill we walked the rest on a very hot day but an amazing veiw as you go up you have to take you shoes off before entering and there are staff there to do that and keep them safe for a small charge. When up there some amazing sculptures carvings into the cliff face it is well worth a visit for anyone visiting that area.

A very nice place to visit, unique in its own way. I think it's a "must" visit. We accessed it somehow from the back and so, we didn't climb the whole way up which saved us a lot of energy plus, if the weather is hot, I recommend having a pair of socks: you need to take off your shoes upon entering the temple and walking towards the caves on hot stones with no shoes was not fun at all for me.
You can either just view if from the outside or pay to walk up. A gorgeous big gold Buddha. Good for all the family

The Golden Temple and particularly the Rock temple are fantastic. Also one of the free admission temples in Sri Lanka, Visit in late afternoon so that you see the sunset from the top-  a truly great view.

Dambulla was our stop after a tiring visit to Sigiriya. Hubby opted out of it after he realized there was a steep climb (nothing like Sigiriya though, which he also didn't climb:)) I was using the SriLanka - The Rough Guide  book, which advised to see the Caves in descending order, which i did. This way, the caves improved in size and splendour. Great tip! The caves in the middle (can't remember the number) have brilliant mural paintings on Buddha's life and times - most of it is in good condition- but they are some blunt patches. A little more of literature on site would help improve the experience for the tourist- most were just wandering around - without seeing much. Make sure to take a guide book. The views from the caves are brilliant- the elevation (not high as Sigiriya) offers expansive view of the surroundings. It is free (no footwear inside the temple complex)We avoided, the tacky temple at the foot of the hill (which also makes some incorrect claims about being the largest Buddha -but it is worded such that - you can't be entirely sure of what the claim is).
Amazing ancient paintings and statues in 5 caves. Fantastic art, glorious sense of peace and the national purple lotus national flower in a pool close to the bodhi tree.

The cave temples are beautiful and exude an awe-inspiring serenity that you must experience for yourself.  The paintings on the uneven rock wall surfaces are just as impressive as the statues. It was nice to see the temple being used by locals for worshipping both the Buddha and Hindu gods. Of course, as with all the big Sri Lanka attractions, you won't be alone.  But, it's well worth the climb, and it can fit into your schedule more easily than some of the other big attractions, if time is a consideration.

Series of 5 caves. Start at the one furthest away and work back to the entrance. Quite a steep steady walk up to the cave. Prob best to wear fixed shoes/sandals and not flip flops. Need to have your shoulders and knees covered, and ideally wear pale colours (all out of respect) And hats must be removed. Fascinating, calming and stunning. Lovely views from the top.
Beautiful temple.  So sacred to the locals. Amazing place for tourists to see. A good hot day place to visit!
We enjoyed the visit with the family and to receive explantation about this popular temple and what it means . we bought few souvenirs and we met a lot of friendly locals . a place to visit
Beautiful and a great visit for tourists. Make sure you pack plenty water and wear comfy shoes as it's a good climb in the heat!
Nice place, specially for those who have interest in Buddhism and architecture. This is mysterious how on earth people built such big and beautiful statues 2100 years ago!!!!
Too expensive. It's £8 and you get no information about anything at all. And they ask for donations too. Absolute rip off.

We  visited Buddha caves in Laos and so were thinking that not much could top that experience . We were so wrong! This is one of the finest examples of complex and integrated religious art.  The level of talent is awesome. Please know that you have to purchase tickets before you climb the stairs to the caves. We took a different route and somehow passed the ticket booth. Staff at the top were kind enough to walk down the many stairs to purchase our tickets and then bring them to us at the top! Remarkable!!  The view from the caves veranda is one of lush greenery, and the temple monkeys are as cute as can be.
New ticketing introduced meaning a steep climb up and then down again to get tickets then up again! Amazing caves but each of the five much the same. If you are into Buddhas worth a visit.

The temple has beautiful painting on the ceiling but not a "simply stunning temple". For me Buddist temples always have a sense of peace and I can't explain why I did not feel it here. Definitely worth a visit but I was slightly disappointed. We went after the ticket fee (LKR 1500) was introduced and many people were walking up the "non-steep route" and had been told there was no ticket only to have to go down the steep route on the other side and come up again. It is about 10 minutes walking up either route. Make sure you have a 25 or 50 rupee note for the shoe check in- or don't mind leaving them somewhere.

This is a world heritage site-- lots of buddhas from the 12th century onwards.  When you get to the top, you pay 25 rupees to guard your shoes from the aggressive monkeys--but this is the day to wear socks-- you walk a long way on hot rocks after you give up your shoes!  One more thing-- they just started requiring tickets --even if you are a student and can go for free,you need a free ticket.  And they made everyone without a ticket climb back down the 300 steps to get one! My gallery husband went down to get ours--there was  no sign at the bottom to warn us-- and I listened to lots of unsuccessful attempts to bribe, cajole or break past the guards--so be sure to have tickets in hand!
Just staggeringly awesome.  You could do with quite a while in here to take it all in, or two visits.

Firstly our Rough Guide states that there is an entrance fee for this site, but this seems to have gone, or perhaps was suspended as we were there around the time of the full moon celebrations. If it's the same for you then please respond by making a small donation when you get there as these are amazing and deserve to be preserved. From the top you have to leave your shoes and get across about 40 feet of very hot rock to a small entrance pavilion, but after that you will be walking in the shade. If you have sensitive feet, take socks. The caves are unique and range from fairly small to huge. The steady flow of visitors means that if you are patient you will have times when you have the cave you are in all to your self. The interiors are well lit and a torch is not required to enjoy the incredible painted walls and ceilings.
