The huge modern buddha statue at the entrance is austentatious but the caves are well worth the climb up the hill. They now charge foreigners to enter the caves.

看评论好多说不用买票的，不知道那是什么时候，我去的时候是要的，而且售票处在山下，不想重新爬山只能加15rmb让人买。洞窟还行吧，维护的不好，有好多褪色的。 the cave requires tickets, and the ticket office is down the hill.if you don't want to go up and down again, you have to pay 300rps extra to ask the guy there go down buy for you

I stayed an extra day here in Dambulla & took a tuk-tuk (RS 200), 6:30, to the Royal Rock Temple to get there before the swarm. I arrive a 6:57 at the “new” entrance, the one EVERYONE uses and cane up the many steps to the ticket taker man. Where's MY ticket he says? You don't sell them? Where's the blanking ticket office? There is NO SIGN I could see of down below, just an arrow “To Rock Temple”....(see picture). Oh, it's down “there” at the “old” entrance. I reluctantly go ALL the way down, no-one speaks English, no-one KNOWS where the ticket office is but finally I see a policeman who directs me. Someone else made the SAME mistake. IF U don't ALREADY have a ticket make sure you find out before you climb the steps. Then I HAD to climb back up the same “old” entrance steps. It's tough for an old man with sciatica in both legs BUT I made it. RS 1500 for foreigners. It's the 2nd time I've seen the caves (2010). Still impressive especially cave # 2. I was caning out towards the parking lot at 9:45.

A short walk up the hill to the caves.  We saw an employee sweep up a lot of litter and simply throw it off the hillside, just outside the caves. We then later saw one monkey eating a plastic bag, and another with his head inside another one. Sri Lanka really needs to sort our its litter problem, because it is frankly disgusting and unacceptable. The caves themselves cost 1500 entrance fees for foreigners, and contain lots of buddhas.

There was a 1500 rupee entry fee for foreigners.  A short walk up a hill then approximately 3 or 4 man made caves decorated with Buddhas in various poses. However I was very surprised to experience a female employee sweeping up rubbish from the paths outside the caves, and simply throwing the rubbish over the edge of the hill. The natural environment around the site was filthy and littered with plastic. It is such a shame as Sri Lanka has so much potential, but they need to wake up and sort out their attitude to litter. I will not be returning.

If you are in Sri Lanka, don't miss this.  Ancient temples created in caves with art still intact.  Totally amazing and well worth the steep hike.  Tip: you can have car deliver you to midway point, cutting the hike considerably.

Dambulla cave temple situated on a rock top is an ancient Buddhist temple. Visit in the evening recommended to avoid harsh sunlight. Don't forget to visit painting  museum located nearby before visiting to the temple.

We were three independent travellers and were told that access to the caves was free. However, after a very hot and quite arduous climb to the cave temples we were refused entry as we hadn't bought a ticket at the bottom! We were very disappointed but decided to go down and give it a miss, as did several other people. Be sure to buy a ticket near the entrance. It is free for Sri Lankan visitors, but not for many other foreign visitors. The ticketing information is not clear or where to buy tickets, so ensure you investigate before you start to climb!

if you'r  'in to culture', of cource this is a must see. If you've seen more the enough tempels, this will be just one more on the list. Be aware that per feb 2017 you have to buy tickets again at the bottom of the mountain (10 USD). It is no longer free.
Amazing place. NEW - get tickets from bottom BEFORE climbing steps. As of 11th Feb. It's not expensive. There's two routes up, steps or a steadier slope which is easier but slightly longer.

Very well preserved, very unique buddhist cave temples that are a must for any Sri Lanka tour. Go early in the morning as it is a bit of a hike and you will have to wear long pants, given that it is a temple.

Quite a climb to reach the cave temple, but we'll worth it. No access for disabled or those with walking difficulties unfortunately. The temple itself is beautiful, lovely views from the top too. No charge to go in. Remember to take something to cover your knees and shoulders.
Interesting place to visit if you're staying in Dambulla (and to shelter a little from the heat). The series of caves is fairly extensive. Can be quite busy.
A very special place and well worth the effort of climbing the steps to reach the Cave Temple. All the more special when you have a guide who can explain the history and cultural relevance.
A bit of a climb up to the site but definitely worth the effort. The ancient caves have been painted in exquisit detail and have been used by Buddists for worship for centuraries.

Its a nice place with a very large statue of Lord Buddha. Their are many monkeys nearby the temple though they don't harm but still if you are afraid of monkeys this place is not for you. Do have the Jumbo coconut which is right there at the parking, charges 80 SRL for a jumbo coconut.
The monastery and all the statues are totally carved into the rock and is nice to hear the history of this temple. It is located on a hill, with a great view. You cannot miss it!
Its a world heritage site dating way back to the first century BC. Its a cave covered with murals, Buddha statues. Start climbing the rock  in the morning before its too hot.
Must see! Beautiful place and an easy walk up the hill. Walk to the museum nearby. It's quaint and has an interesting story about the history of Sri Lankan temple painting.

The views from the cave temples are spectacular. Get a drive to the top, then walk up many steps (easy) to arrive at the temple. Wear socks as you must take off your shoes and the pavement can be hot. You can leave your shoes outside with the shoe guy or put them in your bag which is easier. Beautiful paintings on the walls, sitting Buddhas, reclining Buddhas, small and large. Very impressive. There are 5 caves to see altogether, and lots of monkeys running around. They won't bother you if you don't feed them.

Our guide explained that these caves were originally constructed to hide the kings and only later took on a religious significance. They brought back memories of the Christian caves we had seen in Cappadocia, Turkey. There are 5 Temple caves. One has  "magical" dripping water because it seems to run upwards along the ceiling!

From the start, this site is beautiful and not to be missed. Once you pass the golden Buddha you climb up to the cave temples - which is a bit of a walk, but I think you can get a tuk tuk to the top too. You have to remove your shoes, and cover your arms and legs to enter the caves, and there is a stall where you leave your shoes. There were five caves in total, and we were advised to start in the one furthest away from the entrance to get the full effect of the size of each cave. The statues within each cave are beautiful, I've never seen so many in once place. Really would recommend taking a slow walk back down from the caves to fully appreciate the beauty of the surrounding scenery. Also...be careful if you buy some mango from one of the sellers...the monkeys will have it from you!

Dambulla rock temple was built in the 1st century B.C. and it is a World Heritage Site since 1991. Reaching the caves involves a steep climb. The complex of five caves with over 2000 sq. meters, has a mixture of religious & secular wall & ceiling paintings & sculptures, the largest area of painting found in the world! It contains over 150 images of the Buddha of which the largest is the colossal figure of the Buddha carved out of rock and spanning 14 meters.

These caves are a UNESCO site which are well worth visiting. The hike up is moderate, but the caves and the labor involved are well worth it. Some of the caves are better than others, but this is a cultural and religious site of great beauty. The workmanship is quite amazing

Our driver very kindly got us hallway up the hill to the caves, but we still had ten minutes climbing the stairs to the top. There  is a circuitous road that will get you up there in about 15 minutes without the steps. Shoes off (as normal) and deposited for the usual 25lkr. Make certain that you visit all the caves as some in group only went in two! Well worth having a good guide with you who can tell you all about the images and statues. Sadly any views obscured by the low cloud.

Quite a climb up to the Dambulla caves but once there and with shoes off we entered the complex. Five caves altogether looking quite ordinary from the outside but once inside especially cave 2 WOW it took ones breath away with the size and beauty of the myriad of buddhas. One could photograph inside which was an unforeseen bonus. A must visit despite the climb.
Very nice temple. A few stair up and you have great view and the caves are very nice. You have to take your shoes off and pay 25 LKR for it. Recommendable.

We visited Dambulla on a half day trip from our base in Habarana, only half an hour by bus. The site is also easily accessible by bus from Kandy, about 2 hrs. Ask to be dropped off at the golden temple  (you'll know it when you see it), saves you the trip back from the bus station. We didn't visit the temple or the museum, only the caves. Visiting the caves requires proper dress, but a sarong is available for rent, 100 rupee. This you get at the entrance to the caves, where you leave your shoes. Someone will watch them for 25 rupee a pair. Entrance to the caves is free, so this is the only money you spend here, drinks and souvenirs aside. The stairs to the caves start in the back, on the left side of the museum. It takes about 10 minutes to get to the top, by staircase or ramp. This is where you leave your shoes. Beware, the pavement gets quite hot in the afternoon. There are 5 caves, 2 and 3 being the biggest and most beautiful. They are all filled with painting and sculptures from top to bottom. For those who want to know more, a guide stands ready by the entrance. The entire visit will take about an hour, including going up and down again.
After spending several days previous to visiting here seeing temples, I was pleasantly surprised with this one.  While it was quite a walk to get there, it was well worth seeing.

I visited the caves at golden temple and stunned with the beauty of that place. Lots of Buddha statues are there and heard that built by a king two thousand years ago. Also the atmosphere was amazing surrounded by trees. Lot of monkeys hanging around that place but not to feed them.
This is a place that shows you the ancient Buddhist culture of srilanka well. If you visit dambulla don't miss to visit..
must visit place, these are old buddha caves in Dambulla. beautiful hand paintings on wall. view from the way to caves is spectacular.

Like most temples in Sri Lanka the Buddah statues are new and rather gaudy looking. The temples are not at all as elaborately decorated as in Thailand or Myanmar. All in all most were a bit disappointing.

Please bare in mind that visiting here is requires visitors to cover up, woman must cover legs and men must have shorts lower than knees. Its quite a breathtaking place, beginning with a lengthy climb to the temple itself, not idea for anyone with a walking disabilities, remember to take water as it gets very hot here. The steps are steep and on route will be faced by persons begging, sellers and of course monkeys.

Steps! Many of them! But worth the climb. After climbing to the top, watched by scores of monkeys who nimbly jumped past everyone, the caves are an amazing sight. How they did all this so many hundreds of years ago is fascinating. The caves (5 of them) are filled with Buddha statues of all shapes an sizes, and the fresco paintings are truly amazing. Add to this the view from the top of the surrounding countryside and it's well worth the effort.
The golden buddha is probably worth seeing but the rest of the temple belongs to Disneyland and doesn't really deserve its place at the bottom of the fabulous Dambulla caves.

Making the tacky golden temple number one over the Dambulla caves is absurd! The painted caves are an absolute must-see and a treasure of humanity recognised by UNESCO. Exceptional frescoes and statues in the 5 caves open to public and wonderful views of the valley underneath all the way to distant Sigiriya rock. Be prepare to climb the 1000+ steps though, but cheeky monkeys all the way up make it much easier than it sounds!

It should be a place with paid ticket but we were lucky that no need to buy any tickets.  You have to climb some steps before arriving the entrance of the temple.  You must take off your shoes by keeping at the store (with charges), keeping in your bag or just placing on the road.  It's quite impressive when you are in the cave temples. Remarks: bring towel to clean your feet before putting on your shoes. The shoe store-keeper will put some food near the shoes which are placed on the road which attract monkeys so that you may have to pay $$ to these men for help.  Please note!
The walk to the Dambulla caves is a fulfillment of a dream. The paintings on the wall, the depictions of the Buddha, of the Hindu gods and the feeling of oneness with nature. This is truly special.
Among the oldest Buddhist temples in the world. A short climb up the hill. Serenity and peace and natural beauty.

A visit to the Golden Temple is certainly worth your time. You have to conquer some steps but the caves with all the buddhas are really impressive to see. Some even have an Egyptian style but the most special thing about these caves, is that it has statues of Buddha but also from the Hindu gods Vishnu and Ganesha. The entrance is free starting from 2016. You do have to pay to store your footwear, 25 Rupees per set.

Be prepared to walk up the hill to get to the caves. You would be asked to take off shoes before getting into the cave area. Someone would charge you 25 rupees for storage, but you could place the shoes in a bag and bring them with you. Also, bring an extra pair of socks, and antiseptic wet towels to clean your feet afterward. Only 2 caves were opened at the time we visited. The large one housed many buddha statues and it was worthwhile to study them in details as they adopted different position and held different signs with their hands. We spent around 2 hours there.

We visited as part of our trip to Sigiriya and thought it a wonderful place, I wish there had been less visitors to soak up the atmosphere of what is clearly a wonderfully spiritual place. The wall paintings were really impressive. My only tip is take a pair of socks, you have to walk barefoot around the caves and the floor can be really hot. Monkeys to see on walk up also very photogenic!!

not my first time to visit cave temple. this one is no special & the Buddha statues also quite new but paintings wall is nice. uphill to temple is another stuff to enjoy although many monkeys around but feeling good as well. avoid noon time go here at it is quite hot.
Will not say much about this as the element of surprise is jaw dropping. A must visit. You do have to remove shoes and hats prior to entering.

Enjoyable walk uphill with an magnificent view and the caves with a wonderful athmosphere of ancient times when monks were living in the jungle to practise their meditation in solitude, next to wilderness and animals. One of the highlights in Sri Lanka

Fantastic temple to visit. Built in a rock, serves as cave temple. Many small rooms you can visit, really nice wall paintings and statues. Entrance free. Bit of walk to reach it on top but really worth it. (Be aware of monkeys!)

Wow, I absolutely loved this temple, just incredible, so many different sanctuary's and Budda mural Paintings. A very special place indeed , a must visit if you are out this way. An easy day trip from Kandy. - you could also include and elephant  Safari at one of the Nationals Parks in nearby Habarana

The visit to the Golden Cave Temple was a unique experience. It was hot (30 degees) and you had to climb many steps to get there but when you finally arrived you saw a “temple” built in the past yet active and prosper today. Through 5 different caves you can see 150 or so painted Buddha statues. You move with the croud from one cave to the other, observe the statues, listen-in on a prayer, and feel an authentic mood of worship. We visited other temples, standard ones, yet this one tands out of all.

There are 5 different caves that were created at different times atop this rock. What is truly spectacular about these caves is that in addition to the beautiful statues, the walls are painted.   A plaster is made from oyster shell and some additional ingredients that is placed directly on the rock wall.   The wall murals are then painted on this plaster inside the caves.   When you walk into the caves, the feeling from the wall murals and the statues is overwhelming.   It is such a spiritual place.  The caves were built over many centuries with different kings wanting to build out different caves to thank the monks that lived here.  These caves are not to be missed in Sri-Lanka.  An absolute must.

Like the temples in here, it took me few hours drive from kandy to here but well worth it. Not many visitors and i like the small hill and the small scale of temples. It didnt charge you any entrance fee, i paid for the guide but not because i wanted any guide, i wanted to contribute to someone who maintains the temple well. It cant recognize my english typing here. And i cant change my setting to english into chinese in the app. So stupid 為什麼我一定要用中文寫我的評論而不能用英文呢 在設定上也找不到語言變更 好麻煩一點也不user friendly 不知道要怎麼才好 不想我評論是吧

The cave temples are worth seeing, even though you have to climb a ton of stairs to get there. (Ask your driver if he knows the shortcut to skip half the stairs.) You do have to remove your shoes, and on a hot day, the stones are unbearable. Wear or bring socks so you don't burn your feet. The sheer amount of Buddha statues in these caves is worth seeing, and don't forget to look up and see the painted ceilings.
This site is beautiful and defiantly worth the trip to Dambulla. Breathtaking. Take some water because it can get very hot in the caves

Very nice set of cave temples with many different painted caves and buddha statues. Some stairs to climb but ok for all levels of fitness. P No charge for entry when we visited, only bring a sarong and pay the shoe-keeping-guy a small tip.
Very interesting and beautiful teple.  Unusual in many ways, and the story behind the temple is facinating.

The cave temple in Dambulla is definitely worth seeing. There is a short climb up the stairs which is not dificult and, in fact, it's quite enjoyable because there are a lot of monkeys to keep you company :) Don't forget to take something to cover your legs and shoulders, on hot days it pays off to take a pair of socks, as the stones can get pretty hot to walk on barefoot..and it's FREE!!! They cancelled the 1.500Rp fee :)
This was probably the most amazing place I've ever been. It's incredible. Words or pictures cannot describe. Just go and see it.

Arriving at the foot of the rock up to the temple you are confronted by a giant golden Buddha surround by buildings which would be more at home in Disneyland!! One contemplates whether to make the effort to treck up the hundreds of steps to the rock temple. Believe me it is worth it, the temples are magnificent and I would rate as one of the best in SL the colours are dynamic and the carvings exquisite, don't be put off by the garish buildings at the bottom, make the effort, you will be well rewarded.
Breath-taking cave and Buddhist cultural heritage. Nice walk to the temple. In front of the temple you can observe little monkeys fooling around.

Headed here as part of a private tour.  Temples are beautiful, well maintained and for artwork that's 2000 years old? It's work seeing if you have the time. You have to walk up the mountain on steps out a path so would not be suited to ppl with mobility difficulties. Don't visit the hindu temple/ shine there there's nothing really in it and the guy at the entrance will want to make you a string bracelet.

This place is awesome and i do love this temple. Statues were mind blowing. Without any doubt this place can be rated as a nice temple in sri lanka. Greatest view ever. Nice place not only for buddhists but for any one.
Nice to see the sunset from here. Caves are good to see. Loads of monkeys and the golden Buddha is nice.
The temples are beautiful and if you cary a tripod you can get amazing pictures of the small statues and painted ceilings. A lovely place to visit.
The monks have done a really nice work to make these lot of Buddha statues and hand painted walls. We really liked this place.
If you go to the cave temple you should visit the golden temple, too. The statues are a really nice handwork.
If you are in Dambulla you should see this temple. The walk up the hill is nice. To see the different caves with the paintings and the status are impressive.

A nice climb through a path decorated with greenery and golden lamps takes you up past the enormous outdoor Buddha and into a little cloister system. Herein, you'll find Buddha upon Buddha situated in adjacent caves. Intricate wall paintings are the real highlight. Buddha is everywhere, and therefore nowhere - after you've seen one it's hard to get excited about the other hundred. Nevertheless, the place is special and worth your attention. Watch out for one of the end rooms where strange high frequency noises are emitted from speakers, making it almost unbearable to be there for more than half a minute.

This place would be of special significance to those who profess the Buddhist faith. It's history as to how it came to exist was also interesting - apparently it was built by a Sri Lankan King as a form of gratitude to the monks already meditating aand living in the caves for giving him sanctuary.

The caves are amazingly painted and carry so much history for Buddhism. the walk to the cave is pleasant if not done in the heat of the day and you are rewarded with such views even half way. just beware of the monkeys which can be really aggressive. mind you phones or cameras. sunset views are beautiful.  this cannot be missed. if you do not want to climb all the stairs, round the side, there is an easier way to reach the caves. ask your guide.
I was impressed by the giant Buddha and all the locals visiting the place. I missed the Buddhist museum but just walking around he place is peaceful.

Too be fair, it being the largest in the world isn't a reason to visit unless you are a big fan of big statues. The caves themselves are interesting, there are five and I think both "golden temple" listings on here are the same place! There is a short walk up a hill to them and then you have to leave your shoes at the gate before you can enter the compound so either where decent socks or be prepared to go barefoot. There are many statues in the caves and having a guide will make it make more sense (or get a guide book etc before you come, there are no signs etc.) If you are in the area (e.g. for lions rock) try to pop along, is maybe 2hrs max but some interesting history.

We arrived at Dambulla rock temple at around 11 am, when it was starting to get quite hot and our driver drove us to the half way point, so we didn’t have to climb too many steps in the heat. However, there is no car park there, so after dropping us he had to drive down and park at the lower parking area and wait for us. We had a choice of climbing either steep steps or a steep cobble-stone pathway, and we chose the pathway. Suggestion:  wear comfortable good-gripping flat shoes. If you have mobility issues, you will find this climb very challenging. There are many hawkers along the path trying to sell their wares of souvenirs in the usual way. There are also fruit and flower sellers, but beware of the hungry monkeys who are always ready to snatch a quick meal. There are also drink sellers along both paths. The only cost to enter the temple is to store your shoes at the storage area, before entering. This costs 25rp per pair. There are also guides available for 1000rp if you need one to lead you through the temple. The actual temple itself is absolutely amazing. Make certain you go in to each and every cave, as each one is slightly different. There are also spectacular views from the top.

The cave temple at Dumbulla is a must visit. There is no entry fee. One have to climb stairs to visit the 5 caves on top which houses statues of Buddha in various postures and beautiful paintings. The hill top also offers amazing views.

I went there for a visit with my family in Jan 2017. You need to get a guide to explain what you are looking at. It a mini version of the aganta ellora caves of India. The buddha idols are very well maintained and the place is nice and clean. The are a set of steps you need to climb to reach the temple, difficult for aged people. The fresh cut mangoes bought from the fruit sellers are a real treat, make sure to protect them with your life from the monkeys though :)
Impressive Buddha and statues, with free entry, however many people trying to sell things to you and 100 rupees to use bathroom.
Caves are within city limits. Just about 1km from the road. Lord Buddha in all sorts of positions. samadhi,meditation,reclining. must see. not for wheelchairs.
Nice to have seen! Beautiful views and Old buddhiststyle! A bit hard with all the steps aspecially after Sigiriya!

Climbed the steps up to the five temples, I think it's better to see them in reverse order as cave 3 and 2 are quite magnificent. Beautiful Frescos on the ceiling and statues are everywhere.  Spent 2 hours at the site.  Wonderful
such an amazing place, made in cave, they told us that it has 1000 steps, but that is not true as it took us 10 minutes to get,

Great and well worth it. If you go onto the road behind, there is a shortcut to get up here, then you only have to climb 35% of what you would have had to from the main entrance. Free to get in and only have to pay a small price to leave your shoes outside.

The five caves are reached by a set of stairs up to the top of a hill with fantastic views. We went early in the morning and avoided the general tourist crush. The detail in all of the caves is amazing and it is interesting to see how religious art changed over the years. Definitely worth the visit.
We visited relatively early in the morning before the crowds. It was a beautiful, peaceful day. It's worth a look.

There is a bit of a walk up to the entrance if the temples. Maybe 10-15 min up stairs and there is a lot of monkeys on the way up which add to the experience. When you arrive at the top there is a little stand where you have to give your shoes, which is fine for religious reasons, but I don't like that you can't put them in your backpack. Furthermore, same as before for religious reasons, you can't show knees and shoulders, again will you get charged Rp125 for shoes and skirt. Then you proceed to the temples which are beautiful    and have interesting background stories. But when you first step in to the temples, a "Monk" approach you and start showing you around, which was fine until he in the end started talking about how much the entrance fee was before and how they now made it free, and almost immediately after ask for a donation. As budget travellers we don't have much a day, so we took our wallets out and gave him Rp 100 each, and then he look at as like "are u kidding me" and left. So really sad note to end on so if someone approaches you just say no. The view from up there was amazing and almost worth the climb without the temples.

It's worth hiring a guide at the entrance. They will explain everything to you. There are four caves with centuries old history. The climb is moderate, but feels long because you can't see it all from the bottom.
Modest climb but well worth it. The Cave temples are very special and worth the effort to climb.Highly recommended.

We went there early in the morning.  There were a lot of locals there as well, praying. Entrance fee is free. The cave temple is well preserved and beautiful . A must visit place in Dambulla. UNESCO as well.

As usual it's a bit of a climb to the caves. The five caves are in granite rock and at the top of many steps. Fortunately, you can keep your shoes on while climbing the steps. When you get near the caves there is a place where your shoes can be stored. There are lots of Buddha statues in the caves, and some impressive sleeping Buddhas carved out of the rock. There are paintings on the walls and roof of each cave.

This temple is one of the top destinations for us on our long journey to Anuradhapura. The cave temple is just magnificent with intricate artwork all around the caves. It's better to take your time and walk through each cave temple absorbing the fabulous art. We did not encounter any fees to get in as foreigners or locals. Great views of the country as you climb up to the top. Optional: our driver recommended hiring a local guide that was at the temple premises to explain things since there is a lot of history here. We paid him 500 LKR which we thought was well worth. Beware of the monkeys: they don't tell you this when they sell you flowers at the bottom of the rock to take to the temple. The monkeys are unusually aggressive and will snatch anything from your hand that looks like food. So if you need to carry flowers from the bottom to the top, cover them with a non-transparent bag. The climb can be a bit tiring. Take plenty of drinking water and a towel to wipe off sweat. Since there is no entry fee, please consider donating what you can to the temple.

First impression isn't great. It's a very Disney sort of approach, all glitzy and touristy. Once you start climbing up though it all changes. The walk up the hill is long, if you aren't very fit then just take your time. There are plenty of spots to stop and take in the view. The caves themselves are very impressive, some of the paintings are as old as time and so well preserved. Please don't be "that tourist" and try to take photos of yourself inside, you will be spotted by the CCTV and be made to delete your photos.
One of the best attractions in Kandalama, Dambulla close to Heritance Kandalama. Very close to Dambulla City.

Dambulla Cave Temple was one of the highlights of our trip in Sri Lanka. When you enter the temple, there is a modern temple building with a huge Buddha image. The highlight comes after you climb to the cave temple behind. it There are several large caves with a very large amount of different old Buddha images. This is a sight you should not miss when touring in Sri Lanka

Dambulla Golden Rock Temple is worth 1 visit and is really a quaint and peaceful location with around 157 Buddha Status in over 5 caves in the temple. Try going at early in the morning since time and energy both can ve saved.
this place has to be promoted more. similar artistic and cultural value like Sigiriya Rock, no other place in the world is similar to this ancient temple

Having visited many other cultural sights in the previous couple of days, we thought we might be a little disappointed by the Dambula Cave temples, but that was definitely not the case. By reason of age, boldness of vision, and sheer beauty and scale of execution, the cave temples are hugely impressive. For some reason there was no one there collecting the usual US$10 tourist admission fee when we visited; that was a bit of a bonus, as the cost of entry to the main tourist sites in the ancient cities region does add up, especially for a family!

I was so impressed by this site. The hike is not so bad, but try not to go in the middle of the day, as it can get hot. You can take as many breaks as you need to get to the top. You will need to remove your shoes, hat and sunglasses to enter their sacred place - this is a buddhist sacred site, so you must respect their customs, which also includes not to take pictures given your back to the Buddha, touching the Buddha, or sitting on top of the Buddha; believe it or not some people do try these pictures. There is a small stand where you can leave your shoes and pay about 50 rupees per pair. There're about 4 main caves, which display beautiful hundreds of year old wall paintings and statues of different sizes of Buddha. Unfortunately, I didn't have a guide to really get a grasp of everything, but you can hire one at the entrance of the site. It is suggested that you spare a small donation to the temple. I bought a mango with chili powder on my way down from one of the ladies, but watch out for the monkeys, and they love the fruit. If you buy fruit eat it standing right next to the ladies :) Majestic views from the top. I spent about 2 hours here.

They didn't allow Muslim females with head covered. So if for religious reasons you don't want to uncover your head don't climb up all those stairs to find out you can't get inside. View of the city is good

don't miss the temple and climbe in the afternoon in order to sea the sunset,biside the incredible caves where are the Buddha statues.It is a great spiritual athmosphere,and the printing caves are amazing.It is a great emotion.
Dug inside a huge rock you will find a series of 5 caves with buddhas peacefully resting and meditating.

An easy climb relative to other attractions. 5 caves in all & all are amazing given that some of the statues inside are carved from granite. No entrance fee but watch out for well dressed locals claiming to be guides who offer their assistance for free or "up to you" & then put the squeeze on at the end. Donations may be a better option
Amazing temple with all the buddhas. It was very quite when we went so we could really enjoy. Don't miss it.
Nice to see the caves, interesting paintings. Wouldn't belong in UNESCO heritage in my mind though, nothing so impressive.

Marvellous example of art and engineering could be seen here.Perfect place clean and scenic place. Evening time is the perfect time to visit where in you can see sun set and also experience cool climate
Disappointed by the poor maintenance, I visited 40 years ago when it was spectacular, it is a shame there has not been more effort to keep the site clean

Great views up hills and fascinating artifacts inside the cave that tell us stories. Its a UNESCO site and all the wall painting and artifacts was well preserved. To understand Sri Lankan culture and belief visit this place and you learn a lot. I recommend to whenever you are in Sri Lanka dont miss to visit this wonderful Buddhist cave.

The place is on the top of a hill, make sure u wear non-slippery shoes, the view outside is breathtaking abd from the inside u can see many statues for Buddha, such a calm, full of history, and mysterious place

It was prt of our tour, i loved the place with its mystery, you have to climb up so you better wear comfy and not slippery shoes.. To get inside the main temple, u have to wear decent cloths and take off ur shoes -keep them with the shoe keeper for a small fee of 50 rps... outside and inside the temple u will b greeted by many monkeys, you will find some natives who sell water, mangos flowers necklaces and many more 😍the temple on the top, inside has many statues for Buddha.. such a calm place.. very damp and wet though.. but the view from the outside is something to die for just sit back and enjoy a breathtaking view of mother nature..

When we arrived there, we passed a golden Stupa (normally they are white in Sri Lanka) and stood in front of a huge golden Buddha, sitting above a big mouth which accommodates a kind of museum aside a radio station... this all looked terribly kitschy to me kept me climbing up the thousand steps to the Golden Cave Temple! (That is a separate topic under Trip Advisor)

Having climbed to the top of Sigiriya Lion Rock yesterday morning, a few hours later in mid afternoon I did the trek up to the Golden Temple Caves. Prior to the ascent, I visited the Buddhist Museum for a token entrance fee of 200/- Lankan Rupees. I was surprised to be the only person at the time but enjoyed the visit which enhanced my understanding of the Buddhist Faith. The ascent to the Caves is another exhilarating experience but you require to be reasonably fit. The Temple comprises 5 Caves. I had already read up on the Temple and was aware that the Statue of Buddha is the tallest in the world. Monkeys are encountered on the trip - I was amused when one monkey jumped at a vendor holding freshly sliced pieces of mango and made off with his loot - was unable to capture the moment on my IPhone..... The Golden Cave Temple is a must see if you are able to make the climb.....

Well worth the 600 steps up to these wonderful Buddhist caves. They are not steep. Great views. The caves can only be accessed with a guide present. ( Due to previous tourists climbing on a Buddhist statue for a photo shot..go figure?!!) Shoes must be removed.
way back from Sigiriya and lunch at Jungle resturent (Colokia dine and rest) @ sigitiya
This is a very old and a beautiful temple. A must see location if anyone is visiting Sigiriya and Dambulla.

Up in the hills, moderate walk. Even when it is crowded you can still feel the beauty of the place. Well worth the visit. If you are worried about the steps, get a tide to the halfway point, much easier as just two sloping paths
If in Sri Lanka you have to see this place. Very old caves inspired by Buddha. We really enjoyed this attraction. Go early to avoid big crowds.

We called in as part of a private tour. It is a fair climb to the top of the hill to visit the caves with the Budist shrines although not too difficult if you are not fully fit as long as you take your time,

When you'll get to the place it's impossible not to notice the huge gold Buddha statue on top of the first building. 🗿 That's not the temple: start going up on the staircase and, after a few minutes, you'll reach the entrance. 🏯 The temple is incredibly build in the mountain. 🏔 It's full of statues and paintings and you'll probably see some monks praying. 🙏 The area is full of monkeys jumping from tree to tree. 🐒

The stairs are easy, a very peaceful and moving insight into Buddhist, and Sri Lankan history. Go at lunchtime and avoid the swarms of Korean tourists with no respect for Buddhist culture (maybe a bad experience on my part). Be respectful, cover up, remove your hats, don't point, photograph an edifice of Buddha with anyone in it and be quiet. The five caves are all equally fascinating. Take a guide if you can as there is no interpretation. Really interesting. The monkeys are hilarious in relation to the hapless tourists!
No entry fee. A very steep climb to the top. There are 5 caves with statues. We did not have a guide so did not understand the why there were so many statues. Would help to have a guide.

The Golden Cave Temple is really a series of five indentations where chiseled sanctuaries were carved into the rock face of an overhang.  The walk up to the caves is fairly brutal and the way is lined with macaques and touts.  The stucco painting and statues within said caves are quite impressive, particular in the largest of the five 'caves'.  This place is a worthwhile visit but don't let the 'cave' misnomer drum up any expectations.

So you may be satiated with Buddha statues by the time you get here just like seeing paintings of Madonna col bambino on a tour of Italy, but the simple craftsmanship will amaze, inspire, and make you feel something

The climb up to the cave temple is a good one. You are presented with fantastic views of the city from above there. Watch out for some really nasty monkeys though , they snatch and eat up the offerings you buy( I saw that happen). Also You dont need a guide. And avoid buying anything from the stalls, its a rip off , you get the same things at a lot cheaper rate from normal souvenir shops

This is the best preserved cave temple in the world so you are up for a grand experience! As you enter, you will find a big entrance leading to a museum, skip that, it is chargeable and not the real thing. Take the left hand side entrance to the real cave temple. Now get ready for two main things: 400 stairs to climb up to the mountain that contains the cave temple, and lots of people trying to sell you lotus flowers and souvenirs. You will also see plenty of starved monkeys trying to snatch the flowers from you to eat! As you reach the top, you are required to remove your shoes, and then you go in. There are 3 or 4 caves whose walls have been entirely painted with Buddhas and spiritual figures. There are also fascinating cement monuments of Buddhas, one of which is an impressive reclining Buddha. What I found amazing was how the painters managed to use the caves ceiling topography to design the drawings and complete them in a very artistic way! Such a shame the draining water from mountaintop is actually causing major damage to certain parts of the ceiling and side walls making the drawings go away. This site is a MUST see, a once in a lifetime experience! Don't miss it please! And guess what??? it is free of charge!

Beautiful temple.World Heritage site.Excellent View from the top.5 caves which needs to be explained by a local guide.There no entry fee.but do answer to your nature's call b4entering the temple.They charge 100lkr for peeing.

A short climb up the hill, followed by visiting 5 temples which are next to each other. Quite interesting when you can see the locals going through the rituals. Ask for a guide at the door if you'll like to learn about the history of the temple.

This is not 1st time i visited with my family. It is a great place.  It is better that if allocate delegated  legal persons to  describe and  educate the visitors about the history of this place. There are books  but it is not enough to get quick understanding .

The path is tough to climb for someone with leg pain.  So those of you having leg pain avoid climbing as there are many stairs to climb..  But the view is breathtaking from the top..  There are many caves inside which there are statues of buddha..  Beautiful and clean at the top and scintillating view of the nature at the top of the hill

We were not supposed to visit this temple but at the end we got some free time to go there. 15 minutes walk through monkeys, steps, stones, trees....finally the entrance. The best is the atmosphere in the cave, where ceiling, floor and walls become all the same in a spiritual atmosphere. I suggest to visit it, it's free and you will enjoy the walk as much as the place itself

We drove through on our way to Sigiriya and spent 90 minutes here. There's a large golden Buddha and a moderately steep staircase and rock path which takes about 15 minutes to climb. You take your shoes off and pay a fee (usually way too much for someone simply holding your shoes! You could probably put them to the side for free!) entrance to the caves was free. There are about 5 caves: 'once you have seen one, you've seen them all' unless you're really into Buddhist relics. Some nice sculptures and painting on the ceiling. Some good photos if your camera is good in low light. It's pretty hot walking up the hill, bring a small bottle of water each.

This is just an amazing experience. The steps up to the caves take a bit of time, but are very wide, and feel very safe. For those who do not like steps, there was an alternate path, also a reasonable grade. My 12 years olds and my 70 year old parents made it up with little difficulty. Most of the path is shaded, but it is probably still more pleasant in the morning which is when we went. The cave frescoes and the statues are stunning. There is no admission to enter, just a nominal one to leave your shoes at the top when entering the caves.
The stairs have to be climbed. Not favourable for old and disabled persons. The scenic beauty on the top is really mesmerising. The Fresco paintings in the caves are really precious.
Located on the Kandy road. Free entry. The area is vast. The Buddha statue is really big. Religiously significant.

After a climb of flights of stairs, a huge rock was the first thing you see at this site's entrance, with breathtaking view of the surrounding mountains. The Golden Cave Temple holds a vast quantity of Buddha statues inside this piece of rock. Coupled with the ancient painting on the ceiling, it's simply amazing. I was in awe.....😲 A must see attraction.

The climb is not for unfit people! You will climb up a very steep hill and i mean steep.  When you get to the top, you will pay 50 rupees to keep your shoes safe. Don't pay more than that. The temple is a fantastic display of ancient religious art and was worth the climb. If you start the climb at around 4:30pm, you will make it for an awesome sunset. Definitely a mist see.
it is out first sri lanka temple experience.  walking around barefeet is quite interesting. if you want to visit a temple or two, this one is worth a visit

My family and I throughly enjoyed visiting the cave paintings part of this temple. The stupa and gold Buda where good but the best part was by far the ancient paintings. The day before this we had visited the polonnaruwa ancient city. Which had a hefty entrance fee and was nothing we had not seen before at other temples. Defiantly recommend this instead. We had looked at trip adviser reviews prior to visiting where we where advised that we had to purchase tickets at the bottom of the hill before the (fair hike) up to see the caves. We asked around and discovered that we did not have to pay at all just to visit the caves you only had to pay to see the museum. Which my family had seen enough museums and stupas. Tips: Go early to beat the rush Go on a dry day so you don't slip during the walk up Make sure you dress appropriately (covered shoulders and knees) Wear comfortable shoes for the walk up and you just have to pay 25 rupee to leave your shoes before entering the caves.
This is Buddhist temple  on a rock and roof of temple also rock. you can walk on rock to see the temple with beautiful  surrounding and nice views too.

Historic place . Lot of old Buddhist temple socially one big temple which is called golden temple . This is just 3km away from dumbella by stand . You can take Tuk tuk to reach there . The Buddhist temple over rock in cave are just so beautiful . The architecture of the work are must respect full . One hour will be enough to visit this place .

Really disappointed ourself to visit there . We were three friend today morning , there are nothing so much interested for us . Just a few old scenerio and drawing . Nothing special for young age people .
This was one of the highlights of my trip to Sri Lanka. It's hard to believe there is no fee to visit this very special site.

The climb to the top is about 20 minutes at moderate pace along rock stairs and slopes and its every bit worth the effort. There are around 5 to 6 cave temples with statues of Buddha of various positions and sizes. The roof of the caves are covered with exquisite painting.

There is a long flight of stairs and our guide did not tell us about it. Be sure to wear good walking shoes and wear clothes that cover your arms and knees otherwise you will be turned away at the top. But it is well worth the climb. The caves are amazing and the views are great.
Absolutely stunning. Make sure to wear the proper attire and to be respectful at all times. The statues are undergoing some restoration but are incredible. 😍

We were not prepared at all to find so many things about Buddha's life, but this place turns you into his fan. The guide explains all the meanings of his positions. On the way up make sure you take a sun umbrella and enough water, as on the top you can't find anything. At the entrance of the temple you must take the shoes off.
It may have been pouring rain, but it did not dampen our spirits or appreciation for this wonderful location. There is a reason UNESCO chooses it's sites.
It may have been pouring rain, but it did not dampen our spirits or appreciation for this wonderful location
We were not expecting to see such large and numerous statues... pleasantly surprised! You can definitely go after a trip to Sigiriya. Try the mangoes but watch out for then naughty monkeys!!
This is one of the only religious sites I actually liked in Sri Lanka. Not to many people,  amazing views and not costly for tourists. Definitely worth a stop.
Must see sight here and very impressive craftsmanship.  Combined with golden temple caves and giant Buddha statue

The temple is really nice. It gives you a sense of spirtuality. Would be useful to go with a guide to explain you all relevant aspects of the same. You will be able to see a view of 'Sigiriya' rock while climbing up towards the temple.
Quick walk to the top. Once there, the cave temples are an awesome sight to see. All in, this trip takes under an hour.
A good hike to get to the cave temple.  It is amazing to see how the temple and the status sculptured from the mountain.

We visited this place in Sigiriya during our Sri Lanka road trip. The GOS took us to the rear of temple . After talking to a local we got to know that it was a shorter route to the temple. This was the second climb of the day for us. The caves are adorned with statues and the walls roof beautifully decorated . You are permitted to take pics inside the caves. You can't visit religious sites in short or sleeveless. So better dress up accordingly or carry a scarf to cover .  There are a couple of guys who can take care of your shoes. Don't pay more that 5 LKR though they may try to ask for more. There isn't any ticket to visit this site.

It's part of our route to kandy. Many tourists will come here. If you are taking public bus, it about 15-20 walk, or just opp the wholesale market; just ask the local will do. Free entrance. 10-15 mins easy climb with steps. Expect to see monkeys along the way. You will have to pay Rs20 to collect your shoes just outside the temple or you can just put the shoes in your bag.

They used to charge entry fee to the caves but they stopped. At least that's what I think has happened, as old signs requesting people to get tickets are still seen here and there....The caves are not really caves, they only appear to be caves. However, they are truly fascinating, each different. Some of them (no. 2 especially) are incredibly rich in decor and symbolism. The climb can be exhausting. The views are great and the monkeys entertaining.

Quite a few steps with some steep rock flanks between. Recommend good walking shoes. If wet it could be slippery under foot! As always out of respect take something to cover your knees if you are in shorts (men too) as you are visiting a temple at the top.

We've been lucky with the timing, beautiful sunset and not so hot. The cave temple is different and beautiful. There are also many monkeys along the way, do make sure NOT bring lotus flowers which the locals will try to sell them to u. That's because the monkeys will snatch them from u and eat the seeds in the flowers.

Once you are here you will only need 1.5 hours to visit this temples. Can be quite off-putting with the huge golden Buddha in front but walk through the gates, up the numerous flights of stairs and you will be pleasantly surprised at the magical find. In my opinion, this is a must-do in Sri Lanka as it is accessible, quick and truly magnificent.
After a short climb, there are five beautiful caves to visit. It is worth the visit. The caves are filled with lots of Buddha statues.

This large complex includes an enormous Buddha statue and some wonderful cave temples. It's a bit of a walk up to the top but definitely worth it. There are a few different caves to check out at the top, all intricately decorated with wall paintings and statues.
I enjoyed climbing up the stairs to the Cave Temple with all the monkeys scattered all over the place. The frangipani flowers smell amazing. The temples are great to visit, the landscape is relaxing.

Do not be put off by the Disney Land appearance of the entrance. Quite a few steps to climb and therefore a reasonable level of fitness is required. The caves contain some lovely statues and paintings. Make sure you have plenty of water and watch out for the monkeys who will snatch anything. Well worth the visit.

We really loved our experience here. I would recommend 45 min- 1 hour to give you time to enjoy. There were 5 temples of varying sizes. I particularly enjoyed the buddhas lying on the side like in the first temple. It was all carved into a rock thousands of years ago. Our driver took us down a gravel road to a smaller entrance which made the walk shorter. We walked down to the golden Buddha afterward. Please be wary of the monkeys, as they eat the flowers you can buy for the shrines. One jumped up my husbands back to get the flower from my sons hand. All in all a great experience!
Check out all the caves around the temple. As this is free for tourist, it is a must visit for anyone who is in Dambulla. Other places such as Sigiriya can be a bit costly.
Do not miss this site. Beautiful Buddha statues and paintings inside the caves. Beware of the monkeys.
The temple was very educational for the children it teaches people to respect other religions especially buddhism.There are ancient paintings that are really cool!

Temples in the caves with over 150 Buddha sculptures. It's amazing and totally worth the visit. Can be challenging to go up, but though won't regret when you get there. Monkeys on the way up are a special attraction!!!

After a lot of stairs (quite a challenge again after climbing the lion rock a few hours before) you arrive at the dambulla rock cave. For us the visit didn't take that long, you enter each of the five caves, and that's it basically. The five caves are beautiful though. Especially the painted ceilings we thought were nice to see. Also, you could visit the caves for free, which is quite rare in Sri Lanka not having to pay for an attraction ;-)

The Dambulla cave temple is on a small hill top. The climb was little steep but it is a very serene experience once you reach the top. The caves will have various statues and paintings of Buddha. A lovely experience. Tip: Avoid visiting both the Cave temple and Sigiriya rock on the same day as both require steep climbing.
it was a different type of temple and it was my first hand experience visiting such a temple. found it different, unique and mesmerizing

Fascinating place. Where you have to go. We visited in December and liked the history and the nature they adopted! Even you don't see a monkey for 3 minutes, they are still watching you. Therefore be careful with food. My wife survived the attack easily, but she was shocked for a moment :-)

An awesome temple built right in the caves. There are 5 caves to see. Start at the 5th and work your way forward. You can leave your shoes at the bottom (you have to take them off at the top of the stairs anyway and a guy tries charging 25lkr to look after them - all the locals go barefoot)
We walked up to the Golden Cave Temple in the middle of monsoon rain.  It was worth the climb up slippery steps to see the amazing caves.

We visited fairly early, so not too busy. An amazing site with so many statues. Climb was a little steep in the heat but well worth it. For me this the highlight of an incredible trip around Sri Lanka

If you go after 1pm it's free. I'm hard to impress with tourist attractions, but these caves were actually really amazing. The art work and the Buddhas are beautiful! The only impressive site I have been to in Sri Lanka

The golden Buddha statue is huge and was built from Japanese donations in the 1990's. In front of the statue is also a huge golden Stupa.. I didn't visit the caves at the top and it was too hot and humid for me.

I still can't believe what a massive surprise this place was. It was seriously incredible. We were leaving Sigiriya that day and travelling to Kandy and stopped by on the way through. The restaurant at the bottom of the climb will hold your bags for you whilst you climb for 100 rupees. Take water for the climb - it's longer than you think! When we got to the top you have to pay a few rupees for the guys to look after you shoes (maybe like 40 rupees or something like that). It's free to get in. The views from the rock are incredible and when you get inside the temple wow just wow. The paintings on the inside of the caves are amazing. The best temple we went in on the whole of SL by miles (way better that the temple of the tooth in Kandy).
Beautiful place to visit for an hour or two, and free even for tourists! A great idea is to start in cave no 5 in the back and then visit them backwards and end in no 1 for an extra wow-effect

Sri Lanka's Largest Rock Cave Temple. No Entrance Fee. Approx 200-300 steps to climb up. Lots of monkeys on the way. 5 separate caves. After climbing up, you will have to take off your shoes before entering the caves. They do have shoe racks for LKR 25 to hold per pair. CARRY waterbottles. Caves are so beautiful and peaceful.
One of the best temples in Sri Lanka. The location is very scenic and gives you top mountain views. Worth visiting.

There were flights of steps as well as slopes to walk up to the caves. The walk can be a tough one on a hot day. Before entering the cave temple, we needed to remove our footwear. For those wearing socks, they would be able to walk more comfortably on the hot ground. There are 5 cave temples within the compound, all situated besides each other. It would be very useful and informative to have a guide with you as there was no information board in English in any of the caves.

We took a suicidal taxi cab day trip from Kandy and stopped in Dambulla after climbing Sigiriya in the morning.  The cab was about 7,500Rupee and took 2.5 hours.  When you walk into Dambulla, you're confronted by a huge gold Buddha built in the 90s, but don't worry about that.  Climb the steps up to the caves and you'll see Buddhas from 2,000 years previously, pretty amazing, apart from the hairaising cab up there...
Temples with scores of buddhist statues. The way the caves paintings have been preserved and looked after is commendable.

The entrance to the temple complex is dominated by an immense golden Buddha, built this century. It marks the start of the climb to the much more ancient temples up in the caves. The climb is not too taxing although, in places, the steps give way to worn bedrock which could be slippy, particularly if wet. If you're a bit of a fatty it will be more difficult. The temples in the caves house more tha 150 Buddha statutes in a number of separate chambers. Shoes have to be left at the entrance to the cave complex and in really sunny weather this could be a test for soft Western feet! The view from the top includes the distant Sigiriyah (Lion Rock) which is an altogether much sweatier climb. Both Unesco sites, however, must be included in any visit to this area.
Actually golden temple and cave temple are same. it is a good place to visit and for a change, no entry fee for foreign visitors which you will not find anywhere else in srilanka.

This place is very good as you can see lot of budha status. The side leaned big statutes of budha. Their are lot of stairs to climb but definitely  lesser than the lion rock. You may cover the whole temple with climbing in one hour.

The entrance is horrible looking !:D if you go way to the top its worth seeing. Better to check yourself info about temples and spare money on the guide. Entrance is free. Beware of some monkeys. You need also proper outfit and take off your shoes (you can hide them in your backpack and not pay)

If you stop in Dambulla (we stayed there two nights and went to Pidurangala and Sigiriya by bus) you have to see caves on the top of the hill. The way up is easy and there is a lot of monkeys on the way up. You can see this cave temples for free! Inside it's very peaceful.

I traveled here with my girlfriend, the temple is beautiful and very unique. I'm not particularly religious, but still enjoyed the amazing art work and building. It's a walk up to the top and we managed to see everything there in 20 mins so it's not a full day activity (unless your a Buddhist of course) When you enter the temple you have to take off your shoes so take a back pack you can put them into as there are so many monkeys! As with all tourist attractions in Sri Lanka you will find the sales men trying to shove hand made elephants and printed tshirts onto you, just make sure if you like the look of something you haggle right down to a price you think is fair and don't go a penny over. Saying your price and walking away works 95% of the time. I witnessed a guy pay 6500RS for a elephant, I got the same thing for 1500RS.
Offers an excellent view atop the hill.. some cimbing to do. Few temples with scores of Buddist statues of various sizes & forms.
Some uphill clibing to do. Temples with scores of buddhist statues. One of them a huge sleeping Buddha.
The golden caves are a place that must be visited. The way the caves n paintings have been preserved and looked after is commendable.

Don't be fooled by the large golden Buddha that adorns the roadside below the caves. Claims that it is the world's largest are nonsense , it isn't even the largest in Sri Lanka. However this should not detract from the cave temples themselves which are some 500 metres behind and high above. The climb up to them, either by steps (400 of them) or ramped stone pathway is perhaps physically challenging for some but well worth the effort. Packs of monkeys will entertain you, begging for titbits, as you make the climb.Once at the caves entrance you will have to leave your shoes at a kiosk for a fee of 25 rupees, and continue barefoot, a pair of socks is a good idea to protect against the hot stone walkways and cuts caused by grit. One can only marvel at the craftsman ship in creating the figures and ceiling frescoes, and no visit to this area is complete without visiting the cave temples

The climb up to the cave temples isn't as bad as we were expecting after reading other reviews. There is a few sets of stairs but nothing too taxing. There is even a second route up with minimal stairs but a slope instead for anyone who may struggle with stairs. When you get to the top to enter the temples shoulders and knees must be covered. We had to pay to leave our shoes outside but if you take these off before you begin to approach the temple you could put shoes in a backpack and save some rupees be careful because the ground can get hot!! The advice we were given was to do the 5 temples in reverse order as they grow in magnificence - we agree! Walk straight to the end and do the temple backwards. The temples themselves are beautiful inside if you are there in the height of the day no torch is really needed you can see the paintings on the walls. The best thing about this attraction is it is now free of charge, watch out for the monkeys. Follow our journey on Instagram @twolostllamas
The golden temple is very beautiful and it gives an insight into the religion tourism of sweet Sri Lanka
Great it was awesome and I'd recommend that you come to Sri Lanka as soon as you can to meet the hospitable people and taste the spicy foods
I was amazed by the beauty of this temple the paintings are most beautiful thank your for sure an amazing experience

This is something not to miss if you are right here at Dambulla. You will be amazed by the size and number of the Buddhas inside the caves. It's a bit hard to climb all the stars if you are not a sporty person but it's ok you can take your time. This temple is probably the first archeological site of the cultural triangle. It is a world heritage site Largely recommend this to anyone, its worth the experience. And it's absolutely free

The Dambulla cave Temple is truly an astounding place to visit. The pairings, the Buddha statues, the positive energy, the peoples faith...difficult to describe in words. Must visit to experience it personally.
Our guide took us around the cave temples and we were fascinated by the history of the kings. Definitely worth a climb.

There are 5 temples to visit. A delightful combination of simplicity with detail and technical skill. If the notion of 3000 years of Buddhist culture is not enough, you can reflect on the fact that people actually inhabited these caves before the arrival of Buddhism. You can wander quite freely from one to another, I have visited several times and have always been lucky not to find myself in a crowd. This is a quieter and more peaceful experience than some of the more famous sites, the caves are quite dark allowing you to soak up the atmosphere.

The Golden Temple is a must see, beautiful surroundings fronting the sacred lake, with a fascinating interior. We saw a stately elephant and other wildlife around the lake. We missed an evening visit due to heavy traffic between our hotel and the attraction, which we are told is quite magical, but managed a morning visit. Tourists don't get to see the sacred tooth though, which is well protected in the shrine within several ornate containers. Anyway this is a cultural 'must-see'

We had no intention of stopping here on our fully packed journey around Sri Lanka but your driver was nice enough to bring us on the way to Sigiriya and I'm so grateful! The climb to the temple is definitely challenging in the late morning heat so it is probably best to visit early in the morning before the sun's rays start to kick in. There's plenty of monkeys on the way up as well that are happy to pose for photos. The Golden Buddha is a stunning site and can even be seen during the climb up Sigiriya Rock and the surrounding area. The caves are beautifully painted and have lots for different points of interest and statues. Entry is also completely free!!! Very surprising for a country that seems to charge tourists for everything and our driver explained that the president removed the entry fee. Wish I could have spent some more time there to properly explore and should have included this in our travel plans.

travelled here with see lanka travel in early afternoon.  the climb up is quite hard lots of steps and uneven rock .  monkeys on the way up . lots of them , felt a little uneasy as so many came running down the steps towards us . at the top the cave temple is stunning .5 rooms all very different , ranging in age as well . some vendors on the way up and down but no is all you need to say , they dont persist . great views across to sigiriya way away in the distance . worth a visit

It's a nice place to visit. The paintings in the caves are very old, dating from 1st centrury BC. The monkeys are fun, you can easily take pictures of them. The view from the hill is not as stunning as they write so. Remember that the entrance to the Cave Temples is for free and do not get fooled!
impressive paints and bouddhas in 5 different caves monkeys everywhere several stairs to climb before visiting this temple , 20

The entrance to the temple is free and involves a 20 minute climb - and it isn't a steep climb either. The ancient statues and murals inside the caves are magnificent and provide a glimpse into Sri Lanka's history. Watching the procession of devotees and their rituals provides an insight into Sri Lanka's culture. A guide might be helpful to those looking for detailed explanations on each of the statues and murals. The view from the top is also stunning. End the descent by enjoying a refreshing King Coconut :-)

Went in early afternoon and the caves were almost deserted. The paintings on the cave ceiling are mesmerizing. Interesting how each design follows the twists and turns of the cave. Buddhas are well displayed in each cave.

We travelled on a  2  week round  trip to Srilanka november  2016. It was  arranged by a  national well-known swedish  travel  agency  called  Solresor. The  island is  as  green  as a  green  emerald. We  visited many  places in  the  Island among  other  places  was  this great  place which  is  full architechture ,history  and  culture to  see and  experience.It  was  really  amazing.

Climb to above is not quite an effort. You have to pay for the storage of your shoes (20 rupees) and there is no entrance fee. The restaurant below is for tourists but it's OK. And then there is the caves themselves, very impressive. Begin with the last cave and then count up to the first,  because this way you go from small to large.

I was here in the  morning, so the temperature was ok, not hot yet.  Walking towards the cave, you may see lots of monkeys, so be careful around them. Many vendors as well. The hike up to the cave will take you awhile if you make little pit stops, but I promise you, once you get there, you will like it. The cave with lots of Buddhas are very impressive and great. Monks were worshipping at that time, I wish the people (possibly tourists) would talk calmly and softly as there were many people worshipping. I think many people enjoyed the place and found it spiritual. I say, what you see inside the cave is very impressive so take as much pictures as you like as it is allowed.

It's a fairly strong walk up hill to the top but very worth it then. There is no entry fee for this you just donate. Also there are people who will take your shoes and you pay them too a little too 25 LKR per pair. Remember this is a site where you need to cover your legs and shoulders. Then the caves themselves are teeming with statues of Buddha. Hundreds of them in all sorts of sizes and poses. Ancient and in excellent condition. You don't have to be there long but it is a well worth it.

The experience of visiting here was really unexpected. The quantity and quality of the Buddha and other statues in the caves was quite stunning. The walk up is not too strenuous and unlike the UNESCO sites there is not an entry fee (only a donation is requested). Quite beautiful.
This is a must when in Sri Lanka. Very well organised and our guide was awesome.  The vendors can be a pain but just say no. It's a good walk.

If you see only one buddhist cave temple in Sri Lanka, let this be the one. Only for fit people (there's more than 400 steps to climb), but the it's worth the trouble! Since spring 2016 the entrance to the temple is free.

Very conveniently located on the roadside near Sigiriya. Upon entrance there is a museum well decorated with a huge golden Buddha idol and concrete-made lotus petals. The building itself is very eye-catching! There is a stairway on the left leading up to the cave temple. A short hike of 15 minutes takes you to a spot from where the splendid view of entire Dambulla will mesmerise you. Even the Lion's rock of Sigiriya is clearly visible. The temple complex is well preserved in its antique form. The four caves house more than 100 Buddha figures in different postures. The frescoes painted on the ceiling and walls echo the glory of the ancient art and culture.

It was a bit of a climb to get there but well worth the effort. Lots of Buddah's in the buildings of the monastery. Quite cool inside but lovely views across to Sigiriya. Worth spending time wandering around the site.

This is a great place to go when you are touring around Sri Lanka. Make sure you bring socks because you have to take your shoes off! Also, go in the morning, walking up steep steps in the afternoon is NOT funny! Great place to go

While it is on the tourist "must see" route, I thought the site was a little jaded and perhaps a little worn around the edges.  A bit difficult to figure out the significance of each group of statues too as there is very little information at the site.
good cave temples with lot of buddha sculptures. there are around 5-6 caves and its pretty worth visiting. but it requires little climb of the mountain.
If you are a tourist this is a must see place as it has a great sri lankan culture and the religion mixed up in here.

Buddhism really fascinated me. More than I imagined it would. I love how genuine all Buddhists I have met actually seem. They all seem to care for others and don't force their religion upon you. It was amazing to see the caves and I found it so moving that we are aloud to see this even though me and my partner aren't Buddhists ourselves. I think we under estimate how special it is for them to allow us to see this. It was fantastic. Our guide was very sweet and you could tell how much love he had for Buddha. It's amazing to find out the stories behind each different Buddha statue. I can't give too much away but it's a beautiful place to see and you'd definitely be a fool to visit Sri Lanka and miss this out. It can be a long drive to get there but it's so worth it for what you see. Beware of the monkeys outside the temple though haha! I had one climb on my head!

by far the biggest temple that we saw duringour travels of Sri lanka and boy were we glad to have got to see this. The Temple is huge, gold and and stands out for miles. do not miss out and once done take a long walk up to the cave where you will get to see quite a few cheeky and some cute baby monkeys!

certainly a long walk to get to this place but well worth the trip, at least the room is very cool in the shade and away from the basking sun. a guide took us around the cave and everything here is enriched with a great story. amazing to think how all the statues got here considering the height that we were at.

Me and my wife came here on our way back from Sigiriya to get a bus back to Kandy. We wished we had more time to spend here as we only had about an hour. We were surprised as it was free. Such a rarity, comparing with other massively overpriced Sri Lankan attractions. The cave is in a beautiful area and you will see stunning views from the top. The temple it self is small, but you can take a lot of time admiring the statues. There will be a person who can rent you a towel to cover your knees if you are wearing shorts. He will ask for 200-300 rupees. He is just ripping you off. Do not give him more than a 100!

We found this temple particularly moving.  It has an ancient and profound beauty ... and we arrived just after lunch, before the tour busses, so had the site all to ourselves for awhile.  Quite magical.  And the resident monkeys offer great photo ops!

Must see if you are visiting Dambulla area! A 20 minute walk up hill, steps and natural rocky path, you will get to the top of the hill where the Golden Cave Temple sits. There are 5 caves, filled with beautiful ceiling art/painting, statues and artefacts. The walk up and down can be slightly tiring but the views and surrounding nature make it well worth it, plenty of small monkeys running around and some come quite close. A few locals waiting on the paths with 'memorabilia' and various souvenirs or fruit, I wouldn't bother buying as they charge a lot more than the local shops in the towns.

Went twice - AM and PM amazing view both time, though in evening the lighting effects make this place more serene and dramatic! Remember you can wear your shoe all the way to to the top. It is 15- 20 minutes hike up. Bus stops outside! This can be a day trip from Kandy very easily. If you plan to stay in Dambula ( Good option for cultural triangle) plenty of options walking distance from here- home stays are cheap and awesome! If you wish to go to  Sigiriya or  Anuradhapura or Polonnaruwa just take 10 LKR bus ride to Dambula main bus stand ( 10 minutes) and all these buses will be available! Going to main bus stand will give you plenty of options for onward travels! Tuk Tuk is pricey. Sigriya is 30-45 mins bus ride while Polonnaruwa  1 hr 15 Mins or so.
My favorite Sri Lankan site, rich in antiquity and Buddhist lore.  There is a manageable uphill walk to the entrance of the 5 caves.  Well worth the visit - leave  plenty of time to wander.

While returning from Sigriya Lion Rock and Minneriya National Park, we stopped by this Golden (Buddha) Temple in Dambulla. It was around 7:30 when we reached there. Everyone was tired enough of climbing lion rock and safari activity, so couldn’t step inside the temple, so we just witnessed the entrance only and left for Kandy. But now after returning I regret that I should have seen it from inside and visited the nearby Dambulla Cave Temple also. So, I must say never leave anything behind but your footsteps.

A fascinating visit to the Golden Rock Temples in Dambulla, we arrived late in the day to see these fantastic rock temples which were started in the 1st century B.C. These temples laid untouched for century's as the jungle and vegetation took over until a senior British General decided to absail up the rock only to unearth these hidden caves full of such important historical carvings and writing. It's difficult to believe that these Buddhas were hand carved and painted from the 1st century B.C. A truely must see stop off on the rich cultural trail.
A beautiful serene place.   The caves have so much history and art to offer.   Make a day of it and enjoy the sights.

We thought being a cave temple we would head down but be warned there are quite a few steps to get to this temple. Once you do reach it, however, it is fascinating and well worth the climb. Again make sure you are dressed appropriately, trousers recommended for men and women need to cover up also. Great to see the views from so high up and all the monkeys that cover the steps on the lead up. Once inside the caves (4 in total) you'll see lots of different buddhas and can learn all about the history (with a guide).

It is the size of structure that is intimidating and awe inspiring.The serenity around the place is very peace giving. Must see. Should you feel the urge to answer nature's call, you could use the toilet, rightfully tucked away in a corner,for LKR 100 per person.

You need to walk up approximately 400 steps to reach the cave temple complex. The climb is not too difficult since you can take breaks along the way. There are several temples to see with Buddha statues and paintings. It is a very popular destination for tourists and Buddhist devotees

After looking at the reviews and photos, I guess I was expecting more. Felt it was a let down. Thank God they removed the requirement of entry ticket. Also it's Definitely not for older people who are not physically fit.
Entire site and sculptures carved out of mountain side It is like being in an incredible museum But you can touch the 1500 year old statues Definitely a must see

Dambulla Cave Temple A very popular place of visit with tourists & locals all alike, this temple was donated by King Walagambahu in the 1st century BC to Buddhist monks. Dambulla is also a World Heritage site and has one of the most impressive of Sri Lanka’s cave temples. Once you arrive at the temple site, you'd need to climb up - approximately for an hour or so (the last bit of the steps are quite narrow) where you'd reach a complex of five caves with over 2000 sq. meters of painted walls - with the  ceiling being one of the largest area of paintings found in the world. These caves also contain over 150 images of the Buddha, of which the largest is the colossal figure of the Buddha carved out of rock spanning 14 meters. Outside the temple grounds you'd find a small pond with lotus growing in it, and the views are quite spectacular around the mountain of which the temple is based.
