If you have to select one of the many Buddhist heritage temples in Sri Lanka, this could be one of them. It has all the elements of a temple excursion. A steep walk, beautiful large sized statues, and lovely wall paintings and frescoes. This one has a good view on the top as well.

Beautiful temple on the top of the hill . One can get a great view of the city below but be prepared for a bit of a climb. Interesting insights about the Buddhist culture after visiting the temple. Recommended for all travellers.

A must see in Dambulla. Huge statues cut from stone in several caves are really impressive. Prepare to conquer a lot of steps to reach the caves, but it definitely worth your efforts. While climbing you may meet monkeys which seem to be indefinite to visitors so you're free to take funny pictures of them. Better visit 1.5 hour before sunset and you'll get a unique opportunity to watch the sun going down while the wind is blowing your hair at the top of the hill...
Perhaps a stay over here is not needed, but the caves and golden temple are worth a visit. Just don't climb it in the rain like we did.
This was very impressive to me--it's amazing how all of these caves were preserved through time.  It is a very spiritual visit.
Looks like there are two Rock Cave temple listings here.  Already put in a review on the other listing, so at least I'll get credit for this an also uploaded a picture.  Have a nice day.

There are special requirements when visiting a Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka, which is that your knees are covered and you take your shoes off.  So you either wear long pants/skirt or if wearing shorter shorts you wear a Sarong. As I was wearing cargo shorts, the first guard at the complex let me in as my shorts were right at the knee line.  So up we hike up to the main entrance to the mystical caves where the second guard stopped me and said I could not go in because my shorts showed 1/2 of my knees.  But  I'd already paid someone to watch my shoes!  Yep, lack of communication is everywhere.  As my tour guard returned looking for me, I told him no Sarong, no entry.  So he leaves and just happened to know someone who had a spare Sarong.  Amazing.  It was the prettiest pink with blue flowers you have ever seen.  So what the diddle, I put it on and went in.  To me I looked utterly ridiculous in this spiritual place, but at least my knees were not showing. The caves are quite amazing.  I had done some reading prior to the trip but never knew it was would be this mysterious. Truly one of the cultural highlights of the trip. So here is what you need to know when in Sri Lanka.  Buy a Sarong and keep it handy if you are wearing shorts.  Know that you will have to take your shoes off and there is a charge for someone to watch them at every temple.  Be flexible.  You will get wrong advise and instruction all the time.

A short trek up to the temple , first stretch is steep & a bit tiring , but it was all worth it, there is a hindu temple & then followed by a series of caves with Buddha s statues in meditation , preaching & sleeping position.
This was so like stepping back in time!  I don't know how this was completed by man and so many years ago.  Very colorful
This was amazing walking through these temples and seeing how perfect and complete they are and oh so colorful.  Hard to imagine walking in here and visioning the people building this
Easily accessible... very near to Dambulla town... lots to see.. if you are a Buddhist this is a must visit place.. Panoramic view from the top...

After big golden buda at the entrance ( very impresive ) we had to climb quite some stairs and hill. From outside the view is nice but nothing impresive. When you step into the cave surprise awaits you. So many statues ( pure art ). So peaceful and magnificent. Not to miss.
Well worth the walk up the very steep hill! You enter all 5 and are blown away by art and sculptures
It was worth a revisit especially with our friends who were visiting Sri Lanka for the first time.  It was a very special experience for them.  We were happy to share this experience with them.
Highly recommended to visit here to experience the history of Sri Lanka. You will experience the Buddhist culture.
Dambulla Raja Maha viharaya or the golden temple is one location must see if you are passing by here. You will learn a lot about Sri Lankan history and the art and craft of good old days.
to see the Buddha's  untouched craved in the cave after so many years was breathtaking. I advise you to have a pair of shocks with you incase you don't want your foot burned from the pavement
It is a bit of a trek to the top but there is monkeys the whole way up to see. The temples are beautiful and worth the climb. In incredible condition and really interesting to visit.
Interesting temple on top of a hill. So many idols of Buddha in the caves. Worth the climb up the hill.

It is a nice historic monument. It is short climb up a hill  (fleet of steps). It is not a too tiring climb. Once up there, you have a series caves with so many buddha statues. So many idols in different postures. Amazing to hear that these several hundred centuries old.

having visited temples in Thailand and China before this is a fairly un inspiring temple. Probably reflective of the local economy. more than 600 steps to climb to enter the temple whihc are fairly strenuous
having visited temples in China and Thailand previously this temple is somewhat dissapointing. very steep climb to the top to see the golden cave (600 plus steps)
We made a route deviation from Kandy to Colombo to visit Dambula and Sigiriya. Cave temple is a site one must visit to see an ancient statue of Budha carved from a rock over 2000 years ago.
Spectacular roof frescoes, in mostly good condition, despite or maybe because of the humidity.  Caves can be crowded.

Dambulla cave temple also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site and a truly magical place to visit. Don't let the gaudy entrance down below fool you - up the stairs the experience is very different. It is beautiful and calming. The Buddhas and wall art are amazing. Wear shoes you can slip in and out of easily. There are some nasty monkeys on the stairs going up and down so beware of your things. Allow a good 2 hours.

It's quite a trek to the top but once there the views are fantastic. It just gets better when you enter the caves. The statues are breath taking and paintings on the ceilings are beautiful and definitely something not to be missed. I would absolutely recommend seeing this and you will not be disappointed.

Early start or late afternoon is best to visit as it is a long walk up to the caves and mid day heat would make it an arduous climb.  5 caves at the top and each with Buddha's and ancient drawings.  Good view from the top.

After climbing Lion Rock, this ascent to the caves was an easy trek. The macaque monkeys along the way made it an entertaining climb too! They are like the "pesky squirrels" where I live. The caves are awesome and so hard to describe. Pictures don't give you the feel either. This is truly a must visit! The artistic work in these caves must be appreciated. Remember to bring your water and hat and apply your sunscreen.
Good place to visit.. caves were more or less maintained..  but beware of the monkeys..they can snatch away your belongings..
A bit of a hike up the stairs to the top of the hill but well worth the trip. Beautiful temples and gorgeous Buddhas- a totally cool place to visit.

In Temple of Rock, also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, founded in the first century by King Valagamba as a sign of gratitude to the monks for having defended by his enemies during his exile. In the natural caves are five sanctuaries with numerous Buddha images in various sizes and poses. Frescoes in the natural caves, statues and bas-reliefs, Buddha carved in the rock, definitely an attraction to see. And don't forget the monkeys that live in the temple.
Very nice temple. Beautiful paintings, great Budha statues. No entrance fees ! Only 25 rupees for storing shoes. Many monkeys, but they are friendly, no problems with them.

This is an amazing temple constructed within a series of caves.  The art work inside is incredible, with every wall and ceiling covered with images of Buddha and so many statues and stupas to look at.  The tree outside of the temple is apparently a sapling from the Bodhi tree. Take water and wear appropriate clothing. Definately worth a visit.
Stunning views all around Dambulla area. Go in the morning or in the afternoon. Mid day would be hot
Bit of climbing, but fully worth it. It's amazing to see what ancient kings has done in Sri Lanka. Must see this place if you visit Dambulla, Sri Lanka
This is seriously worth going to see, the caves are so spectacular. We went in off season so didn't have to pay entry. Would thoroughly recommend, and it's an easy 2.5 h bus from Kandy.

We visited these caves on a day trip from Kandy. The golden Buddha out front is possibly the most impressive thing there. The walk up the mountain isn't too strenuous but you'll probably get very sweaty. You can see Sigirya from the top. Take something to cover your legs and shoulders. It is described as 5 temples/caves. Its more like 5 alcoves full of various types of Buddha statues. If you want to take pictures bring a camera with good flash. And the ground will be very hot! You can't wear shoes but you can wear socks. Go on a Sunday. Its free! Otherwise it's 1500 rupees (I think) Definitely worth it on a Sunday, not so sure otherwise.
Great temple and there is no admission fee now. The museum, where you have to pya, is not worth it imo

We visited on a Sunday and it was free for us to get in (I dont know if that was due to the day but it was good for us being on a budget!). The normal price is 1500lkr each but I dont know if its worth that price. It takes about half an hour to walk up the steps to the cave temple, and it is a nice walk where you can see monkeys and nice views of Dambulla and the surrounding mountains. The caves are pretty awesome and full of different buddhas. We spent about maybe half an hour in the caves and another 20 mins walking down. Theres also a musem at the bottom for 200lkrs each and a huge gold buddha statue. Would recommend if you have the time but try to get there on a Sunday so you don't have to pay!!
Each of the caves has a unique atmosphere. The stories of the Buddha are beautifully painted. it will stay in my memory for a long time.

Surprisingly this attractions wasn't included in our organised tour of Sri Lanka, so we got a taxi and visited it ourselves. Amazing, stunning, huge Buddha statue sits above the Golden Temple, with a dragons mouth forming the entrance. The entrance to the caves is to the left-hand side, weirdly uphill. Bit of a steep walk, but take it slowly and it's worth it. Several hawkers along with way, but all friendly and actually sell some good souvenirs at cheap prices. Leave shoes at the entrance and pay 25 LKR on your return. Wearing socks is useful as the stones are very hot. 5 caves with amazing Buddah statues of various sizes. Very colourful. Caves shut for 15 minutes at prayer times.  Notices indicated no photography, but everybody was taking photos and guides didn't stop them. Don't sit on the benches though!

The walk uphill is reasonably strenuous especially in the banking sun,  but it is really worth it. The artwork and statues are around 1000 years old and are very well preserved. The Buddha statues are fascinating and you can photograph them easily. A guide is not necessary as information is available. The view from the top is lovely. A definite highlight on the cultural circuit.

The golden Buddha in front of the entrance is impressive and then there is a steady climb up to the caves.Each one is full of statues and paintings asking to be photographed. Don't forget knee and shoulder coverings for the ladies, the entrancew guards can be quite strict about this.

There is no entry fee for all people. The temple has its heritage and rich culture displayed in the form of cave temple. There are series of three such cave temples inside if you count distinctly. Great exercise and a treat for your eyes!

The Golden temple is located on top of the hill. So there is a bit of climbing and there are no options like cable car or trolley car for aged/specially able people. The temple is huge and again a lot of walking inside with steps! The entire cave temple is full of statues of Buddhism. Without the knowledge of the thirthankaras (as called in India) it is impossible to understand why there are so many statues and what they mean. But I truly enjoyed the uphill climb and the entire temple.

We stayed for 2 nights in Dambulla and we visited The Golden Temple in Danbulla. It is impressive with big buda statues and cave drawings. Cave is on top of the hill with beautiful view (much better than on Lion Rock in Sygiria).

The first thing you see is a giant statue of a golden Buddha which is very beautiful, you can visit the museum of Buddhism or to take a hike to the actual cave temple. The hike is not the easiest one (a lot of steps to the top) but not the longest. I recommend to go in the morning/evening, avoid the mid day heat. The cave temple is very pretty, peaceful, worth the hike for sure! and the view is stunning and impressive.
Great piece of architecture, beautiful frescoes which have survived through ages , you will be amazed how such beautiful architecture was possible with no scientific development or modern tools

It is a steep walk up to the caves. Left our shoes at entrance for 25rupees. Didn't need socks as the 5 caves are close to each other and connected by a covered walk way. Many Buddhas in each cave & the caves ceilings were covered in lots of frescoes painted at different times. Didn't take a guide - just used our guide book. A monk was on hand to offer blessings which was a lovely touch. We did this site after Sigiriya Rock.

Humbling experience visiting this marvel of a place on top of a hill. The painting on the ceiling are still very much intact while the buddha images are still in shape. All buddhas inside show the seven positions. Important to leave shoes so you either have to be barefoot or wear socks inside the caves.
This is a must to visit for Art and Culture lovers! Beware of the tuktuk drivers down the road.
we went to this temple during our holiday in sri lanka. we loved the place, its free of charge . better to climb in early morning or afternoon around 16.00. recommand

The Rock Cave Temples in Dambulla were a highlight for me.    They are well maintained and the colors throughout the caves are amazing.    So many beautiful large Buddhas and wonderfully painted ceilings. The monkeys around the Temple are so timid and the views over the countryside excellent.
Quite a tough climb up the stairs with a toddler in the heat, but by no means impossible! There are stunning views at the top and my son was thrilled to bits to see the monkeys wandering around.

We went here as part of an oranised private tour. Stunning views inside and out, a really peaceful and beautiful experience. We had a buddist blessing at one of the temples thanks to our guide who was so knowledgeable about this venue. It is slippy on the rocks in the wet and you arerequired to remove shoes.

The Dambulla Cave Temples are beautifully maintained, with hand painted rock ceilings and original gods, goddesses and statues in every corner. There are tour guides that can speak just about any Language to help you along the way, expressing the meaning of the caves and its surroundings. The only slight issue we had was the lighting kept going out leaving us in the dark... but it's a ancient cave what more could we expect. However it's natural beauty lit up by sun light though the small doors was a beauty of its own. - Photos are my own.

Dambulla Cave Temple is one of my favorite place in Sri Lanka. You have to climb the rock, so it is advisable to visit morning or evening. Love to see sunset. There are so many monkeys and some little wild animals like rabbits you can find there. Nice Place after all.

This was surprisingly good, excellent in fact. I was trying to compare them to the dunhuang caves in Xinjiang...... Sadly my memory of the  latter date back to the 80s so I'm happy to stand corrected. These are pristine, and I was stunned by the intricate ceiling designs and paint. It's quite possible these R just younger and/ or have been refurbished. I found particularly striking the painted feet of the reclining Buddha in the first cave, really beautiful. There are about 4 or 5 caves, unfortunately it was prayer time?? And they were being locked up so our time was fleeting. Overall, I think these are a real standout compared with some of the other Buddha sites we've visited and some of those were spectacular. Lastly, they are free - a nice change from the  standard 25-30 bucks most sites in SL slug tourists.
Fascinating UNESCO heritage site with a rich history, incredible statues and frescos related to Gautama Buddha

We stayed for 2 nights in Dambulla and we visited The Golden Temple in Danbulla. It is impressive with big buda statues and cave drawings. Cave is on top of the hill with beautiful view (much better than on Lion Rock in Sygiria).
great plae, nice  paintings   . My travel  agency took me  there  and was a gret idea, after a 10 minutes  lk,  very hard,   but it is great to see the  caves and the  buddhas

The travel agency  insisted I should go, I did not want to  go that far, so thy at exotic travel, insisted, my tour guide  was  great  and  we walked like 10 minutes high  steps, but it  was  worthy,  magical   temple  over the rock, in the bottom  you have  food, bathrooms, then a  big  golden buddha, and  then  the  steps to the rock you will  find  a magical  place
It's nice BIG Budda statue. Famous place for Buddhist..It's nice temple and. You have a good museum ..

The golden large Buddha on the temple grounds is impressive!  Many people buy flowers as an offering but beware, there are monkeys that will aggressively pursue you!  It's a steep climb to the caves so be prepared for the steep steps and uneven paving.  There is also no railings for those that struggle with steps or have other disabilities.  The caves and statues are very impressive and not to be missed!  It is one of the highlights you will always remember.

Approximately 2 to 3 hours  distance from Kandy. With amazing cave paintings and over 100 Buddha statues dating back to the B.C. period, this is a must see, but the climb up to temples in the heat is draining.. No singles tops  and long pants are needed out of respect for the religion.

I had no idea what to expect as I had not seen any images of the temple before visiting. The experience was breathtaking and, this was not just because of the required rock climb to reach the temple entrance. The way that the temple has been incorporated into the rock and its crevices enhances the sacred nature of the site. For those who may have little interest in religious landmarks, you may still be impressed by the artistic achievements of the range of Buddha statues & fresco paintings. I have seen a number of temples throughout Asia but, this one holds a special reverence for me. A delightful surprise! Though I do not suggest that the site is age restrictive, a steep climb up the rock via carved steps is required so, this may exclude access for some less able bodied individuals.

Dambulla cave temples are an unexpected treat. The gift that keeps giving. There are five caves in this temple complex,two smallish and three quite large. The guide books give no idea of the scale. The caves have intricate delicate paintings and many many Buddha sculptures . Beautiful reclining Buddha in one cave and scores of life size and larger than life size statues in others. Take some lotus blossoms , there is bound to be images that speak to you, leave them an offering in homage to the exquisite beauty. On a more mundane note, the monkeys on the walk up are very photogenic, the museum is very ordinary.
The walk up to this was not too steep and was well worth the climb.  The art work was amazing and was one of our favourite places, truly amazing.

Royal Rock Temple is an iconic structure projectly rightly in most of the travel and cultural publications from Sri Lanka.The complex dated as early as 1st century BC consist of five separate caves with more than 150 beautiful and stunning images of Buddha. There is an entrance ticket and most ideal time to visit is few hours before Sunset.The climb is bit steep but there are ramp type path to reduce strain while climbing.Each cave consist of images of Buddha including 15 metre long reclining Buddha in first cave, longest second cave with Buddha under Makara Thorana, some Hindu deities and various colourful images.This is a living Holy place and it is advised to wear proper clothes particularly not exposing above the knees and sholders. It's better to wear a hat and also carry a water bottle. At the entrance there is a modern Golden Temple built with donations from Japanese and if time permit one can visit the same. On a clear day, Sigiriya is visible from distance. The enchanting view of Sunset is not to be missed and fortunately the crowds also disappear by that time.It's breathtaking and remarkable experience not to be missed.
all the temples are close together,no entry fee, very beautiful carvings and paintings. Well preserved only a short walk up

Dambulla Raja Maha Viharaya is one of the largest cave temples you can find in Sri Lanka. You should climb the mount (yes, it has many steps and the walk is really nice experience) which will take around 30 minutes. On the top of the mountain you can find 5 caves under a vast overhanging rock. The great people who built this temple had carved with a drip line to keep the interiors dry in rain season. There are 5 caves, 2 big caves and 3 small caves all are filled with nice Sinhalese paintings and Buddha statues. All together there are more than 50 Buddha statues including 14 meter statue. Also there are some statues of Sinhala gods and Kings. The most important thing of this temple to watch out for is its paintings. All 5 caves are filled with various paintings of Lord Buddha. You can find many traditional Sinhala texture patterns, flower patterns and hundreds of thousands of Buddha paintings. Every inch of the ceiling is covered with paintings and that is amazing. According to the historians, those paintings were completed during 3 eras of Sri Lankan history. The temple was built in 1st century by King Valagamba, then some statues and paintings done by King Nissanka Malla in 12th Century and finally some more paintings and modifications done by King Kirthi Sri Rajasinghe in 16th Century. The paintings are still in really good colors and condition. Hence this is a religious place, you should worn a suitable garments when u visit it. This place is a huge tourist attraction and you can find many local and foreign tourists almost in everyday. If you need to pay more hours with the paintings, its really good to avoid weekends. The parking area is huge. The newly build Rangiri Dambulla Viharaya is also there and there is a huge gold plated statue of Lord Buddha (which they claimed the largest sitting statue of the world). There is a museum too, but you have to buy tickets to watch it. We didn't go there. If you need to find some coolest Sinhelese paintings, Dambulla Raja Maha Viharaya AKA The Golden Temple is the ideal place to visit.

After a very short steep climb be prepared to be transported back in time to magical caves with Buddhas, honey paintings on the walls and lots and lots of history. Please observe the different positions of the Buddhas in the caves, they all mean something else.

Cave temple on top of the mountain. Amazing view and statues. Must listen to guides in the temple to understand the values of the place and statues. Beware of chip monkeys  on your way up the mountain as they can take your belongings and runaway. But they are so sweet creatures can fall in love for their behaviour.

After visiting a lot of different tempels in Sri Lanka we think this is a totaly different experience! There are five different caves you can visit, they are all different and nice to see! We arrived at the temple at praying times and than they close the caves for 15 minutes. When they opened the caves again it was a bit busy at the entrance of the caves but we really enjoyed seeing it. After the caves we visitef the museum, this was a bit disapointing and we would not recommend it!
Cave after cave of huge statues. 3 large rooms across a range of centuries and all containing very impressive statues.

Well, you start with a nice walk up the mountain. We spotted the lion rock on top of the mountain. The temple itself is just amazing. Try to avoid peak hours so you can take your time and wander in this place on your own tempo

It's a heavy climb but the caves a special. Lots of buddha's and paintings. It's unique Make sure your knees and arms are covered. On top you can rent a sarong for 100 rupees. You also need to pay 25 rupees for storing your shoes

My wife and I climbed up one afternoon. A bit of a hike and a bit hot, but well worth it! The caves and statues are very impressive We recommend a guide. On the way up I bought some flowers as an offering. If you do that be wary!  The red faced monkeys will aggressively pursue you. Hold your ground! Recommended
We loved this, after the golden tooth temple we had been to previously this is just as good and different. We enjoyed this visit and would highly recommend,
Superb place to be. Visit this place after sunset and you will feel the serenity. The large statues of Buddha and the monks - its a different experience
Such a lovely and peaceful place to visit.. very clean and well organised. This place is pious and makes you calm. Must visit

The Golden Cave Temple complex consists of 5 caves, each with Buddha statues in varying states of either lying down, sitting or standing up. The detail of carving is quite impressive, as are the wall and ceiling paintings (frescos). There are superb views of the surrounding countryside from the top, and on a clear day you can see for miles in the distance. However the climb is a strenous one, but should be alright if you pace yourself accordingly. There was no charge for entrance to the caves at the time of our visit (August 2016), however do confirm before going as the ticketing policies keep changing.
A really nice place to visit, the statues are very well preserved. And the view is good from the top. The entrance is also free :) and you get a bit of exercise to get there (bonus).

Visited the Golden Temple of Dambulla and loved every minute. The facade is fantastic with its giant Buddha over looking the main square. The cave temple is at the top of a steep hill but the peace and tranquility of the complex is well worth the climb.
its a bit of a hike up, but the temples at the top are worth it! beautiful statues and nice view at the top! Mind the monkeys :P and make sure to have clothes with you to cover up before you enter

This is a really Nice tempel with great views along the climb. I was expecting a tough climb, butbto be honest, it wasn't that hard! (Please take your time to have a look at the beautiful wallpaintings! ) Maybe because i went around 4pm, iT wasn't that hot anymore and around 6pm there was a beautiful sunset!

After a short drive from our hotel,we arrived at the Golden Temple,very impressive and our guide had great knowledge of which parts to visit and explained everything to us. Was very hot and there was lots of pilgrims there visiting. The climb is quite a long way up and in some parts quite steep,so elderly and disabled people will struggle,even some locals struggled up there. But once up the top and visit the caves it was fantastic. Beware that you have to respect the custom of removing your shoes which is uncomfortable and walking up it the heat is tiring. Dont go near the hundreds of monkeys up there and dont buy any food as they will ponce on you. Very impressive Buddha statues and they are a fantastic photo shoot,but you cannot take a picture of your partner or friends with a statue in the background as a no no. Steep walk back down
Good Place, prepare yourself for Climbing 500 Steps..!! take the slop instead of the Steps.. you wont feel the tiredness..

There is an approx 15 mins climb up the stairs. The climb is tough but worth it. You have to take off ur shoes before entering into the temple. There is no entrance fee, but we did pay 100 rs to use the toilet.
Golden Caves of Dambulla - Very Interesting Cave Temple complex steeped in history

Visited this historic attraction 10 am approx beating the majority of the crowds that came later in the coach loads. Steep climb with both steps and flagstones to negotiate.  Give yourself plenty of time to navigate the steps and stones in both directions.  On a hot day which this was on September 12th take plenty of water as this climb is taxing on the legs and knees.  Thoroughly enjoyed our visit and would recommend this trip to anybody who wishes to see 2000 years of history. At 54 and reasonably fit I thought this would be an easy ascent!!  My legs ached after this visit.

The Golden Temple, will be on your way to Sigiriya the Lion Rock. We have visited on the way back from there. After climbing all the steps in Sigiriya, here was another tough task. You have to go all the way up to see the Buddha statue. There was a small Hindu section as well. There is few rooms and each room got number of Buddha statue except for the first one it contains the sleeping Budhha. If you have visited the same in South East Asia then this place will be normal to you.

The Dambulla cave temples are located up a hill (approximately 10 minutes walk on steps and uneven ground) .. Some trees give little shade during the midday hours .. The cave temples are fabulous, the paintings still very well visible and kept, the Buddha statues stunning ! An absolute must while being near .. No entry charges!

going up to this temple is basically a hiking journey, you should be fit, dont carry anything with you, you need to take off your shoes once your at the temple, so its better if you have socks on or just take a pair with you... its nice to see.. free entry..
Great to see the golden stupa and giant golden Buddha, and get some photos, but not much more to it. We weren't really interested in the museum!

One get to see age old caves and the amazing paintings done on the walls along with various Buddhha Statues. The climb up there is quite a task but that's worth it. Also, it's free now. HIRE A GUIDE for better understanding of the place and related history.
One get to see age old caves and the amazing paintings done on the walls along with various Buddhha Statues. The climb up there is quite a task but that's worth it. Also, it's free now.

A quick walk up around 100 steps surrounded by monkeys and dogs looking for shade and you approach the caves. The caves themselves are amazing and the detail on the statues is something else. There is a big monstrosity of a gold Buddha below the caves with toilets next to it. A few Tips: Men and women need to cover their shoulder and knees before entering any of the caves. The caves are free but you need to take your shoes off before entering, there is a man who will mind your shoes for 25 rupees (around 10 pence). It is extremely disrespectful to turn your back on the statues so no selfies with the statues in the background.
Well worth a visit. A bit of a climb but truly beautiful. An amazing Temple with amazing pre Christ art.

The 5 caves hold some of the finest work seen in South Asia - from frescoes to statues. The fairly robust climb to the temple is best done in the morning or evening when the sun is not beating down and the stones at the temple are not too hot for the bare feet. Once in the caves, you'll be in for a special treat : each cave has its own unique feel - nothing is repeated. The cave temple is a must-do for any traveler to Sri Lanka.

We didn't know quite what to expect. From the road, you see a massive Buddha set against a hill above a monstrosity of a building that houses a museum on Buddhism and other structures, including some form of radio station. Knowing it was the Golden Temple, we found our way to the stairs. This is one of the sites where the main attraction is free of charge for non-Sri Lankans. The hike up is hard going, especially in the middle of the day. However, even people of poor fitness should be able to do it at a gradual pace. The highlight is at the top of the hill where a series of caves hidden behind a monastery-like building houses many impressive Buddha statutes and painted walls and ceilings. Take your time through here, although there is very little in the way of notes for visitors on what the images represent in the caves.
The caves are almost the only thing to visit in Dambulla, buy they're really impressive and beautiful. I expected they would be bigger, but you can visit them in less than a couple hours

Amazed to see how ancient Buddhist monks wrote the Thipitaka in the olden style. The Buddha statue in the top of the mountain is about one km away from the main temple. I thought the vehicle park needed tar matting to avoid dust.
Rather pleasant 10 min hike up to the temple. Excellent views above the surrounding area and lakes. The buddha statues and caves are definitely worth visiting. Big plus: it's free to enter the temple
Beautiful temple at top of a mountain/rock. Lots of tourists, not very peaceful place to go. Breathtaking views, highly recommend to visit.
Steep uneven climb to the top but well worth a visit. Great views and interesting temples. Would suggest visiting early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat!

A really historical place to visit so much history and beautiful Buddha's to look at we had a guide to show us around and explain the history it was extremely fascinating. We were a couple with a 10 year old son we all really enjoyed visiting
A wonderful temple to visit with so much history and beauty to look at. The whole place had a very calming feel to it a very special to visit. A bit of a walk up but fantastic

Just spell bounding and you will keep wondering who must have created these pieces of genius. Masterclass in all terms. A cave carved out of a giant rock and those marvelous statues in different postures carrying so many secrets over the centuries. Must must see place when you in Dambulla or Sri Lanka. Memories and experience of lifetime.
Five cave temples built into an overhang on a large gneiss monolith. The walk from the base of the hill to the caves is a little strenuous in the heat of mid day so better done early.

Our driver suggested we popped in on the way back to the airport from Sigiriya and thank goodness he did These cave temples are amazing - and free! Try to go with a guide as lots to point out in the cave temples Clean cafe and washrooms at adjacent Buddhist TV station

There is no entrance fee anymore but the money for the shoekeepers :) The caves are interesting but not exciting. Do not vist the buddhist museum downhill. We try to see all museam on our trips but this is kind of funny. It is not worth it at all. It's not the money but the time you should save.
The climb is steep but my 5 year old son climbed with us. The best time to visit is by 8.30AM and on the return journey pop into the museum.
Definitely worth a visit. The place is beautiful and peaceful. There are some steps to reach it so be prepared for the initial exercise but worth it.
I took advantage of one of the local guides who went into great detail of mans history with the site , very interesting and worth the trip.

This is a Sacred place to Buddhist all over the world. Currently this is a world heritage and in here you can see 5 natural caves turned in to Buddhist temple and each cave it can see lots of Buddha status. also there is a fount on roof and the water flow appearing in the surface of the rock. The fountain supply the water whole trough the year even in the dry season.

If you have seen some amazing cave temples in your day then this probably wont blow your socks off. Also - if you make the mistake of going in summer like we did then get there early and don't cover up straight away. YOU WILL DIE OF HEAT EXHAUSTION. The climb to the temple was harder than climbing Lion Rock. Also, you'll need to take your shoes off so make sure you do it before you get to the place that charges to hold them. We tried to put them in our backpack but they wouldn't let us so do it before they see you.
Firstly be aware that it is a steep walk up a rocky hill to get there. Very lovely the way that the caves have been built into the rocks. Can get quite busy No fee, dress appropriately for temple

This place is special, i spent minutes in one of the rooms, staring at the Buddha statue, it had special energy. You can't miss it if you are interested in Buddhism and sacred places. Unforgettable experience.

This place is special, i spent minutes in one of the rooms, staring at the Buddha statue, it had special  energy. You can't miss it if you are interested in Buddhism and sacred places. Unforgettable experience.
This place was a part of our self exploring trip to Sri Lanka. We visited the cave temples, without much of expectations, it was quite an average visit overall.

Old sacred place of Buddhism. You can imagine there how monks meditate there 2000 years ago. Lots of monkeys on the steps to the temples and beautiful view from the top. No entry charge from last year. Yes!

Well worth a visit. It is free at the moment as there is a dispute over ownership of the caves. It is temple so the usual applies, no bare shoulders or shorts, remove hats and shoes. But you can wear socks, the ground is very hot!

We went on a visit at the beginning of September, and the entrance was free. It was a really beautiful visit, and the caves are spectacular! As noted elsewhere, when you get to the top, start with the furthest cave first and work your way forwards, as they increase in majesty in this direction. A few notes: 1. Avoid in the baking hot sun or pouring rain, as it is a fairly steep climb to the top. 2. Take plenty of water. 3. Cover shoulders and knees all the walk up and make sure to take your shoes off st the top before entering the main cave area entrance. You only have to pay 25 LKR per pair. 4. Wear socks! The stones get very very hot in the midday sun and so it is a good idea to wear socks and avoid pain! 5. Avoid the monkeys, as they can get quite aggressive. 6. The toilets are at the bottom, to the right of the museum and cost 100 LKR per person, but they are clean and even have toilet paper! 😀👍
Very nice place with beautiful view. You have to walk a few stairs to there. There are monkeys which like to eat flowers :)
If your in Dambulla it's a really nice visit. Not too long, the caves make it a little different and while going up the stairs you get a nice view of the area. And now it's free.

This is something not to miss if you are Dambulla. We've been travelling from Kandy to Trinco and decided to cut the journey halfway and stop at Dambulla for only one night - this is something is extremely recommend especially if you are travelling by bus in Sri Lanka. In the afternoon we've spent 1.5 hours visiting the Golden Cave Temple. You'll be amazed by the size and number of the Buddhas inside the caves. It's a bit hard to climb all the stars if you are not a by athletic but you can take your time. Extremely recommend. Worth the experience. Ah, and it's free.
This is Buddhist temple. This temple is situated at mountain but it gave very pleasant experience. The statues and paintings of Buddha makes us very calm and cool. I never forget this temple.
I cannot explain this place. Its simply beautiful and simply explains the life of Buddha and the dhamma. Outstanding work of art and architecture. Must must go
After few hundreds stairs together with lots of monkeys (and babies!) you get the chance to see stunning Buddhas inside the caves. Really worth the experience.

This is the main attraction in Dambulla, you need to climb quite a few steps to reach the  cave temple. It would take your 30-40 minutes maximum to see all the caves. You would be mesmerized by the dedication and skill that would have been put in to paint the whole ceiling with continuous images of Buddha. Tip: Do this early morning as afternoon heat can be unbearable. You cannot enter the cave temple with shoes(though you can climb the stares till there with shoes).
We found the ancient paintings quite extraordinarily beautiful. Well worth the short walk up the hill.

I thought Id have enough of Temples, but not so, this place is awesome, not the right word for a religious place; I know but I can explain it any other way, the time it took to carve this out of the rock...frankly has to be seen.  I suggest you get there early in the day to avoid the crowds

You can probably cover the caves in about an hour but you have to climb about 150 stairs to get there. The buddhist sculptures are not the finest but the number and its location makes it a worthwhile site to visit. You have to take out your shoes to visit the cave, and I went in barefoot without socks. Bad call - cos I was bitten some sort of termites that caused a bad allergic reaction - pulsating heartbeat and rashes. Good thing I got antihistamines. Wear long socks!

Have to go with around 150 stairs and can get in tho the cave temple.  Middle of that there is a pot with water some water drops from the top of the cave fall into the pot..it keep happening every single second but a mystery is it wont nevel fill with water...water level is same as 500 years ago..pretty cool ha.. Tip. never ever keep your wallet or bag on the floor or rock.monkeys will take it and go away//lol

Had to climb like a 100 stairs to reach the caves on top, but it was worth it. We didn't have a guide so won't know much about the caves, but the paintwork atop the ceiling and silence of the statues make you wonder about how resilient the artists must have been. At the risk of sounding poetic- The view from the top spanning across the lush greens of srilanka was breathtaking.

We visited the Cave Temples after climbing Lion Rock earlier in the morning. I would recommend doing both early in the morning before the heat starts to pick up. There are quite a few steps up to the top with water, ice-cream and fresh mango sellers on the stairs on the way up. There is a dress code so be sure to wear longer shorts and cover shoulders etc. You have to take your shoes off to enter the temple – I would recommend a backpack to put them in or there is a small charge for them to be watched. I regretted not bringing my guide book to these temples as the buddha's are very interesting and I would have preferred to have known the significance of the stances etc so try to avoid my error and bring a guide book along. The ceilings are particularly intricate and all of the caves have something to offer. I enjoyed the visit and would recommend to those in the area but probably wouldn't go out of my way. It is free which is always a plus!

We had half a day to see this attraction as part of a two day trip and really enjoyed it. Firstly let me say that if you're elderly or infirm in any way there are over three hundred steps to the caves and the climb can be very tiring given the heat, there is however a small stall selling water etc about half way up. Once there the views are brilliant and the statues and caves fascinating. There is a dress code so no shorts above the knee and no shoes can be worn inside the temple.Would recommend a visit. I really enjoyed the visit and would recommend a visit.

Having just climbed Sigiriya, I hadn't anticipated another monster climb up to the Cave Temples - be warned: there are a lot of steps in the direct heat so take water, walking shoes and sun protection. To be clear, there's not as many steps as Sigiriya but if you're doing both on the same day, expect to feel it the next day! At the top, you have to remove your shoes so a pair of socks will spare your feet from the hot ground. You'll also be expected to be appropriately dressed for a temple (shoulders and legs covered). There are loads of cheeky monkeys along the way as well to keep you entertained. The temple themselves are absolutely beautiful and offer respite from the blazing sun.
You can not forget to climb the stairs to go into this five temples  excavated in the rock There a thousand budas painted and a hundred statues.
This is a must visit if you are in the area. Bit of a stepped walk to the top but well worth it. Facsinating history
Definitely should not be missed. One of most amazing and impressive places i have vidited. Remember to look up - paintings on the ceiling are gorgeous!

The climb to the top is not the easiest if u have young kids but once you get there it's mind blowing. If caves of this nature with its amazing artistry was in an European country be rest assured it would have been a unesco world heritage site. Pity that it's not looked after well by the Sri Lankan authorities as it would be a shame if our future generations don't get to enjoy this. A must see to anyone visiting Sri Lanka and also a must see to all locals to understand how great their heritage is.

Great few hours, long walk up to the top not as much a sigaria but can be warm so take loads of water, wear good footwear and go early 7am. Take a stick for the monkeys to get rid of them and enjoy. It doesn't cost anything. You'll be up and back in 1.5 hours.
The cave temples narrate a lot of history. wear very comfortable shoes and try and finish this early in the day.
The temple was the best temple I have visited in Sri Lanka. Buildings in the cave were mysterious and full of statues of Buddha. You have to proper clothes and go there without shoes.

The cave temple is dedicated to Buddha and is worth visiting, especially if you love history. A few tings to note: make sure you wear long pants or buy a sari ($2) from a vendor at the entrance. I was not told of the walk to the caves, which is along 250+ steps in intense heat. Wear a hat and watch out for monkeys who will try and take anything you have. Do not feed them and stay away from the ice cream vendors along the path.

We stayed in Kandy and drove to Sigiriya in the morning.  After the climb there, we went to Dambulla - we were all tired, especially the kids after doing Sigiriya.  We had to climb a good 10 to 15 minutes before we reached the caves - but thankfully, the steps were not steep. The phenomenal number of Buddha statues inside the 5 caves leaves you amazed in Dambulla!   They are in different sizes and poses too.  The paintings and the statues are a beautiful sight.  It was very quiet when we went, felt very peaceful! We need to wear full pants - no shorts are allowed.  A vendor outside the caves, lends a long cloth  which you have to tie around your waist to cover your shorts.

This is a perfect place to experience loads of amazing wildlife (and Sri Lankan heat!) as it is a massive walk up to these beautiful caves. When you get up there you must remember to bring socks because you will have to take your shoes off to go in. I'm glad we had a pool to go to afterwards!

I've never visited a cave temple and this was very nice. I cannot believe how much work it has been to manufacture these caves. Very special to see. The golden entrance alone is gorgeous to see. There are many steps to climb, but that's okay to do. You get rewarded with a beautiful view! We went early in the morning so the tiles weren't that hot to walk on and there weren't many other tourists! We were there around 8.30.
Just stunning... Another great cultural place to visit. You don't need to wear a sarong as wee feel people are being told to tout first sales in the village.  A must see one of place.
One of the most interesting buddhist sites in SL, worth a visit, but beware of monkeys, they steal everything
Beautiful statues in the caves - must see (but beware: 370+ steps before you enter)

So glad I visited this temple. En route from Sigiriya, our driver stopped here. We actually had no idea where we were, and left our shoes at the entrance, as it is a temple. We came upon these steps (carved out of stone) and decided to climb them (barefoot) - we didn't realize that they'd keep going! Once we got to the summit, after a long climb, we finally came upon the temple with the beautiful sanctuaries - each sanctuary had a sleeping Buddha, and each subsequent Buddha was larger than the one that came before it. The details on the carvings, the colours, the number of statues - was quite breathtaking. Go slow, plan to stay a while and take in the sheer beauty of it all. Lots of people were there, and on the way down, there were several Sri Lankans selling things - magic wooden boxes, bracelets, etc  - if you stop to look, they will try and sell you something - I only had large rupees on me(5000) so didn't really buy anything, but they were very persistent. Lots of cute little monkeys in the area too, some mothers carrying their babies.
A great visit at the temple.also a very great watch out. Unfortunately there are a lot of monkeys at the entrance... so be carefully
This is a very great place with a great history... we enjoyed this trip. Be carefully  there are a lot of monkeys. 😂

We love this Cave temple, better than any other temples. The entrance is free but you can give donations to the temple office. The paintings on the cave walls  were breathtaking! and it just felt so peaceful being there.

It was my first Experience visiting a Buddhist Temple.The experience was Serene. It had calming and soothing experience. The staircase leading to the temple is very challenging physically. So take your time climbing up there. There are steep steps so make sure your footwear is comfortable. Since it is a religious site, please make sure that you have covered your body; local frown upon very low shorts and skirts. Once reaching there you will have to take off of you shoes/sandals. There is a shoe rack where they charge LKR 25 for a pair for safe keeping. Once your journey starts with the temple be prepared to be awed by 150 Buddhist statues in 4 or 5 caves. There is also Hindu Temple as well. RECOMMENDATION: Have a comfortable footwear Have a Backpack for water bottles. Water bottles at staircase are priced at LKR 100 (Cost is LKR 60) HIGHLY RECOMMENDED: Do not do Sigiriya Rock and The Golden Temple Dambulla on same day. Physically it is not possible
By going up to the mountains to visit the caves, my family and I were able to see historic statues which put me at awe. It was a lovely experience to learn of such beauty within Sri Lanka.
Lots of Buddhas, some huge. Very interesting to learn about Buddhism and the history of the country, Kings, invaders etc through this place!
Very rare cave Tamples made in caves looks very old ancient structure, one must visit and do take care of your clothings, No Head cover, Shoulder and Knees should be covered too.
It was great Buddha Statue huge in size a great view and must see place at Dambulla. Just at the lower end a Cave Tamples.

This takes your breath away. Easy to walk up to. Monkeys everywhere on the way up. When you get there it is a small site but just so beautiful. Very hot outside but very cool in the caves. Very well worth it.

You have to climb about 500 steps in (usually, as in our case) high heat and humidity (this wasn't even the hottest time of year). The caves are all together and feature Buddha statues and wall and ceiling paintings. Inspite of photography being limited in the caves, we could see how some paintings are being lost forever.
We went there from dambulla with a tuktuk. On Site a tvGard asked 200 SLR for each backpack so we put them in a tuktuk to sigirya for 1K and visited GT

Definitely worth a visit! It is a cave monastery, and consist of five caves that have hundreds of statues of Buddha, and mural paintings. The surrounding park that leads up to the monastery is also beautiful and worth taking a stroll in.

To visit Sri Lanka and not make the effort to climb to the caves would be a wonderful life experience lost. We had already climbed Sigiriya on the day we visited and there was a moment when we considered not climbing to the caves. The climb is not too challenging, but to do it straight after the big rock was a bit of a push - especially given how hot it was. The effort was well worth it. I am not a spiritual person, but this was a spiritual experience. The beauty, the realisation of significance and age of the paintings and statues was incredible. This is a must do site seeing outing while in Dambulla.
Lovely temple, well worth seeing this, but get up early for this so you do not have to que for a long time
Stunning, free and very beautiful. Not hard to walk up, views from the top make it worth while and it takes your breath away when you get inside. Sooo amazing - a no brainer

After spending over 4000lkr at Sigiriya in the morning it was great to do something free! The caves themselves are interesting, and people still give offerings there. As a Buddhist temple you need to have knees and shoulders covered and remove your shoes. If it's a hot day take socks as the stones get hot. It's a bit of a walk up to the temple (200ish steps?) Some terrain is uneven/without steps. It's hot work but not hard. Don't bring food with you/ east food on the way up. There are lots of monkeys here. They leave you alone but will think your food is for them if they see it (watched a couple hurriedly putting biscuits away when they realised the attention they were getting from the local simian population!). A few hawkers and 'guides' about, but a simple 'no' stops hassle. Note: there are very few shops/restaurants around the temples. Everything is much further into town. Make sure you take what you need with you (water etc).

You have to climb almost 500 stairs to get to 5 cave caves. All caves are back to back and features Buddha statues. It is very scenic and must watch if you are in Dambulla. Thy charge Rs 100 for toilet service and Rs 50 for footwear keeping. This is not correct in my sense. Otherwise they dont have any entrance fees. Plan for morning or evening, noon times are very sunny.

We visited this place on our back way from Sigiriya to Kandy. Nice place with tallest golden statue of Buddha. To be more accurate, it's tallest in world only among similar one. The thing is that Buddha is represented in over 90 different poses each has its own meaning. Saying all that does not reduce the value in any way of that amazing place. Do not forget to visit cave and museum.

This was one of my favourite experiences in Sri Lanka, and it was free! I strongly recommend a visit. Heads up: you have to cover your shoulders and knees. My suggestion is that you go up at around 4 pm as it takes about an hour to do the Cave Temple. When you're done, instead of heading straight down, you can sit on top of the mountain and watch the sunset. The view from the top is gorgeous! Enjoy!

If you have to make choices what to see and what not, do not skip this place. Quite a climb on proper steps take you to the top of the mountain with a lovely view and to the entrance of the tempel. Monkeys on the way up. Even though it van be busy with tourists, the atmosphere around the tempel complex is solemn and quiet, which gives a good impression on how it has been all those years, The statues and paintings are impressive and beautifull.

We really liked this place, you can enjoy a beutiful view at the top and the paintings in the caves are very nice. I recommend that you take some water with you, you will definitely need it once you get there.
This is a good stop over on your way to the East. The cave temple and the beautiful tall golden statue of lord Buddha are good photo opps.

Be ready to climb up the steep hill as it is worth every step and you will be rewarded by a beautiful cave temple and amazing views from the top of the hill.  Lots of different buddha statues with thousand year of history behind it.  Try to visit in the evening so that you dont get hit by the heat!

Good it's free but read review on Golden Temple there as I said it's OK to see it but nothing as special as you get in Thailand. All the caves are the same really and we got a little bored. Less than hour and you've done it all.

We stayed in Dambulla where the hotel was 10 minute walk so we walked there along the roadside. Great entrance with the huge buddha towering inside but not as impressive as you get all over Thailand. It's benefit though is it's free to walk up the steep steps to the caves. Watch out for all the monkeys around free, we saw 1 jump on a mans back from behind and bit him! Just go careful and walk away from them you'll be fine. It's good that this is free, shocking as all they want is money money money everywhere, rip the English off. Take water with you to walk up, rest if you need to on your way up. Caves are OK but they are all really the same thing in each. Again nothing like Thailand so we found it a little boring. Water is sold up there half way up if you need to buy it for 100 rupees which is good. Water everywhere really over there is 60-100 so I dont mind paying 100 when you are sweating and out of breath. Takes like less than hour really and you've done it. We then went on to Polonnaruva after which is 1 1/2 hour drive away so easy to fit these 2 things in same day.

The caves are absolutely stunning. Beautifully carved Buddhas. You can see many monkeys during the climb up. Don't miss Sigiriya in the distance! Best of all is not too many tourists and no entrance fee, although we might have just been lucky in this aspect.

Very pretty place! The climb isn't that tough, the view is great, the monkeys cute and the cave temples spectacular. It took us about an hour and a half. Since they stopped asking money for it, make sure to make a donation.
Thoroughly interesting and amazing. Of hundreds of of budda statues I found one that mesmerised me and made me stop and reflect, me a non believer.

Steep walk up the hill, made easier by the funny monkeys but best in the early mornings. I would recommend not taking any food on the way up to avoid any unexpected encounter with a hungry monkey! They aren't dangerous at all, but known for their curiosity... The view from above is breathtaking and worth the effort, and the buddha statues in the caves are just unspeakable. However, my main piece of advice is to HIRE A GUIDE in order not to miss any of the hidden secrets of such wonderful spot. Personally, I was very lucky to have Suresh by my side - a local guide that accompanied me throughout my 3-weeks trip in Sri Lanka. I had read a couple of reviews about his driver & guide services before my trip and I am absolutely delighted after it!! Highly recommended, experienced and modest guide ready to drive kilometers to please his clients. If you want to discover the authentic Sri Lankan landscapes and culture through the eyes of a local, do not hesitate to contact Suresh. Hereby his website, with contact details, rates, testimonials and photos of various clients: http://www.srilankanchauffeurguide.com/index.html Enjoy your stay in the magical island of Sri Lanka!

The Golden Temple has been built by cutting into the rock face at the side of a hill. There is a nice walk to get up to the temple, it is not too strenuous and offers nice views of the surrounding areas. It is quite impressive that the temple itself sits wedged into the side of the hill. Many interesting statues of Buddha and also wall paintings. Just don't forget to cover up, although if you forget to you can hire a shawl for 100Rps

Impressive to see because it is manmade; you climb 100-150 steps to come to the caves; nice view on Sigiriya from there. No real need to take a guide. I loved the last Kandy king statue Spend around one hour.

The five caves are set into the rocky hillside and there is quite a climb, stairs and hill path to reach them. You are rewarded with lovely views from the top and five caves with lots of Buddha statues inside. We accepted the services of a guide but we didn't learn a lot... two caves are 2100 years old and three are more recent. It got quite crowded but was worth the trip, lots of monkeys to be seen on the path as you climb. Note: women need to cover shoulders and legs, you can buy shawls and sarongs at  a stall halfway up if needed.

Have read a lot of reviews saying once you have seen one Buddha you have seen them all, yes and no. If you have seen them in SE Asia they are slightly different here. Even if you haven't seen a Buddhist temple before it's a very good example in a unique setting. The wall paints are amazing and still very bright due to restoration. There is a steep walk up some stairs to get to the top but I do believe there was a ramp I saw to the left had side of the stairs that take you up, I could be mistaken. As the title does say it is free, but they do have donations boxes all around. It would be a shame to let a piece of history go to ruin like so many others.
One of most famous buddas shrine and historic place...no much steps to climb to the rockcave temple..but could be hard to climb in noon due to heat...

As everyone has said, some steep steps up to the the caves.  The monkeys on the way up have been known to take things so be careful.  Once at the top you have to leave your shoes outside for 25lkr.  Would be a good idea to bring some socks as the stones do get hot or the red ants may get you :-)  Enjoyed the different caves and the history of the king and how he stayed with the monks when in exile.  Views are stunning across the country and across to Sigiriya and the rock.. Well worth a visit... we went just before dusk which was ideal.  Toilets 100lkr

A bit of a climb to get there but not too much of a problem.  Lots of cheeky monkeys to see en route! The caves were free when we went and we understand this is a recent change. It's hot on the walk up once you have to take your shoes off,  but inside the caves is lovely and cool. You walk from one to the other and the whole visit doesn't take long.  Both the statues and paintings are impressive and the setting is very serene. There are a couple of small but lovely lotus ponds outside the caves too.

Entrance is now free. Lots of stairs to get up (about 325) but definitely worth it when you get there.  Five caves in total with loads of Buddhas, beautiful painted ceilings and spectacular views.  The huge golden Buddha on the bottom level is pretty spectacular too. As with all temples, cover up legs and shoulders. Tip the shoe guy at the top. Watch out for the monkeys!

Well worth the hot steep climb these ancient cave temples exude a sense of peace and mystery. Take water and a hat and small change to mind your shoes - the five chambers it is the ancient fresco paintings which are at their most enigmatic. Lives up to the hype.
This rock temple offers beautiful Buddha statues in a very beautiful place. The climb up  the stairs is tough but it's worth it.

A steep climb up to the caves, but it is well worth it. Five cave temples, each more stunning than the last. No surprise that women are expected to cover up, but men with short shorts or exposed shoulders will also have to hire a wrap.

One of the main temples in Sri Lanka. Very nice and interesting place, specially the paintings on the wall. There is a lot of stairs to climb to reach to the top. It would better to visit it early morning or late afternoon.
Wonderful history .  We were pleasantly surprised at what we saw, as had not read a lot about the cave before visiting

Nice to see but we didn't spent a lot of time there. The ground gets quite hot during the day which can blister your feet if you  are not wearing socks, because you need to leave your shoes at the entrance.
have seen them all. Well I know that's my opinion, so for my family and I it was not that great an experience, since there was nothing special about this place.
Five caves.  Our guide book suggested we start with cave five,  the one furthest away.  Good shout.  In this order caves get progressively larger and more impressive.

Download some history / info before you go. Knees & shoulders to be covered as is place of worship. Shoes must be removed at top of climb before entry. Free entry at moment, 50rupees for car park, 25rupees for shoe locker.

This place is amasing and due to a dispute over proprietary rights is free to visit so enjoy it whilst it lasts. In each cave you will find a beautiful selections of buddha statues. And I will say no more so I will not spoil you the surprise.

They have done a good job with the statues in the cave. Once you climb the stairs, there are a few caves to explore all next to each other. It's nice going from cave to cave and seeing all the detail painted over the cave walls.

Loved this place. It's really cool. I was a bit worried after reading about the monkeys and nearly didn't want to come here because of that but they were actually fine. They didn't bother us at all and keep their distance. The walk up to the cave temple isn't difficult at all. It's steep enough I suppose in places but not really. Once you get up the first set of steps that's actually halfway. You need to cover your knees and take off your shoes. There is a guy minding shoes for 25 rupees a pair or else just leave your shoes on the ground. The caves are really interesting with lots of different little areas. It's definitely welll worth a visit.
Climb was very easy and short. The temple is composed of 5 différents caves but my favorite is the second one. The visit should take less than 1h. We stopped by on our way to lion rock from kandy.
Good very nice  I enjoyed and nice location from dambulla  city half hours been Sri Lanka u have to visit this nice place
Very good place and good education I think u a in dambulla u have to visit this nice place children also enjoyed

The golden cave temple offered fantastic views of the jungle on the walk up, and an amazing experience on the inside. Never before have I see so many Buddah statues in one place. Bring water for the climb, and ensure you are covered up (both men and ladies), at least shoulders and knees. Socks are also advised during the summer, as the floor can get very hot and shoes need to be taken off. Would definitely recommend!
A brisk climb to the top, and a really big Buddha. Go early - the heat makes the climb worse than it is. The caves themselves are interesting, but you won't spend more than 30 mins there.

The caves were semi-interesting in that they're all very similar with multiple statues of Bhudda. Not worth travelling to from afar though. The setting itself is nice as you walk up some steps to the top. The exterior of the building is nice too but unless you are especially religious, I'm not sure there's much to see after a quick 30 minute look around. We didn't have to pay due to some ongoing dispute we were told but I think normally you have to.  Cost of 50 rupees to leave your shoes at the stall as cannot enter the caves with shoes on. Due to the heat of the stones outside, may be worthwhile leaving your socks on though.

It's quite a steep walk up a lot of stairs to get to the rock caves. You need to be dressed modestly to get in. The caves themselves are full of statues of Buddha and they are all beautifully painted. There are also some Hindu shrines / temples to look round as well. The views from the top are also very impressive and there are monkeys everyhwere you look.

Like many of the temple sites in Sri Lanka this is a must see. The walk up is not that hard, it's hot but it's not a difficult walk. The caves are pretty cool but my only issue was the surrounding of the cave area with electric fencing to keep the monkeys. Sad sight seeing the monkeys the other side of the fence. Anyway that's being pedantic but yes go see this place and it's free entry!!

Our visit to the cave temples was free.  I am not sure if it is free everyday however.  The walk was lovely with some great views from the top.  I also thoroughly enjoyed the amount of wildlife we saw.  The caves were alright but very similar to all the other temples you will visit in Sri Lanka.  Very strict on clothing there however, a lot stricter than the other temples we visited.

Everything about this place was amazing. From the moment you arrive and see the giant gold Buddha, to climbing the stairs and seeing so many monkeys and then the highlight is the caves. For anyone interested in history, art or archaeology, this is a must. Surely one of the world's great treasures.

The cave temple is good to see with numerous Buddha statues inside three caves. I had a guide who could explain the history behind the caves but even without the commentary it would be a pretty impressive sight. And the monkeys you see on your way up add to the visit.
This was a nice stop on the way to our hotel - it was a longer an expected walk up the hill though and quite strenuous.   The caves themselves are great to see.

Get started early to discover these super 5 caves... it does get very hot after 10am. Wear good walking shoes as some places along the route are slippery. Wear socks as shoes not allowed within the grounds of the temple. The ground does heat up. Shorts and short sleeve clothes not allowed, so cover up as is required to all temple visits. The Statues are fragile and need care so show respect and dont take pics with your backs turned towards the statues. Enjoy the Calmness in the caves.

Stunning position to learn some history of Buddhism. Fabulous walk up to the Golden Rock caves via a range of steps and track. An added bonus to see the monkeys so close up. The caves are just tremendous. The size of the statues are amazing and the whole site has a sense of tranquility despite it being fairly busy.

Beautifully preserved paintings & statues in this temple. 25 flights of stairs get the heart pumping. Ensure your knees are covered & do the walk in flip-flops so it's easy to leave your shoes outside (25 Rupees per pair). We enjoyed the fresh mango 'fries' on the way down although they did attract the monkeys
August 2014. Spectacular caves with neck-paining buddhist ceiling murals. Well worth the hike up (bring water). We did not go into the buddhist museum at the entrance.

You look at the Golden Budha and think whoa this looks great, then behind it is 700 steps leading you too an array of different rooms that have statues that 600 years old. Don't wear thongs, runners are recommended, you will have to take your shoes off before going into the temples.
A must Visit Site in sigiriya with beautiful history. though its very high to climb. Too many monkeys en route to the top. good juices in the restaurant after finishing the visit.

Its worth the climb although in the heat, it takes longer to reach the rock caves. Its best to visit early before the sun gets too hot. The caves and statues leaves you in awe. Although it is in need of restoration. As a religious place, one must take care to cover and not reveal too much.  We did not pay an entrance fee nor did we see any counters. Try to avoid feeding the little monkeys as they are pretty bold and tend to attack.

As you enter the premises you see the imposing golden statue of Buddha. And when you climb up and enter the caves dug into the rock, you see scores of brightly painted Buddha statues  - different postures, sizes, colours. You can spend at least 2 captivating hours admiring the statues.
The hill climbing is part of the discovery of these 5 caves. The paintings brings an other dimension to this religious place. An other spiritual experience you cannot miss.

The cave temple is beautiful and is located at the top of a mountain, presenting an excellent aerial view. The temple presents historical information about various avatars of the Buddha and Buddhist preaching. The temple requires climbing up about 500 steps and there is a steep ascent and it can get really tiring before you reach to the top but it's worth the effort.

Fantastic historical site for buddhism. Largest collection of ancient buddha statues. Get a guide, there is so much interesting historie you can miss. Great oldpaintimgs in the caves. You can see all in 1-1,5 hours with guide
A peaceful temple steeped in history. Find a guide to explain the history behind the Buddha statues and you will thoroughly enjoy the visit to this beautiful temple
A must for travellers in the area, has to be seen really as the pictures you see do not do this attraction justice!!

Unlike the other sites in the cultural triangle (anuradhapura, sigiriya and polonnaruwa) which cost at least USD$35/pax for entry, this temple was free for entry. However, it is one of the most well-preserved sites which inspired awe more than anuradhapura did for me. Truly beautiful, and a must-go.

Worth a climb up in the morning. It's a 15-20min slow walk. Apparently tickets were required but we walked in without seeing any ticket counters. The exterior of the cave temples resemble European architecture but the inferior is 100% Buddhist. Frescos or wall paintings are vivid. The rooms get smaller and smaller so you move towards the back. Highlight for me was the statue of the King which resembles an European princeling. Never figure out his name though!
No entrance fee at Saturday Big Buddah on street level. On the left sigth after 15min climbin stairs you reach the top and the caves. Very imperessing.
Loved it. The views were amazing and so was the place itself. Great to teach the kids about ancient history.

This is a must see if you visit Sri Lanka. Do not be fooled by the Golden Buddha at the foot of the hill. Go up the winding path or the steeper steps to the left of the garish temple to the top of the hill to reach the prize. Apart from the stunning views across the plains, with Sigiriya in the distance, you get to view a wonderful set of cave paintings and statues of Buddha. This site consists of 5 caves each having it's own wow factor. They were created it is believed in the 1st century BC and added to up to the 11th century. It is a UNESCO world heritage site. The climb is longer than you expect, one of those "are we there?" "oh no, we're not" walks, so bring some water with you. There are people selling water halfway up the hill at a reasonable price if you forget. Photographs inside the caves are allowed but do not take a photo of someone standing in front of a Buddha statue as this is very insulting to Buddha. Entrance is LKR1500. You must leave your shoes outside the area so be careful, on a hot day like the day we were there the stone is like a griddle for your feet. Enjoy.

Well worth a visit but can do justice in an hour. Avoid heat of the day as climb up to the caves is steep ( especially if you have been to Lion Rock). Series of caves with amazing sculptures.Remember no selfies out of respect or sitting on the tables near the statues. However photos are allowed. Must see but for us an hour visit.

What a great deal of history! This temple dates from 2100 years ago, it has been home to monks and even a king hiding from invading enemies. Just a short climb on the mountain and you find this amazing temple carved into the mountain with plenty beautiful Buddha statues and guides who explain the story of the place and the religion. It was a very enriching experience for me and my wife during our Honeymoon in Sri Lanka.

The Golden Temple at Dambulla is a relatively new construction which is why it lacks that old world charm the neighboring city of Polonnaruwa offers. But the temple has been constructed beautifully so it makes for a charming stop when in the city.
Largest Buddha on Dharmacakra pose. Beautiful painting on the cave ceiling. Need to hike up to the cave. Nice view.

There is a bit of a climb so it's best to go late afternoon. It's free except for the tip (to watch your shoes). Something to see, all the walls are painted, really nice. When we were there, school children arrived and offerred flowers and prayed - beautiful to see.

Very impressed by what is inside the caves, definitely worth seeing!!!!! Especially since there is no charge. The walk up involves a climb which should be avoided in the heat of the day but isn't overly challenging. Dress to cover up legs and shoulders or won't be able to go into the temple caves.

After a few steps you get to a series of caves that have been turned into a temple. This is a unique experience and very interesting too. Be mindful of the monkeys around the temple as they will steal anything that looks like food from your hands.

The climb is pretty steep but I thought it was well worth it. Once at the top there is a series of different door ways that open up to different individual rooms. The painting on the ceiling are very beautiful. I would recommend this site if your in the area.

Amongst the prime archaeological sites like, Anuradhpura, Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya I rate Dambulla as the best for gigantic amazing monuments of Lord Buddha, his disciples & stupa in the caves constructed on top of mountain. Before reading the review, please see the images of Dambulla Golden Rock Cave temple: 1. On google search engine 2. In sightseeing travel websites 3. In this review of mine 4. In the review of this attraction by other trip advisor members You will get the real feel of what amazing scriptures you are going to see on top of the mountain inside the caves. There are following five caves that houses amazing scriptures of Lord Buddha, his disciples & stupa: Cave 1: The Devaraja Lena – The cave of ‘Lord of the Gods’ 45 feet sleeping postured Buddha Idol Cave 2: The Maharaja Lena – The cave of ‘Great Kings’ This is the most attractive & large cave. It has stupa surrounded by 11 seated Buddha idols with 60 more idols Cave 3: The Maha Alut Viharaya – The cave of ‘Great New Temple’ Reclining Lord Buddha idol of 30 feet. 50 Buddha idol surrounding the prominent seated Buddha idol. 42 standing Buddha idols & 15 more seated Buddha idols in this cave Cave 4: The Pachima Viharaya – The cave of ‘Western Temple’ Identical Buddha idols in meditation pose Cave 5: The Devana Alut Viharaya – The cave of “Second New Temple’ Reclined Buddha statue of 32 feet with many standing & seated Buddha idols. 2 of the seated Buddha idol have hooded cobra How to reach using public transport- bus & train? A)	Bus 1. Kandy to Dambulla by bus (Tkt less than 150 LKR, journey time 3 to 4 hours) This route will drop you at the bus stop in front of the Dambulla Rock temple. a) There is direct bus from Kandy to Dambulla b) Also you can board the following buses at Kandy viz: Polonnaruwa, Kaduruwela, Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, Vavuniya, Jaffna etc that goes via Dambulla 2. Colombo to Dambulla by bus (Tkt less than 200 LKR, journey time 4 to 5 hours) a) There are direct bus from Colombo to Dambulla b) Also you can board the following buses at Colombo viz: Polonnaruwa, Kaduruwela, Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, Vavuniya, Jaffna etc that goes via Dambulla After getting down at Dambulla bus stop, take tuk tuk, it will be less than 200 LKR to reach to the Dambulla Rock Temple at 2 km distance in 5 minutes on Kandy road.
