B) Train, tuk tuk & Bus Nearest train station is Habaranna B1) Train: Colombo to Habaranna Train (Tkt less than 300 LKR journey time 4 to 5 hours) Board any train going to Anuradhpura, Trincomalee, Jaffna etc going via Habaranna. B2) Tuk tuk: From Habaranna railway station, take tuk tuk (three wheeler) & come to Main Habaranna bus stop. LKR less than 200 LKR & 5 minutes journey. B3) Bus: From Habaranna bus stop, board the bus going to Kandy. LKR less than 50 LKR & 45 minutes journey. Dambulla Rock Cave Entrance fee: LKR 1500 When facing the gigantic Lord Buddha Idol the ticket issuing office is to your right. Ticket issuing office does allow tourists to keep their luggage free of cost. When facing the gigantic Lord Buddha Idol, you will find steps to your left that lead to the caves on top of the mountains. It is 30 minutes trek. Road & steps from foothill to the caves on top of the mountain is of concrete cement. PS: While on the route to the top of mountain you will come across one junction, where T shirts, shirts, hats & other souvenirs are for sell. Then on the route ahead you will come across monkeys. So take care of your belongings from the monkeys. Before entering the cave entrance on top, you have to remove your foot wears. There are following two options to keep your foot wears: 1. Paid foot wear stand: Pay LKR 25 2. Open space at one’s own risk From top of mountain, one will see good scenic panoramic view. You will surely like this Unesco’s archaeological world heritage site very much. All the best…

The visit to the Golden Cave Temple was a nice walk up steep steps.  The climb is a short one of 30-40 mins.  There are a lot of monkeys so beware of your possessions. The location is beautiful and the views from top are incredible, greenery on all sides.  The temple is dedicated to Lord Buddha in various forms and sizes.  If you are interested, do take a guide, maybe you will come out with some detailed explanations of the place. The walls and ceilings are beautifully painted and you can get good pictures without flash and see some incredible results. Take time and walk around.

The Dambulla Cave Temple. Dating from the 3rd Century B.C. These caves are unique for the amazing painting on the ceilings and for the statues - all of which are carved directly from the bed rock. It takes a walk up a what feels like a thousand steps but the reward is pretty neat. Some great views along the way and the ubiquitous monkeys will keep you entertained. Entry is  free but there is a nominal charge to mind your shoes before you enter. This is a great stop along the road to the north. There is a nice cafe serving healthy/safe to eat fresh juices and coconuts at the bottom.

Go in late afternoon...nice and quiet and very peaceful. Caves were also interestong...to get there is a little climb so only combine with sigirya rocl in same day if your condition is good enough. Just enjoy!
Lovely location, the steps are steep with lots of monkeys but the views are spectacular and the cave art work is stunning.

again it charges admission fees and it's just a cave temple, similar with those in Thailand with free admission. not worth visiting. never trust the tuk tuks here. better get your hotel to call one if you need

The initial Large golden Buddha statue is at ground level. The cave temples are accessible via a steep climb up steps which may take 30 to 40 mins. Take plenty of water and sun protection. Gets busy with locals. Worth seeing.

This is a great place to visit. it takes your breath away. So many statues though many of similar size and form. It used to be once just niched into the cave though today an outer wall protects these ancient statues. If you go early in the day, or late in the afternoon, and beat the large groups of tourists, it is a very spiritual place. Mid day: it is a tourist site and loses some of its magic.
Thoroughly enjoyed our visit, the culture, various paintings preserved intact. Got to understand in detail the detail the essence of Buddhism with a good kind hearted soul who explained all to us.
Good place to visit, worth the climb to enter the cave.  Be careful with what you wear, as there are restrictions on your clothing.
Beautiful area to go to. Wear or take socks with you that you can wear when you remove your shoes before entering the temples. The stones are hot as fire.
Lots of steps to the cave temples. Be warned and bring good shoes. No entry fees currently, which was a bit confusing as there is a sign for tickets.
It's a bit of a climb to get up and you have to ruin the gauntlet with the cheeky monkeys but the atmosphere in the caves is lovely and the paintings are awesome.  Well worth the effort.
300 metre high a tremandous place.budha sitting and leaning posture was good.nice view everywhere.staircase is fine.u can go top of the hills by using it.it has a buddah museum too.

The golden temple of dambulla is one of the best preserved cave temple complexes in Sri Lanka , protected by monkeys ever ready to pose for a picture . The dim lighting induces a sense of peace and calm as you move through the 5 monasteries flanked by 157 status of Buddha in their various mudras and draped in exquisitely detailed mural painting which cover the walls and ceilings like a carpet.

Look it doesn't matter what religion or belief you have it overrides it. This is art. This is history. This is sacredness not to be missed, we nearly did and I am so glad we didn't. The little hike up to the caves, yes you will be sweating. Dambulla is hot. The 5 caves all unique in their own way. Tourists don't use flashes. Ancient frescos don't like them. And no entry fee, crazy for a place like this.
Be prepared for a bit of a hike up stairs to reach the temple. But it is well worth it. many different statues as well as the paintings make it a very interesting and beautiful site.
The climb to the cave temple is very steep and tiring. You may wonder why it was built on such a high place, but that could be the reason it is well preserved after hundreds of years.
Worth the visit and the caves are worth the steep walk up with spectacular views, amazing paintings and Buddhas in the 5 caves. A highlight
Great cave paintings and Buddha statues, amazing view of the world below. Tough climb through steps or gradient, but worth a visit.

You can't miss the site as the largest Buddha in the world in gold is at the entrance! The Buddha is impressive but it just signifies the start of the journey up to the cave temples. It is a long walk up especially on a hot day. Eventually you reach the top and there are great views right across to Siguirya. Please make sure that you are suitably dressed for the temple- ladies shoulders covered and long skirts - below the knees and men no sports shorts. There is a check after leaving your shoes. The temples are sensational cave after cave of Buddha statues with painted ceilings etc. Some are breathtaking. After looking at them you pay the man for looking after your shoes and make your way back down the long slope. Watch out for monkeys thriving your food!
Amazing , never will you see so many pictures or statues of Buddha in the one place. Watch out for the monkeys on the way up - the babies are a little like gollum!

The temple and the gigantic buddha in the town are a sight to behold, but take the time to climb up the hill to the cave temples - pace yourself , avoid the monkeys and enjoy the view - and then marvel in the caves themselves.
Huge golden Buda on top. Not much more to see. Spent 5 minutes here on the way to Rock Temple, Shock os way more interessante. Free entry, Pay 50 rupees to park car.

Faith does wonders to human beings who in turn create wonders for others . We did not enter the temple but went around appreciating the huge gilded statue of the Buddha and the temple complex. If you are prone to answer the call of nature make it a point to do it in any restaurant before you enter the temple complex . The toilets are not only primitive but you need to pay one of the highest rates in the world to use it.

600 foot climb but great view from the top. Well worth the climb. Bring a cold drinks and dress cool. Remember shoes come off at all temples and ladies must cover to the knee and shoulder covered too.

this place is truly magical, mystical and beautiful. Walking up the zillions of stairs not knowing what beauty lies ahead. Seeing the temple, just being there made me peacefull. The image of the first sight when you walk up there will never leave my mind and heart again, and when I close my eyes I can see this picture as if it was yesterday! Love that place!

It was big but there isn't much else to see...we didn't go to the museum hence didn't really know the history of this temple. We were very keen to visit the cave temple so left very early. Nice temple which is free for entry too. Worth a go.

The temple is in the cave and was preserved over the years. I really enjoyed it but it was so hot and I got a heat stroke! So make sure you get plenty of water and shades.... We also didn't manage to get a guide, but the Buddhas and paintings above our heads were very impressive. Definitely worth a visit!

It's worth the walk up the stairs to see these Caves. Each cave has a different colour, and the life size statues are painted with beautiful colours. Make sure you wear clothing to cover shoulders and knees. Try and time your entry to each cave around the tour groups  - there isn't a lot of room in them when a bus load enters.  Hint - they move on quickly to leave you time to  enjoy the painted walls, roof and statues. There isn't any information available on the Caves at the site, so if you are in interested in the history you'll have to research it.

I started to climb the stone stairs to this cave temple around 7:00 am. It's not hot at that time. And wind there waked me up. I saw a lot of monkeys playing on the way. They were very cute. Those statues and frescoes in the caves are well protected and almost intact. I was surprised by them because they were created in a similar form of Mogao Caves in Dunhuang which was far far away from Dambulla. But Mogao Caves are even more amazing. Buddhists built thoes wonders no matter in Sri Lanka or China are devout artists. Do not miss this temple. And it's totally free for everyone to visit.

I started to climb the stone stairs to this cave temple around 7:00 am. It's not hot at that time. And wind there waked me up. I saw a lot of monkeys playing on the way. They were very cute. Those statues and frescoes in the caves are well protected and almost intact. I was surprised by them because they were created in a similar form of Mogao Caves in Dunhuang which was far far away from Dambulla. But Mogao Caves are even more amazing. Buddhists built thoes wonders no matter in Sri Lanka or China are devout artists. Do not miss this temple. And it's totally free for everyone to visit.

Situated on a rock about 150 meter rock Dambulla rock temple and the huge golden statue of Buddha is a great place to visit. There are 5 caves with different sizes and there are so many statues of Buddha. Statues of King Valagamba and Ananda also there along with statues of Hindu gods. If no visitors, you can meditate in one of the caves for hours as it is cool and silent.

After the hot stair climb (hey it's only 430 steps, it's not that tough), the cave temples are well worth the effort. Multiple lying Buddha statues, one of which was carved from one piece of granite (resplendent with red soles of the feet), the cave temples are really impressive yet sombre. Some large caves, some small. So do yourself a favour, look up! The ceiling paintings are original and sublime. I'm not religious but it was very worthwhile! Go early. It gets hot ! Remember to wear something covering your knees (guys and girls). It's now free entry. 50 rupees to park your car and 25 rupees to have your shoes looked after while you are in the cave temples (no shoes permitted). Beware the monkeys and street dogs.

It is a very well preserved set of cave Temples. It reminded me of the Ajanta Caves in a strange way because that is more paintings where as these are more temples. It is a steep climb and the stairs are not very good. However, once you reach the top you realise that the climb has been very well worth it. I would highly recommend it to all the people visiting the Cultural triangle of Srilanka.

I'm a professor of comparative religion, so our visit to the Golden Temple was a highlight of our tour of India. We went on a Sunday morning. We saw no other foreign tourists among the 1000's who visited that day. But the crowds of people all around us in 42 degree heat were courteous and helpful.

Unbelievable sight. Short climb maybe 10 mins if slow. It's hot so go early. Need sarong and covered shoulder. Beautiful amazing caves. In awe of paintings. Get a guide very informative. Free entry now . The museum at 200 rupees very sad no descriptions not worthwhile. Allocate 2 hours l think

The cave temple is just wonderful. We fortunately started to climb early (around 500-600 steps) and avoided the strong sun and heat. There are many buddha statues and lot of paintings on the walls and ceilings which are I am told is 1000 years old. They have built the tallest Golden buddha which is a sight to behold. The place is clean and well maintained. The only thing you have to beware of are monkeys that will grab any food you may or if it thinks you are carrying!
majestic architectural and religious wonder.  Built into a rock.  How did they do this without modern technology?

The Dambulla Temple Caves (Buddhist Temples) were wicked amazing. I had a personal guide there for the temple, and he explained how there were 4 different temples in the caves, and explained the history and the statues' meanings in each temple, it was a beautiful site. There were paintings on the wall, and even on the ceiling, and in once cave, there was holy water, where there was water drifting from the caves, but the water was actually traveling UPWARDS instead of down, which was pretty cool! To get to the cave temples, it was a bit of a climb on uneven ground, and my guide explained how the monks had to climb up barefoot, i wanted to try it but i actually wanted to reach the temples sometime that day. When we reached the caves, we had to take our shoes off and walk the rest of the way, i attempted to go down some of the way barefoot, it was pretty hard but I'm glad i did it. Some of the school children that day made the entire trek up barefoot! Anyway, i recommend the site, it was absolutely beautiful.

We live in SE Asia and have been to what seems like a million temples. What makes this place so fantastic is that there are series of caves each packed with various Buddah's and the walls are all painted. Couple that with the fact that the whole cave is carved out of one massive boulder and it blows your mind. There is a long walk to get to it so it may not be ideal for those who find it tough walking steps or walking on uneven surfaces. The view from up there is also very nice. It only takes about 2 hours to do all together and you will be glad you spent the time and walked up the hill.

In the city of Dambulla lies a hub which has been treasured by many kings since the 1stcentury B.C.  Dambulla Rock Temple houses some of the most unique drawings and shelters 150 statues of Lord Buddha. Also, enjoy the breeze and natural view very much when we climbed the rock.

This is a high place to climb just a short distance from Sigiriya. One of the best attractions in Sri Lanka. At the lower ground is a temple with huge golden Buddah statue. There are many steps to trek in order to reach the cave temples but it's worth the journey. It shows a nice panoramic view of the surroundings of mostly green scenery, and the nearby villages at the peak. The entrance is free. Make sure to bring a bottle of drinking water to quench you through the journey to the peak.

Lovely murals n paintings..must visit.scenic beauty from top of city. Beware of monkeys especially when carrying any lotus flower in ur hands for puja n eatables not to be carried to avoid attacking from them.

climbed this with friends and it was really amazing about this temple, there were many statues which was amazing. and you can climb this with out paying anything for entrance tickets . beautiful panoramic view

Dambulla Raja Maha Viharaya also known as the Golden Temple is a beautiful temple which is built under a solid granite rock (built on a cave). It's famous for statutes and the pictures drawn on the rock wall. And also you can see water drops coming from the middle of the rock (ceiling) which collecting to a big pot. The temple situated on the top of the mountain and you will need some effort to reach there. Well worth to visit.

It is a long hike up but well worth it.  A series of caves await.  Each one a temple in its own right and all come with cave paintings.  We were there for a couple of hours looking at all of the sculptures and murals.

It is good news to learn that the Golden Temple now does not charge an entrance fee. My local friend said climbing from the left side of the temple concrete stairs does not need to pay entrance fee, and our group climbed from here. So we do not know any charge from another entrance Only thing is that two female from our group said they paid Rs.100 each to go toilet. Date of Visit: June 17th morning

The Golden Cave Temple is something to put on your bucket list. To reach this UNESCO site you'll have to do a bit of a work out: either by stairs or winding path to reach the top. Go early to beat the heat and take your time with the ascent: you'll be rewarded with magnificent views once you reach the summit. Watch out for cheeky monkeys and sleepy dogs. Leave your shoes with the minder at the entrance and step inside the large wooden gate. The 5 caves are beyond words, so spend time drinking in all the beauty and wonder to write your own description in your mind. The caves become very warm and stuffy once a lot of bodies are in there. It's advisable to bring a bottle of water with you too.

This temple has an amazing array of wonderful Buddhas in & around five caves; plus murals - all dating back to the 1st century. Stunning but be aware it's a long walk up many steps (not steep) steps. So flat shoes, water & sun cream are essential. Also, the views when you walk back down are stunning.
It was absolutely worth it - once in the lifetime experience. Beautiful views, lots of nice people on the way up to the temple and monkeys of course.

Really enjoyed our visit to the Golden Temple & Caves. It is so beautiful and it is completely free for entry to the caves and to see the Golden Buddha. You are recommended to give a donation. In comparison to some of the other tourist sites which charge crazy money for tourists to visit this is very good & would definitely recommend a visit if you're visiting or passing through. I'd allow about 2 hours for the complete visit including getting to the caves etc.
The Golden Temple is a very nice temple. The caves and the the golden big Buddha is so nice. The place is free to everyone and absolutely worth a visit!

We started the climb late afternoon. It is a bit of a hike specially considering the heat but once at top u are amply rewarded. Can't stress enough to start with cave no. 5 and then move backwards to cave 1. U will know the reason later. Caves are simply stunning and give you a sense of inner peace. As u leave don't forget to soak in the beautiful views from the top just outside the cave gates.

The Dambulla Golden cave temple is atop a small hillock. There are about 600 steps to be climbed or the winding ramp path could be used. The climb is gentle. More than a temple, this is a cave complex comprising 5 separate caves in which many Buddha idols have been accommodated. There are Buddha statues in sitting, standing and reclining postures. Some of the Buddha idols, mainly the reclining ones are huge. The cave roofs and sides have intricate paintings that has lived through the centuries. The five rock cut caves are on the side of a large rock that resembles a crocodile body. There are monkeys that are bound to do some mischief is some portions of the path. So beware of one of them snatching away plastic covers. There is ample parking available in the ground level. There are some shops selling flowers and other convenience items in the bottom level. There is a restaurant and other conveniences also there. The view from the top is good.
Not very many temples left for visit free of charge .  Very good caves and beautiful temple . worth to visit

As of 2016, it's free to visit here! It's a bit of a hike to get to the temples, maybe 30min up paths and stairs but very neat to see. The temples are carved into the side of a mountain so when you go in, you're in caves. On the walk up Prepare to see wild monkeys everywhere!!! This is a place of warship so respect the locals who are actually there to pray.
Went there on 5th June and there is no fee to be paid. Great place to visit then. At time crowded but if you just give it some time, the caves can be emptied and you are alone there.

We found this very interesting. Would highly recommend wearing flat shoes and taking water with you as its a bit of a walk up to the top. The views were amazing. Watch out for the monkeys though, we witnessed them pinch a bunch of flowers from one lady.

I started counting the steps we had to climb to reach this magnificent temple. Let's just say it was over 200. But don't be put off by the thought of climbing, it is fairly easy and done in stages. When you reach the top it is amazing. It is housed in 5 caves and each one quite spectacular in its own way. Reclining Buddhas, intricately painted ceilings, too many Buddha statues to count. Definitely worth a visit.

Simply amazing to see the gigantic buddha carved out on a single rock and the walls of the cave decorated with intricate colourful paintings. Standing there, one can almost feel the mystical past of that area. A must visit.

Beware the many steps up to this set of temples but it is worth it.The views,including Sigiriya in the distance, are fantastic.The 5 temples repay the effort and are quite stunning.Avoid weekends when it is crowded.No restrictions on photography but please don't sit on a statue to be photographed as someone did.....causing the monks to ban visitors for a while.

Well worth the visit. Amazing caves and statutes of Buddha. No entrance fee. We went around midday. Really windy up there. You need to enter barefoot to this place.There is place to keep you shoes at the cost of 25 rupees for each pair. BEWARE of people suddenly approaching to show you around and latter asking money. We just told politely to one person that we dont need a guide. All the caves are amazing. We enjoyed our tour there.

Dambulla Golden Temple Declared as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991, the most venerated and visited place in Dambullah is the Golden temple, popularly known as the Cave Temple. Dambullah is 150 km north of Colombo in central part of Sri Lanka. It is about 75 km from Kandy. The Golden Temple is spread over 5 caves which contain more than 150 statues of Gautama Buddha, few statues of Sri Lankan kings and mythological god and goddesses like Vishnu, Hanuman and Ganesh. In addition, the caves have paintings and murals drawn centuries ago.

We took the bus from sigirya to dambulla. Strange enough it was 80rs going and 65rs for the way back (price for 2p). There is at least a bus every half an hour. Don't believe the tuk tuk drivers when they tell you there is no bus. The tempel itself is free. For the museum, you need a ticket (don't know how much because we didn't enter). The caves are really amazing! We went in the late afternoon, when it cooled a bit down. It's easier to walk barefoot when it is not that hot. They ask 25rs to keep your shoes while you visit the temple.
For experiencing something different and exotic, a beauty from the past! A short distance from Dambulla city-center and so no excuse not to do!

It's a bit of a hike but worth it once you get to the top. The temple it's self is a pretty standard temple but the fact that it's built in a couple caves makes it unique. Plus, the views of the country are pretty great.
Imposing structure. This ancient temple is  short drive from Sigiriya and in elephant country. It was built over several centuries and consists of several temples.
Well worth the effort climbing up (but beware of non-qualified guards masquerading as guides)

It's a very good experience. The temple is unique & it's beautiful. The scenes from up are very nice. You can see the Lion's rock from up there. It's recommended to do both, the Lion's rock in the morning & the temple in the afternoon because they are relatively close
The cave Temples are worth the climb. It is steep and there are a lot of steps but but they should definitely not be missed. They were one of the cultural highlight of Sri Lanka for me.

Visited this in Feb 2016, and even though it was hot summer outside, the interiors of this place were cold as winter. Enjoyed the peaceful experience. You get to see hundreds of Buddha statues here. And each one of them is just beautiful. There are some huge Sleeping Buddha statues, they are magnificent. This is a must visit in Sri Lanka.
Interesting geological formation with paintings on the roof of the caves.  The walk up is quite far but worth it.
I loved the caves in Dambulla. They are now free and definetly worth the climb up. Very beautiful but beware of the monkeys.

First off, there's some confusion about cost of Dambulla online (and outdated information). When we were there, there was no longer an entry fee to Dambulla. We asked our driver to be sure, and he said they were no longer charging a fee. So that's a big plus, but I'd recommend at least making a donation to help them preserve this. The history of the temple is pretty neat, so read into before heading up. The climb isn't bad at all, and even if it gets warm, the caves are comfortable. The carvings are definitely inspiring, regardless of what you're interest is - spiritual, historical, architectural, etc. While the caves seem relatively small, the detail involved is incredible. Definitely a must see.

I thought it was 10 US dollars but when I visited it was free. Get yourself a pair of socks to visit the caves since you can't wear shoes and the floor can be too warm. The views are sometimes even more amazing than the caves. You can buy water (and several souvenirs) in the way.

Five different caves with various Buddha statutes and original wallpaintings in them.  Some close for 15 minutes when offerings are being taken. The walk up to the caves is steep at a particular point early on, but then it's a normal steep climb.  Remember to take socks with you as the ground can be very hot and it's still a little walk from storing your shoes to the main entrance of the site. If you can, have a guide with you in the caves as the wall and ceiling paintings describe lots of history.  Our guide was great as he gave us lots of information.

The cave temple at Dambulla is simply breathtaking! It is hard to believe that such incredible works of art are possible by humans. The long climb is well worth the effort, and one is also rewarded by the beautiful views as one climbs up. Truly, a place well worth visiting!

Great experience visiting the Golden Cave Temple. Please be aware that the walk to the cave temple may be slightly tricky as it is quite steep and uphill, but it is well worth it! Also don't forget to bring a bottle of water!
The temples in dambulla and excellent and we'll worth a visit. Free entry too. Get a lift to the top if you can and walk down as it's a steep walk up.

Stayed in dambulla at sevenrich guest house just around the corner from the caves. These really are worth the effort to visit and show a lovely side of Sri Lankan culture. I was surprised how beautiful they were. Free too!  What a bonus..  Top tip...take a bag to put your shoes in and some old socks to then put on and walk around in as the floor is incredibly hot

Free to enter just rp25 for storing shoes. Ground would be very hot in the day so bring socks. Bit of a climb but nothing strenuous. Not easily accessible for wheelchairs or persons with disabilities. Saw the monkeys grabbing people's food out of their hands so watch out. Worth a visit...nothing amazing though. Each section looked the same. I wouldn't travel to Dambulla specifically to see this site. Tip: You can easily visit here and climb sigiriya rock in one day if you set off early.
A magnificent sight, well worth a visit. The caves and temple are very well preserved and maintained. Certainly worth a couple of hours of the trip.

Dambulla is a small town in Sri Lanka but it is very famous for the caves temple.At the road level there is 3 floors building which is a museum and on the top of the building there is a big golden satue of Budha.(By thw way it is unlikely to to do picture for a person infront of any statue of Budha).On the left side of the museum you can climb stairs to the caves temple where there are 5 caves, each one has its own purpose and name. From the caves level you see a beautiful view over the surrounding countryside, and you see from there the Sigiriya rock.This place as the sigiriya rock not recommended for less than young adults because it has long way up from the museum to the caves but not dangerous as Sigiriya's steps. Enjoy the trip and do not forget a bottle of water, and do not wear shorts,short skirts or sleeveless top.
Really good trip to Dambulla 👍 Beautiful views, good feeling and really beautiful temples. If you on the way to Sigiriya is absolutely must to visit.

The golden Buddha is impressive from a far, but near close you can't gasp (or photo) it. Also the imperfections, like huge wasp hives, are seen when you get close. To reach the cave temple you need to climb a significant number if stairs. The temple is impressive comparing to other Buddhist temples. Foreigner tickets costs 1500lkr, but it is easy to miss the tickets booth and no one is checking the tickets on top. 'storing' you shoes will cost you 25lkr. Overall I recommend visiting it if you haven't had your share of Buddhism attractions yet.
This place is worth a visit. but beware with the monkeys.don't you dare bring some lotus flowers or any food on your way to the temple, just to be safe.

Tourists are just that, they come they see they rush off. Places like this, IMHO are best kept for the reverent believers who come with faith, respect and offerings. Visitors are not permitted to wear footwear and some may find this extremely difficult on one's painful soles. The stone pavement hurt and don't add to a great experience.

Can't agree more with some of the previous reviewers - make sure to bring socks! Otherwise you risk frying your feet because you have to take off your shoes before you enter the temple. The caves were OK, although after seeing couple of them you can pretty much guess what comes in the next one. To get to the temple you need to climb numerous sets of stairs which was not a problem for me but could be quite an obstacle for elderly or someone with small kids. Lots of monkeys make the climb a bit more fun.

Probably because I've seen quite amazing temples in other Buddhist countries like Myanmar or Thailand, but these were at best average. The art is bland and there are quite a few statues, and that's about it.

The climb is long and arduous in the Lankan heat. The temple itself is calm. There is a dress code. No sleeveless and no shorts. Keep that in mind. Carry socks as foot wear isn't allowed and you need to protect your feet in the hot sun

The cave temples are a UNESCO world heritage site. It is a hard walk up especially in the heat and humidity.  However - no pain, no gain! There are five caves. The first cave houses a dying Buddha carved out of stone.  I found this cave particularly awesome. The other caves have images of Buddhas with many different styles of Buddhas. The caves have wonderful paintings on the ceilings.  There are also cave inscriptions from the second century BC. This site is an important historical site and well worth visiting. It is an easy stroll down and take time to watch the monkeys.  Their antics are funny and they are not afraid of humans - so make sure you are not carrying food or other bags. Take plenty of water and socks are a must when visiting this site.
make sure to visit this temple when in Dambulla. you will be amazed by its artistic details and the preservation of the arts within the caves

The golden temple and the cave temples are an absolute must see! The main entrance is right on the main road through Dambulla so you cannot miss them. Entrance to the cave temples is free (guide books tell you its 1500 rupees - this is not the case) however, it is suggested you make a donation. The climb to the cave temples has quite a few stairs so make sure you have some water - would suggest going in the morning because the sun can get pretty powerful in the afternoons. The cave temples are a beautiful site, well worth the visit!

The golden cave temple is a must see on a visit to Sri Lanka, I was in awe of the frescoes and the reclining Buddhas, it is simply beautiful. The climb to the top is quite tough in the heat, so be prepared, but you can stop along the way for a break and watch the monkeys. You do have to take your shoes off to enter the temple and it can be quite hot, a good idea to take some old socks with you. It is free entry, so defiantly a good sight to see. Highly recommended!
What a magical place to visit. I had an amazing experience here that will stay with me for life. Highly recommend everyone to visit.
The best part of my journey. Here you can see hundreds of Buda  statues and get more information about Budism
Well worth the climb to view some amazing Statues of Buddha. Best seen with the help of a knowledgeable guard, the history of the site is worth investing in a good Guide.

The Golden Temple is breath taking from the moment you arrive. The large Golden Stupa as you arrive is a fore taste of the rest of the site. The Temple has a huge statue of Buddha which greets all visitors . Be warned the climb to the main temple buildings is steep and on the day we climbed it , it was very hot with not much shade. Also be warned - Wear socks! you will have to remove shoes before entering the temple and the ground gets incredibly hot.

The Golden Temple of Dambulla is a cave Buddhist temple of the IX century BC., carved into a rock, with numerous statues of Buddha. The stone temple of the Sleeping Buddha is the largest cave temple in South Asia. This temple is a sacred place of pilgrimage for the past 22 centuries. In the creation of the cave temple complex many rulers of the island were successive involved. The temple complex consists of several caves, located at an altitude of 350 meters, and numerous niches whose surfaces are painted with Buddhist murals. The temple is located on a wooded picturesque mountain top. In the church there are 5 main caves and rocky remains of 25 cells. In different caves are 153 Buddha statues preserved, 3 statues of Sri Lankan kings and 4 statues of gods and goddesses, as well as wall Buddhist art with a total area of 2100 m². The temple is the largest collection of Buddha statues, many of which are over 2,000 years old. The temple got his sobriquet ‘Golden’ from the 73 statues covered with gold. Around the temple a lot of monkeys are living. Many of them are very aggressive with a well ‘watch out’ for your belongings. It can happen that monkeys can just grab something straight out of your hands.
of course I will visit I love to see museum of course wax model is perfect ... different type of statu is was amazing I will visit again

We visited on a very hot day and the climb is strenuous, although well worth the effort.  You have to take off your footwear and then walk a long way over VERY hot stones.  The caves are excellent and well maintained.Very impressive.
This is a beautiful place to visit. Very spiritual with so much history. There is a climb to the top but it's worth it. The views are beautiful.

Very interesting caves - really helpful that we had our driver to guide us around. Take care if you have sensitive feet, as you cannot wear shoes & you need to step on stones which are extremely hot!!

Fantastic to see, but has a short climb up to the caves with steps to start with and then steps or slopes. either way tiring ! but well worth it. Take some small notes with you as you will need to pay to get your shoes back ! ( 25 rupees I think )

The first thing you'll see is the huge sitting buddha on top of the temple. Don't be fooled with the majestic buddha, there is a 10 minute hike up the hill to see different buddhas inside the cave. drink and bring water and be careful on your way up, monkey is everywhere. You'll be amazed inside the cave temple, you can sense the spirituality of the place. :-)

Worth to visit this place. On ground level big golden buddha statue is good for prayer. We were aware that it will be a steep climb so we took water and umbralla with us. It was very hot and humid so both help us to climb up. Once we are up in temple worth to visit this place. Its ancient temple with good wall painting. Good place for meditation. Scene from outside is good. Lot of monkeys but  no harm. Banyan tree and Lotus flower pond is good to see. Dr Jain

Worth to visit this place. On ground level big golden buddha statue is good for prayer. We were aware that it will be a steep climb so we took water and umbralla with us. It was very hot and humid so both help us to climb up. Once we are up in temple worth to visit this place. Its ancient temple with good wall painting. Good place for meditation. Scene from outside is good. Lot of monkeys but  no harm. Banyan tree and Lotus flower pond is good to see. Dr Jain

What a climb!  Hot and sticky!  Sweaty!  Worth every drop of perspiration!  The statue of the Buddha, even before you begin the climb to the Cave Temples, is fabulous to see! Lots of pilgrims, devoted and determined make this climb - old people, too!  You'll not see a place like this anywhere else!  Go!  Do it!  Then treat yourself to a liter of cool water and a good rest!

a long walk up many steps and in the heat can be quite difficult remember to take water to drink along the way. the walk from the the shoe counter into the temple can be very painful in the heat as the floor is literally burning. I would advise taking a pair of socks to protect your feet from burns. This is a busy shrine and very popular it is free to get in at the moment. there are many different carvings of buddha as he progressed through his life, definitely worth seeing

We were aware that it would be a strenuous climb, so were well prepared but in spite of it all the heat really got to us. Its hot muggy and the sweat will pour down in buckets. Then you reach the top! Its cool and calm and the temples are repositories of calm. It would have been better if some information is placed near the temples so that we can understand the history, but since its not there read up on the history before the trip. fantastic views at the top.
Exceptional experience in top of the hill. The monkey are prezent on the way. In the summertime the stone floor are verry hot almost impossible to walk without shoes.

A LOT of stairs and very hot and humid but so worth it. Wonderful and spiritual place. Felt like we'd had a shower before we got to the top. Cheeky monkeys all the way up.  We saw one drinking out of a coke bottle!  Lovely view too.  Well worth the trip.
very beautifully painted caves + nice views + free of charge (if you don't get a guide) + cute monkeys

This was our first climb to a temple. It was interesting to see the temple carved in to the rock. You'll need to take long sleeves and pants or a longs skirt up to put on before you go in to the temple. There's a man a the top who'll look after your shoes for a small fee. We were there end of March and it was hot. My feet were burning in some places so take socks to stop your feet from burning on the hot concrete. There were lots of wild monkeys on the way up trying to get food off visitors.
Beautifully maintained, lovely surroundings, no entry fee, really something special. Best to arrive early.

Fantastic.  One of our best visits.  Stiff climb in heat and humidity but so worth it.  Lovely Buddhas, quite spiritual if that takes you, and amazing view too. Don't wear mascara, as it drips off you!  It's beautiful. Lots of monkeys. We saw one drinking from a coke bottle.  Can't upload the photo but it was quite funny.

Temples here give you a perspective on how building architectural wonders would always in the purview of our forefathers. The 5 temples here range from 1 B.C. to 1900s, and the start difference in their quality as time progresses is highly evident.
This was free when we visited which was nice considering most of the tourist attractions in Sri Lanka over charge foreigners. It was an interesting hour. Try to get there for sunset.

The hike to the near top of the mountain can be tidious on a hot a humid day like ours but once at the top the visitor is well rewarded of his effort. From cave to cave you discover wonders after wonders in a peaceful atmosphere. Crowd was not an issue on the day we visited either because in the middle of the new year celebration or dur to the heat of the day. We could only recommend taking a pair of socks with you if you visit on a hot day as walking bare footed on scortching hot slates is another chalenge.
Very well worth a visit. But the climb can be tough in the heat for older people. And you should take socks with you unless you want your feet to be roasted

The hike to the near top of the mountain can be tidious on a hot a humid day like ours but once at the top the visitor is well rewarded of his effort. From cave to cave you discover wonders after wonders in a peaceful atmosphere. Crowd was not an issue on the day we visited either because in the middle of the new year celebration or dur to the heat of the day. We could only recommend taking a pair of socks with you if you visit on a hot day as walking bare footed on scortching hot slates is another chalenge.

When we stopped off at this place by our tour guide, he told us that this place was very high up. The climb was ok but the monkeys. The monkeys were out to get us on the climb! But the climb was worth it. We visited all of the cave temples and the models and history were beautiful! Even the children enjoyed it!
After a nice walk up the hills, passing dogs, tourists and monkey's you get the the cave temples. Remove your shoes and leave with the shoe watcher (RS50) Then prepare to be amazed!

Worth the uphill walk, both the images in the caves and the views.  The detailed decoration in the caves, not deep caves more an excavated overhang, is beautiful. For legal reasons it is currently free.
Well, there are 5 caves filled with buddahs all size. If you have time, you can go there. If not, you will not miss anything important

The best thing about the Dambulla temple is that it is free. It is quite a demanding walk up to the top. We listen to our tour guide and went at 11am but should have gone at 8am as you walk up under the blistering sun. Teh temples are intersting but very over crowded so you loose all sense of tranquility. You also need to remove your shoes and there are lots of sharp stones on the floor so be caereful, would not be good for young children. There are no explanations of what you are seeing so after a while it all looks the same. Don't bother visting the museum, there is nothing worth seeing.
Great place on the top of the mountain. Climbing does worth the thing. The place is packed with Buddha statues
After climbing about half an hour or more, sweating and tired, you see just marvelous place - several (4) big halls full of Buddha statues. Really must visit for meditation.

These buddha's are cool but I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to visit the cave. Definitely worth a slight detour though if you're in the vicinity. Oh and the ground gets quite hot during the day which can blister your feet if you're not wearing socks as shoes are left at the entrance.

We hadn't realised there was a climb up to the caves which was a bit of a challenge in the heat. The view from the top was beautiful and the caves were interesting. It was quite busy and very hot actually in the caves too.

Overnight flight from London and a four hour drive - after the climb of 300 steps felt very relax and calm to be at this Golden temple - the massive caved out sleeping figures of Bhudda in each of the five caves surrounded by many other figures in different poses We were glad this must see attraction was completed before we checked in our hotel to retire Attraction free of charge since March 2016 by SL govt

Nice cave/temple. A tougher walk than I was expecting having just climbed Sigueria Rock. Nice to see but I wouldn't be spending a huge amount of time there. Lots of monkeys and people selling stuff on the way up the hill. Huge Buddah also nice to see on the way up too.

A steep climb to and a mad dash across scorching stones (take a pair of socks to put on to protect your feet) and you enter the rock temple complex.  A series of five caves. Buddhas of varying sizes and poses fill each room and date from 300 to 1000 years old.  The huge reclining Buddha was particularly impressive. An impressive site but hard work in the midday heat.  Never was a water seller a more welcome site.

A religious site, so cover knees and shoulders - and you'll have to remove your shoes so take socks to protect your feet from the hot ground. There is a good walk up the hill to get to the caves - two routes, one a slope, one steps with some shade to catch your breath or enjoy the views along the way.  Not as arduous as the Sigiraya Rock climb as it seems much shorter and there is more shade / space along the way. The caves close briefly in the morning, around 10:30 for 15 minutes or so - so if you don't see any caves, hang around they will re-open the doors!  The 5 caves each have separate doors and whilst the area was busy, none of the caves was over-full, you can enjoy and appreciate the painting and carvings in each - though one is very small so only a handful of people at a time. The golden Buddha statue outside is stunning, and the area below is very pretty with shady areas, flowers and benches. Well worth a visit

There is quite a walk up a hill in searing heat to reach the cave temple, lots of monkeys. The temple itself was interesting cut into the rock with very large lying Budda statues. It's a bit uncomfortable due to the heat and lack of ventilation.

This place was one of the best things I've seen during my Sri Lankan road trip. Five caves carved under a huge 150m tall rock, with plenty of Buddhas statues and tempera paintings all over the walls. It is well worth a visit: the atmosphere is just unreal. Take a couple of hours to walk through all the spaces and admire this wonderful place. Beware there's a lot of monkey in the temples' surrounding. I'd advise you not to feed them.

Interesting Buddhist temple carved in the rocks from over 1000 years ago. A climb up more steps ( after Lion Rock this challenged our legs!!) An impressive array of Budda statues inside 5 rock caves all painted impressively around the interiors. A man guided us around and told us some history for a tip. Be aware you must dress appropriately and remove shoes inside. Also, no photos with people posing with the statues, but you can take photos of the temples without people.

Huge buddhas but it wasn't a highlight.  We visited straight after Lion Rock so thought we were in for another huge climb but you get to the first cave and all five are right next to each other.  You have to take your shoes off and staff wont let you enter without giving your shoes to a person for money to look after but there is no reason to leave your shoes behind.  Put them in your backpacks.  Take some socks so you don't burn your feet on the hot stones.  Some lovely arches for photos.  To visit in the morning costs money but in the afternoon heat, its free.

Seen from miles around this huge Buddha sits at the foot of the steps to the world heritage site of the temple on top of the mountain dating back thousands of years. The steps aren't for the faint hearted or unfit, made harder in scorching heat. Once at the top, the old temple which was carved into the side of the Rock is a surprise, less commercialised and steeped in history, even the original doors are thousands of years old. This shares its sanctuary with a Hindu temple which is equally fascinating- the steps back offer a great back drop for some scenic photographs. Wear clothes to cover your shoulders and below the knee. Useful to wear socks ( no shoes allowed) as the stone flooring gets very hot, I mean burning hot.

A beautifully built temple on the rocks! Worth visting! There are two options for climbing.. Slope and stairs which makes it convenient for everyone! If you are interested in the history...engage a guide!

We were on a trip the day we went to the Cave Temples and it was the last site on our list after a long day. We arrived rather late in the day (just before sunset), but this seemed to be the magic time. As we climbed our way to the top, the sun setting over the horizon, made everything that little bit more special. After passing a few people on the way up we thought we might of been too late but we were in luck. We had the ENTIRE place to ourselves. Enjoyed walking around without the hassle of big groups. Fantastic time to arrive. Would definitely recommend the Cave Temples as a place to see and definitely last sight of the day. Makes for better photos!

Set in three main caves you see hundreds of Buddha statues given by different kingdoms as homage. The caves are very impressive and the view of the countryside from the terrace outside the caves is beautiful. It's a steep walk up a hill - but nothing like climbing up Sigiriya - definitely a site to visit while in Sri Lanka.

From Sigiriya Lion rock it takes you about 20 minutes to get there. When visiting the interieur of the temple you have to wear appropriate clothes (long trousers or skirt) but it's not necessary to go inside. You can only see the statue of Big sitting Buddha which is very impressive, like in Thailand.

Golden Temple, or Golden Cave temple is one of the most important Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka first occupies in 1st century BC. We arrived in front of the Buddhist Museum that looks like a lion with open mouth. The entrance to the museum is in the centre of the building, and you have to pay to visit. Entrance to the caves is on the left hand side and is free. We climbed stairs, the actual temple is 160 meters above the museum. On the  steps local people sell flowers, and local copper and brass trinkets. A lot of very brave and agressive monkeys run from behind and snatch flowers from visitors. From Temple we saw beautiful view of the valley and lake. Under big rocks several entrances lead to five caves with lots of Buddhas, and some king statues. All the walls and ceiling are heavily decorated. Overall very impressive, and you get real sense of great age.

This is the primary temple of Buddha where people of Sri Lanka come to worship. Note it the entry is made free from March 2016 onwards so do not pay anyone. There was a fee of 500 LKR earlier which has been stopped by the Govt. of Sri Lanka. The Musium entry is charged. There are steps climb to reach the high temple where there is sleeping Buddha and the unstopping flow of water. Must Visit again.

Our driver dropped us off part way up the hill reducing the climb by 100 steps, a great help in 38 degrees. Take socks, the floor is baking. Start in the last cave & work up to cave 2, by far the most impressive. We had a local guide take us round, not something we would normally choose but our driver arranged it. The guide was excellent, informative but not boring giving just the right amount of history. Some of the steps are narrow & steep so decent shoes are needed.

Tip: Be sure to pack socks to protect your feet from the hot floor. About 300 steps up (or 150 if your driver knows the shortcut), are the temples. Our guide was excellent, and we learned an awful lot. Be sure to see cave 2, look up and keep an eye out for fishes. If you're sensitive to loud/high pitched noises take ear protection for cave 4, where an irritating noise is protecting the fresco from caterpillars.

These cave temples are really cool, but you must take all footwear off, meaning you will burn the bottom of your feet in the hot stone courtyard! Once you've survived the burnt feet, go to the very last cave and view that first, then work your way back towards the entrance. The detail and colours in each cave is nothing short of spectacular, such a cool place to check out!

This temple is up on a hill.  Sleep walk but worth it.  Watch out for the monkeys on the way since they will help themselves to any loose food items.  Each of the rooms containing numerous Buddhas is more remarkable than the last one.  Very impressive

The Dambulla Caves were not included as part of our travel itinerary, but we asked our driver/guide to take us there after reading about it in our guide book.   I am so glad we did that - it is a site not to be missed.   An intriguing site with wonderful frescoes - some apparently dating from the medieval period.   It's a bit of a hike up the hill to get there - but our driver/guide made it easier for us by taking us half way up in the car!
The climb up to the caves is tiring, but the views make up for this.  Once the caves open, they are spectacular but very claustrophobic if busy.

Dont miss the chance to visit this temple its amazing, carefull with the monkeys hide ur food ! Take water with u and  hire a guide to tell you the story of this temple for about 500 rupies near the upper entrance

Was surprised it is now free entry. The frescoes are in fantastic condition and statues are incredible. We saw many school groups visiting and making offerings. The hike up is relatively easy and do-able by all if you take your time.
Absolutely worth the climb of 600 steps. The Cave Temples are beautiful, full of history and fascinating!

We started the stairs climb towards the temple after 10 and the sun was quite strong already, so don't forget your sun cream. All the way up, monkeys were roaming around; they are always seeking for food. Especially around the fresh fruits sales stands where obviously a lot of people feed them. You can also find bottled water to buy on your way. Ladies must have long trousers or skirts and have their shoulders covered. If you have forgotten that, you can find scarves for rent at 100 rupees (less than a dollar). The site consists of 5 cave-temples. Very spiritual place.
Amazing old temple. Beautiful Buddhas and rock painting. Entry for free. Bring socks with you the floor can be hot during the day

The golden temple is the ground temple for the main attraction in the area which is the cave temples, most of the pictures here are for the latter. It is not that old and there is a touch of politics about it between the locals.

On the way back from Sigiriya, we passed by this temple, and our driver was smart enough to drive us through a shortcut to half the climb, which made the rest easy. Be careful during the climb from wondering monkey if you have kids, they will snatch the food easily. The group of caves, drawings and idols are interesting and rich, worth to get a guide to give more information (if they know what they are talking about). The distance between leaving your shoes and the caves might be longish, especially during midday where the stones are very hot. The place can benefit from more cleanliness.

Beautiful temples rich with history and amazing statues - a small climb but worth it. Make sure you cover your legs and shoulders - also worth taking some socks to wear as you aren't allowed in with shoes - the floors can get very hot so sock are a must if a hot day
Don't want to spoil it just go! Beautiful and moving, the steps aren't that bad and worth the trip. Watch out for monkeys after your food!
It's a bit of a climb for very young kids but at the top the 5 temples can be done in 30 minutes and the number of Buddhas kept things interesting for the kids. It is a "must see" place.

One can feel the gargantuan Buddha the moment you step in the premise. The way up is little arduous but worth it. The cave houses a variety of ancient Buddha statutes. I didn't read about the history. But I could feel the reverence people show for Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Like many other places in Sri Lanka, tourists pay for a hefty ticket price but locals are allowed to enter free. If you are in Dambulla for its historical significance this is a beautiful spot for your curious eyes

A nice, well maintained temple at the entrance and then a walk upwards - possible to manage both for older and young people. If sunny whether bring an umbrella as walking shadow just as all Lankesian does. You have to remove your shoes before entering the cave area. Put them in your back pack or leave them at the shoestand and pay a small fee to the shoeguard. A tip: have socks on your feet since the ground is very hot on shiny days. All the caves look much the same but walk through them all doesn't take long time so do that. Pictures are allowed. Nice views outside the caves. Bring water. If you want to buy a secret wooden box souvenir - which you do not find in many other places - do not buy for more than 2000 rupees.

A nice, well maintained temple at the entrance and then a walk upwards - possible to manage both for older and young people. If sunny whether bring an umbrella as walking shadow just as all Lankesian does. You have to remove your shoes before entering the cave area. Put them in your back pack or leave them at the shoestand and pay a small fee to the shoeguard. A tip: have socks on your feet since the ground is very hot on shiny days. All the caves look much the same but walk through them all doesn't take long time so do that. Pictures are allowed. Nice views outside the caves. Bring water. If you want to buy a secret wooden box souvenir - which you do not find in many other places - do not buy for more than 2000 rupees.

With several interesting and ornate cave temples that were created over different decades, the Golden Temple is an interesting study.  Loads so sellers and monkeys on the path.  Recommend you go at the beginning or end of day (although by the end the school groups are showing up).  When you enter the temple area, start at a the back and work forward to see the positive progression in time.

It was a bit of a climb, we went just before dusk, and there are a lot of steps to endure so take water.  There are monkeys and friendly stray dogs on the steps which add rather than detract from the ambience. As with all temples you should be appropriately dressed, knees and shoulders covered and footwear removed. On the outside of the cave temple there is a pretty white washed building with picturesque arches and a pretty pond. The cave temple itself was a fascinating cultural experience.  A mix of mural cave drawings and huge Buddha statues.  We had a guide with us who was able to explain everything.

these cave temples are amazing - but do take socks!! the barefoot walk is long and you can really burn your feet - the stones are soo hot. there are several caves all amazing,and the climb up to them is hard - but the views and the experience are well worth it.

An awesome location, a decent walk up the hill to see the temple on top. Street markets and plenty of monkeys to see on way up - cold water also. The temple is a really spiritual place and its respectful to take your shoes and hats off. The walk is a short 15 - 20min climb to the top, you won't be disappointed.

We weren't expecting another climb, but it was worth climbing up to see the 5 cave temples which are still in use. The statues and the wall & ceiling painting is wonderful. Don't bother to visit the new temple at the foot of the hill though.
Very interesting, 3 caves of different decades. You have to climb the hill to visit. Beautiful view from the top. Small restaurant and toilet near the parking lot

More than anything we had a little difficulty in climbing the 400 wteps since we are 70+ old, but t was worth it, The paintings and the Statues are well preserved and no wonder it i s a World Heritae site.

The golden Temple of Dambulla is a well preserved Temple and is a World Heritage site. There are many - about 80 caves spread over a vast site amongst which just about 5 of them are,important where you can see, very nice and well preserved paintings on the walls  and many statues of Buddha and a couple hindu Gods,To reach these caves' you have to climb 400 steps, which is a bit srainuous for older people, though it is worth it!

We went to the Golden Temple in the morning the day after Sigiriya.  Given the locations it seems comparisons are inevitable so here goes; Sigiriya is in terms of attractions moderately expensive and the Golden Temple was free at the time we went (our guide informed us this was not always so and may not remain so).  Also the climb up Sigiriya is steep and all steps, by contrast Golden Temple is a far gentler incline and you can choose between steps or a slope.  That is where the comparisons end though and as with all things they are capable of distinction. Golden Temple is easily accesible (comparitively so) and the climb is very pleasant.  The view from the top is picturesque and the temple caves particularly beautiful.  The history behind the caves is fascinating although not explained particularly fully at the site itself so research prior, or a guide is advised.  The most impressive caves are the first ones (the last having been converted by a king from the store room it was initially to house his buddhas) but in terms of completeness I'd advise going from front to back chronologically. We visited relatively early in the morning to avoid crowds which given the sie of many of the caves may become very crowded at peak times.

Well worth the trip out to Dambulla. Grab a taxi from Kandy & they will stop off at interesting attractions on the way. Spice gardens worth a look, we also visited a wood carving workshop. Keep in mind they are all selling something. Feel free to tell your driver no, if you're not inclined to have a look. The cave temples are situated up in the mountain, so a hike up a hill passed a few monkeys to reach the . Covered knees & shoulders required. Shoes off. The art work is amazing dating back to around 4th century BC.  Several caves to wander in, all with subtle lighting creates perfect ambiance.

very sad to see that u have to shell 100 rs for using toilet in dambulla cave temple. mafia is looting people openly and temple management is not doing anything... IMAGINE 100 RS FOR USING TOILET very pathetic state u have to pay money to visit temples.....

Fantastic place with over 150 buddhas in I think five caves. The buddhas are in great shape as they are constantly maintained in a excellent way. The disneyesque golden Buddha in the entrance is something different The stairs up to the caves are a bit steep but there are vendors selling food and drinks if you get thirsty on the way. There are also a lot of monkeys fooling around. When you are up you have to remove your shoes before entering to cave temple, the stones you walk on can be somewhat hot. You are greatly rewarded when entering the caves. The first one is impressive but as you move along to the next caves you fully understand the magnitude of the caves. Not only are the Buddhas impressive but the floor, the walls and also the ceiling are filled with decorative patterns. Best in Sri Lanka The disneyesque golden Buddha in the entrance is something different. At the time of my visit there where a big parties of chinese tourist that unfortunately did not behave so good. There were talking aloud and disturbing the tranquility of the place. The locals have to tell them to keep their voices lower.

Beautiful temples set within five / six caves. It's amazing history and beautifully carved. It's a bit of a walk up hill to get there, with lovely views on the way up. Make sure you take water. These were some of our favourite temples we visited.

Our bus took us up a back route, where there is a well-trodden path around locked iron gates, so the climb from the golden statue at road level was avoided. The rest of the climb is still steep and there are large, jagged rocks waiting to trip you. Why this path isn't repaired with the help of some poured concrete is beyond me, as donations are coming in every day. You have to leave your shoes before entering the temple, but keep your socks on, else the heat will hurt your soles. Once you have seen a couple of caves and the fine statues, the others will seem to be similar. There are good views of Sigiriya from the top.

As with many sites in the Cultural Triangle there are a lot of steps involved here but the site is worth the visit. The images and statues in the caves are fantastic and the overall setting is really nice. The golden Buddha are the bottom is something to see and is one of the largest in the world. As with a lot of sites no shoes are allowed so bring socks as the ground can get hot.

The main temple is spectacular with the huge golden Buddha and the statues of monks. From there it's a steady climb through hawkers and monkeys til you reach the cave complex. The caves have been turned into temples which house many statues of Buddhas and some amazing frescoes on the roofs and rock walls. A really interesting place and well worth a visit!

This place is a must visit but timings of visit should be in the evening as the climb in the sun is very difficult. Climbing is totally worth for the view from top and the paintings in the five temples are a treat to art lovers. Unbelievable that they have remained in such a good condition.Anybody with fair level of exercise can undertake this climb as there are slopes also if steps are not suitable. Over all it takes just about one and half to two hours to climb up, see and climb down. Much easier climb compared to Sigiriya rock temple.

We found the climb very exhausting, having arrived the previous evening, the heat was draining, but it was worth the climb to the top, a must see attraction, but take socks to walk in, and ladies take a cover for shoulders and knees.  Well worth the climb.

The climb up to these caves is a little strenuous - especially if you do it immediately after climbing Sigiriya Rock as we fools did! About one third of the way up the path divides - a sloping road heads right, the steps head straight up. Personally I found the steps easier going up and the slope going back down, but each to their own. The temple is of course a shoes-off place and is *incredibly* hot underfoot, so you absolutely need socks - I saw so many people hopping around with burning feet. There are 5 caves, and following advice from someone on TripAdvisor we started with the farthest and worked backwards, that way you leave the most stunning ones to last. It's useful to take a torch if you want to really appreciate the wall art, but even without you can see quite a lot. The sculptures and paintings are really very special indeed, many of the sculptures dating from the 1st century, although they look much more modern having had dozens of coats of paint or gilding over the centuries.

This was my favourite temple to visit. You are met by a huge Golden Buddha and ornate buildings when you arrive. There is a bit of a climb to get to the top so wear sensible shoes. Once you get to there the views are spectacular and there are lots of monkeys running about to keep you entertained. The caves are very impressive filled with statues and painted ceilings, I loved how the temple fits so well in the mountain. A 'must see' in my opinion.

These caves were well worth the steep climb up to them. The sloped walkway is easier (but slippier on the way down) than the steep irregular steps. Once at the top you will be required to remove shoes, and the stones are hot! Make sure you wear a top that covers your shoulders, otherwise it will cost 200 SLR to 'borrow' a shawl. The caves are amazing, so it's worth having a guide to take you through them. A definite place to visit in Sri Lanka.

Long walk to the top and very busy with schoolchildren when we went.  Going into the caves at the top is interesting - so many Buddhas! Take socks as you can't go into the temple with shoes on so they'll help protect your feet.
My wife and I enjoyed our visit to these caves. It was free the day we went (Sunday) but I am not sure if this is always the case. This probably should be on everyones list when they visit  Sri Lanka

The cave temples are located at the top of a 15-20 min climb on well paved steps. There are 5 small temples in all with numerous statues of Buddha and other deities carved of stone. Apart from the statues you'll find several murals and paintings on the walls and ceiling of the temples. The climb up to this world heritage site is well worth it. The site is outside Dambulla town and can be visited by car. PS: There are a few vendors along the way selling various wares. We bought a wooden carving which was a book with hidden chambers; however, we feel that we were cheated as the vendor never returned the change after our purchase but insisted that he did so. It was our mistake as we got engrossed with the purchase, but just want to flag that one should be careful if shopping here.

Very nice Buddhist temple with amazing prehistoric value. This place located in culture triangle of Sri Lanka. The place is famous among locals and foreigners because of prehistoric value. DJ Travels Sri Lanka guided us to visit this place. This place story began in 1st Century B.C. when it was already established as one of the largest and most important monasteries. Valagamba of Anuradhapura is traditionally thought to have converted the caves into a temple in the first century BC. There are steps to climb up to this cave temple its little difficult but there are many trees beside the way to temple , we can stop and continue our climbing , your tiredness of climbing avoid by the monkeys on your way they are so friendly. When you reach to cave temple in one side you can see famous Sigiriya Rock with beautiful panoramic view and the other side will see a small mountain as my grand mother said this mountain has a nice story. In ancient time to built this temple the King has get help from giant peoples who were in Sri Lanka. They have been worked hard and they needed more rice for food, therefor more and more rice has peel out and putting to this place when passing long time to built this temple it has gathering more rice peels and become a mountain. When you visit this you can enjoy with many of things and stories behind this. Invite to all have get this experience to your life.

We really liked this place ! we enjoyed the way up watching the monkeys and found each one of the caves very interesting and impressive.The temple has a great view.Take water with you and socks can be useful to avoid burning your feet as you will have to take your shoes off.

Basically it rooms filled with statues of Buddhas in various  poses and ceilings painted with even more Buddhas. If you're not a Buddhist you might be a little underwhelmed by the whole experience, especially after a bit of a climb in the heat of the day.  I'm sure anyone can appreciate the artistry. No need to pay an entry fee but you are expected to give a donation. The Shoe Care service is Rs25 per pair. You also need to pay for the toilets. 1 hour is plenty of time for a non devotee visit.

Spend a whole day in this beautiful and meaningful temple in conjunction with the Golden Cave Temple. It will give you a deeper sense of understanding and an inner peace - much needed in today's world.
The walk up the hill to the cave is not for the faint-hearted. Once there it is worth every breath that you spent. Take your time and don't rush through the experience.

If you're a tourist in Dambulla you must visit this place. Make sure to bring something long to wear if you're in shorts or a Tshirt if you're in a tank top or else you won't be able to go in. Also this place used to have a charge of over a 1000 SR but now is free ;)
Across the road from where I was staying there was the temple which you have to walk up a steep hill but its worth visiting as there is a great view and history.

First of, start early. It is a climb to get to the caves and especially if it is hot you want to do them early in the morning. One because of the heat and two you have more time in the caves with fewer people. The caves are full of beautiful statues and paintings, pay especially attention to the ceiling.

This cave temples are surprisingly beautiful. The sight is situated on the way from Sigiriya to Kandy and you can recognize this place by the magnificent gold temple on the foot of the hill. The climb to the temple is a little bit strenuous but much easier then the climb of the Lion Rock in Sigiriya. The view during the climb and from the cave temples of the surrounding area are stunning. The temples itself are also a must-see. There are four caves and the first two are the most beautiful. I would say start with the cave at the end of the temple and work your way back to the entrance, then you will visit the most beautiful caves as last. We liked the second last cave temple the most (or second from the entrance), in this temple you'll find a lot of beautiful statues and wonderful wall and ceiling paintings. If you have the change to visit this cave temples then we highly recommend to visit this.

When had assumed the caves would be at the bottom of the hill and were a bit surprised to have a moderately long climb to reach them ( would recommend hats, sun cream and water - non of which we he taken!) We had a guide who was fantastic, he was able to explain the history and significance of everything very succinctly and really made this one of the best visits of our trip

Quite the climb to get to the caves. Several different chambers with well preserved statues. Many people took time for meditation within the chambers. Men and women have to be covered and they do rent cover, but a surprising price. Once we retreated to the bottom we decided to utilize the bathroom. To our surprise, it was a 100 rupees for foreigners and free for nationals. This is getting a bit much.

Our tuk-tuk driver told us it is for free. Before the caves some local people ask money for watch out your shoes, not necessary, but it is nothing, but help for them. The caves are beautiful, and really hot, that's why a little bit hard to stay in a cave for longer time.
nice trip doesn't take long and you get to meet monkeys.. and of course the temple with many beautiful statues.

We went here at about 9am and it was very busy- queuing to get in the caves was quite uncomfortable. They were quite nice once inside but nowhere near as good as other 'must see' attractions in the cultural triangle. If you are nearby then go early/late to miss the crowds but not worth a trip here in its own right.

The Golden Temple and surrounding area is verging on Theme Park feel but it is well worth moving quickly on to explore the fabulous Caves.  Much more interesting if you have a good guide or guidebook.

One thing - obvious in hindsight - you have to climb up to the cave temples. Tons of stairs in the extreme heat, some in shade, some not but mostly stairs so not actual mountain climbing. Nice views along the way and from the top so definitely worth it! 5 cave temples, start from the far end as they get bigger and more decorated towards cave 1 and 2. Tons of monkeys along the way give to an interesting climb too. The attraction became free of charge some weeks ago. We visited on sunday morning, around 9 and by the time we were coming down(11am) the car park was getting full of buses so its well worth it to go early.

Unfortunately we had to visit this temple after lunch and the huge amount of stairs under the super hot sun was really tiring. If u can choose, come hear early in the morning, as it will be surely much cooler. The temple itself is composed of 5 caves each of which has different cravings and paintings inside. Start from the end, as the fist caves are the most impressive. Get socks!!! U have to take off ur shoes and dress modestly. No water seller up the hill, so bring some!

The Golden Temple was on our to do list and, although we were not impressed, we did not regret the visit. Notes: 1-Make sure you wear comfortable shoes as you will be required to climb stairs. 2-Expect to cross dogs and monkeys as you go up. 3-Local drivers who are not certified guys cannot be with you during the visit.

A hot walk up steps in the midday sun..after the magic of sigiriya, the caves were interesting but would have happily skipped them if they were out of the way. On the plus side entry was free when we visited and the view at the top was nice.
Free entry, amazing art, worth visiting these temples, if your in dambulla this is surely not a miss kinda thing, specially 5 cave temples, they have got great art.

The giant Buddha at the bottom of the stairs is beautiful. Quite a few stairs to climb but there are monkeys to admire as you climb. The caves are amazing. 5 in total. The second one was my favorite with various Buddha's. Everything was so colorful from the statues to ceilings. Great views as well. If wearing sandals bring socks, the bricks got quite hot in the sun.

This was a must on my list and I'm glad I was able to see it. I was dropped off by my driver at the entrance and was warned about the many steps going up, but I didn't mind. If you have water, I would suggest bringing it with you. It was very hot and my only regret was not bringing water with me. There are a lot of monkeys to keep you company on the way up. They don't bother you. There are also a few vendors. You don't have to remove your shoes. There is a small entrance fee and they are very particular about the rules you must adhere too. They do not allow you to take selfies and you cannot turn your back to the statues. So please be aware of the rules as they are very strict. There are five sanctuaries filled with statues. If you are lucky, you may get to see a prayer service that happens during certain times of the day. When I first arrived, there was a prayer service in session. You are not allowed to enter if you do not practice the religion, but it was interesting to see. Even though this place it open to the public, you must obey and respect the tradition and not get in the way of prayer and worshipping. The dress code is casual and their preference is long skirts, pants, sarong and something covering the shoulders. I would recommend this to anyone including families with small children.
Very interesting Buddhist Temple with lots of fascinating history. Worth having a dude to make the most of your visit. NB No hats, no shoes and legs must be covered.
A long walk to visit the caves but well worth it. Very interesting and informative guide who explained all about the caves and status.
