The best cave temples I have seen so far. The temple is situated on a mountain slope and when you reach there, you realise that you have got a treasure. The intricate patterns on the walls and ceiling are mesmerising. The 150 statues of Buddha in 5 caves give a spiritual feeling.

There are quite a lot of steps up but anyone should be able to manage it maybe at a slow pace in the heat. There are lots of monkeys to see along the way climbing the trees and running around but they're not dangerous. The temple is definitely worth the trip I don't think you'd need a tour booked, just get a tuc tuc and ask for a guide on arrival. We saw a local school group carrying out a ceremony with their teacher that was lovely.

This involves a longish walk up (but not as bad as Sigiriya!) plenty of steps,so come early when it is cooler. There are 5 famous caves that are open to the public,full of Buddahs and other religious sculptures
Got here early morning,as it gets busy very quickly. A nice place to see and visit.Plenty of monkeys here to keep you interested.

Very impressive temple, many different structures within its compound, the name comes from a very large dome covered in gold leaf. The most interesting section for me was located high up the hill, accessible via a wide stone staircase that is always full of movement. I have visited it twice in the last 5 years and found it always busy with locals and tourists.

These caves are located a short distance from the town. They are accessed by walking a rather long set of steps. The 5 caves are great to look at especially some of the murals. It is best to start at cave 5 at the end of the walkway and walk back to finish at cave 1 as this way you can see the caves getting progressively more interesting. The caves are actually free which was a nice surprise!!!!

We saw many temples and heritage sites on our 20 day tour of Sri Lanka and this was one of the best. A good slightly exhausting climb to the top takes you to a series of five caves open to the public. They are carved out of the side of the mountain are so are quite dramatic. Large Buddhas some reclining. marvelously decorated caves with lots of history. Does not take too long to visit all five, maybe an hour. Worth the visit.

Four of us after a day of travelling stopped off here for a visit. Lots and lots of steps but just take your time, watch the many monkeys, and prepare for Temple visit. Take off shoes to get in and carefully walk through the hot paving stones. Ok once in and very enjoyable sights. Definitely a must visit!

The Cave Temples are well worth a stop whilst in Dambulla area. A collection of 5 caves dating back over 800 years, this is a homage to Buddhism and the practices of monks. Each cave tells a small story, starting with the youngest (cave 5 at the far end) through to the oldest (cave 1). Each contains Buddhist imagery of Buddha and various paintings. Entry free of charge, this is quite recent since changing hands.

Having started the drive north out of Kandy  early in the morning and with a long day at Polonnaruwa ahead I was in two minds as to whether the stopover in Dambulla was worth it. It didn't disappoint! The walk up to the temple complex has amazing views of the surrounding countryside, and was full to the brim of very cheeky monkeys and their young. The temple complex itself, though much smaller than I expected, was sublime. The beautifully painted ceilings and sculptures are really something to behold. Cultural sensitivity is important at these sights and no flash photography is permitted, nor are photos where the models back is turned on the Buddha statues. Entry is at no cost.
One of the only places where tourists are not charged admission. Nice walk up to the temple. Five different adjoining caves with Buddhas in each.

Your reward for climbing a number of steps is a fantastic Golden Cave Temple.  Be prepared to remove your shoes and hat before visiting the caves.  The walking surface is not too bad, but an extra pair of socks to cushion the feet was helpful.  There is no admission charge to visit the Golden Cave Temple which was a pleasant surprise.
impressive, beautiful. you have to visit but find out with your guide a time when it is not to busy as you will like to enjoy the calming ambience which reigns in this place.

Not sure how much it is to visit here but it's worth a look. Lots of Buddhas as you'd expect and lots of history. Not much to read as far as I recall so the history of the statues, though relayed to us via our guide remained largely a mystery. Just make sure you've visited the toilet before as the one we found next to this attraction was poor - and that's the new toilet, even our guide refused to use the previous toilets.

This is a sacred site with a peaceful atmosphere. It can be accessed by walking though the Golden Temple and following the path up or via a separate path just after the Golden Temple. As it's quite a steep climb, l recommend going early or going for the sunset. There's a spectacular view of the fertile, green plains all around and a few mountains in the distance. There is no entrance fee (for now) and you leave your shoes before the entrance. I recommend starting with the last, fifth cave and working your way to the entrance. The fifth and first cave are the smaller of the five as they are almost entirely taken up by reclining Buddhas, the first being the oldest and the last being the most recent. Look out for the spectacular murals on the roof of Cave Two which depict the temptations of the Budda. Once you've seen these ancient Buddhas, others will seem like gaudy, plastic imitations!

Hot walk up many steps although the monkeys were great. It was difficult to understand the differences between the different caves although the fact so many artifacts are there was very powerful. Wales up the the veranda base of the golden Buddha which was great and super views. Had a refreshing fresh king coconut at the end. It was worth an hour of time en route from Sigiriya to Kandy

After climbing 150 meters in a mix of steps and slope, one realizes it was worth the effort. Five caves with many very interesting figures and paintings. The view of the valley was fantastic. Make sure to take water to drink along the way.

Steep climb up to cave temples but worth it! Take some socks as have to take shoes off and very hot under foot. 5 cave temples with spectacular Buddhas in various positions. Incredible to think they were built many hundreds of years ago.

Planned stop on the way between Elephant Corridor and Kandy, worth the stop & climb in the heat - recommend to get there early! Having done Sigiraya the previous day, this was harder climb (steps & over rocks) to get to top..  stunning experience a would recommend. Shoes are left outside for a small charge, so be careful on the uneven cobbled surface. Several natural caves that have been turnrd into temples with elaborate paintings and statues of deities. The temple at ground lvel is most impressive and it worth the 1-2 hour stop.
Interesting, atmospheric.  We took one of the official guides for 1000 rupees and while the visit was short (there are only 5 rooms to look at) provided much needed context.

The walk to the top is doable by those of varying fitness levels, it's not overly hard. Once you reach the top take some time to enjoy the view over the valley below. Vendors are set up approximately half way up selling water, snacks and souvenirs.

We stopped at the Golden Cave Temple on our way from Kandy to Sigiriya and we are very pleased we did! Even though it was hot & humid - mid 30's (degrees C) when we arrived early mid afternoon last week on Thursday, it was well worth the climb (many stairs) to the top! The interior of the caves are in excellent condition - the frescos are beautiful! The Buddha's are also in a very condition. We were fortunate to miss a couple of bus loads of tourists - as we were leaving, they were arriving….if you would like to avoid crowds, I'm guessing it would be best to get there first thing in the morning and that's when it's also the coolest part of the day! I would take a bottle of water and don't forget your camera! The bonus was that this is now a free attraction!

Its a nice place where people go to worship. Lots of tourist as well. Lots of monkeys. A long walk to go inside the temple. Two ways either clim the steep stairs or walk on the uphil way. I managed to go to the top however it started pouring cats and dogs and we did not have an umbrella. Going back down hill was slippery the only option was to use the stairs. Overall a good experience
This was such a fabulous experience. On a steaming hot day, with sweat pouring, it was worth the discomfort to see this amazing display.
Really enjoyed this Temple. So much to see and very beautiful. Travelled much further afield to see temples only to find best on doorstep.
Very steep climb but impressive caves and collection of buddhas Largest golden buddha I had seen outside.

After a short uphill climb you reach this religious site so shoes have to be removed. There are five caves in total hosting a vast array of Buddhas, other statues and murals.  It is very impressive and the quality of the objects is outstanding. These caves are thought to date back to the 1st century BC when the then King converted them into a rock temple. Subsequent rulers added modifications. The frescoes and the 15m reclining Buddha image are particularly memorable. The quality of the workmanship is remarkable. Outside the caves there are fine views of the surrounding countryside. Of course it's touristy and popular but still worth a visit.

Carved in the rock this temple is a result of a lot of hard work - monolithic Buddhas and very beautiful frescoes decorate the interior, the exterior is in a good harmony with the surrounding. Worth the climb. No tickets needed (for once) but you still have to pay the shoe rack.
Loved this place and well worth having a guide to learn the history of the temple,,, the paintings are increadable well worth the climb up many steps to the caves
Worth a visit a must see in Dambulla while you are there go early or late as very hot during the middle of the day
Well preserved temples.  You need a guide to get the most out of a visit.  There are 5 temples - some fairly small rooms that can get crowded - so pick your visiting time.

Seems odd passing a huge golden buddha that was erected fairly recently and that acts as the entrance to the buddha museum.  Didn't bother going into that (looks a bit disney-ish).  A long climb up to the cave temples, why is there always so much litter and these types of temple?  The caves themselves are stunning - but I can imagine that t can be a bit hectic at times.  Choose when you visit to try and avoid the worst of the scrum.

I was in Sri Lanka for a week and saw many things...many disappointing things.  But the Golden Cave Temple was the most fascinating.  Five separate caves filled with ancient Buddhas and cave paintings.  Absolutely fascinating and unique.  Put at the top of your list in Sri Lanka.

There is so much to see and so much to learn.  Get yourself a guide as you enter, so that you don't miss anything.  The caves can be stifling if there are a loton of people. Remember that you need covering, so choose a fabric that breathes.  Take your time.
If you want some room to move, you might want to go on a weekday.  There is so much to see and so much to learn.  Aquire a guide as you enter so that you get the most from this experience

This visit was really exceptional and very beautiful. Five caves in a row at the top of a short climb with lovely views of the surrounding country side. Raj of Raj Tours drove me there to save taking a bus - great driver and tour arranger at rajtours1@yahoo.com
A temple worth visiting. The statues and paintings of Lord Buddha were awesome. Carry you camera. A half hour climb, definitely worth it.

An unexpectedly long hike up to the Golden Temple and you have to remove your shoes to enter. Once inside, it's actually quite impressive, but I think it's possible that there are a few too many Buddhas - it's really all there is, room to room. The experience may have been dampened by the torrential rain storm we got caught in, but this wasn't the best or most impressive temple I've visited.

On arrival it was hard to know what to make of this World Heritage site.  The Golden Temple is a large, modern looking temple with a huge golden Buddha on top and heavy gold decoration.  It looks a bit unreal and Disney like.  However this is not the main attraction.  There is a short but steep climb up to the top of the hill behind the temple, where a series of caves contain ancient paintings and carvings.  Buddha is the main figure, but there are some Hindu gods and human figures too. You will need to remove your shoes and leave them with the shoe check men before going onto the top area where the caves are located.  The caves are big and well lit and are walked into directly from the outside - the are more like rooms that happen to be natural.  There is no need to go 'underground' or to do any scrambling about.  They are also well lit (artificially) and dry. The paintings and sculptures are beautiful and incredible for being so old.  The caves are really highly decorated.  I found the second and third of five the best, but all are worth looking into.  There are probably good views from the top too on a clear day, it was raining very heavily when I visited. Remember it is a religious site so behave respectfully and keep shoulders and knees covered and remove hats.  Do not take any photographs of people (including yourself) inside the caves, as it is considered highly disrespectful.  You can take as many as you like of the caves and decorations, just without people posing in them.  Flash photography is not banned surprisingly, but out of consideration to other visitors and to preserve the art I would suggest switching it off. The site is well worth visiting as it is unlike anywhere else I have visited and the quality and level of preservation of the decoration in the caves is very high.
The age of some of these is amazing, but there is not a lot of difference between Buddhas!  Would have been a good place to have had a guide.

This temple is one of my favourite places in Sri Lanka! very impressing five carves with numerous Buddhas made of various materials. I was not aware that this temple requires a small hike (but no need for solid shoes, unless it rains on the way down like in our case).

There is also great scenery from the hilltop. One cautionary is not to leave shoes on the patio before going into the site.  We did it as many other tourists did.  We put the shoes along the edge of the patio together with many other shoes.  When we came out, our shoes were not there, neither were most other shoes.  As we searched, we found that off the cliff over 2 meters down there were a lot of shoes.  We couldn't understand what happened.  There were clearly a lot of monkeys nearby, did they do it?  Not likely.  Somebody has to apologize.  So we are sorry for leaving the shoes there.  Why did we have to take off shoes anyway?  Did lord Buddha really hate shoes?  I can't imagine how.
We weren't too impressed with this temple. It seemed a bit monotonous, one cave after another, with similar statues. It was on our way to Sigiriya, so it didn't matter too much. Otherwise, skippable.

Do not take your shoes off too early , there is checkpoint uphills , Beware of monkeys: I saw moncey attacing local woman, so keep eywe on women and children .Wach your glasses. But worth of visit despite of noisy chineese people having very few respect on Budha temple.

We preferred this to Anuradhapura, although it was cloudy it was still a good climb up the steps to the caves We skipped the golden temple and enjoyed the antics of the monkeys that lined the steps The caves were fascinating

Free to visit as of February 2016, as our guide told us the monks had a disagreement with UNESCO and pulled out. We didn't bother with the temple itself, but spent a lot of time with the cave paintings.  They were done with natural paint produced from a certain kind of wood, a process you can see if you find yourself in one of the many carving workshops in/around Kandy.  The paintings themselves are extensive, in five different caves.  It's a bit of a climb to get up to them.

Do yourself a favour and check out this amazing place, even if it does get quite crowded on weekends and especially around midday. Be advised though that its best to start seeing the caves at the far end furthest away from the entrance and then working your way back as this will save the best cave paintings for last

A really nice unique place to visit. Presume weekdays would be less crowded for a visit. There are two paths up the rock which run parallel a few feet apart. One has the rock only with an incline and the other path mostly has steps carved from the rock. Personally I find climbing steps is harder. Its a 30min climb. Unless you have bad knees the climb is not hard. You CAN wear shoes/slippers until you reach the top of the rock! At the entrance to the cave temple at the top of the rock there is a place to keep shoes/slippers for a small fee. The caves with lots of Budhha statues and images are a wonderful sight. It would help to get a guide to explain the historical stories otherwise which the sight might be a bit boring and valueless.

Visited the temple a couple of times while staying in Dambulla: it is a very peaceful (not too many tourists!!) place to relax, meditate, enjoying superb artistic works as well as wonderful views...and it is free :-) !!! Highly recommended!!!!

This is a fantastic temple. Worth the steep climb up. There were elderly Sri Lankan women doing it and I was very impressed. Few things...toilets 100 rupees but will let you in free is smile nicely and they have no loo roll. At the top you need to take your shoes off. The ground is roasting so take socks. If you dont want to pay to have someone watch your shoes  you should take an extra bag to put them in (they wouldn't let us carry them). We went just after lunch and there was about 15 people there!!! Absolutely no one and we could take fantastic photos. When we left at 3pm hundereds of locals and tourists turned up. Looks like 1pm works a charm. On a side note: Some westerners were disrespectful and went behind the bench barriers, I could see it upset the locals. They also thought more about getting the perfect picture than respecting quiet praying locals. If they are praying think twice about wipping out a huge camera as it is a sacred location to them.

This was a good experience if you get there before the crowds. After a short hike up a mountain, past some of the least aggressive monkeys I have ever seen, is an temple from the first century BCE which was built into the mountain. The Buddhas incredibly are craved from stone and had been repainted many times over the centuries. Not as impressive as Sigiriya, but it's nearby so come early, as it is a tranquil and beautiful temple before the buses arrive.

The first impression was overwhelming - a 100 feet / 30 m Buddha. The area around is clean and attractive. I wanted o visit the cave temple but hadn’t had rupees. I asked if I can pay with US$ or EUR. The answer was really unfriendly and no, only rupees are accepted. A friendly answer would have soften my disappointment. So I couldn’t visit the cave temple but went up the hill. The way up is sometimes steep and slippery when wet.

This temple was created in 89-77 BCE era by King Walagamba. However it was modified later kings also. There is a walk to this place which is in incline land. Sigiriya and Pidurangala can be seen while climbing. There are 5 caves with painted with lot of Buddha's pctures. Open time is 7 AM to 7 PM. Beware of monkeys while you going to this place.

We were heading Sigiriya when we decided to stop here and it was such a nice experience! Prefer the golden temple rather than Kandy tooth one. Peaceful, good views, wild and surrounded by monkeys which we liked so much. Oh and also it was free! Before it was around 1000rp but when we went they were painting the Buddha and nobody asked for money, tickets etc.

For a sec I thought I was in China, because there were so many Chinese people at this location. The chanting sound was so peaceful. The Chappals/shoes/footwear will cost you per pair 0.17 USD. The artistic work on top roof is great, and it almost equivalent to ajanta ellora caves. The Statues of Buddha are great and you could wonder how come all this come in so small caves. Must visit if you are in Sri Lanka

The ancient Rock Temple at Dambulla with over 2000 years of history behind is a must do for any visitors that come to Sri Lanka, situated in the center of Cultural Triangle, easy to get by from Kandy, Sigiriya, Pollonnaruwa or from Annuradhapura. You will start your journey at the modern Golden temple with one of the largest Lord Buddha Statues and climb you way up to the rock temples, where you will discover the ancient cave temples, you will be amazed by the artistic capabilities of the artisans who have lived thousand of years back an the creativity, attention to detail that they posses. though the caves and the golden temple attracts many visitors and pilgrims it will give your mind and body peaceful treat. the devotees will offer flowers and worship and the ancient beauty will mesmerize your thoughts and get them in to peace. recommended to where long clothes and white preferably, there are many troops of macaques and wild life can be spotted on the way to the rock temple while climbing the rocks.
Walk immediately up the hill to the temple built in the 'rock'...Enjoy the marvelous view, and the the temple with gigantic Buddha and frescoes on the walls and ceilings....
This is an important place to visit in the cultural triangle.  It is well worth the climb up the hundred or so steps.  Remember this is a sacred place so dress code is important

Walk up a thousand (or more) steps to see these beautiful temples...but you have to be barefoot since they are temples which means do not go in the middle of the day you will likely burn your feet on the hot rocks!  Bring water since the walk is pretty long from the parking lot.  Inside the caves are pretty cool though (temperature).  I would say an hour is more than enough to explore all the caves.

The climb up was actually more rewarding than all the caves, although the paintings on the ceiling are really lovely. I found it horrifying that people continued to take flash photos while the local tour guides looked on.
A much visited temple complex quite worth a visit. Lots of caverns, Buddahs and visiting Sri Lankans, few foreigners. But worthwhile to be one of them.

After a steep ascent, your efforts are rewarded by the magnificence and beauty of colourful paintings you see inside the caves - which are five in number but the first one being the largest. Also adoring in this cave is a large number of statues of Lord Buddha, the biggest one in sleeping posture. If you are travelling from Kandy, this temple appears (cannot be missed) on the left side about 5 kms from Dambulla bus terminal. You can ask the bus driver to stop there itself and alight. Highly recommended for those who love history and architecture

A tip- go early in the morning before the crowds get big and the sun becomes hot. This is an impressive site but be warned there is a lot of uphill walking before you reach the peak and the caves. This is another piece of Sri Lankan history that it is important to see and understand how the various rulers provided homage to there faith. This leaves us as visitors with an incredible site of separate temples within caves (dont worry once you are at the top it is easy to walk around !). Here you have numerous Buddahs of all sizes. In addition you get very good views of the area - on a good day you can see Sigraya (which is a must visit). Don't be put off by the tacky look at the bottom- the exhibits at the summit are very impressive. There are numerous monkeys in grounds but they all appeared harmless.

I had no idea of what to expect and the 2nd cave took my breath away. Although sleeping bhudda is not rare to see the soles of his feet in the first cave are exquisite. The location in natural caves with a panoramic view is truly magical.

Thoroughly enjoyed this. An astounding number of bhuddas in the caves which are all very impressive. The monkeys are very cute! There is a lot of trash just thrown over the walls "out of sight"... but thats the only negative aspect. The hike is not as bad as others say. We didnt pay any entrance fee which was even better!

A wonderful rock monastery above Dambulla village, a 20-minutes walk from bus station and 30-minutes climb from the modern Golden Temple. Be careful of steep stairs and beware of monkeys! Once on the top, you will find the white monastery carved into the mountain (remove your shoes before entering the main courtyard). Excellent views from top. The four caves are wonderful: the first one contains a 14-meters long reclining Buddha; the second (the largest one) has dozens of seated Buddhas, two statues of kings and a white stupa (incredible because it was also carved inside a cave!); the third one also contains seated Buddhas, roof and wall paintings; finally, the 4th cave (the smallest one) is the most peaceful, very good for a short relax in silence. Photos (without flash) are allowed inside the caves, but only TO Buddhas (not WITH Buddhas!). Ticket price is USD 10 (in the morning) and FREE in the afternoon. The afternoon visit has another advantage: the marvellous sunset! My advice (this is what I did): arrive in Dambulla in mid-afternoon, visit the site around 4-5 pm, enjoy site and sunset and finally move to Sigiriya (by bus is only 40 minutes far, ticket price Rs 30-40, every hour until 19.30) and stay there (which allows you to climb up Sigiriya Rock in the early morning). Dambulla is one of the most amazing places you will see during your trip to Sri Lanka. Really unmissable!
It was a great experience for me. Very big temple. For elderly people, it may be difficult to climb the rock.lot of carvings
Must visit place those who are travelling to Dambulla. Been there almost every year and will be going over and over again
Ancient Sri Lanakan pilgrims.. I have been there many times and will be going there over and over again...Feel So peace and get attracted pure Buddhism.

+ Many interesting caves with statues of Buddha and many cave paintings beautifully crafted Great views from the top of the surrounding valley History in abundance - Many steps from bottom to top Timing is opening of the temples create queues

We loved the Cave Temples in Dambulla. You need to take a tuk tuk to get there from city centre but is not far away and not expensive. There are plenty of stairs to reach but once you reach the visit will worth it.

This was the very first stop on our eight day tour of Sri Lanka.  We didn't have any expectation. Climbing the steps in the heat when we were tired from the previous day's journey was well rewarded once we got to the top!  Ancient cave with the most impressive wall paintings and Buddhist carvings. A perfect first introduction to the country!

The temple is worth the effort it takes to get there i.e more than 500 steps of steep climbing... Beautifully maintained and preserved statues of Buddha, along with a Vishnu Dev Temple as well. absolutely stunning view of the surrounding area and the calmness and tranquility of the place will make you feel "I Don't want to leave this place"
A long haul up the steps to the cave temples - well worth it though - caves, views and monkeys make this a fantastic experience. Do take water with you.

Very spiritual and beautiful temple.  The murals and the buddhas in various positions are in great condition and still very beautiful.  As you wonder from room to room, you feel at peace and privileged to be there.

Having visited most of the sights around Anuradhapura and Habarana, this was my highlight! The golden statue at the entrance is magnificent. The walk to the caves is quite strenuous especially if you have dodgy knees but doable if you take it steadily. Handrails to help most of the way. The walk is well worth it as there was so much to see in the temple caves. The statues and artwork were remarkable and in superb condition. I should have read up about them before visiting to have made the most of the trip. Views were great from this vantage point. Best of all it's FREE!
I felt that all the caves were similar. The photos and hype built up expectations that were not met.
Gorgeous temples, definitely must visit. Great view as well! Quite some stairs but not too bad, avoid the heat and go early morning or late afternoon
Impressive collection of Buddha's in the 5 cave temples. A step climb with a big reward. Enjoy the apes on the way up. There is even a little Hindu temple that is worth wile visiting as well.

Not sure if we went on a special day or if they have had a change of heart but the Dambulla Caves Temples were free to visit when we went. This was one of the highlights of my visit to Sri Lanka and even better than I was expecting. The cave temples are well worth a visit - are not like anything else I've seen. USEFUL INFO: If you are visiting on your way to or from a different town as many people do, you can leave your luggage at the book shop for 200rs per bag. Sounds a bit expensive but it's a hassle-free solution for those travelling on to or from Kandy the same day. I was charged a disgusting 100rs to use the bathroom and there were no other options. Also, I was the last in the queue of ladies and by the time it got to my turn it was just me. When I came out of the toilet I found myself locked in and no one around. I had to break part of the door to get out. Wasn't happy.
A good climb up about 600 steps to the caves containing many  statues and a huge reclining Buddha. Watch out for the bold monkeys along the way. Worth a visit!

We came here after visiting the sigirya rock. So temperature was a bit on heavier. Also the steep to reach temple drained us out. So we didn't have enough steam to go all the way up the caves. But we visited temple. It is good
This cave temple with a long history is full of cave paintings and I have always loved to visit.  View over the country from the rock is truly breath taking.

Great little hike up a mountain. Get some lotus before you get up and make sure the zillions of monkeys don't snatch it from you. The caves are spectacular. Lighting and ventilation is rudimentary. Bring a good camera or a torch to see all the beautiful colors.

This is now free, which is good. Don't be put off by the shockingly kitsch museum at the bottom of the stairs, entirely constructed from resin, it rivals Disneyland. The walk up to the caves is tough if you are old or unfit, but it is worth doing. You have to leave your shoes just a little too far from the entry for comfort and wuss or not, the ground is bloody hot in the afternoon, I looked on with envy at the people with socks on. Stunning caves and a fascinating history behind them, the caves with Buddha carved out of the rock are a testament to stone carvers, who would have had the most rudimentary tools. We had the good fortune to be almost alone in these magical and majestic caves. Nasty monkeys on the stairs so do not have food on view.

We were very surprised that we did not have to buy any tickets to this unesco site, even though you can find 1500 Rs price everywhere. Beautiful but very busy. Use the old way out, it is much more interesting and romantic than the stairs. Very quiet there.

Golden temple and rock temple are the same thing.  You start at the Golden Buddha and walk up a steep path to the caves.  It's amazing how they carved the statues from the rock! Lots of monkeys and really pesky vendors who follow you even if you say no. Usual temple attire required: cover knees and shoulders, bring socks for sensitive feet.

After a fairly hard climb of around 4oo steps the result was worth every ache. Monkeys guide you along to the caves where a wonderment of statues abound with great views of the surrounding countryside. Free entry is great to allow all pockets to afford this special place.
Beautiful temple on the rock. Amazing place with five caves. No admission charge. It is worth to come to this hill. Beware of monkeys who are waiting for your inattention :)

One of the best places that you shouldn't miss during your visit ti Sigiriya in Sri Lanka. The golden temple is next to Rock temple and you need at least two hours to cover the area. take a bottle of water with you as you need to climb the rock for 20 minutes (adults age 40 over) if a gloomy day you must carry ur umbrella...

The giant and largest Buddha statue welcomes you to the site.  An uphill hike to get to these caves in the heat and humidity.  The reward was wonderful.  The caves are very impressive.  Many, many Buddhas to see and photograph. Again as with the majority of temples, you must remove your shoes once you get to the top of the hill.  If your feet are tender, take socks.  Most of the Buddhas are made of wood, others are made of sand  and clay.  Beware of the macaque monkeys on the way up and back.  They do not fear you.  There area few vendors if you want souvenirs.  Take water.
Nice historical Temple and atmosphere.  Lots of steps with dogs and monkeys everywhere.  Great view from the top.  No admission fee - bonus but are donation boxes around
don't miss the opportunity to visit these cave temples. Breathtaking! It is worth the climb, you will be rewareded

The Dambulla cave temples, otherwise known as The Golden Temple are a definite 'must see' for anyone interested in Buddhism and the historic cultural sites of Sri Lanka. They get very busy with coach and tour parties so our advice if you are can independent traveler is to get there as early in the day as possible (sensible for avoiding the heat too). It is a steep walk up to the entrance but once there you can tour the incredible 5 caves which have been converted into shrine rooms. The caves are under a huge overhanging rock. They contain a vast array of statues (of the Buddha, gods and goddesses) and paintings and are incredibly atmospheric. The whole complex dates to the first century BCE so is steeped in cultural and religious history.

An uphill walk but worth every step, the temple build into the rock is impressive as are the beautiful and numerous buddhas inside the caves. Would recommend you take socks to put on after removing your shoes as the ground is hot and dusty. Don't forget water & watch out for the cheeky monkeys! We very much enjoyed our visit & would recommend
A must visit. Pleasant walk up through the monkeys to the caves at the top. It was devoid of people when we were there just after lunch.
An easy place to visit but it can be busy because of its accessibility. Take note of the number of buses in the parking lot and choose your time.

A very pleasant walk up (yet0 another hill is worth the time and energy. You will not only enjoy a view of the local countryside near Dambulla but find yourself in one of the more interesting Temples in Sri Lanka.
Many steps up to this cave in the rock, but you are rewarded with over 150 statues of Buddha from various periods.
An absolute must if you are in Dambulla.  Quite a long steep climb but well worth the effort.  Simply amazing.
So much history and amazing views as well. Peaceful and tranquil with so much to see and visit. Take care and proceed slowly

This was our first experience of temples in Sri Lanka and our guide, Jagath, made it possible for us to totally enjoy this attraction. All the information we were given was very impressive. Yes, lots and lots of steps and walking over rock, slow and sure footing is needed for this visit but well worth it.

Good temple in a nice location. You have to climb 100-200 steps and a few slopes to reach the temple. They charge you to take care of your shoes outside the temple Rs 25 per pair (which is clearly written on the signboard) but they asked for Rs 50 per pair from us but once we pointed to the sign they took Rs 25. So be careful. Also be wary of the guides who follow you and start talking about the temple. You can get better and accurate info in the guidebook. Ladies wear something that covers your legs and shoulders. Overall, a nice temple to visit.

The caves have been carved out of huge single rock.The hillock it self looks of single rock.One has to climb more than 300 steps to reach the top to, the caves. It definitely test one's physical endurance. A marvellous carved/sculptured cave and Lord Budha in "NIRVANA", SLEEPING and Meditation postures gives a holy and poise feeling to visitors. Sri Lanka it self having predominantly Budhism following nation, the place definitely attracts people from all sects and historians. A very huge Budha statue and a huge pagoda invites one to the place can been seen from a far distance and the museum are sunjects of interest. The place is well maintained.
Well worth a visit though there are lots of steps which aren't great for the elderly or infirm.   Don't put anything of value down without keeping your eyes on it!

Lots of statues of Buddha in a series of deep caves.  It was interesting but not recommended if you can't handle lots of steps - about 300-400, I think.  Also be careful of belongings - my camera was stolen.

I visited the caves as part of a two week tour of Sri Lanka and it was one of the highlights for me. I'm not a great uphill walker due to an ongoing illness, but I took my time to walk up to the caves and it was worth it. The Buddah statues inside the caves are stunning when you remember how old they are. I agree with other reviewers regarding toilet facilities, there aren't any near the caves and the ones near the entrance aren't great. Make sure you have your own toilet paper and hand sanitiser.

A newcomer to Buddhist art as well as Sri Lanka, I found the cave frescoes and statues a revelation, and well worth the fairly long climb in the heat, and following guidebook advice, went to cave 5 first,the largest and most impressively filled, then cave 2, and then had had enough. But the artistry and faith expressed are amazing.

It is probably the best Buddhist Temple seen with five caves  and numerous Buddha's  and others in praying position. It has been well preserved and is a very special place in Sri Lanka and now run by UNESCO and at the time we visited free of charge. The car park and restaurant at the entrance are quite tacky and detract from the place but definitely worth a visit.

Very interesting place Great views Be aware no toilet on top No water ( need to pack) Shoes are left outside- back pack can't handy Minnie's are very funny, be aware of eating/ trying to eat something- they are well organised and try and still whatever comes from a noisy wrap! Temple is very impressive, beautiful Good library on starting point
Most amazing buddha temple hidden in the caves. The modern temple doesn't worth the visit, but the caves can't be missed!

This cave temple is situated at the top of the mountain and requires a climb of approx. 400 steps. It is worth the climb!!!! The view from the top is amazing!!! The statues in the cave are very special in their size and the way they were carved into the rock. This is truly a wonderful sight...... Well worth the climb to the top of the mountain.

Dambulla Cave Temple is the largest cave complex in Sri Lanka that is under UNESCO protection. It's truly impressive place that is highly recommended for visiting !! There are 5 caves. The oldest one - the Cave of Divine King - belongs to the 1st century BC. All 5 caves have 153 statues of Buddha - standing, seated, etc... !! There are also beautiful and well-preserved wall paintings. It's one of the oldest and important monasteries that is still functioning. You should have comfortable shoes to climb the rock. It's about 20 minutes to reach the Temple. Please, mind there are two ways - stairs that are quite steep (shorter way) and a bit longer way that isn't so steep. There was a rain when we were climbing the rock and both ways were a bit slippery. Shoes and shorts are not permitted in the Temple. There are beautiful views of surroundings when you in the Temple !! There are also a lot of monkeys that are sometimes funny and sometimes annoying. Caves and views are worth to climb the rock and feel the history  and beauty of Sri Lanka !!!!

We visited the temple during our week escape to Sri Lanka and on the way to Habarana. Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site in Sri Lanka. We have spent about 2 hours there after tackling a steep 30 minutes climb. Spectacular paintings inside the caves with many Buddhas in different poses and well-preserved painted ceiling in the Golden Temple that tells parts of Buddha's life. There are plenty of monkeys outside the temple so be careful but the site is certainly worth a visit.

We've spent 2 interesting hours in Dambulla. After paying the entrance fee (at the foot of the hill) we tackled a steep 30 minutes climb to the 5 temples. I was most impressed by the painted ceiling in the Golden Temple, telling parts of Buddha's life. They were very well preserved (retouched, no doubt). Also the miriad of Buddha statues was quite nice.

seen form the outside it seems a bit excessive but it's really worth visiting. first you go up to the temple, which is carved in a rock, where the buddhas await for you then you can visit the museum, which is interesting too

Most unique temple I have been to in Sri Lanka. The ceiling paintings were cool to see and there are so many Buddhas. Very pretty view from the top of the mountain. The temple itself is free to visit. The cave temple is to the left as you approach from the bottom. Worth the stop. Tips: 1. Make sure your knees and shoulders are covered or you may need to pay 50-100 rupees to borrow some fabrics. 2. When you are close to the top, take off your shoes and carry them to avoid men trying to take your shoes to "watch" them for money. No need to pay them, just carry your own shoes around. 3. Be prepared for lots of stairs to the top. Would not suggest if you have health problems with walking up many stairs. 4. Apparently there is a fee to park in the lot that they do not tell you about. 50 rupees. 5. Bring water as it is very hot up there!

This is a world heritage site and a must do if you are visiting Sri Lanka. It has about 153 Buddha statues but each one is so unique and exquisite. It has been maintained well not just in terms of cleanliness but the lighting is also just right. The was a good walk to the top. Not too long and exhausting as Sigiriya. We had our 6 year old son with us and he enjoyed it too. Please remember to take enough water and few dry snacks as you don't get anything till you come back down. Also sun hats, sunscreen and a pair of socks is a must (shoes aren't allowed inside the temple and surrounding premises so on a hot day your feet might get scorched). The King coconut at the entrance after you are done with the climb is a must!

We visited straight after Lion Rock, Sigiriya, and were pleasantly surprised to find that after 8 January there was no entry fee (not sure for how long). Yes, it is a bit of a climb, but not as much as Sigiriya. Shorts above the knee are not permitted for men and women, there are a number of hawkers selling trousers on the way :) Shoes are not permitted and there is a man at the entrance to the temple who will look after them for 50 rupees a pair (£0.25). The temple itself is not an expansive sight, but very nice to look at. There are plenty of monkeys outside the temple. Certainly worth a visit.
Well maintained place. Good to see the 5 caves from nearly 2000 years ago. The climb up was made easier with well maintained stairs and pathways.

Wow you arrive and best go with a guide to get all the history . The golden Buddha is so big when you first arrive . Again it's amazing how this was built all the way up the rock . It's a good steep climb up stairs in hot weather it's challenging but fun . We were laughing at the monkeys on the way up they just play about at your feet . When you get to the top the views are spectacular . It is amazing how the caves are built into the side of the rock and all the statues are made of stone and how it all looks so well preserved . Photos are forbidden if you pose in front of a Buddha with your back to them .but you can take photos . Amazing experience . Definitely worth the money and again dress code is knees and shoulders covered .

An interesting site up a fairly steep climb.  Spectacular paintings inside the caves with many Buddhas in different poses. The gentleman at the entrance desk is one of the unfriendliest people I ever came across in Sri Lanka though!

Try not to do this in the midday sun like silly me! It was very hot and a lot of stair climbing. Once at the cave you are transformed to a different world. Was stunning. Remember to start at the end and work your way back to the first doors (cave 1)
beautiful buddha scuptures and ceiling paintings. We got there very late in the afternoon when most people have left already so we got the caves all by ourselves to enjoy

The caves are stacked with effigies and paintings of great detail, colour and quality. They are ancient and it is hard to see how they could be captured in such detail when times were primitive and they were completed in a cave without decent light.  Hats off to our forefathers!

The temple is just so tacky. By contrast the caves are filled with gorgeous effigies and ancient (1,000 years old) paintings of exquisite beauty and quality. Pretty sharp climb and be warned the caves get hot so dress comfortably ( gents need to cover knees) and be prepared for crowds if you can't get there early. We had a tour guide who told us the significance of the paintings and really added value to the experience. Highly recommended.

At the extreme left when facing the temple complex you will find stairs to the caves. It is quite a steep climb. Not sure of how many steps but maybe takes around 15 mins to reach the caves. It was raining when we went so quite slippery in some sections. You need to ensure that your knees are covered or else they will not allow you. No shorts allowed. The murals on the roof of the caves was interesting and there were several Buddha's spread across 5 halls in the cave complex.

It's in a large complex and you have the view of the Golden Buddha looking down at you. The steps on the far left takes you to the caves but right next to that there are steps where you can go up to the complex of the golden Buddha and worshippers give their offerings.

We visited on some sort of significant religious day and were mercifully subjected to free-entry, so our overall experience of The Golden Temple was entirely positive! The caves are wonderfully decorated with paintings on all the walls/ceilings and giant statues. Photographers: bring a tripod!

We visited on some sort of significant religious day and were mercifully subjected to free-entry, so our overall experience of The Golden Temple was entirely positive! The caves are wonderfully decorated with paintings on all the walls/ceilings and giant statues. Photographers: bring a tripod!

This place has a touristic outlook to it, with not so clean courtyard or the usual cleanliness you see around Srilanka. The heritage property is very charming though and not to be missed on our cultural triangle tour in SL. The murals are wonderful.
This ancient cave temple is well maintained and is a must visit on a trip to Sri Lanka. The large statues and the paintings dates back to hundreds of years and are certainly a must see.

This is the first thing you'll see when you arrive at the Dambulla Cave Temples. The Golden Buddha is massive and you can probably see it from quite a way away. We didn't go inside but the entrance to the cave temples is round the side of this. You can walk up on top and have a look down. That's about it.

Thoroughly enjoyed the experience.  I was under the impression that it was 1500 Sri Lankan Rupee entrance fee.  It turned out to be free - I went on a Sunday (don't know if that makes a difference.  An unexpected and pleasant surprise. There is a reasonable climb to the top - although saying that - it is not too much for even the unfittest of people.  A little effort required that's all. The cave temple has great extended views and some wildlife in the form of macaques on the way up.  The temple itself is spread over 4 or 5 entrances over about 100 metres or so.  The walls have paintings of Buddhas and there are many Buddhas spread over the 4 or so caves. The experience should probably take about 1 and a half hours or so.  Worth the effort, saying that though, it is worth noting that you are around 2 hours from Kandy to the site.
Dambulla Rock and Cave Buddhist Temple is situated one and half hours from kandy. you can see very ancient arts in the cave. your next destination should be Sigiriya rock castle.
This is a stunning place to visit - though be warned - it's not a cave underground - but you have to climb a lot of steps to get there - not for the faint hearted - or unfit.  But worth it. Beautiful

1500 rupees and a tiring climb up the mountain with garbaged surroundings reveals several dark and neglected caves with several modern / repainted Buddha statues. Unless it has a strong religious meaning for you, skip save your time for more interesting places in the area

1500 rupees and a tiring climb up the mountain with garbaged surroundings reveals several dark and neglected caves with several modern / repainted Buddha statues. Unless it has a strong religious meaning for you, skip save your time for more interesting places in the area

The intermediate difficulty walk up the hill is certainly rewarded with these striking temples. The drawings are impressive but a little hard to see--dark cave  A good guide or guide book are essential to appreciate the narrative and symbolism of the representations.
I would suggest to start from the last cave, so that you can leave the largest one (which is the second one actually) among the last ones.

To the side of the Golden Cave Temple you'll find so many steps that lead up to the Cave Temples. There 5 in total and each one gets more and more impressive. Its amazing to see such intricate details in the cave formation as well as the statues inside. Definitely worth the walk up. There#s many steps and you have to walk up in bare feet so be warned!

Very interesting place. The slight climb up the hill is absolutely lovely and you can meet monkeys, squirrels on the way. The temples themselves in the caves that you reach after climbing are fantastic evidence of art. The drawings in the caves are exquisite. A lot of Buddha statues surround you once inside. Peaceful and lovely place on top of the hill.
Had to climb one and half kilometers to reach the destination but it was quite nice up there with a great view

We went to this cave temple not really knowing what to expect. And still we were disappointed. With the costly entrance, we did expect the place t be cleaner. We are nu culture buffs but still were unimpressed. take a backpack so you can take your shoes with you and for women have some cover for the legs or you won't get in.
The entrance fee of 1.500 Rps. is at least too expensive for what you see. The outlook from the hill is nice and free of charge.

A short (but steep) hike and a small but peaceful temple. Go into any of the rooms and you will see thousands of Buddhas and relics jammed into this place. The tranquility of the venue is a stark contrast to the jumble of art inside the temple.

The caves are just a delight. The drawings and paintings are exquisite. The colour and pattern on such a rough roof and walls is spectacular. I am genuinely surprised that there are any reviews that suggest this isn't a MUST see in Sri Lanka. A real highlight for us.

This place is total garbage. Plastic bottles and other garbages all over the place. It is a total disrespect for Buddha and for the visitors compared to the expensive amount paid (10$ ticket entrance, same price as the Louvres museum)
Climb a lot of steps. See lots and lots of Buddha's in caves on top of the hill. If you like buddhas and steps this is a must see.
Do not miss this! A wonderful place to go back in time; Amazing colors. Amazing art The only inconvenience is the long way up .
The hike up the hill to reach the temple is a good exercise, the place is interesting for the first 10 mins then things begin to get repetitive.
Had a good driver/guide who gave us a lesson in Buddhism. The temples are very hot inside, so don't stay too long in there!
It's a climb. but worth it, even if you have to fight against the stream of locals that go there over the holidays. Cover up....

It was quite a hike to the top of mountain in hot weather, but temple itself was really worth seeing it. Take some old socks with you, as you need to take off shoes entering temple territory, but the pavement is really hot.

I've followed Buddhism for some time now, which made me eager to visit the Cave Temples while visiting Sri Lanka. The pictures, however, don't do it any justice. Warning for those with dodgy hips, there's a lot of steps - 600 odd. It was a warm day and I needed a few dabs of the old handkerchief on my furrowed brow. But once you get there, five different temples, carved out of the mountain, provide jaw dropping excitement. The Buddhas are fascinating, especially the four large ones in resting or nirvana position. Make sure you do this if you visit Sri Lanka, it's proper decent. It's the waaaaaaaay. It's the way it's the way.

There are two sites listed in TripAdvsisor for Dambulla.  One is listed as #1 destination and labeled Golden Temple, the #2 destination being called the Cave Temple.  This is unduely confusing as there is only one site.  Furthermore the image provided for the Golden Temple is an image from the cave at the top of the hill with a stupa was built in the 5th century AD. So  the two entries should be merged. Do not make the mistake of staying in the buddhist complex at the bottom of the hill.  That is the more recent, more shiny part, complete with a tacky looking Buddhism museum and a center of religious management including a radio.  Where you will want to go is up the hill, and requires paying a fee.  But both your financial and physical efforts will be richly rewarded. It is indeed the largest and best preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka, hovering some 450 feet  over the surrounding plains. The site is beautiful,some of  the statues and paintings in these caves date back to the 1st century BC.  And the murals and ceilings are beautifully covering the raw cut lava rock.

Well worth the trip and the hike up the hill. It is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka, and an amazing site with five caves under a vast overhanging lava rock populated with statues of Buddha and bodhisatttvas, gods, and kings, under sprawling ceilings with intricate religious paintings adjusting beautifully to the unequal rock cut.  A beautiful view from the top over the region.  A peacefull atmosphere.  Quite a contrast to the tourist oriented site at the foot of the hill, complete with Buddhism museum housed in a tacky pink creature architecture.  Entance osts for the cave temple.  Need to remove your shoes
We are talking about caves century I bC which is amazing!! You have 650 steps until the top but it will worth it. Do not forget to dress properly because it's a temple.

Visited with the family and even the kids found the caves fascinating.  Not too large, but there are many well-maintained statues of Buddha and murals to see.  The views from the top are also breathtaking.
It's one of the few things to do in Drambulla but but worth the visit. A sacred site and fascinating how all the Buddhas were arranged in the caves.

Officially it is possible to check your luggage at ticket sales counter.but it cost 200Rs in addition to expensive entrance fee.But the locals said there are a hut for the security guard which is located about 40steps from the bottom, and you can check your luggage for free.

Dambulla is a beautiful place enriched with so many hills, valleys, pools, and agricultural lands etc.  This place is internationally known because of the cave temple.  These temples are monasteries of Buddhist monks since first century.  The height of the rocky mountain is 600 ft from the bottom land.  The contributions from the rulers of SriLanka in different centuries made this temple in such a way.  There are many intermittent steps on the slop of the mountain to reach the top. The cave temple is very attractive.  There are five main caves in which the statues and paintings are displayed.  These five caves are made under a single roof.  Most of the statues inside the caves are Sri Buddha’s, some are Vishnu, Ganesh , and few of them are those  former kings of Sri Lanka , contributed much for this construction. At the bottom of the Rock there is Golden temple which is now acted as a museum.  This archaeological site is considered as  world heritage center by UNESCO in 1991. The very attractive part of the Golden Temple is the 100 ft high gold plated Buddha statue placed on the top of the museum.  Even though the cave temple and monasteries are centuries old the golden statue is made few years ago.
We made this trip from Sigiriya. It is only 30 mins from Sigiriya. You can also visit here if you are travelling from Sigirya to Kandy - it on the way.

Visited here on a very rainy day but it was still really worth the trip and the climb. It is quite a steep climb but taken slowly it is absolutely fine and probably takes around 20 minutes. The caves are truly fascinating with an incredible number of Buddhist statues. They are in really good condition and very well looked after. There are people selling and touting on the way up but they aren't too persistent and in no way are they annoying. A definite must see if you are in this area of Sri Lanka
The cave, the art, the status, the objects, the ambiance takes you back to the age it was created. Remarkable photos are guaranteed ;).
Some of the best heritage observing sites in Sri Lanka. Amazing environment and an amazing view from the temple
Guidebooks will suffice. Bring a bag for your shoes, donate for a blessing. Toilet facilities for women don't have tissue or flush. Just be prepared
Great stop with food, refreshments and quiet places to sit.  The temple and caves are very interesting.

The caves are quite interesting although a little repetitive. The frescos on the ceiling and walls were impressive as were the enormous statutes of the ruling Buddha. Ladies remember to cover up shoulders and knees. You need to leave shoes at entrance and it is recommended that you leave them with the shoe racks as the monkeys are very brazen. I put my pack down for a moment to rest and a monkey made an attempt to snatch it....it got aggressive when challenged. Finally buy your tickets before you climb ... It is a long way up, many stairs and slippery rocks (after rain). Photos can be taken inside the caves. It is a little pricey but if authentic, the caves are impressive.

The caves offered a series of rooms with statues in them. The first one was fine enough, but room after room, each room/cave showed similar statues. I tried to find some information on the history of the statues, how they came to be where they are, where did they come from if they were placed here, but I could not find anything. It just seemed a bit made up. After climbing what seemed like a million stairs in intense heat, I was disappointment not to see something more historical and profound, to be honest. They should include more history and details to make this trip worth it. Especially since you have to buy a ticket for 1500 for each person. Also when you get up there, they ask you to remove your shoes but offer no options for people who might not be wearing socks (like me). I almost burnt my feet walking on the hot ground. It was very uncomfortable and definitely took away more of any possible charm for me.

on the way to Sigiriya by bus we passed "Rangiri Dambulla Rajamaha Viharaya" and in the bus there was nice song abut this temple. That makes us to visit The Golden temple where the meaning of RAN is gold. Is is a very old temple that is why it called rajamahthe clergy.

Perhaps poor prep on our part but climb is steep and, in humidity, a little tough. We stopped here on a traverse from Kandy to Trinco but if you make a 4 hr round trip to here and you can't climb the stairs (as my wife could not) then you may be disappointed. You can enter the lower modern temple which is free. LKR 1500 pop for the cave temples plus 25 for your shoe storage. Temples ate well worth the effort and fascinating. More expense if you want a guide (plenty available) otherwise you guess or pre-read the guide book!

This was the 5th day of our Cultural Triangle trip. We hired a car with driver and visited all the beautiful places in this area. This will sound spoiled, but this place just ranks lower compared to Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa and Sigiriya. The temples are truly beautiful of course, but there is very little variation. There are just so many Buddhas, after two temples you just loose track and count and (sorry) interest. The big sleeping Buddha in the first cave is a master piece and it's difficult to imagine this whole statue is carved out of the rock it is still part of. This is amazing. Overall this place just brings too little of variation.

It is claimed that the cave temples here are very old, but even though as a visitor you pay a steep price to enter (remember - buy your tickets at the bottom - 1500 rupees) once you are at the top you have to leave your shoes and on exit pay yet another fee for the shoes....  (Sri Lanka is all about those tourist fees!). The temples are "interesting" if you like looking at Buddha sculptures, but unfortunately there is no information available at any of the temples to tell you more about it.  No dates, no explanations.  Even Buddhists don't know what some of the figures are.  The only temple which appeared to be in use was one of the first ones, which was dedicated to Hindu gods and had priests in there doing ceremonies and blessings.  The rest was more like a museum, but without information ..... The views from the top is spectacular ... but you can get that without buying a ticket. The climb is steep and long, but doable with children and there are plenty of space to rest.  And many vendors keen to sell you trinkets you have probably seen everywhere else in Sri Lanka too....

This is a beautiful set of rock cut sculptures painted in hues of gold and other colours. They depict the Buddha at various stages of his life. The intricacy with which these have been carved from sheer rock face is astounding, given the rough terrain and lack of technology in those times. There are a lot of steps to climb and monkeys to look out for.
They chargr 2500 srilanka rupees per visitor so I suggested dont waste money on the museum just have a walk and take pics in the free area,all temples look same there no big difference

Remember to buy a ticket before you set off on the climb. It can be slippy in wet weather, but well worth the views. Do take something to cover arms and legs. Shoes will need to be left before entering. There are several cave temples, each one better than the last. Great history and art work with a totally feeling of solitude. So good to see an electric fence to ward off the monkeys. If you are taking an offering of flowers do watch or the monkeys will try to take them. A good experience for anyone wanting to see many statues with history.

5 cave temples carved into the rock.  15-20 minute walk/climb up stairs.  Beware of monkeys and sellers. The ticket includes a visit to a museum but the museum is not worth your time - a lot of replicas; half the exhibit is about Buddhism around the world.

It's worth walking the many stairs to the cave temple (even in the heat). The only thing to need to be aware of is the monkeys, if you buy flowers near the entrance it's like placing a sign round your neck saying 'come and get me'. The cave temples are well worth it, with drawings on the roof/walls and many statues. Just take your time to look around and take them all in.

The goverment should be ashamed at charging such ridiculous entrance fees! For this reason alone i would give it a miss as there are so many beautiful temples around to enjoy without leaving a huge whole in your pocket, especially if you are travelling as a large family

The Golden is wonderful. We have been there late afternoon and after visite we sat on rock and watched sunset. You can watch the sunset without entering. Just claim the steps up and watch if you don´t want to go inside.

As most places in Sri Lanka, non Sri Lankans get ripped off paying a huge anount of money for a temple which should be free or donations. This leaves a horrible taste in the mouth and we felt irritated by this. Yes, by all means charge us a bit more but not a huge amount more. It put me right off Sri Lanka. It seems it is all about making money at the expense of people from abroad who have co e to enjoy a country. Some of the places are also UNESCO funded so there is no need to take this kind of view. We met lots of people who felt the same way. Come on Sri Lankans, stop ripping is off. It does not make us like  it. There are a lot of steps to climb and a lot of dogs and monkeys on the way. Overall, I don't think the p,ace is that good. The views and the breeze were good.
This is a once in a life time experience. You must check it out. Bring water and cash. This experience is not free.

Be prepared to climb steps with lots of friendly monkeys in attendance. The Cave temples themselves are fantastic. Some of the guides there did not look too happy with tourists taking pictures-those photos are allowed. Loads of parking space available. Loos are only located downstairs near the ticket office & are filthy. Take your passport if you come from a SAARC nation to avail a 50% discount.

We went to the Cave temple shortly after visiting Angkor Wat in Cambodia, so I guess after that every temple is kind of ... unimpressive. Nevertheless the view from the top was very nice! I would recommend to just climb up the hill and to not buy a ticket to the temple but just enjoy the view!
really astonshing place. like every other temple do not take photos of people in front of 'holy items'. funny how ancient painting are better preserved than recent ones.
Steps up to the five temples. Read up about the caves before you go to fully appreciate what's on show. Fantastic..allow plenty of time to view. A must see !
The cave temples are a magical place full of ancient spirituality. If world peace could be summoned in one place, it might well be in these temples.
Had a good climb up to the cave temples, ut worth the climb! Lovely statues in the caves and beautiful sights! Love the peace and serenity there.

Its a great attraction, except they charge any foreign visitor Rs.1500, which is sad, given this is a buddhist temple and one of the principles of Buddha is not to have attraction to wealth, however this temple just does the opposite. I would rather this changed to a donation than a mandatory fee/ticket!!

The Sri Lankans of the yesterday years must have been a fit lot! Quite a steep and long climb but in the end rewarded with a panoramic view of the area and a series of remarkable caves with original frescos and Buddha statutes - some dating back several hundred years. Only criticism is that the lighting could have been better; the caves remain somewhat too dark to appreciate many of the paintings and carvings.

Very well preserved temple. With caves where statues are standing along the walls most impressive are the well preserved fresco's in the ceilings. Impressive is the big budha on top of the budha museum next to the entrance of the rock temple. Nice detail is that on the right side of the museum stutues of monks are posed walking towards the temple along the rock wall
How wonderful! After an uphill walk of 30 minutes you arrive to this wonder of the world! Be sure not to miss it!
Amazing peaceful place with numerous beautiful buddha statues... Gives u a feeling of peace and calm.. Dont miss it, for whatever reason ever if u come to lanka

V went to dambula after sigirya, so even the 300 odd steps were difficult to climb.. But at the end it was worth it.. One if the best religious places to see.. plus the buddha cave statues r amazing. It was drizzling when v went.. but still happy that v didn't give it a miss..
We were going to give Dambulla a miss. So glad we didn't. Stunning caves and ancient art work. A nice short excursion from Sigiriya.
Set on top of a hill inside the cave this temple is just breaktaking The walk up is an easy scenic hike The view from the top is beautiful!!
Awesome experience at cave temple very picturesque though on a little height but worth visiting and exploring history with magnificent status of Lord buddha

These Vave temples are situated above the Golden Buddha temple of Dambulla. You can either climb steps or walk on the road to reach this site. These are  Ellora caves type structure with so many idols of buddha in the caves.
It is the temple dedicated to Lord buddha. It has huge idol of Lord buddha and beneath it they have Museum.

It is a bit of a climb to get to the temples, but there are proper steps. The 5 cave temples are all filled with Buddha statues and paintings. I’ve visited other cave temples in South East Asia, but this complex is certainly one of the most beautiful I’ve seen. Recommended. As this is a religious site, your knees and shoulders should be covered and you have to leave you shoes outside the temple complex. Socks are allowed.  If you decide to leave your shoes at the attendant with the shoe rack, the price is 25 LKR.  There are a lot of monkeys running around, so take care of your belongings. The entrance price is 1500 LKR.
Despite the long and tiring climb to the temple, it was most worthwhile.  The architecture and sculptures of Buddha are awesome and inspiring.

The caves are as old as 2000 years. There is a climb of around 300 steps to the top. The view is very nice. The caves themselves have been maintained very nicely. The outer facade is painted white and the place is clean. There is dim lighting inside the caves so that the paintings and statues can be seen. It was a very peaceful experience. Definitely worth a visit.

This is a bit of a climb however gaining insight is never an easy thing. There are two ways up and down, by ramp or steps. At the bottom its a little bit crass with a large screen TV on a wall of a TV station and restaurant  that we were informed was owned by a monk. Sort of made me think of US TV evangelists. There is then a large modern (relatively ) sitting golden Buddha next to the TV station. There is an entry fee which you pay at the entry level. You can then start your climb passing through a layer of trinket sellers. Shoes have to come off at the top (there is a shoe store which holds your shoes for a fee) and suitably modest clothing should be worn. Once you get to the top you hand over your tickets to gain entry to the caves. The number, size and nature of the Buddha statues is impressive. There is a reasonable view of the surrounding countryside at the caves. Impressive simply to see what human beings are willing to do for their spiritual leaders. If you are a Buddhist this would have far more meaning, to me a non Buddhist it was an interesting walk but not very enlightening but that's my fault not the Buddha's .

We really enjoyed our trip to the temple it was close to where we were staying so was a must visit. The climb up was good (though definitely recommend not wearing jeans!) and we saw lots of monkeys which was a great bonus. At the top you have great views of tge Sri Lankan countryside and can even see sigriya rock. You must enter the temple barefoot and can leave your shoes outside for 25rps, oh and don't forget to get your tickets at the bottom for 1500 rps... The temple itself is made up of a number of small rooms with various depictions of Buddha its short visit (we only spent 30 mins in the temple itself)  we didnt have a guide but there were plenty there if you need or would like one. All in all a nice morning activity with monkeys and some culture.
The outside of the cave temples are beautiful but actually not a great deal to see inside the caves.  Also pestered quite a bit on the walk up the hill by people trying to sell stuff.

To reach the temple, you need a lot of breath. The walk (a long staircase) is all uphill, but when you get upwards the show is unique. Outside the temple looks small, but entering the rooms you understand the big job that the monks did, digging caves inside the temple.
Really good temple built into caves. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you are passing or going to Sigiriya rock. 1500 rupees entry ticket.

First off, the climb up to the caves is not difficult. There are proper steps or paved pathways mostly and you can just stand to the side and take a short breather or a long one while enjoying the view as you climb. At the entrance to the caves, you have to proceed barefoot. There is an attendant with a shoe rack where you can deposit your shoes for Rp25 or stuff them in your bag. There is a complex of 5 main caves, all of which are open to visitors. None of them are particularly big but all of them contain statues and frescoes. Some lighting is provided inside so it’s not difficult to take pictures. Most of the statues and paintings look to be in very good condition despite their age, so presumably some restoration work has been done. Of special interest is the largest cave where water dripping from the cracked roof is said to be holy and the water was running upwards along the roof, although that was somewhat difficult to make out. Outside the caves, there is a nice view of the countryside and plenty of elf-eared monkeys running around. We spent about an hour and a half at this location in total. It’s certainly worth a visit especially for the frescoes, which are in better condition than others I have visited across Asia.

The country has many many temples, all very expensive to visit and not many are worth the visit. This one is on top of around 35 steps and is really interesting. Of course you need to take out the shoes and leave them outside after paying a small annoying fee...

We went there after the Sigiriya  rock fortress and it wasn't in the same league. Many of the paintings and statues appear to have been touched up extensively . Large number of monkeys who sit on the steps leading up to the temples. Worth to visit there and can get a different experience with caves.
The temples are a nice thing to see in Dambulla, but are overpriced and overrated. I was expecting more.

The stairs seem never ending but there are touts on the way up selling mango and drinks, as well as the usual tat. Just make sure you buy your ticket at the bottom before you climb! Guides are available to show you around but not necessary as the carvings speak for themselves.
The Golden Buddha is beautiful and can be seen from the ground, but if you buy a ticket then climb up to the caves, the amount and beauty of artwork is astounding.

Nice location. Worth a visit, particularly for the nice ceiling paintings and the variety of Buddha statues. Nice views from the temple site. Needs a bit of climbing, but this should not stop you. Take your time, even if you are a bit older.

These caves are nearly 2000 years old and are STILL functioning as live temples and places of worship. It's amazing to know that the shrines have been carved into the caves. There are 5 caves in total. The first 3 are pretty big and it's worth have a guide book (or wikipedia) explain them, otherwise they look a bit samey. The last 2 are much smaller at the same time more intimate. Note that you don't need to take off your shoes until the entrance near the top of the climb up. You'll want to keep them on as it can be slippery after rain.

As a non Buddhist it was a little difficult to understand why so many idols were created however as a visual experience that reflected believers devotion, this is an experience not to be missed while you are in Sri Lanka. This is a large site that can absorb significant numbers of visitors, however for the best experience in the caves you probably want to visit before it gets too busy.  There is also a bit of uphill walking, so getting there early before the heat is also a good idea.

There is a nice story about the caves where you basically get to see many Buddhas in different sizes and poses. If you are into Buddhism you will find it nice and worth climbing to the top, after seeing an average museum in a swimming pool-alike interior (humid, with tiles on the floor). In my opinion you won't br missing much if you skip it. Maybe some funny monkeys along the way.

5 caves in all - self guided - but better with a local guide or a member of your party familiar with the traditions and development of the caves - some intricate cave painting on the walls and ceilings a highlight.

Offers 5 cave temples to explore at your leisure - if you aren't overly familiar with the traditions best undertaken with a guide who is well versed in the development of the caves and the buddhist paintings and sculptures  - visually interesting and an easy site to negotiate though possibly not for those lacking ambulatory capacity.

Temples are by far one of the best preserved of the ancient Cave Temples in Sri Lanka.what you are here to see is not at the bottom of the hill but at the top of the rock.Every hour there are buddha preast helding a cerimony lasting 10 minute to pray and thanks,There are also resting Buddha with foot aligned, two fingers under his face meaning is in a meditation status, before reaching Nirvana, highest level of transcenOver the centuries the caves have been decorated with statues of Buddha and wall murals over the cave walls and ceilings. The rock temples(5 of them) are certainly worth the climb, they are simply mind blowing. Wonderful place!Buddha statues carved from the rocks with brilliant colours , the colourful paintings / designs on the walls and roofs of the caves and amazingRichly decorated, beautifully carved buddhas and the reclining buddha was huge. Lots of different sites to look at.If you are very fit and young you can probably do it in 15 minutes,Need to climb 300 to 400 stairs to go up.We would recommend to do that site on a day trip from Sigiriya or other at your choice.

This site houses the cave (rock) temples, a Buddhist museum, a stuppa and The Golden Temple. The caves are beautiful - visit them in reverse order (from cave 5 to 1) to build up to the most impressive Cave 2. A bit of a climb up some steps but beautiful and worth the effort! Just make sure you buy your tickets before you start climbing the steps (from the ticket office on the right hand side of the museum building) The Golden temple (for a none Buddhist) is mainly a giant gold Buddha.
