This is not the worlds largest as one sign clams. In fact it  is not even the largest in Sri Lanka. But it is still very big! The museum is the only disappointing part - small, a lot of Buddha statues and little to no labeling! But entry is included in the ticket price for the rock temple so people still go to it

We visited on a stinking hot, humid day so we're very sweaty by the time we got yo the top? Need to be pretty fit and/ or take it slow as it's quite a strenuous walk up many steps- our calves were sore for 2 days afterwards. A great view from the top and the Buddha filled caves are magnificent . A expensive entry fee and the annoying very small but extra fee to "mind your shoes " were the only negatives to this very deservedly popular World Heritage listed site.

Nice place to visit. The walk up the hill is a good experience. If you go on a cool or rainy day, it will be more enjoyable. The tickets for entering the caves has to be purchased at the foot hills. If you go up without taking the tickets, you cannot enter! The tickets are a stiffly priced, though.

Visiting Dambulla an important holy place in Sri Lanka should not be missed! At the foot of the cave temples stands this modern GoldenTemple completed in 2000. These 5 separate caves contain about 150 stunning Buddha statues & paintings. Some of Sri Lanka's most important religious art was first created here over 2000 years ago. The place is absolutely beautiful!

Make sure you get a guide, I felt the caves were slightly overpriced for what you paid for. The walk to the top was beautiful and the same goes for the view once you were at the top. There's a beautiful stone staircase you need to climb and there's monkeys all along the way, they will take your food and flowers if you buy any so just be careful for them. People try and sell stuff which is pretty standard. I felt like this wasn't so much a cave temple more a tourist attraction. Anuradhapuras temples were still used for the locals as a place of peace and tranquility.

The temple caves were interesting however I made a pretty big mistake. I didn't get a guide to explain the background story of the temple caves to me. We have come from Anuradhapura where we spent a 7 hours walking around temples and stupas and it was pure magic, that was because of the guide we had. My favorite thing about Anuradhapura was that we didn't have to pay that much for what we saw, we paid the Tuk Tuk driver 2500 rupees to drive us around all day and too give us an awesome tour, he knew everything and was the best. I felt like the 1500rupees we paid today was 100% not worth it. Yes the caves look cool in photos but really it's nothing as special as half of the things we saw in Anuradhapura. My favorite part was the climb to the caves, beautiful walk up the mountain via a wide stone stair case covered in monkeys and amazing sites. If you have the money to spare like we do then do it but if you're traveling on. Tight budget and you still have more too see them I suggest you save your money for kandy or somewhere you're interested in

Worth a visit. You get to the museum with a large statue of Buddha painted in gold color and get tickets there. Post which it is a climb to the caves. Our driver and guide took us through a side route which helped cover around half the distance in the vehicle. Then it was a walk through a rough path, you could take the steps or the rough forest kind of path. Our kids wanted to go through the rough. Once at the top, you end up spending quite a bit of time admiring the sculpture, art and visualizing what it must have been to create. Very well maintained, neat, the locals take a lot of pride and explain every bit of history which they are aware of. The size of the sculpture and the sheer number of statues, along with the art work across the ceiling is worth the effort and time spent in getting here. Comparison with Ajanta and Ellora in India is inevitable. Both locations stand tall in their own right. Not to be missed.

It's a beautiful cave temple . It has many steps to climb. My kids enjoyed climbing the steps. It was raining but we enjoyed the rains too. Saw waterfalls from the caves. The view was awesome. Might be a difficult for elderly people. But have an alternate path without steps too. Can go by car but the entry was closed when we went. The tickets have to be purchased from the main museum . The caves are very well preserved and beautiful. Have different kinds of Buddha statues. Can spot many monkeys.

A place with a historicall  value bound with some ancient stories. One of the main historical  temples relate with kings times in the Country. You need to climb up on a rock to be to the Temple surrounded with beautifull sceneries  of the nature. This is a sacred  place and so you have to give the due respect.

The caves are truly beautiful.  We saw all five.  We waited outside along with everyone before the doors were opened and then quietly entered. The painting and all exhibits our stunning.  Make sure you take a sarong/sari or something to cover your legs and shoulders - you will not be allowed access to many of the temples without covering up and showing this sign of respect (applies to both men and women).
Bit a trek up to hill but nice  to see it and you can spot some monkeys around ;-)  As all attractions in sri Lanka overpriced (1500 ruppe )

Awesome, amazing, magnificent this does not even begin to describe the Dambulla Cave Temples. Caves are dated back to 1st century BC and consist of 5 caves and over 150 images of Buddah. a must see in Sri Lanka.
Good temple. huge idols. Need to climb 300 to 400 stairs to go up. Good view from top for couple of pics.
Good temple. huge idols. Need to climb 300 to 400 stairs to go up. Good view from top for couple of pics.
Everyone shall visit this. I was suprised for the second time here how nice it is. Climbing up  is a bit difficult in hot weather.

Absolutely amazing to see this old temple, well worth a visit. Just be irritated that you pay 1500 as a foreigner, much more than the locals, just as almost anywhere in Sri Lanka. In addition you will have to pay for leaving your shoes before the temple, again more than the locals. Not much, but that's the simple fact of squeezing anything out of tourists - who may either suggest Sri Lanka as a future visit - or not. Still suggest to go and see this cultural relic!

Arriving at the gigantic golden Buddha statue and museum overlooking the city, the golden temple was something that we had heard a lot about and were looking forward to. After a slow and gradual ascent, one reaches the actual caves. Once inside, there are simply no words to explain how pure the art and history of this place appears to be. Every cave had numerous statues, large sleeping Buddhas, elaborately hand-painted ceilings and ornate walls. Every form, every minute detail is painstakingly chiseled or painted out and the place oozes an energy of pure positivity. Being a UNSECO site, the lighting is well done with subtle lamps lighting up the statues and cave interiors at the right angles for it to seem larger than life. And that it truly is! It is highly recommended to go post noon when the sun is receding and then to watch the sunset from atop the hill. This way you get to see the caves when there is natural light as well as enjoy a gorgeous dusk. Overall, this is the place that I felt the most drawn to during my entire Sri Lankan trip and having seen statues of the Buddha in Japan, this is definitely unique for its Asian art forms, cultural backdrop and legends portrayed through paintings. Such a divine feeling!

The Golden Cave Temple is fascinating and beautiful.  It is a perfect place to learn about Buddha in all its poses from sitting to reclining to sleeping.  The wall murals are very well preserved and the site is lovely.  A must see.

Totally enjoyed the visit to the caves. It was a visit which felt very spiritual as well interesting archeologically. I must say the cave dedicated to Vishnu and other deities had a particularly moving atmosphere with its monks reciting mantras and parents bringing their babies to be blessed.  The monkeys added a fun touch to the visit, even saw one chewing gum!
Amazing place.. Definitely not to be missed while visiting Sri Lanka. Lot of monkeys around, so watch your belonging. Otherwise very safe and pleasant to walk around.

It is quite unique temple arranged in the cave on the top of the mountain It isabout 15-20min walk up the hill to reach it. Lots of monkeys on the way to the top. It is worth doing when you are near by, like Sigiriya I would not go there just for this temple itself. Entrance fee: 1500rupees

wonderful place very nice and all are very friendly there ,i can see not enough in this beautiful tempel and can say ,,all should visit this cave tempel of Dambulla,it is very good to arrive for all by bus and if you can take a tuck tuck or taxi,i enjoyed it very much
It was an interesting place to visit. Where you get to know a lot about Buddha. Beware of monkeys take care of your belongings and enjoy the view and you can get some amazing shot from it.

We had an amazing time to see about the Golden Temple. Very impressive. The only thing it bothered us was, the floor was quite wet and we had to walked as barefoot and quite slippery inside and barely can see which way to go.

It was sensational to see the gold cave temple of dambulla its great and after my first days with disaster I enjoyed the time here and I can say it was famously. I say all people which come to dambulla must see it. Super great

The climb to the temple is sometimes tough, but definitely worth your effort! In your way up, you’re been entertained by monkey, but be aware that you don’t go to close. Take some water with you during your climb. The caves are amazing. There are a lot of beautiful statues. It’s is very fascinating to see all those different statues and to hear about the rituals. We were there when a little ceremony needed to take place. It was time to feed Buddha. Everyone needed to leave the caves. One person stays behind. He locks the cave and feed Buddha. After 15 minutes the caves were back open and you can continue your visit.
The place is to be seen to be believed. Simply amazing.  Ignore the couple of shops enroute as the guys are quite cranky.
It's worth knowing the history of these temples. Be aware that you mustn't take pictures with the Buddha!

Everything is sold here, by the name of Buddha. Shoe keepers are 'vultures' - they thrust you to give Rs. 25 for "compulsory keeping" of a shoe pair (So, Rs. 1000 for a 40 people group!). Better put your shoes in a polythene bag and insert in your back-sack, before you reach the last stone step (otherwise these keepers won't allow you to enter, unless you handover those to them). Just like Sri Maha Bodhi and Kandy Tooth Relic Temple, this temple also 'detached' from the earlier common ticket for 'Culture Triangle' and developed as a separate 'bad business spot' with a Rs. 1,500 entrance ticket for foreigners disregard of at least their religion (except for Buddhist monks). Your Nature's Call is also poured as money into its Chairman's hands. Heard of his attempt to 'detach' this site from the UNESCO listing and make a sole 'dollar fountain'. Remember this site is not any more a property of 'Sangha' (the common monk society) but his personal ownership. There is some social benefits to the surrounding Buddhist society, including the TV+Radio transmissions. Business purposes have disgustingly destroyed the 'Buddhist' and 'World Heritage' impression. Anyway, better to avoid this place, as long as this torturing continues.

The Golden Cave temple is dedicated to Buddha and has been built over the ages, The oldest reportedly around 1st century BC to around the 18th century. There are numerous statutes of Buddha as also statues of Hindu gods and also of some of the Sri Lankan kings. It is fascinating to see the carvings which must have been painstakingly done in the ancient times. The artistry is  worth appreciating. There are also paintings on the roof at various places. You have to climb about  to reach the caves. Tiring on a hot day.

I and my colleague visited this temple on 27th August.  This temple hold much history.  We saw many interesting colorful pictures and giant statues there.  We saw lots of things around small area.  Our guide explained everything very well.  We saw water Lilly also.

We had a good day in the temple. From the heights of a beautiful view of the forest cover. I recommend not to climb the mountain in shorts, and then forced to cuddle towel, as the entrance to the temple is forbidden to open legs to the knee.

Very beautiful temple in Dambula. It is easy to get there, tuc tuc from Dambula costs from 100-200 rupees. The whole sight seeing takes around 1 hour. I recomment getting a tour guide because there are many things that you can miss if you dont have proper information. Also there are a lot of monkeys which make the true athmosphere. Cave temples are amazing, all 5 of them. The climb is not too heavy but i advise to take some water with you.

My first visit in Sri Lanka was that temple! U need to walk up on the mountain for 20 minutes in a little bit difficult way for old people, for me was perfect. You can enjoy thw mountains and the monkeys hugging eachother, but the best part is when u arrive to the top and u see all this nature beauty and this amazing caves full of peace and beautiful buddah images! The sculpturws are gigantic and thw draws in thw wall amazing. Too much peace and calm. It's a must to visit it!

In my opinion it was so full of tourists that it lacked atmosphere. It had also been restored to such an extent that it felt a little like a Disney version of reality. In my opinion if you get the opportunity to visit Mulkirgala (16km north of Tangella on the South coast) I will skip this one. Worth visiting the fruit and veg market that is on the left hand side of the road before you reach here. (Not that important but the toilet facilities are terrible).

The Dambula Cave temples should be a part of everyone's itinerary when they visit Sri Lanka. One can either club it with the Sigiriya visit or drive from Kandy. I do not remember whether SAARC nations pay a different entry fee or not. I think I paid 1500 LKR. The climb to the caves is pretty tasking. It takes a good 15 to 20 minutes to reach the top. The steps are steep and the path is made of cobblestones. At the entrance to the cave temple you are expected to leave your shoes behind. You can either leave them outside or pay 25 LKR and leave the shoes with the attendants. Women and men are expected to dress modestly. Women must be sure to keep their legs and shoulders covered. The cave temples are well kept and display numerous statues of Buddha in various forms/poses. The frescoes on the cave ceiling are also worth noticing. The huge size of some of the statues is overwhelming. Posing to click pictures with the statues is a strict NO. The view from the top of the hill is also wonderful. Carry an umbrella incase you climb up during mid day .

This was an unexpected delight. The guide books do not do it justice, you have to be there to fully appreciate the incredible number and range of Buddha idols, the cave paintings and the setting itself. As with many of Sri Lanka's attractions, there was a considerable climb involved but it was well worth the effort. There are five cave temples, each different and reflecting a different time period, but it is the carvings and statues which have to be seen to be believed - incredible.

We were on a tour of Sri Lanka and as part of the tour we stopped at the Golden Temple. Here you will find a giant golden Buddha, with a number of statue monks at each side. This is a spectacular sight, and can be seen from the road. But it doesn't stop there, as around the back and up above the Buddha are the Cave Temples of Dambulla which were also spectacular. NOTE: The walk up to the cave temples is not for the faint-hearted - it is a cobbled pathway and steps which is steep, and takes around 15 - 20 minutes to climb. Once at the top it is all worth it, as the caves are full of carves stone Buddha's in all of the familiar "poses". We were told that the caves were preserved with the help of the British back in the 1800's, but these days the whole site is a UNESCO cultural site. You can take photographs in the caves, but you must not take "selfies" as this is considered extremely disrespectful. You must also remove your shoes, and women must cover their shoulders. I'm not sure how much it cost as it was part of our itinerary and therefore pre-paid. Even if you don't know anything about Buddhism, you will find this place amazing. An excellent 1/2 a day out.

The first thing we did after checking in our hotel was to visit the cave temple. Luckly our hotel was next to the temple so we had no troubles reaching it. Climbing up to the top can be quite a task but the view from top is amazing. Once on the top you'll be asked to take off your shoes and then you'll enter the temple. It was a learning experience and we got lot of new things to see amd learn. Highly recommended.

This is an absolutely awe-inspiring, unique UNESCO cultural site.  The big golden budha and temple at the foot of the hill can be viewed on ground level, but you do need to be mobile to hike up stairs and slopes before reaching the heart of the historic treasure-filled caves.  Paintings, scultures, monkeys and wonderful panoramic views greet you.  Indulge! Budget 2 hours at least.

When you are visiting Dambulla in SriLanka than this place is must to visit, its a master piece of architecture and having 148 BUDDHA IDOLS carved from stone including one 40 meter plus sleeping Buddha. Its on height so please be carefull, climbing its little difficult.

Far up on a rock are the 5 caves featuring amazing art work in the shape of many Buddhas, all carved out of rock thousands of years ago. The biggest of the caves, cave 1, is featuring the most impressive lying Buddha - surrounded by almost an army of more Buddha images. The paintings of the ceiling are truly outstanding, considering their age. The caves get smaller in size as you move on, but each cave offers new fabulous sights which should not be missed. The cave temple can be accessed next to the Golden Temple, both situated at Kandy road. Bring along your heat absorbing socks to climb the last of the rock steps leading up to the caves. The granite steps leading up the rock can be climbed with your shoes on!
It was quite a walk up the cobbled stone pathway to the caves but once there - even for the older members of our group - a beautiful place not to be missed!
to reach this temple you have to climb a lot of steps. be aware of monkeys. do not instigate them.if you leave them alone, you can go your way peacefully.
Golden Cave Temple is the  main attraction in Dambulla and a must visit if you ever visit Dambulla. Very famous among the local and foreign tourists..

Another great cultural site in Sri Lanka and a must visit if you are interested in culture and if you are in Dambulla. Dambulla cave temple is very famous among the locals and is patronized by many all throughout the year.

It took about 30 min to climb to the cave temple. It was well worth it. Very interesting and can get very busy. You have to remove your shoes off before you enter the temple and there is a little way to walk  to the entrances, so if dry take socks as the ground is very hot.If you are taking photos you will need to use flash.Sometimes it is worth  a little wait to let larger groups go through as some caves are quite small. Take plenty of water with  you and be careful of the monkeys if you are carrying food of any kind. The museum at the bottom was interesting but very warm inside as there was no a/c

Built into caves in the rocks.  There is a climb up lots of stairs to get there so a level of fitness is required.  One marvels at just how these huge statues and laying down Buddahs were carved into such low roofed caves in side of mountain.
Wonderful walk up to the caves but the monkeys can be aggressive. The views from the top are lovely. All of the caves are different and the art work is outstanding. A very memorable experience.
Wonderful temple, very unique and worth the climb up. Quite cool inside so a pleasant respite from the heat.

It definately worthed climing the 364 steps. To enter the temple we had to take off our shoes. It is said to be one of the most impressive buddhist temples, and it really is. For me, the statues in all caves (some with enourmous size) show the kings' gratitude and respection to the buddhist monks, which impressed me the most.

We visited as part of our tour and really enjoyed the climb to the caves with monkeys everywhere. We you arrive the paintings and statues in the the caves are amazing and unbelievable that these were created so long ago. Well worth a visit x

The experience of going up the caves was a bit disappointing because I had another image of the caves but it was more like organized caves. Nevertheless the paintings inside the caves and statues were beautiful. Do ask for a 50% discount on tickets for SAARC countries.

I was a bit disappointed to climb up the hill because I was under the impression it was going to be a cave-like experience. But it was like well organized caves. The paintings and statues inside the caves were indeed beautiful. It is an expensive ticket for what you see up the hill but SAARC countries get 50% discount so be sure to ask for that. The ticket is only for going up the hill to see the caves, otherwise the Golden statue of Buddha can be seen up close without a ticket.

If you visited a lot of temples already, this is not worth a visit. It's quite expensive (12 dollar,  10 euros) and it's includes only four caves of duplicated statues. The view is nice, but you can see the view without paying. Do go see the Golden Buddha statue, that one is beautiful and free to visit.
Located close proximity to Kandy- Jaffan High way ,About 10km from Dambulla town ,A world heritage site , Worth visiting on your way,

A once in a lifetime experience. Easily accessible, not over crowded, magical and unforgettable. Don't forget that your shoulders should be covered and that you must take off your shoes - so come prepared with socks.

The walk up to the Monastery is enjoyable in itself. There are a few stalls half way up with water, clothes and souvenirs. There are also lots of monkeys around, so watch you have no food as they will steal it. There's a peaceful and spiritual vibe in each cave which you feel when walking around and it's quite something to think of the work that must have gone into carving the caves. There were a lot of Sri Lankan families when we visited as the locals use this monastery as a place of worship. Worth a visit.
Its a really amazing place to travel to and visit for a few hours. Buddha statues are very well maintained, and gives us an insight into the various Buddhist tradition. Its a must visit

We loved these cave temples, quite awesome and lots of history.  You can visit the indoor museum first then take the walk up hill to the cave temples.  There are 5 cave temples in all but only 3 were open to the public, and the statues are amazing.  Like all sacred places in Sri Lanka you must remove shoes (but you can wear socks) and headwear, and cover legs so it's a good idea to have a sarong in your bag.  You leave your shoes at a kiosk before entering the temple area.  If you are touring Sri Lanka's temples then this is a must visit!

This is a must see location.  There is a bit of a climb but one you are there you will be treated to some wonderful sights. Be warned there is little in the way of opportunity to buy a refreshment after the climb and descent.

The amount of work put into these caves must have taken them years. Its a must when visiting Sri Lanka. Amazing place. You hike all the way up and at the top before you go in you can pay to leave your shoes or just put them in your bag. Bring socks as the run in the sun on the hot stones can burn your feet.
Beautiful UNESCO site, 150 Buddha statues hidden in caves in the rock. Relaxing walk up to the temple and beautiful scenery.
Besides being a nice walk through the jungle leading to the temple, the site itself is mind-blowingly beautiful. Around 150 Buddha statues, hidden in caves in the mountain.
Buddhist ancient cave temple ...Dambulla is a World Heritage Site (1991) in Sri Lanka but the ambient was going fade due to the haphazard development around the temple

We were quite excited to visit the caves but were disappointed upon learning that headscarves aren't allowed and so we couldn't enter. What really pricked me was that the 'Sikhs' community are allowed their turbans as it is part of their religion, yet the head scarves which are part of Islam aren't.

Excellent place to relief mind and unite mind... calm .. quite and good place to meditate. It is a Buddhist temple and this cave is hundreds years old.  Very coulouful statutes and arts inside the cave. A natural cave converted to a temple by ancestors. Very nice place and a historic place to visit. from up on the mountain, you can see the landscape.
eventhough the caves are almost similar, but each has its own signature and recites Buddhism in its won way

it is a long way up... whether you chose to do it by stairs or by the normal road, you got to sweat but it is worthy. donkeys will give you some breaks and will amuse you till you arrive to the top. it is a unique philosophy to learn about Buddhism and their meditation and how they believe in Buddha and how actually they see him… you should get you water from the beginning because sometimes water is not found or sold the further you go.

I enjoyed this, lots to see. I did a group tour which I wish i had done it on my own and taken more time. I would say that some of this attraction is not suitable for those less able, the modern temple is easy to get to on foot but to climb to the cave temples is a lot of steps up. I quite fit and was struggling at points. Once up though the views are fab. Also don't wear flip flops - coming down the steep slopes is tricky with those type of shoes! And make sure you cover up both shoulders and way below the knee for men and women, a few ladies were turned away who had sarong style wraps as they don't totally cover you up - stick to trousers to be on the safe side.

Maybe it was just that I'd seen too many temples, or the fact that there were so many rude, loud tourists, but apart from the fine painting on the walls and ceilings, I could have given it a miss. Ritigala monastery was much more worthwhile in my opinion, and there was not the masses of hawkers trying to sell us anything.

The huge coach park and large modern buildings including a Buddhist TV studio tell you this is a major attraction before you get to the climb to the world heritage site, which pilgrims have visited for 22 centuries. It's worth it. With more than 150 Buddhas and wall paintings, the Hindu shrine near the caves' entrance was also busy when we visited.

I believe this is a world Heritage site. The temple is on a hill and you have to climb steps to get to it but worth the effort!! A serene spot with hundreds of statues of the Buddha in caves. The caves are covered in wall and ceiling murals. Never seen anything like this before!!
I was really looking forward to this stop in our trip, and it ended up being utterly disappointing. The cave painting were nice, but after a few minutes everything began to look the same.

golden cave temple is a fantastic place to visit for any one in any walk of life, 100 plus Buddha statues in ancient but brilliant colors the history behind the temple, the view from the temple terrace, negative gravity dribbling water and many more. It's always better to be at the temple around 7.00 in the morning or in the evening to avoid harsh sun while climbing the rock avoid feeding monkey as they could be a neusance to you

Some times its not a good idea to read your rough guide before you visit somewhere, I believed the hype a little too much and expected to be blown away but found the whole experience a little underwhelming, the three coach loads of camera wielding Chinese tourists that descended en mass didn't improve my mood. I would recommend going early in the day to avoid the crowds and the heat as with all religious sites its customary to remove your footwear by midmorning the ground is scorchingly hot, so beware.
Beautiful  place to visit. So much to look at & the sheer amount of artifacts is amazing.Allow plenty of time for your visit.

one of my most memorable place, nice view and love it's calm and peace environment. Frescoes are wonderful and you can see a fountain from the rock ceiling in the Rock cave. Very historical place and anyone must see this place. Take water bottle and you can get a guide to explain the Dambulla temple. Very clean environment and well maintained.

We probably made the mistake of doing Sigiriya Lion's Rock in the morning and the Golden Temple in the afternoon. It was quite an exercise for us that day doing 1200 steps up in the morning and around 360 in the afternoon. We also had the bad luck or maybe it was a good luck also of going there while it was drizzling a bit. It provided for a cooler climb than Lion's Rock but also a bit slippery if you're not careful. Some steps are real stairs while other portions are just sloping rocks. It's a beautiful temple, properly maintained and lighted too and as is customary for some temples there with relics and such, some parts are only open early or late in the day, that's why we went there late afternoon. The entrance fee was 1500rupees per person. Shoe safekeeping is 25rupees per pair at the entrance. You can go around on your own or you can opt for a guide. He was the guy at the entrance of the temple. He will charge 100rupees per person to explain everything to you. If you don't want him to accompany you be clear about it because as is usual with some of these areas, they will simply accompany you and make you think they are part of what you pay for as entrance and they will charge at the end.
This temple is so special, beautiful, peaceful and spiritual, a must see for any visitor to Sri Lanka. Whatever your religion or beliefs this is an amazing temple to visit and spend time at.

Don't miss visiting here. It's quite peaceful and relaxing. It was misty when we were here and this added to the beauty.. fortunately our driver cum guide was quite knowledgeable also explaining the religion well...

This is a beautiful and interesting temple with some nice cave paintings on the walls and ceiling. The climb is not too difficult but some level of fitness is probably required. The fit person will probably take 10-15 minutes and the less fit about 30 minutes. Best to do it in the morning to avoid the Sti Lankan heat in the afternoon.

a bit of a trek up lots of steps to get to the temple, lovely views, lovely temple. Leave shoes at the entrance and cover shoulders and legs. On the way up I bought some lovely flowers from a Sri Lankan lady and then further up the little monkeys stole of me to eat! Was very funny!

One of my fondest memories of Sri Lanka. Quite a walk uphill so do carry some water and stop along the way. Might be tough for elder folks as too many flights of steps to climb. Shorts not allowed for the guys and girls and no sleeveless for the girls. But all said and done, do make an effort to go see this place. You will be blown away.
Try to go here morning 7.30-8.30am to avoid tourist, the painting in cave are spectacular. There are a lot of monkey along the way to cave, be careful if carry any plastic bag.

Looks a bit garish at first sight but the caves themselves are very interesting with many statues. It's quite a climb up steep steps and slopes so some less able in our party found it pretty challenging, especially as it was very hot and humid.   Take water with you as there's nothing at the top or on the way up.    We were in a tour group and our local guide felt that the entrance fee was very pricey, and we gathered that it's privately owned now and not much is channelled back into it.

Visited the Golden Temple of Dambulla where inside stone caves, there are statues of Lord Buddha. It is situated on a top of a hill, so you have to climb and climb and climb but after some effort you would reach your destination. Important: Beware of crafty monkeys. Make sure you are hydrated. Remember to carry an umbrella and a water bottle or two.

If you are planning on visiting the Cultural Triangle of Sri Lanka, do make the trip to Dambulla. Located near Sigirya - the Lion Fortress - but unfortunately not part of the Cultural Triangle ticket, Dambulla is considered the spiritual heart of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. The five caves, carved from the 150 metres granite rock, house over 157 statues and thousands of paintings of Buddha and his life. Do listen to the guidebook and see the caves from cave 5 to cave 1. The most impressive are at the front. Like most of Sri Lanka's attractions, entrance isn't cheap, at 150LKR (USD$10-ish). I personally think it's well worth it, but be wary of the cheeky monkeys who will try to steal your food and lotus flower offerings (much to the laughter of locals!)

Go early before the heat of the day melts you. It is a bit over the top outside but quite inside. Beautifully decorated though the heat from tourist bodies is probably adding to the fungus damage. See it before it is lost forever.
Just like the reviews tell you - it's a 'must see'. Do attend with someone who can tell you something about Buddhism.

Another highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka this year.  While the environs have altered dramatically in the eighteen years since our last visit to Dambulla Rock Temple, the temple itself retains the unique sense of continuity and spiritual tranquility.  It can be a challenging climb for some, but if you start early and climb in the cool of the morning it is an experience unlike any other we have found.
Very interesting visit to the temple although very busy for the ceremonial occasions. wonderful insight into the age old rituals and figures of reclining Buddha.

A very interesting visit to the Golden Temple.  Be warned there is a climb of some 450 step but what you see when you get there is stunning both in terms of the sculptures and also the views.. Take water with you we did not. Shoes are removed at the temple as with other Buddhist visits we have made. The monkeys are entertaining too. Please also respect that you should not pose with Lord Buddha in photos.

The temple is 2 km away from Dambulla main bus stop (write "Dambulla Bus Station" on Google Maps if your are not sure where it is). We walked all the way to the temple (and back), it was a very interesting 30/45 mins walk. If you prefer, buses stop in front of the temple. Entrance fee should be 1500rs (I haven't noted down the price, so I am not 100% sure). Before starting the climb to the temple, buy the ticket at the ticket office. The ticket is then collected at the top of the hill. The walk up takes about 20 mins at a moderate pace. Once at the top, take your shoes off before entering the inner complex. Shoes can be left in a safe place for 25rs. Or you can keep them in your bag for free, up to you. The temple is a wonderful little complex of caves, frescos and statues definitely worth visiting it. If you go in the afternoon, as we did, you can then sit outside the inner complex and enjoy the nice view from there waiting for the sunset.

A short but steep climb is rewarded but some fascinating cave temples. These are decorated all over, and the style and painting changes from cave to cave depending on age. Worth having a guide to tell you which is which. The views from the top are fantastic also. A tip; take "temple" socks. It's a reasonable walk from where you have to leave your shoes, and if it's hot, it can get quite uncomfortable.

This beautiful temple is carved into a rock face and has beautiful outlooks as well as a beautiful temple. The walls and ceilings are painted beautifully and well preserved despite being very old. The statues are beautiful too.

I visited the caves the day before Sigiriya. They are spectacular.  The artefacts ate simply breath taking.  The climb up top the caves is not arduous.  Beware of cheeky monkeys who will grab carelessly placed bags.  As a place of workshop you can't wear shoes into the site. There is a place to leave them outside for a very modest fee. Don't haggle. In Australian currency the fee is about 25 cents! Well yaya what i was charged but i look poor when i travel ☺. Once inside do remember that this is a place of worship. A gentle reminder but i feel it is s privilege to visit places like this and always seek to respect the beliefs of other people. Not so the many people i saw taking photos of others worshiping.  Anyway. .. take your time here.  The caves are not huge but they are spectacular and you'll need time to truly take them in.  I went late in the day and lingered for about 2 hours.  Enjoy ☺

Its a bit of a climb to the top but well worth it. The workmanship was unreal, to carve these caves by hand from the mountainside is a feat in itself. Many statues of Buddha adorn the caves, and there is wall art and ceiling art also. The view was nice and there are plenty of monkeys to keep you company on your journeys up and down. Our group had our own guide but it could be done without one.
very impressive, i suggest early morning or later afternoon for visit, wear proper shoes and cover your shoulders to respect the sights please.

Its very inspirational place with such a atmosphere! Little climb to the top is not difficult, make sure you have proper shoes and plenty of water ( no flip flops i suggest). I would recommend to visit either early in the morning when they open or later close to the evening time. Please respect the philosophy and do not touch, or take picture with the statues, i have seen some tourists doing this, made me upset a lil bit.

When we arrived I saw the gawdily decorated temple at the base of the hill and my heart sank.  There was a mixture of steps and slope up to the Dambulla caves.  A tour was given to introduce us to the five caves which contained painted ceilings and so many buddha statues!!  Good view of surrounding hills from the top.  I liked the exterior of the buildings too - they don't look like caves from the outside.  Worth a visit as part of tour to Sri Lanka.

fantastic visit in combination with the golden temple below. was quite a trek to the top of the hill. steps and path were well maintained so not hazardous but a lot of steps so energy needed the temple at the top was well worth the walk and monkeys were entertaining on the way. the temple itself was so serene and quiet and the views of the surrounding countryside breathtaking. this is a religious community so some respect and moderate behaviour is appropriate. to think that the temple complex was carved out of the mountain using nothing more than primitive hand tools is humbling. a cultural gem.
Not only the temple is very nice but also the way up is not so tiring and the monkeys are just so cute.
Definitely worth a visit and the view from the top is amazing Not very busy in the evening which was great
Interesting place. We got a guide but would not recommend getting one Go at sun set..... View is mega

Lots of steps up the hillside from the car park area but well worth the climb. A series of caves full of Buddha carvings and paintings made at various times over the centuries. All are in a pretty good state of repair and the site is truly one of the crown jewels in the Cultural Triangle area of Sri Lanka. The best time to go is late afternoon when the crowds have been and gone for the day - you will get to see all the caves without them being full of other tourists

You climb about 200 stairs and what you see is another temple like many of you have around the area. The view is nice but for my opinion if you saw one you saw them all. It's better to pick a special one.
A stunning place! Although a bit of a climb it was worth it! Great views and great sights! One of the loveliest temples I have visited!

The climb to the Dambulla cave temple complex is nowhere near as taxing as the climb to the top of Sigiriya Rock and is a great alternative for anyone who is scared of heights or not physically fit. Whilst there are lots of steps, if you take water, a hat and sunblock and stop for rests along the way you should not have a problem making it to the top. You will be rewarded with great views and cave temples full of Buddhas and beautifully painted walls. There is also the opportunity to photograph Macaques, although beware of making eye contact with some of the adults - who can be a bit aggressive and cranky.

I read the review on tripadvisors which proclaimed that this is a must see place in Sri Lanka. But it is really not worth the steep climb up the mountain.  There are a few caves and all of them feature similar Buddha statues albeit a little difference in size. Disappointing as it was not an easy climb and weather was hot and humid.

The cave temples can be accessed by a short yet mildly intense trek over well laid out steps and rocks. The route contains some touts and fruit sellers. Caps or hats are not while modest clothing is required in the temple premises. The five temples are each fascinating in their own right and the Buddhist museum at the entrance is also very interesting. The statues and paintings are beautiful and with a knowledgeable guide, they come to life in the dark yet cool caves.
A rather steep step climb with little areas for breaks. Loads of monkeys so hold onto your belongings. It is incredible to find these pieces of history so well preserved.

Hello, My name is Bogdan Muncus and together with my girlfriend we visited this beautiful Golden Temple of Dambulla in September 2015. I have to say that is a must seen temple on your tour in Sri Lanka, a work of art with beautifull caves on the top of the hill. Very well preserved statues of Buddha inside the caves and a very peaceful atmosphere.You can find a lot of monkeys near the caves, but be aware, they can be aggressive. In conclusion, do not miss this Temple during your vacation in Sri Lanka! Best regards, Deborah & Bogdan Romania - 15.09.2015.

The cave temple in Dambulla is a must visit place if you are travelling to Dambulla area in Sri Lanka. The temple contains ancient cave paintings related to Buddhism. You need to climb the rock to visit the cave temple, and if you are climbing make sure that you take enough water and other requirements. Since this is a religious place you need to adhere to the formalities as instructed.  You can’t wear any hats or shoes when you enter the temple on top. You have to keep them in the counters near the entrance. Also you need to dress in a way that you are not revealing too much of your body. For men try wearing long jeans a shirts. Tourists requires to buy a ticket to enter into the temple, which can be bought near the entrance of the temple. There are large amount of monkeys along the way which can be troubling sometimes. Try not to feed them to avoid any hassle. There are several caves inside the temple where you will find number of statues of lord Buddha and other gods. Also paintings can be seen on the rock ceiling. You are allowed to take photographs inside the place. However note that the light in the caves are low hence you may need a good camera to get quality pictures.

You need to climb the rock to visit the cave temple, and if you are climbing make sure that you take enough water and other requirements. Also paintings can be seen on the rock ceiling. You are allowed to take photographs inside the place. However note that the light in the caves are low hence you may need a good camera to get quality pictures.

Very interesting and beautiful ! The Cave temples are a gem and must visit place in Sri Lanka. You really do not need a guide to visit these caves, done at various periods in time and filled with loads of Buddhist sculptures and paintings.

There are five cave's and each one as a story , 1) Dev Raja Viharaya 2) Maha Raja Viharaya 3) Maha Alut Viharaya 4) Pachma Viharaya 5) Devana Alut Viharaya This is a mogern temple lying at the foot of the cave temples hill established as a monastery
Amazing peaceful place. Beware of the monkeys and don't ever feed them. A lot of sellers as usual but be brave and say no. Would go back.

I really enjoyed my time visiting this attraction. There are portions that are totally a scam to bring money into the place, yet there are other portions that are really fascinating and truly worth taking the time to stop and check them out.

I really had a great time visiting the caves in Dambulla. The trek up the numerous series of stairs was invigorating. I totally suggest going to this in the later portion of the day as the heat and number of people visiting the  caves diminishes. Be prepared to pay a bit of a hefty entrance fee, but honestly, it's really worth it! While my time visiting the numerous world heritage sites and temples in Sri Lanka was filled with frustration as the blatant and systematic foreigner-targeted price gouging, I really couldn't be too angry after experience the many delights of the Dambulla caves. The Buddha statues are true works of art, and there is a sense of peace and calm that fills you as pass through the numerous caverns. I captured some amazing photos of my time here, and overall can't say enough about this experience. It's a MUST see!!! Just GO!!!!!

The Naga Tribe arrange this cave and presented to the Buddha and for his students. This temple really belongs to the Naga tribe. One of the main tribes of Hela. 1 st Bce King Valagamba presented big land for this temple. And ordered to built two stupas inside. After starting to make statues of Buddha, inside of this cave also started to make statues. Different times carved many statues. The most important statue carved on a monolith granite. Resting lying Buddha. Later this cave divided in to 5 rooms and now you can see 156 statues of Buddha. In the period of King Nissankamalla (1187-1196) he spent 17 pots of gold to plate 77 statues of Buddha. One is the big resting lying Buddha in the 1 st room. Gold plated only Buddha's cloth. Not the whole body. This is the only Buddhist monastery have the gold plated statues Buddha. All other temples gold was grabbed by the Portuguese, Dutch and the British.

Although the temple looks a little garish from the ground with it's gold temple and kitsch dragon mouth the real attraction are the cave temples.  I wasn't sure  I would manage the 400 steps up to them as I'm getting on a bit and have arthritis in my hip but our driver took as up a road where we could join the climb half way up which was a lot easier. The caves are mind blowing with the buddha's having been carved out of one solid granite rock. Everywhere there are beautifully painted murals and it is mind blowing that most of this was done in 2nd century BC.  If you visit take socks as the rock outside is very hot and you obviously have to remove your shoes. Well worth a visit.  It's mind blowing and stunning.

Without giving the game away too much, the stories behind these caves are fascinating and the frescos represent an amazing charting of the religion. Loved visiting here and the small museum was also fascinating, the highlight, a monk marking our visit on palm leaf in the traditional way. Was quite special.

Very nice view from the top of the hill. The caves contains wonderfully well conserved Buddhas and wall paintings. 400 steps to climb but you can rest if needed so don't be afraid of the climb. Take you time it is worth the effort.
Really interesting.  The cave is situated at the top of the hill, make sure you have good walking shoes on.  There are also a lot of monkeys here and some locals selling crafts.
5 caves with wall paintings and Buddhist and Hindu Statues. Very impressive and good atmosphere. Don't miss this.
This temple is a must see if you go to Sri lanka, the caves have multitude of colorful statues, small stupas which you can take pictures from as you wish.

I was pretty sceptical about heading to another temple only to get ripped off for being white, but I really did enjoy this one. It is quite a walk up a long hill with yet more stairs, so be prepared to sweat a fair bit before arriving to the destination. The views are good but if you have been to Sigiriya or Pidurangala before this, it has nothing on them for a view. The caves themselves have some interesting artefacts and are large, cool and interesting.
Definitely worth a visit!!! The paintings and the statues in the temple are incredible!!! The view from the top of is amazing.
I was really surprised after visit the golden cave temple.I have been there when i was little.But this time I was well aware of the history of this temple.
Amazing place, well worth a visit. Fantastic paintings on the walls and ceilings with loads of Buddha's in the caves
Fantastic historical cave temple. The paintings on the walls and ceilings are spectacular and it is well worth the climb up the steps to get there.

Last week i visited the place. WOW!!!! Excellent place to visit in Sri lanka, Golden temple full of Buddha statues with colorful. The place are clean and Neat. From this top you can see the beauty of Sri lanka. I love IT!!!!!

Quite a climb to the top but worth it! I wore flip flops which weren't ideal, some of the way up/down is rock rather than steps so I would say wear something with a bit more support. Lots of monkeys on the way up which are quite cheeky, I think they could smell food in our bag so kept jumping on to it, but it was all good fun! Once you get to the top there are 5 caves to look into plus a Hindu shrine. We had a driver guide who gave us some background in each cave which was good, especially for the awakening of Buddha that is depicted on the ceiling in one of the caves.

The cave temples are a magical place that breaths calm and peace. A short climb on a few set of stairs and you will reach the caves. Please remember to buy tickets from the office before climbing, otherwise when at the top, the security will send you back down to purchase the tickets. Personally, I have found this set of temples, the best we saw in Sri Lanka.

What a beauty after this difficult way up about 700 stairs. Take you're time with pace a walk up, these caves aare amazing as you can understand all carving is done inside the caves. Very impressive really recommend a must see in Dambulla
walk up a lot of steps to an Amazing view. Temples are really interesting - the murals are beautiful and the whole thing is very peaceful, definitely worth going

This cave is amazing. Full of Color. Make sure you bring good quality of camera because this cave is low light and dark. Try to climb on the side way where you can see family of monkey around. I take tuk tuk from my hotel in sigiriya to go here, and pay so expensive around 1700. If you stay in Sigiriya just take public bus to dhambula for 30 mnt ride and you pay around 40 Srilanka rupee

This and the Golden Cave nearby are really interesting and well worth the effort to get an idea of the Buddhist influence and history. Both sites can be visited in half a day but be prepared for a climb to the Golden Cave.

Just astounding to see the archaic frescos and link them to the history. Is worth the few pennies compared to other severely overpriced working temples. The hike up is uncomfortable and horrid in the sun but with time is worth the effort. A few monkeys accompany you on the way and there are also a few sellers to fend off. What awaits at the top is just stunning and humbling really. The clarity of the frescos and well kept Buddha statues is impressive. Was also tickled with Buddha radio and TV station broadcasting at the bottom and the temple donated by South Korea

Beautiful temples within the rocks - each of the five 'caves' has its own atmosphere and collection of Buddha statues and wonderful wall art. Quite a long walk up the hill - and don't forget to wear suitable clothes for a religious site (ladies - cover your shoulders and probably knees too). Lots of monkeys in the hills around.

This was a rather rushed visit because I just finished climbing Sigiriya when I decided to proceed to Dambulla for the Golden Cave Temple to complete my wish list. The Cave Temple is a steep climb and considering the very limited timeframe it turned out to be a gruelling experience. Could have enjoyed the trip were it not for the great rush.

We went here after the rock fortress and it wasn't in the same league. Many of the paintings and statues appear to have been touched up extensively . The highlight for my children were the monkeys who sit on the steps leading up to the temples .

This was a lovely visit with a bit of a climb to get here and enter the caves. Once inside very surprised at the amount of carved Buda  inside and the beautiful decorated walls and ceilings so well preserved there are about 5 caved with very large carvings inside so worth a visit There is also a modern temple at the base of the climb with great views Don't forget these are religious sites to be respected
Well worth the walk to the top with some very unique things to see. Be careful of the monkeys though as they stole our flip flops.

At the base of the complex is a modern temple which is very brightly coloured and worth a quick photo, but it's the cave temples at the top of the cliff that you head for. there is a bit of a steep climb up to the temples, which can be slippy in wet/damp weather so wear sturdy footwear. The temple complex is white on the outside and runs along the ridge of the cliff making it look very  attractive. Inside there are a series of different cave temples which have been dug out of the rock. It is dark inside but the wall carvings are impressive.

This is a very beautiful and peaceful place. There is a strenuous walk up many steps to the actual temple but the rock carvings are certainly worth the exertion! There are dozens of carvings of the Buddha which make this a truly mystical place to visit. Watch out for the monkeys on the way up and down, they will steal anything!!

I had not known about this place and the steps to get there were a worry to me with a bad knee, but I am so glad that I persevered and gradually walked up the steep slope. This temple, built inside a very large rock some 2000 years ago is something you shouldn't miss. There are 5 caves in total all decorated from ground to ceiling with paintings and statues of various Buddhas. It is over 2300 years old and was a refuge for the King during war. This should definitely be on your itinerary as should not be missed. It is well worth the visit and the views are spectacular.

Great place to go to and visit, especially inside. The tradition for some people is to buy some flowers as you go up, to leave in the temple. You will therefore see some people selling flowers on the way. Closer to the place, you should take off your shoes as you are not allowed in with shoes. You can take a plastic bag or a small useless bag to put your shoes when you take them off. You can then leave them somewhere near where most people leave their shoes. There are people who take payment when you leave your shoes with them. A lot of people pay for this service, which in my view is available if you simply put your shoes elsewhere around the same area. We were not aware of this till we saw some people doing it. You should also be dressed modestly, otherwise you may be denied entry. If you are denied entry, some local people will be close by, ( that is their job, not official though), to provide you with appropriate clothing items for a charge. There lots of monkeys that you see on your way up and down to the Temple. My digital camera cover was snatched by a monkey on my way up, but was able to retrieve it. It was hilarious!

Loved this old temples. Compared to other attractions it's half the price. We paid 1.500rs each. It's quite a climbe to the top but on the way you can find shade under the trees. When we were halfway we didn't take the stairs. To the right is a path without stairs and it easier to walk. The caves are beautiful with nice statues and paintings all around.
fantastic historical temple, an easy climb up the steps and a wonderful view around, well maintained old monument

One of the temples most beautiful I've ever seen. The climb is long but worth it. At the base is a modern temple, nothing to do with the old. The paintings and statues inside the caves are beautiful, incredible as they dug into the rock. Wonderful.

The temple is very nice from the outside.  We could see the Monks in praying position in line inside the temple.  We were too tired coz we had finished Sigiriya earlier. We did not want to go inside coz of the tiredness. There is entry fee for this. All i can say is that the caves did not look real but looked like man-made.
Not to tough to walk up and you are rewarded with a cave world of ancient Buddhas. Each King added there chambers of magicial Buddhas to create this wonder.

The Golden Caves are beautiful and worth the 15-20 minute walk up. This is a paradise for those who are interested in photography. So many Buddha's in so many different poses. I was worried about the walk up because I traveled with my mom who is 60 and has bad knees. We stuck to the trail option (not the stairs) on the way up. It does look a bit steep (ie: intimidating) at a few parts, but there are handrails along the sides for the most part. If you are concerned, just take your time and go slow! Once we got to the top, was pleasantly surprised by the nice breeze and the peaceful view (including Lion's Rock in the distance). The caves are interesting, but the ceiling is also very detailed. I enjoyed cave 2 the best, as it is the biggest of the 5 and you can just take your time and walk around without feeling like there are too many people. On the way down, we took the stairs - which was a lot easier on both our knees. There are monkeys along the way but they do not bother you, if you don't bother them. Please be considerate about getting in front of their faces (especially if they have a young one). Also, on the way down we bought slices of mango from the vendors, which was very good to just stop for a minute, have a bite, and admire the surroundings. (Bathroom facilities here are not the best but will do if you urgently have to go.) Enjoy!
The walk up is very easy, the artwork is heavily oriental influenced, and the cave temples and the view is stunning!
It's a very nice site to see. I suggest this more that many others. Complexe pf cave painted and full of buddhas.

Go early to avoid the heat. The steps seem endless on the climb up to the caves when it's hot. Take water and socks with you. There are monkeys sitting on the railing watching you struggle up the mountain. There are also men selling moonstone and other jewellery. One even showed us a shortcut near the top which was appreciated. Four caves are very interesting but Cave number five was smaller and less beautiful. The paintings are incredible.

There are a LOT of stairs here. Perhaps if I hadn't climbed sigiryia earlier that day I'd have been a lot more peppy and up for it! The caves themselves are beautiful and it's fascinating to see so many buddhas of all shapes and sizes. You do have to remove your shoes so maybe pack some socks as the ground gets very hot! Also just be wary of causing offence; make sure your legs and shoulders are covered and take off your hat and shoes. Also don't pose next to the statues as this is seen as deeply disrespectful. You can also get a good view of sigiryia in the distance. A must see for budding photographers.

We went up with our family and an elderly couple. There were lots of stairs to climb to get to the top, and overall, it is an okay place to visit, especially, for those who want to see  lots of Buddha statues that were made during the reigns of different Sri Lankan kings.
Awe inspiring sacred temple. A must visit. Be sure to wear long pants / ladies dresses that cover your knees. Best time to visit morning before 10am and after 4pm as the heat is tolerable.

Be prepared for quite a few stairs and have your shoulders covered.. As is standard for any temple. The Dambulla cave temple complex is a Unesco World Heritage site. It consists of five caves in which there are Buddha statues and wall paintings contributed by Sri Lanka kings over a span of two millennia. The site is not large, however the quality of sculpture and painting is very good, and it is interesting to see how the image of Buddha evolved over the centuries. To access the site, you need to park on the new parking lot next to the new golden temple. This temple has a huge modern Buddha statue which definitely attracts attention, but is unremarkable other than for its size. I would recommend to avoid the golden temple and accompanying museum. Tips: - The cave temple is at the top of a rock, which is a strenuous walk. Do not forget to buy your tickets at the bottom, near the golden temple, as no tickets are sold at the top. - The site is an active temple, and will be crowded with worshipers. You will have to enter bare foot (there is a shoe minder at the entrance), and have covered legs and shoulders. No hats/caps. If possible, wear white, like the locals do. - Take water - the walk will be hot. - There are lots of monkeys along the path. Make sure you keep all your belongings with you, as the monkeys will be aggressive and steal any food or object they can get a hold of. - When you find a cave too crowded, try to move to another cave which may be less full - Ideally, have a local guide, who can explain the various statues, poses and religious significance - this will add a lot of depth to your visit.

This is a must see when you are in the cultural triangle. The sheer scope of the cave paintings are breathtaking. Best time to climb up to the caves is early morning before the rock face heats up. Watch out for the hoards of thieving monkeys who were observed jumping on to a lady's back to steal the flowers from her hair! There is also a prevalence of hawkers who are very insistent and are known to block your path in their eagerness to make a sale. There is police presence on the rock if you need them. Allow about an hour or more just to take in the caves plus an hour for the trip up and back. Both males and females should wear long pants to enter the caves or hire a sarong for a fee. Ladies are also required to wear a sleeved top (short sleeves are fine). Shoes must be removed prior to entering the caves with a holding service provided for a small fee, alternatively if you are carrying a backpack you could store your shoes in there. The locals climb bare foot or with flip flops, however, as mentioned earlier the rock and steps heat up very quickly, so keep that in mind. It is a good idea to carry water with you.

I visited Dambulla Caves on  short trip to Sri Lanka. I had read nothing about the caves so did not know what to expect. I have to say that on my entrance to the first cave my jaw dropped. The entrance to the Dambulla Caves is up alot of steps, behind the Golden Temple. The Giant Buddha on top of the golden temple is a sight to see anyway but is nothing compared to the caves themselves. Be warned that there are alot of steps, seemingly never ending. I found it quite hard going especially in the heat. You will need to take water. There are also numerous monkeys on the way up - which you either like or get annoyed by. The monkeys are not aggressive but they will steal any food or any flowers you have with you (many people take flowers as offerings to the temple ). There are some great views on the way up to the caves  - a good excuse for stopping and catching your breath. At the top you'll see a series of white fascades   - bizarrely reminding me of old English cottages but these mark the entrances to the caves. There are 81 caves overall, 5 of which are open to the public. They are still uncovering/restoring some of the caves but it's quite rightly designated as a UNESCO world heritage site. The first cave is really small but holds a considerably large resting Buddha. This for me was a jaw dropper. Like other ancient sites, you have to wonder why and how these monuments were built. The other 4 caves are a little bigger but still spectacular and full of Buddhas and worships to Buddha. Check out the ceilings in some of the bigger caves as there are some interesting paintings. Note that you have to take off your shoes way before you get to the caves - it was around 25 rupees to look after a set of shoes. Many local school children walked the whole way up without their shoes but most foreigners held onto theirs until the very last minute I really had not known how much history Sri Lanka has, and I wish I had hired a proper guide to give me more insight into the story behind this heritage site The cost of the tickets was around 15USD, so it was cheaper than the other UNESCO sites in the country , but in my opinion it was by far the best place to visit

As you enter the temple you could be mistaken to think it's just another temple - but if you take the trip up to the caves up top (some 300 steps above)  you'll be able to visit the caves which a brim full of Buddha statues, intricate paintings, lily ponds and wild monkeys - oh and if you go late afternoon / early evening, as you climb up you'll be welcomed by a fresh breeze and a possibility of seeing the sun set.

There is a lot of history to the different caves and statues showing Buddha in many stages of his enlightenment so it may be worth having a guide.  Flowers can be bought on the steps up to the caves and offered at different places in the caves and there will be locals having private ceremonies and prayers for loved ones.  Great respect is shown so ladies must cover their shoulders and legs....a good tip is to always travel with a sarong in your bag as you never know when you will see a beautiful temple to visit in Sri Lanka, I had one rolled up in my bag and it was a saviour on our tour around.  Also you must never take photographs with your back to a statue, it's fantastic that photographs are allowed to showing respect is the least one can do.  Overall, a very blessed and emotional place, all made in the rocks, amazing! I would definitely go back!

Rock Temple in Dambulla, also known as Golden Temple is one of the UNESCO World Heritage sites in Sri Lanka. There is an LKR 1500 entrance fee for the Rock Cave at the top. The tickets are purchased at the bottom of the hill. The walk up is very pretty with monkeys watching over you at the lower portion and many spots to stop and take photos. There are also some t-shirt/handicraft souvenir vendors halfway up the hill, alongside women selling waterlily blossoms to offer to the Buddha. Wear good walking shoes, take cold bottled water, and have a good amount of battery life for your camera. The tickets are not collected until you reach the cave at the top. Prior to entering the ‘cave’, you remove your shoes and pay a fee of LKR 25 for your shoes to be checked in. We were very impressed with the extensive and intricate ancient carvings and sculptures and how well preserved they are.
One of the must visits in dambulla and a historical and cultural locations. If you are passionate about the history and culture of Sri Lanka a must visit. Beware of monkeys.

We didn't plan this into the itinerary but so happy we managed to add into or way from polonnaruva to kandy. Entrance is 1500lkr, I agree the place could be more well organized in terms of information and guiding, however, all the along Buddha statues, wall paintings are beyond expectation. Not too touristic and way up is quite easy,  stunning views at surroundings and don't miss the golden Buddha at the mountain foot.

We like history and culture and to understand the situation be-folded years back in each monument or temple or museum. History wise it's maybe interesting (though it's not really) but the presentation is very poor and there are no explanations to be found around the whole complex - specifically in the museum - which is also  very hot and suffocating. The temple and caves are not worth taking your shoes off (and you have to !!) and walking in agony for a few hundred of meters to them all. There are better places for amazing views and statues (like Sigiriya or Anuradhapura). Not worth the entrance fee (of 1500 LKR per person) and time wasted.

My spouse and I, and one other, visited during a private tour of Sri Lanka. Thankfully, our driver/guide drove us halfway to the top so that we had a bit more time to spend looking about. Dambulla Cave Temple is a World Heritage Site situated in the central part of the country, and is the largest and best preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. We were able to visit five of the caves, each one offering different statues and paintings, all in a great state of preservation.  One experiences a peaceful aura, or atmosphere that is almost spiritual.
Worth a pic stop for its gigantic Buddha statue and the Gold stupa. Entrance is free to the Golden Temple.

We visited on a late afternoon so not very busy. It was quite a climb but aptly rewarded with superb view at the top and interesting cave temples. Our favorite part was the thousand of Buddha images hand drawn onto the the cave roof. Unless you are a Sri Lankan, you need ticket at Rs1500/adult. Purchase at the Golden Temple ticket office. Do not ascend the stairs without ticket as you would have to make your way down and up again as we have seen with some visitors.

One of the hiding places of King Walagamba when he re-group his battle force. Once he got his crown back he turn all his hide places to temples. This one is the biggest cave temple in Sri Lanka. Once you reach to top you will me ancient temple as well as nice panorama view. Very calm and quite place. Recommend for a visit to all foreigners  😀
For me 10 $ it's too much for this temple, anyway it's interesting and well conserved. If it is hot, climb to the top will be not funny!

It is a small climb to the cave and 9 caves all together i believe. Go by morning or evening to escape the heat. each cave dates to a century and says some story and symbols of Buddhism. Certainly a place of history, do not be missed. view of the surrounding from the hill top is very good.

We visited early in the day - best to avoid the heat with the climb and burning feet on the stones . Monkeys are everywhere and I was wishing I had had that rabies shot ! Be careful ! It was a Saturday and there were many local families visiting with children taking fruits and flowers as offerings to the Buddha . The children were divine - beautifully dressed and very sweet . Caves were beautifully presented with many paintings . Well worth the visit

Walked up in the morning. Quite a walk up the hill, especially if hot (is it ever anything else!) Really nice temples in the rocks, well kept. There's even a Hindu shrine (Buddhists' are so inclusive). A few trinket sellers on the hill, but they do take no for an answer. Monkeys too, but they're fine, if you don't feed or annoy them. Huge Buddha statue at the bottom of the hill. Toilets a bit basic.

When I remind myself of the fact that most of this amazing place was carved out of sheer rock and religiously beautified so many centuries ago, it baffles my imagination! Its awe inspiring to note that exact dimensions of repeated designs on the under-side of the rock actually is beyond human effort in that distant past. The modern addition are no where near though.

This is a magnificent place to visit.we stayed in Gimanhala hotel which was half an hour drive from here.we experienced awesome climate as it was rainy that day..HAVE IN MIND THAT U SHOULD WAKE A LOT to reach the final place(the temple)..you can either take the steps or the slope path..you have to pay like 1000 INR per head to get in .....U shall find loads of monkeys wandering here n there..(nice sight) ABOUT THE TEMPLE: there r separate sanctorum for different gods and the buddha is humongous that u cant cover the whole statue wid a single clickk....adjacent to it there r many buddhas statues erected.......it is basically a temple carved out of a rock.....and at the very entrance lies a huge golden budhha...and there is also a museum containing paintings...SO its definitely a nice place  to visit with friends family
very impressed with the structure and though it was hot we enjoyed our visit and would inform our friends to visit this special place as it displays Sri Lankan artistry and culture
Unique caverns with countless Buddha statues. Look for a few Hindu gods nicely admitted into the caverns, too.

I visited Golden Cave Temple in Dambulla in late May, 2015. The weather was quite warm, but the caves are cool. The temple area is so clean, quiet, and visually stunning. I went with a tour guide which made the difference; from Genuine Sri Lankan tours, Koshala was very knowledgeable about the history of the temple, the purpose of the temple, key attributes of Buddhism and lots of little trivia. Its amazing to experience the history of a people from 2100 years ago. Sri Lanka is a beautiful, graceful, friendly country. It was my first visit there, but definitely not my last.
Interesting and a must do if only in Sri Lanka once in your life. Big Buddha's and nice view of surrounding area.
U must visit the place.people who would like to climb and walk through environment while feeling the religious value this is the place

The temple and cave, the carving, the history . You will enjoy a visit to this place.There are tour guides who will tell you the stories and history in English. They also speak other languages like German etc.
Well maintained and nice to see the huge Golden Buddha statue. Don't miss to visit the cave temple where you can see 150+ Buddha statues. On the top of the hill you can see Sigirya hill !!
Very nice and well maintained monastery. There are around 150+ Buddha statues and rock paintings. To see this however you need to have a small walk on the hill!!
It is worth to see these beautiful old paintings .Please do not go with hot sun between 11am -2pm as your feet will cath up with hot sun because you have to remove shoes and walk for short distance.
This is a great temple in the rocks.  The different varieties of Buddha and the Hindu influences there are very good.
Absolutely worth the climb up the hill, to the Dambulla Caves where incredibly beautiful wall paintings and Buddhas, very nicely illuminated.

The Golden Temple is a shame, as its ugliness takes away some of the beauty of the absolutely amazing Dambulla Caves up the hill, about 160m steep climb and well worth it. Beautiful wall paintings and best Buddhas we've seen in Sri Lanka.
It was nice and memorable to visit the golden temple. The place nice and clean and facilities for visitors is also very good.
... But the view is worth it. You can see Damnulla as well as all the way over to the Sigiriya Rock fortress. Be careful with the monkeys as they are all around this temple.

I would love to visit this place again and again. Don't keep yourself occupied only with the caves' interior. Sit down a while before departure and enjoy the majestic landscape of the plains extending as far as Sigiriya. On your way down, after admiring the sculptures and the frescoes, zoom in on the distinctive feature of the Sirigiya Rock Fortress. Also, stop awhile and taste the delicious mangoes the wayside stalls have to offer. The souvenirs may best be left for a better shop.

Quite a climb up the temple. It was raining when we climbed. There are steps but there are also parts where its just a gentle slope on the rock and these parts were very slippery in the rain. If climbing in a dry weather, would be worth it. Must remove shoes. But its beautiful. There are 5 cave entrances. Each entrance will have a different buddhist temple. Really beautiful paintings on the ceilings of the cave. A must go. The walk around the temples would be faster than the climb up.
We were lucky enough to have a guide who explained a lot to us. As you have to take your shoes off, it's worth wearing socks as the ground can get really hot. an amazing place to see,

Now charging US$20 per person, increase from $2 late last year. Quite a large entry fee for quality for the site. Am sure it has cultural and historic significance but no information available at the site. Can use Internet or a guide to find out more. Would be improved if the site and museum had better information. Not worth it for us.
Interesting temple, different from many other ones. It is a long climb , better go early in the day.

Not for the unfit. Worth the sweat getting there. Its hot and there are many steps to climb. Peddlers will try and sell you their wears, up to you, but you can find it all cheaper in town. The Cave temples are amazing and bring a wonderful history to you.

We have been to a few temples and historical sites in Sri Lanka. As a general note, entrance fees in Sri Lanka are overpriced. So I was hesitant to visit this temple after already spending so much money on other sites. But I'm really glad I spent the $11 dollars to get in. It was a wonderful visit and these caves really are a special place, and would recommend for others with an interest in historical sites to visit. I didn't realize how large the complex was. There are several caves to visit, and each of these is covered with beautiful ceiling paintings and sculptures depicting Buddha's life.
the temple on the rock is very impressive the site is really beautiful and on the top of the rock this building is incredible

With. Series of caves 100s of ancient statues, rock cave walls with paintings covering an area of more than 2000sqm, world heritage site assigned by UNESCO since the early 90s, is a definite place you must visit on your trip to Sri Lanka, cost of entry to temple to any foreign visitor $ 13 approx, local visitors no cost, hug parking area left of the modern giant golden Statue area, best times to visit 0630-1000hrs and 1500-1730hrs, in between 1000-1500hrs the sun is up and the rock gets really hot climbing approx 160 meters is tough, very busy during full moon days, takes about 1h30min to complete a visit. I highly recommend anyone to visit this great ancient site..

Having an arthritic hip I was concerned about the climb but whats a little pain when  such impressive caves are at journeys end .Great story telling artwork on the cave walls and far reaching views from the peak. Fun to see monkeys stealing lotus flowers left by devotees and devouring them. interesting to see Sri Lankans climbing bare foot.

We had a tour from one of the guides who was at the entrance (we didn't agree a price at the outset but he was happy with the tip we gave him at the end) this was invaluable as he explained all the basics of Buddhism, which came in handy for our later tours. The story accompanying each cave was fascinating and the paintings were beautiful. The real highlight was the view once you reach the top of the stairs.

The Golden Cave Temple in Dambulla is a very important religious and historical site in the midlands of Sri Lanka. At its entrance, you could see a large golden seated statue of Lord Buddha.
